## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/akwarium-artura.md`

```markdown
# Akwarium Artura

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Akwarium Artura |
| Activity ID | `akwarium` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A calm canvas aquarium. Touching the water drops fish food that the fish swim over to eat; touching a fish makes it blow a few soft bubbles. |
| Category | Open-ended play, observation, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap (pointer down) on the canvas |
| Status | Implemented. Enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff` flag). |
| Source | [`js/akwarium.js`](../../js/akwarium.js), CSS class `.aquarium` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

The aquarium is a low-pressure "watch and nudge" activity: every touch has a visible, gentle consequence (food appears and is eaten, bubbles rise) and nothing can go wrong. It complements the more task-like activities (matching, counting, puzzles) by offering a purely exploratory scene, and it is one of the few activities whose characters move on their own and react to the child's touch.

Since issue #108 the scene differs on every launch (2-8 fish with unique shape and colour combinations), so repeated visits do not look identical.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile from the menu (hash `#akwarium`); `mount` creates one full-screen `<canvas>`.
2. The scene shows a pale blue water gradient, a sand strip, five seaweed plants and 2-8 fish already swimming.
3. The child can tap anywhere on the canvas.
4. Tapping empty water drops a food pellet at that point; it sinks slowly and the nearest fish swim towards it. Tapping a fish releases 3-5 bubbles and gives that fish a small random sideways bias for 3 seconds.
5. There is no completion state; the scene runs until the child leaves.
6. Nothing resets on its own; food and bubbles expire by themselves.
7. A new fish selection is made only on the next launch (leaving and reopening the activity).
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Input handled | `pointerdown` on the canvas (every pointer, so several fingers each add food or bubbles); default is prevented |
| Fish hit test | Nearest fish whose centre is within `size * 1.8` of the touch (about 47-61 px for sizes 26/30/34) |
| Food | Max 10 pellets (`MAX_FOOD`); an 11th touch removes the oldest. Pellet radius 5 px |
| Food sinking | `FOOD_FALL` = 28 px/s down to `H - 36` (above the sand) |
| Food expiry | Removed after resting on the bottom for `FOOD_REST_MS` = 6000 ms, or after `FOOD_MAX_MS` = 25000 ms of age, whichever comes first |
| Eating | A fish eats a pellet when the pellet is within `0.9 * size` of a point one body length ahead of the fish. Several fish may chase the same pellet; the first to arrive eats it |
| Target choice | Every frame each fish heads for the nearest uneaten pellet |
| Bubbles | 3-5 per fish touch; radius 3-7 px; rise 18-32 px/s with a gentle sideways wobble; max 30 on screen (`MAX_BUBBLES`, oldest dropped); removed above the top edge |
| Fish speed | `max(24, W / 14)` px/s, so crossing the full width takes at least about 14 s |
| Turning | Capped at 0.7 rad/s; pitch limited to about 26 deg when idle (`maxPitch` 0.45) and about 57 deg when chasing food (1.0), so direction never flips instantly |
| Wandering | New wander angle (+/-0.35 rad) every 3-7 s; fish start turning away from the side walls one turn radius early (margin `max(70, 1.6 * speed / turn)`) |
| Vertical limits | Fish centre clamped to y from 30 to `H - 50` |
| Fish size | 26, 30 or 34 px (body half-length); tail extends to 1.5x |
| Touch nudge | Touched fish gets a bias of +/-0.8 (half of it applied) for 3 s, still subject to the capped turn rate |
| Failure / scoring | None. Fish are never "full": any number of pellets can be eaten |

Reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion`) is read once on mount: all speeds, the turn rate, food sinking and bubble rise are multiplied by 0.6, and plant sway and tail wag are switched off. Because the motion runs in one `requestAnimationFrame` loop it is not disabled by the global CSS rule (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). The media query is not re-evaluated while the activity is open.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (touch water, food appears, fish react).
- Calm observation of slow, smooth movement.
- Early hand-eye coordination through tapping a chosen spot or a moving fish.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Fish visibly change course towards food and eat it; touching a fish produces bubbles.
- Fish differ in shape (5 outlines) and colour (9 colours) within one launch.
- No text, no reading and no failure state are involved.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on attention, calming or development. The code makes no such measurement and none is claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus through pointer events. **No keyboard support**: the canvas is not focusable and has no key handlers.
- **Screen readers:** the canvas has `role="img"` and `aria-label="Akwarium z rybkami"`; individual fish, food and bubbles are not exposed.
- **Orientation:** the canvas fills the viewport (`position: fixed; inset: 0`) in portrait and landscape; fish and plants are positioned relative to the current width and height.
- **Targets:** there are no fixed buttons. A touch near a fish (47-61 px radius) counts as a fish touch; anything else drops food. A tap on a fish therefore never drops food.
- **Colour:** colour carries no meaning (the shape/colour combination only makes fish distinguishable); no contrast requirement applies to information.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required. A young child can use it independently.
- **Motion intensity:** slow movement, no flashing. Reduced-motion setting slows it further (see section 4).
- **Limitation:** no keyboard alternative and no accessible description of the fish.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Fish are drawn in a fixed order and can overlap each other; there is no collision avoidance.
- Many quick taps create up to 10 pellets and up to 30 bubbles; the oldest are silently dropped, which is not visible to the child.
- The activity has no ending, so it relies on the parent playtime limit (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).
- A tap close to (but not on) a fish within the hit radius produces bubbles rather than food, which may surprise a child aiming at the water.
- Rendering is a 2D canvas redrawn every frame at device pixel ratio (not capped, unlike [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md)); performance on very slow devices is not documented.
- No personal data is involved.

## 8. Configuration

There is no external configuration. All values are constants inside [`js/akwarium.js`](../../js/akwarium.js); changing them requires editing the source.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_FOOD` | Food pellets on screen | number | 10 | top of IIFE |
| `MAX_BUBBLES` | Bubbles on screen | number | 30 | top of IIFE |
| `FOOD_FALL` | Sinking speed (px/s) | number | 28 | top of IIFE |
| `FOOD_REST_MS` | Time a pellet may rest on the bottom | number | 6000 | top of IIFE |
| `FOOD_MAX_MS` | Maximum pellet age | number | 25000 | top of IIFE |
| `COLORS` | Fish body colours | array of hex strings | 9 | top of IIFE |
| `SHAPES` | Fish outlines (`oval`, `round`, `slim`, `diamond`, `flat`) | array | 5 | top of IIFE |
| `MIN_FISH` / `MAX_FISH` | Fish count range | numbers | 2 / 8 | top of IIFE |

There is no fallback handling for invalid values because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything is drawn on the canvas with 2D context calls (gradient background, sand strip, five seaweed strokes, fish bodies and tails, food circles, bubble outlines). The menu icon is inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No fonts, audio or images are loaded.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | When | Pool | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fish count | Each mount (`makeFish`) | 2-8 (7 values, uniform) | Not stored; may repeat between launches |
| Shape + colour per fish | Each mount | 5 shapes x 9 colours = 45 combinations | `Rand.pick(combos, n)` returns `n` unique combinations, so no two fish on screen share both shape and colour (a colour or a shape alone may repeat) |
| Start position | Each mount | x 10-90 % of width, y 15-70 % of height | Uniform |
| Start direction | Each mount | left or right | 50 / 50 |
| Fish size | Each mount | 26, 30, 34 px | Uniform |
| Wander angle and timing, bubble properties, touch nudge sign | Continuously | Ranges in section 4 | `Math.random()` |

The result lasts for the session of that mount. There is no memory across launches, so the same fish set can appear twice in a row. [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) is a hard dependency (`window.Rand.pick`); there is no fallback if it is missing. The pool is always larger than the maximum of 8, so an empty or insufficient pool cannot happen.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression, levels or difficulty. Nothing is persisted between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no formal completion state. Feedback is purely visual: a pellet appears under the finger, nearby fish turn towards it, the pellet disappears when eaten, and bubbles rise from a touched fish. No sound, no celebration, no automatic next round.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/akwarium.js`](../../js/akwarium.js), assigned to the registry entry with id `akwarium`; loaded in `index.html` before `js/app.js`.
- **Rendering:** one `<canvas class="aquarium">`; background, plants, food, fish and bubbles are redrawn each frame in `draw()`. No DOM nodes are created per particle.
- **State:** closure variables `fish`, `food`, `bubbles`, `W`, `H`, `time`; no persistence.
- **Loop:** a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`) with `dt` clamped to 0.05 s; on `visibilitychange` to hidden the loop is cancelled and restarted with `last = 0` on return, so no jump occurs.
- **Events:** `pointerdown` on the canvas, `resize` and `visibilitychange` on window/document.
- **Randomization:** `makeFish` with `Rand.pick`.
- **Resize:** `resize()` sets the canvas to `clientWidth/Height` times `devicePixelRatio` and clamps fish positions.
- **Cleanup:** the returned function cancels the frame and removes the three listeners; the canvas itself is removed when `app.js` empties the stage.
- **Dependencies:** `js/random.js`. No analytics integration.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

The canvas is fixed to the full viewport. Logical drawing units are CSS pixels (`ctx.setTransform(dpr, ...)`), with `W` and `H` read from the canvas client size. Fish, food and bubbles are in the same pixel space as pointer positions (`clientX - rect.left`). Seaweed is placed at fixed fractions of the width (0.10, 0.14, 0.55, 0.88, 0.92) with fixed pixel heights (90-150 px); the sand strip is 22 px tall. Fish speed scales with width (`W / 14`) but fish size does not, so on narrow phones fish are relatively large and on wide screens relatively small. After a resize or orientation change the fish are clamped inside the new bounds; food and bubbles keep their old pixel positions.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable (no assets) |
| Missing `Rand` | `makeFish` throws; the activity would not start (no fallback) |
| Resize / orientation change | Canvas resized, fish clamped; food and bubbles not rescaled |
| Backgrounding | Loop is cancelled and resumed with `dt = 0`; nothing jumps |
| Rapid repeated taps | Limited by `MAX_FOOD` and `MAX_BUBBLES`; oldest items are dropped |
| Multi-touch | Each pointer is handled independently |
| Touch cancellation | Only `pointerdown` is used, so cancellation has no effect |
| Leaving during animation | Cleanup cancels the frame |
| Reduced-motion change at runtime | Not detected until the next mount |
| Fish exactly at a wall | Clamped to the edges; the early-turn margin normally prevents wall pinning (fixed in commit 878598a) |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#134](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/134) reports `node --check` plus a node simulation of `makeFish` over 500 runs (counts 2-8, no duplicate shape+colour) and states that the shapes were not checked visually.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; 2-8 fish are swimming, none stuck at a wall after 60 s.
- [ ] Tap empty water: a pellet appears, sinks and the nearest fish swim to it and eat it.
- [ ] Tap a fish: 3-5 bubbles rise; the fish does not turn abruptly.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap 15 times quickly; no more than 10 pellets and 30 bubbles are visible and nothing freezes.
- [ ] Pellet never eaten (cover a corner far from fish): it disappears after resting about 6 s.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and reopen several times; fish count, shapes and colours vary and no two fish look identical in one launch.
- [ ] Progression: confirm nothing changes with time (none is expected).
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate while fish swim; fish stay on screen and seaweed stays at the bottom.
- [ ] Touch: finger and, on a touch laptop, multi-finger taps work.
- [ ] Mouse: clicks work; no text selection or context menu interferes.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tabs for 30 s and return; no jump or speed burst.
- [ ] Reduced motion: enable the OS setting, reopen; movement is slower, plants and tails do not move, fish still react.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No keyboard operation (canvas is not focusable).
- Fish can overlap one another.
- `window.Rand` is required with no fallback.
- Reduced-motion is only read at mount.
- Relative size of fish depends on screen width (fish size is fixed in pixels).

**Requires verification**

- Frame rate on low-end devices at devicePixelRatio 3.
- Visual quality of the five fish outlines on device (PR #134 notes they were not visually checked).

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar calm, touch-reactive scenes: [Ogród Motyli](ogrod-motyli.md), [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.
- A canvas-and-one-loop reference with the same pattern: [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#3](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/3) / PR [#10](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/10): initial activity (plus a follow-up fix to wall-avoidance margins).
- Issue [#21](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/21): app review polish (UX and behaviour improvements).
- Issue [#108](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/108) / PR [#134](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/134): random fish count, shapes and colours.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/aport.md`

```markdown
# Aport

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Aport |
| Activity ID | `aport` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A park where the child drags and throws a ball and a dog of a random breed fetches it, brings it back, sits and wags. |
| Category | Cause and effect; open-ended play; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag and release (touch, mouse), tap, keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/aport.js`](../../js/aport.js), shared drawings in [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js), styles with prefix `ap-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A dog activity with a play-with-the-dog mechanic (throw and fetch), different from washing ([Myjnia](myjnia.md), [Psia Myjnia](psia-myjnia.md)) and racing ([Wyścig Piesków](wyscig-pieskow.md)); issue [#178](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/178).
- Uses the shared dog drawings of [Rasy Piesków](rasy-pieskow.md) (`window.Dogs`, issue [#175](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/175)).
- Gives a parent the Polish breed name, shown small under the dog.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; a dog of a random breed (not the one of the previous launch) sits at its starting spot with a ball resting next to it on the grass.
2. Initially displayed: a sky strip with a sun, clouds and two trees above a green grass area; the dog briefly wags (calm face).
3. Interactions: drag the ball and release it anywhere on the grass; tap the dog; keyboard alternative in section 6.
4. Response: the ball lands at the release point after a 0.8 s arc; the dog runs to it on a curved path, lowers its head and catches the ball in its mouth (about 0.4 s, or longer after a very short throw), carries it back to its starting spot, drops it beside itself, sits and wags for 2.5 s.
5. A new throw while the dog is running redirects it smoothly; tapping the dog switches to another random breed with a small sparkle.
6. After 3 completed fetches the dog does a happy spin (0.9 s) and a heart rises; nothing counts or shows the number.
7. There is no end and no restart step. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Throw | The ball follows the finger while dragged (lifted 10 px). On release it hops in a 0.8 s arc (height `min(130 px, 30% of the grass height)`) and lies at the release point, clamped to at least 28 px from the grass sides, 46 px from its top and 10 px from its bottom. A tap without dragging throws in place. |
| Dog speed | Planned per throw from the round-trip length `L` (dog to ball to start): total time `T = clamp(1.6 + L / (0.3 W), 3.6, 5.2)` s, speed `1.1 L / (T - 1.4)`, never above 0.6 W per second (`W` = grass width); acceleration is 2.5 times the speed per second, the speed slews towards a new plan at most 0.25 W per second squared. |
| Path | The heading is the direction to the target rotated by up to 0.55 rad (random side, reversed on the way back), fading to zero near the target; the velocity is slew-limited so the path is smooth. |
| Redirect | A throw while the dog is running changes only its target; its velocity is kept. The ball can be picked up again from the grass until the dog has grabbed it. |
| Pick-up and return | The dog stops so that its lowered mouth meets the ball; its head dips 30 degrees and comes up again over 0.4 s (`Dogs.mouthPoint` gives the per-breed mouth spot). The ball moves to the mouth in 0.2 s, shrinks to 60% and is drawn behind the dog, so the muzzle front covers part of it. It follows head, bob and facing at all times while the dog carries it. The hold lasts at least 0.4 s (up to 2.4 s after a very short throw so that a fetch takes about 3.6 s); then the dog returns, drops the ball beside its starting spot (0.3 s) and sits and wags. |
| Throw or tap while carrying | Dragging the ball is ignored while it is held. A keyboard throw (Enter/Space) while the dog holds it lets the ball fly from the mouth to the ring and the dog redirects to it. Tapping the dog switches breed: the ball is released at the starting spot and the new breed sits there. |
| Reduced motion | No head dip; the ball still moves from the grass to the mouth in 0.2 s and the sequence completes. |
| Fetch time | In a Node simulation with a stub DOM, an undisturbed fetch took 3.6-5.4 s at 320 x 440, 544 x 244, 1000 x 600 and 1920 x 1080 grass sizes; the peak speed stayed below 0.6 W per second (0.57 at 320 px wide portrait). |
| Breed switch | Tapping the dog picks another breed from `Dogs.LIST` (never the current one) and shows 8 sparkles for 0.6 s; the breed keeps its position and state. |
| Reward | Every 3rd completed fetch: happy spin, hop and a heart rising for 2.2 s. The count restarts at 0 and is never shown. |
| Faces | Only `dg-calm` and `dg-happy`; no angry or sad face exists. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (a throw sends the dog to the ball) and dragging and releasing with a finger.
- Noticing different dog breeds.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The dog goes where the ball lands and brings it back.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about fine-motor, coordination or social benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus). The ball and the dog are native `<button>` elements.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to the ball (visible 4 px focus ring and a dashed ring on the grass), arrow keys move the ring in steps of 6% of the grass, Enter or Space throws the ball to the ring (it travels there in the same 0.8 s arc); Tab to the dog, Enter or Space changes the breed.
- **Labels (Polish):** the ball ("Piłka. Przeciągnij i puść, aby rzucić. Strzałki przesuwają kółko, Enter lub spacja rzuca.") and the dog ("Piesek: Labrador. Dotknij lub naciśnij Enter, aby zmienić rasę."); the SVG is decorative.
- **Target sizes:** the ball button is 56 x 56 px; the dog button is at least 56 px wide and high (dog width `min(30% of the grass width, 41% of its height, 170 px)`).
- **Layout:** the grass starts below the Back button and fills the rest of the screen, portrait and landscape from 320 x 568 to 1920 x 1080.
- **Reduced motion:** all movement, wagging, sparkles and the heart are driven from JavaScript, so they behave the same; no state exists only in a CSS keyframe.
- **Text:** none except the small parent-facing breed name.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Visual quality (dog size, arc, sparkle, heart) has not been checked on a device (sections 17 and 18).
- On a narrow portrait screen the 0.6 W per second speed cap can make the farthest throws take slightly longer than the planned time.
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/aport.js`](../../js/aport.js): `FLY_S` (0.8), `GRAB_S` (0.4), `CATCH_S` (0.2), `DIP_DEG` (30), `HELD` (0.6), `DROP_S` (0.3), `SPIN_S` (0.9), `HEART_S` (2.2), `WAG_S` (2.5), `SPARK_S` (0.6), `SPARKS` (8), `SPEED_CAP` (0.6), `HOME` (0.25, 0.76), `KEY_STEP` (0.06), `FETCHES_FOR_REWARD` (3). Changing them needs a code edit.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The dog is inline SVG built by `Dogs.draw(id)`; ball, heart, sky and the menu icon are inline SVG.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- Breed: uniformly from the 8 in `Dogs.LIST`; the first breed of a launch differs from the last one shown (module variable `lastBreed`); a tap picks any other breed.
- The side of the curved path is random per leg.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A fetch is complete when the dog is back at its starting spot. Feedback: happy face, tail wag, and every 3rd fetch a spin and a heart. No failure state. The activity is open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/aport.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant: breedId })` on each throw (pointer or keyboard) and on each dog tap, and `Analytics.complete()` when a fetch is completed. All calls are wrapped so that nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. The activity is not in the module's `COMPLETABLE` list (it repeats endlessly), so exit-before-completion is not defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/aport.js`](../../js/aport.js) overrides `mount` of the `aport` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.ap > svg.ap-sky + div.ap-grass > shadow, button.ap-dog (art + name), ring, button.ap-ball, sparkle layer, heart`.
- **State:** dog (fractional position, velocity in px/s, phase `sit`, `run`, `grab`, `back` or `spin`, facing, plan), ball (fractional position, mode `lying`, `drag`, `fly`, `carried` or `drop`), keyboard ring, sparkle and heart timers.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, guarded by `!raf`, cancelled while the tab is hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`; it stops when the dog sits after its wag and nothing else moves, and restarts on the next interaction; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.ap` is fixed full-screen; the grass starts at `max(24%, safe area + 64px)` from the top and fills the rest.
- Dog and ball positions are fractions (0-1) of the grass width and height; pixel positions are recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`, and the ball is clamped again, so rotation never moves the ball outside the grass.
- The resting ball is placed relative to the dog's starting spot and recomputed at every layout.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Release outside the grass | The ball is clamped to the nearest grass point. |
| Drag cancelled by the system | The ball stays where it was lifted. |
| Ball while the dog holds it or spins | Not interactive. |
| Leaving mid-fetch | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. Ten quick open/close cycles leave no loop running. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| Resize / orientation | Positions re-computed from fractions. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |
| `window.Dogs` missing | Not handled. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag the ball, release, the dog fetches it in 3-6 s and sits and wags.
- [ ] Throw again while the dog runs; it turns smoothly without jumping.
- [ ] Release the ball outside the grass (above, at the edges); it lands on the nearest grass point.
- [ ] Tap the dog several times; the breed always changes and a sparkle shows.
- [ ] Three fetches in a row: spin and heart, no counter.
- [ ] Rotate the device with the ball far from the dog; the ball stays on the grass.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab, arrows, Enter/Space for the ball and the dog.
- [ ] Leave and reopen ten times quickly.
- [ ] Small screens (320 x 568) and 1920 x 1080, portrait and landscape.
- [ ] Reduced motion: movement, wagging, sparkles and heart still work.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

The PR for issue [#178](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/178) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM; no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel of the arc, sparkles and heart, and the dog size on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Psia Myjnia](psia-myjnia.md), [Wyścig Piesków](wyscig-pieskow.md), [Myjnia](myjnia.md), [Rasy Piesków](rasy-pieskow.md).
- Shared component: [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js) (`Dogs.LIST`, `Dogs.draw`, `Dogs.mouthPoint`).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#178](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/178): initial activity.
- Issue [#206](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/206): the dog catches the ball in its mouth and carries it back.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/autobusik.md`

```markdown
# Autobusik

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Autobusik |
| Internal ID | `autobusik` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A little bus loops slowly along a village road with three bus stops; each stop has a waiting random animal that hops aboard when the bus stops there. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap / click (also Enter and Space on the bus) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Autobusik is one of the vehicle activities. Compared with [Traktor](traktor.md) it adds a "pick a destination" interaction: the child can ask the bus to stop at a particular stop, and the stop is then served by a gentle sequence (braking, doors opening, animal hopping in). It also lets the child take an animal out again. All reactions are slow and non-failing: the bus never reverses, there is no score and nothing can be done wrongly.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#autobusik`); `mount` builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The scene shows a village (four houses, three trees, sun, clouds), a sidewalk with three bus stop signs at 20 %, 50 % and 80 % of the width, and a road. Three random animals wait, one at each stop. The bus starts **stopped at the first stop** with its doors opening; the first animal is marked "do not board" until the bus has driven off once (or the child touches that stop).
3. The child can touch the bus, a bus stop, a waiting animal or an animal sitting in a window.
4. Touching the bus: when standing at a stop it closes the doors and then drives off; when halted mid-road it starts; when moving it slows to a halt where it is. Touching a stop (or the animal waiting there) makes the bus drive to and brake into that stop (only the last touched stop counts). At a stop the doors open and the waiting animal hops into a window. Touching an animal in a window makes it step out at the stop (bus standing there with open doors) or wave (otherwise).
5. There is no formal completion state.
6. Nothing ends or resets; the bus keeps looping while the child plays.
7. A new random set of animals is drawn on every launch of the activity.
8. The child leaves with Back (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Loop time at cruise speed | `CROSS_S = 24` s (`V = 1/24` loop fractions per second); the front of the bus crosses the visible width in about 14 s or more |
| Start / slow-down ramp | `RAMP_S = 2.2` s (smoothstep) |
| Braking into a stop | `BRAKE_S = 3` (declared); the actual braking duration is `T = 2·D/v`, started when the remaining distance `D <= 1.5·v`, so it lasts about 3 s at cruise speed |
| Doors open/close | `DOOR_S = 1.8` s |
| Animal hop | `HOP_S = 1.8` s (arc height `0.7·AS`) |
| Animal wave | `WAVE_S = 2.2` s |
| Frame step cap | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |
| Stops | `STOP_X = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8]` of the width |
| Windows | 3, centres at x = 58, 140, 222 in a 340 x 110 bus viewBox |
| Animals | exactly 3 (one per stop); animal `i` always rides in window `i` |

Details:

- **Position model.** The bus position is a loop fraction `f` in [0, 1) over a path of length `L = W + bus width`; it enters from beyond the left edge and leaves beyond the right edge, then wraps.
- **Never backwards.** Speed is clamped at 0 or above; braking and ramps only decelerate.
- **Stop request** (`onStop`): the target is set and the bus accelerates to cruise speed if it was slowing. If the stop is too close to brake gently (`D < 1.25·v`) the `skip` flag makes it wait until the bus has gone round (`D > 0.9`). Touching the stop where the bus already stands cancels a pending departure and allows the animals there to board.
- **Boarding:** only one animal at a time, only when the bus stands at the stop, doors are at least 95 % open, no animal is hopping and `go` is not set. Animals that stepped out are marked `noBoard` and do not re-board until the bus drives off.
- **Doors** open only while the bus stands at a stop (`parkedNow`); the door panel width shrinks by up to 92 %.
- **Departure** (`go`): the bus waits for the doors to close (`door1 <= 0.02`) and for hopping animals to finish.
- **Animal in a window, touched:** if the bus stands at a stop with the door more than half open the animal hops out to the waiting position of that stop; otherwise it waves.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is driven by the rAF loop; see section 6.
- **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touching a stop leads the bus there and the animal boards.
- Calm observation of slow vehicle motion.
- Choosing between three targets.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- Ramps and braking are slow (2.2 s and about 3 s); doors take 1.8 s.
- A child can place an animal in the bus and take it out again by touch.
- The three animals differ on every launch.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on attention, planning or language development. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) plus `click` with `event.detail === 0` for keyboard activation. The bus has `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"` and handles Enter/Space; stops and animals are real `<button>` elements with Polish `aria-label`s (animal buttons carry the animal's Polish name from `js/animals.js`).
- **Touch handling.** `.ab` uses `touch-action: none` and disables text selection; no drag gesture.
- **Target sizes.** Animal buttons `AS = max(56, min(76, 0.24·bus width))` px with a 56 px minimum; stop buttons at least 56 px wide and about `max(0.45·sy, 96)` px tall; the bus is `min(max(0.64·W, 240), 0.8·W, 460, ...)` px wide.
- **Orientation.** Layout recomputed on `resize`/`orientationchange`; the stopped bus is always fully on screen (the bus centre is clamped to `[bw/2, W - bw/2]`).
- **Colour.** Animals are distinguished by shape and colour; nothing depends on colour alone.
- **Reduced motion.** Bus, doors, wheels and animals are moved by the rAF loop and JS-set attributes; the global reduced-motion rule does not stop them. The motion is slow. Decorations (sun, clouds, houses) are static.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Limitations:** the three stop signs are quiet, small illustrations; touching the bus while doors are opening is accepted (it only closes them after boarding/hopping has finished). Stop and animal buttons overlap near each other on small screens (animals stand 0.9 to 1.8 `AS` from the stop centre).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Accidental interactions:** the stop sign, the waiting animal and the bus are close together at a stop; a stop touch while the bus is already there with a door closing re-allows boarding rather than doing nothing.
- **Hidden state:** a request for a stop that was just passed makes the bus drive a whole loop (up to about 24 s) before stopping, which a young child may read as "not working".
- **Unclear ending:** the activity never ends.
- **Performance:** one rAF loop is always running; per frame it updates the bus, door, wheels and three animals.
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored; animals are random but carry no personal data.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants at the top of [`js/autobusik.js`](../../js/autobusik.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S` | Seconds per full loop at cruise speed | number | 24 |
| `V` | Cruise speed (loop fractions/s) | number | `1 / CROSS_S` |
| `RAMP_S` | Start / slow-down ramp (s) | number | 2.2 |
| `BRAKE_S` | Braking time (declared; not read by the brake calculation, which derives `T = 2·D/v`) | number | 3 |
| `DOOR_S` | Door open/close time (s) | number | 1.8 |
| `HOP_S`, `WAVE_S` | Animal hop and wave durations (s) | number | 1.8, 2.2 |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 |
| `VB_W`, `VB_H` | Bus viewBox size | number | 340, 110 |
| `WIN_X` | Window centres | array | `[58, 140, 222]` |
| `STOP_X` | Stop positions as fractions of the width | array | `[0.2, 0.5, 0.8]` |

There is no fallback because there is no external input. The number of animals (3) is also fixed in the code (`Animals.pick(3)`, three buttons, three stops).

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The bus, stops, houses and trees are inline SVG strings in the JS file; the animals are SVG from [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.head`); the sky, sun, clouds, sidewalk and road are CSS (`.ab-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css)). No audio, fonts or data files. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **What:** which 3 animals wait at the stops, chosen on every `mount` with `Animals.pick(3)`.
- **Pool:** the 13 animals of `js/animals.js` (Miś, Króliczek, Kotek, Piesek, Myszka, Świnka, Lisek, Lew, Słoń, Panda, Żabka, Sowa, Koala).
- **Uniqueness:** the three picks are unique within a launch (shuffle and slice). `opts.distinct` is not used, so similar silhouettes may appear together.
- **No cross-launch memory:** unlike `Rand.pickOne`, `Animals.pick` does not remember earlier launches, so the same animals can appear again on the next visit.
- Nothing is stored; the bus route and stop positions are fixed.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression or difficulty. The state (which animals are aboard) is not persisted and is reset when the activity is re-entered.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is purely visual: braking and ramps, door panel opening/closing, animals hopping in/out, waving animals and wheels turning with distance. No sound, no celebration, nothing automatically restarts because nothing ends.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/autobusik.js`](../../js/autobusik.js), assigned to the `autobusik` registry entry; loaded from `index.html` before `js/app.js`. Other sources: `js/animals.js` (`Animals.head`, `Animals.pick`), `.ab-*` in `css/style.css`.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG; bus and animals are moved with inline `transform` per frame; the door panel width is an SVG attribute.
- **State:** closures. Bus: `f`, `v`, `ramp`, `brake`, `target`, `skip`, `go`, `parkedAt`, `door1`. Per animal: `st` (`wait`, `hopin`, `in`, `hopout`), `t`, `p0`, `stop`, `noBoard`, `wave`.
- **Animation:** a single rAF loop `frame` with dt capped at 0.05 s, stopped when `document.hidden` and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `bind()` registers `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()`, which re-plans an in-progress brake from the current speed (no snap).
- **Cleanup:** the returned function cancels the rAF, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Persistence/config/analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; `W`/`H` come from `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`.
- **Units:** CSS pixels for placement; the bus position is the loop fraction `f` (0 = just off the left edge, 1 = just off the right edge), so speed and stop positions stay valid after a resize. Bus left = `f·L - bw` with `L = W + bw`; road base at `0.88·H`, sidewalk/stops at `0.6·H`, road top at `0.62·H`, road height `0.3·H`.
- **Stops:** the target `f` of a stop is `(clamp(stopX, bw/2, W - bw/2) + bw/2) / L`, so the bus centre stays on screen even for stops near an edge.
- **Windows:** window positions are computed from the bus viewBox (`WIN_X / 340`) so animals in windows follow the bus.
- Tested sizes: Not currently documented (PR [#104](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/104) reports a stub simulation at 800x500 and 360x700).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Resize during braking:** the brake plan is dropped and the bus re-accelerates toward cruise speed; if it stood at a stop it is re-placed at that stop.
- **Backgrounding:** the loop pauses while hidden and resumes without a time jump.
- **Rapid input:** repeated touches change `target`/`go` state; only the last touched stop counts; wave and hop ignore touches while running (`a.st !== 'in'`; wave only starts when `wave < 0`).
- **Stop too close:** handled by `skip` (it stops on the next loop).
- **Touch cancel / missing assets / invalid config:** not applicable.
- **Unhandled:** no fallback without `requestAnimationFrame` or `window.Animals`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#104](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/104) reports `node --check` and a hand-made DOM stub simulation (800x500 landscape and 360x700 portrait) confirming start position, braking into stops, door open/close, boarding, no backwards motion and no NaN; it says visuals and touch targets still needed a device check.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Autobusik; the bus stands at the first stop with doors open; touch it and it closes the doors, then drives off smoothly.
- [ ] Touch the moving bus; it slows to a halt where it is; touch again to restart.
- [ ] Touch each of the three stops and each waiting animal; the bus brakes into that stop in about 3 s, the doors open and the animal hops aboard.
- [ ] Touch two different stops quickly; only the last one is served.
- [ ] Touch a stop that was just passed; the bus continues round the loop and stops on the next pass.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch the road, sky and houses; nothing happens.
- [ ] Touch an animal in a window at a stop (steps out) and while moving (waves).
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no completion state and nothing resets after all three animals are aboard.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: leave and re-enter several times; the animals vary; observe whether animals repeat between visits.
- [ ] Progression: confirm nothing persists after a reload.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate while braking and while stopped; the bus stays fully visible at every stop and no animal is displaced.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab to the bus, stops and animals; Enter/Space on the bus).
- [ ] Background the tab while the bus moves; return without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled: bus, doors and animals still move.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- `BRAKE_S` is declared but not used in the brake calculation (the duration is derived from the remaining distance).
- `Animals.pick` does not prevent the same animals from appearing on consecutive launches, and `distinct` is not used.
- The motion ignores the reduced-motion preference by design.

**Requires verification**

- Overlap of waiting-animal and stop buttons on very narrow screens.
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Autobusik; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Traktor](traktor.md), [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Mała Łódka](mala-lodka.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md), [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md), [Balon](balon.md).
- Shared: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.head`, `Animals.pick`); `js/random.js` is used indirectly (`Animals.pick` shuffles with `Rand.shuffle` when available).
- Shared pattern: rAF loop with capped dt; position as a loop fraction.

## 21. Change history

- [#92](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/92) / PR [#104](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/104): Autobusik activity added.
- [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): random animals per stop from the shared pool.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/balon.md`

```markdown
# Balon

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Balon |
| Internal ID | `balon` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)); source file `js/balon.js`, CSS prefix `bn-` |
| Description | A hot-air balloon with a bear and a rabbit in the basket rests on a meadow under a pastel sky with four drifting clouds; touching it makes it rise slowly or float back down. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, observation |
| Interaction type | Tap / click (real buttons, so Enter and Space also work) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Balon is the vertical, "up and down" member of the vehicle group and the calmest of them: a single large object with a single main action (rise or descend) plus small side reactions (clouds that make way, animals that wave). It has no stations, loops or targets to reach. Its speed changes are limited by a maximum acceleration, so the balloon never jerks, which suits a very slow, gentle moment of play. Nothing can go wrong and nothing is scored.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#balon`); `mount` builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The scene shows a pastel sky with four clouds drifting slowly, a meadow at the bottom and the balloon resting on the meadow in the middle of the screen.
3. The child can touch the balloon, a cloud, or the bear or the rabbit in the basket.
4. Touching the balloon on the ground makes it rise slowly while drifting gently sideways; a soft glow pulses under it while it climbs. Touching it in the air makes it float back down; touching it again reverses it smoothly. Touching a cloud makes it drift aside by about one cloud width and return over 8 s. Touching an animal makes it wave (2.8 s).
5. There is no formal completion state. At the top the balloon stays in the air (still swaying) until it is touched; on the meadow it stays put.
6. The child can repeat any of this as often as they like.
7. Nothing is randomised and the scene does not restart by itself.
8. The child leaves with Back (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Cruise climb / descent speed | `VA = 1/15` altitude fractions per second (the top third takes at least about 12 s; a full climb about 15 s plus the eased ends) |
| Maximum change of speed | `ACC = 0.04` per second (full speed in about 1.7 s) |
| Slow-down zone | the last `EASE = 12 %` of the way up or down |
| Creep speed | `VMIN = 0.006` so that the end of the way is actually reached |
| Sideways drift cycle | `DRIFT_T = 40` s; amplitude `ampX = min(0.28·W, W/2 - bw/2 - 12)` px; fades in over the first 30 % of altitude |
| Tilt | up to 3 deg with the drift |
| Glow | pulses at `GLOW_HZ = 0.7` per second while rising; fades in or out over 1.2 s |
| Cloud drift | `CLOUD_T = 8` s, displacement `cloudW·sin²(π t / 8)` (about one cloud width and back) towards the middle of the screen |
| Animal wave | `WAVE_S = 2.8` s |
| Clouds | 4, crossing the scene in 170, 130, 200 and 150 s |
| Frame step cap | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |

Details:

- **Altitude model.** Altitude is a fraction `a` (0 = on the meadow, 1 = top; top position `yTop = max(24, 0.05·H)`), and the speed `v` moves toward a target speed only by `ACC` per second. Modes: `ground`, `up`, `down`.
- **Balloon touch** (`onBalloon`): on the meadow it starts rising; otherwise it toggles between `up` and `down`. A rapid sequence of touches only reverses the speed smoothly. At the top the balloon stays in mode `up` with zero speed; the next touch makes it descend. When it reaches the ground in mode `down` it switches to `ground`.
- **Cloud touch** (`onCloud`): ignored while that cloud is already moving; it drifts towards the middle of the screen (where there is room).
- **Animals:** a touch is ignored while that animal is already waving.
- **Drift phase** `ph` advances whenever the balloon is above the ground and is not reset between lifts, so the sideways position at lift-off depends on earlier flights (noted in PR [#158](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/158)).
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is JS-driven; see section 6. **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touching the balloon makes it rise or descend.
- Calm observation of very slow, smooth movement.
- Gentle interaction with several parts of one scene.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- The balloon reaches the upper third in about 12 s or more and takes about 15 s or more to come down.
- Acceleration is limited, so a rapid series of touches never produces jerks.
- Clouds move away from the touch and come back; animals wave; a glow shows that the balloon is rising.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about relaxation, attention or other developmental effects. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) and `click` with `event.detail === 0` for keyboard activation. The hull, the two animals and the four clouds are real `<button>` elements with Polish `aria-label`s (`Balon – wznieś się lub opuść`, `Miś w koszu`, `Króliczek w koszu`, `Chmurka`) and can be reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space.
- **Touch handling.** `.bn` uses `touch-action: none`; no drag gesture. The balloon container has `pointer-events: none`; only the hull (180/200 x 268/280 of the balloon) and the animal buttons capture touches.
- **Target sizes.** The balloon is `bh = max(216, min(380, 0.52·H, 1.1·W))` px tall (about 154 to 271 px wide); animal buttons are 56 x 56 px; clouds are `cloudW = clamp(0.22·W, 120, 220)` px wide and half as tall.
- **Orientation.** Layout recomputed on `resize`/`orientationchange`; the balloon is clamped inside the screen horizontally.
- **Colour.** Nothing depends on colour alone.
- **Reduced motion.** The balloon, clouds, glow and waves are driven by the rAF loop and keep running under the global reduced-motion rule. No CSS animations are used by this activity. The motion is very slow, but it is not reduced for users who asked for reduced motion.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Limitations:** a cloud behind the balloon is covered by the hull button and cannot be touched there; animals sit on top of the hull button.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Accidental interactions:** the hull covers nearly the whole balloon, so a touch anywhere on it toggles rise and descent (harmless).
- **Slow response:** because speed changes by at most 0.04 per second, a child may think a touch near the top or bottom has no effect for the first second.
- **Unclear ending:** the activity never ends; at the top the balloon stays up.
- **Visual stimulation:** low; the glow pulses at 0.7 Hz (below 1 Hz) at no more than about 0.85 opacity.
- **Performance:** one always-running rAF loop; scene updates are small.
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/balon.js`](../../js/balon.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VA` | Cruise climb/descent speed (altitude fractions/s) | number | `1/15` |
| `ACC` | Maximum speed change per second | number | 0.04 |
| `EASE` | Slow-down zone at each end | number | 0.12 |
| `VMIN` | Creep speed | number | 0.006 |
| `DRIFT_T` | Sideways drift cycle (s) | number | 40 |
| `GLOW_HZ` | Glow pulses per second | number | 0.7 |
| `CLOUD_T` | Cloud drift-and-return time (s) | number | 8 |
| `WAVE_S` | Animal wave duration (s) | number | 2.8 |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 |
| `cloudU`, `cloudSpd`, `cloudY` | Cloud start positions, speeds (per s), heights | arrays | 4 entries each |

There is no fallback because there is no external input.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The balloon with its basket and the bear and rabbit, and the clouds are inline SVG strings in the JS file; the meadow (hill and grass rectangles) is an SVG overlay sized in `layout()`; the sky gradient is CSS (`.bn-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css)). The animals are drawn locally by `animalSvg`, not from `js/animals.js` (the PR notes that the shared module was not on `main` at the time). No audio, fonts or data files. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

None. The scene, the two animals and the cloud positions and speeds are the same on every launch.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. No levels or difficulty, and nothing persists between sessions. The balloon starts on the meadow on every launch.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is visual only: the rise and descent, the sideways drift and slight tilt, the pulsing glow while rising, clouds making way and waving animals. No sound, no celebration, no automatic restart.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/balon.js`](../../js/balon.js), assigned to the `balon` registry entry; loaded before `js/app.js`. No shared helper is used.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG. The meadow is an SVG overlay with a `viewBox` of `0 0 W H`; the balloon and clouds are positioned with inline `transform`; the glow is an SVG group whose opacity is set per frame.
- **State:** closures: `a` (altitude), `v`, `mode` (`ground`/`up`/`down`), `ph` (drift phase), `glowAmt`/`gp`, `waves[]`, `cloudU[]`, `cloudT[]`, `cloudDir[]`.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop `frame` with a capped dt; paused while hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `bind()` registers `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the rAF, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Persistence/config/analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; `W`/`H` come from `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`.
- **Units:** CSS pixels. The balloon's top is `y = yGround + (yTop - yGround)·a`, where `yGround = gy + 0.55·gh - bh` seats the basket on the meadow (`gh = 0.13·H`, `gy = H - gh`). Horizontal centre `x0 = W/2` plus the drift, clamped to `[bw/2 + 4, W - bw/2 - 4]`. Clouds move as a fraction `cloudU` of `W + cloudW`.
- **Balloon geometry:** the balloon SVG has a 200 x 280 viewBox; the hull and animal buttons are positioned with the factor `s = bh / 280`.
- Tested sizes: Not currently documented (PR [#158](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/158) reports a stub simulation at five viewports from 640x360 to 1920x1080).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Backgrounding:** the loop pauses while hidden and resumes without a jump.
- **Resize:** altitude is a fraction, so the balloon keeps its relative height; horizontal position is clamped.
- **Rapid input:** repeated balloon touches only reverse the speed within the acceleration limit (PR #158 reports 20 rapid taps staying smooth); cloud and animal reactions ignore touches while running.
- **Short screens:** `yTop` is limited so it never lies below the ground position.
- **Touch cancel / missing assets / invalid config:** not applicable.
- **Unhandled:** no fallback without `requestAnimationFrame`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#158](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/158) reports `node --check`, SVG strings parsed as XML, and a stub-DOM simulation at five viewports (640x360 to 1920x1080, portrait and landscape): the top third reached in 12 to 15 s, descent at least 15 s, balloon always inside the screen, glow at most 0.85 opacity at 0.7 Hz, 20 rapid taps staying smooth, cloud shift about one cloud width; it asks for a visual check on a device.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Balon; the balloon rests on the meadow; touch it; it rises very slowly, drifts sideways and a soft glow pulses beneath it.
- [ ] Wait until it reaches the top; it stays in the air and sways; touch it; it floats back down and settles on the meadow; touch again; it lifts.
- [ ] Touch the balloon several times quickly while rising and while descending; the movement reverses smoothly without jerks.
- [ ] Touch each of the four clouds; it moves aside by about its width and returns after about 8 s; touching it while moving does nothing.
- [ ] Touch the bear and the rabbit (a wave of about 2.8 s) on the ground and in the air.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch the sky and the meadow; nothing happens.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no completion state.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-enter; the balloon is on the meadow again.
- [ ] Randomization and progression: confirm that nothing varies and nothing persists.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate while on the ground, rising and at the top; the balloon stays fully on screen and the basket rests on the meadow.
- [ ] Short landscape screen (about 640x360): the balloon can still be touched and clouds are reachable.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab through the balloon, animals and clouds; Enter/Space).
- [ ] Background the tab during a climb; return without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled: the balloon, clouds and glow still move.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The motion ignores the reduced-motion preference by design.
- The drift phase is not reset between flights (the lift-off position varies).
- A cloud that is behind the balloon cannot be touched there (the hull button is above it).
- The animals are drawn locally rather than from `js/animals.js`.

**Requires verification**

- Whether the very slow start (acceleration limited to 0.04 per second) is clear enough for a child that the touch worked.
- Layout on very short or very wide viewports.
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Balon; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md) (same cloud, animal-wave and meadow drawing), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md) (vertical movement), [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Traktor](traktor.md), [Autobusik](autobusik.md), [Mała Łódka](mala-lodka.md).
- Shared helpers: none used (`js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not referenced).
- Shared pattern: rAF loop with a capped dt.

## 21. Change history

- [#89](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/89) / PR [#158](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/158): Balon activity added (single commit `991e7a7`, no later changes to `js/balon.js`).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/banki-mydlane.md`

```markdown
# Bańki Mydlane

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Bańki Mydlane |
| Activity ID | `banki` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Touching the screen blows a big soft bubble that floats up; touching a bubble splits it into smaller ones; dragging leaves a trail of small bubbles. |
| Category | Cause and effect; open-ended play |
| Interaction type | Tap and drag (touch, mouse, stylus) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default |
| Source | [`js/banki.js`](../../js/banki.js), styles with prefix `bm-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

## 2. Business purpose

- Gives the child an immediate, forgiving reaction to any touch anywhere on the screen: there are no targets to miss.
- Provides a calm "pop-free" bubble toy: bubbles never burst loudly or disappear abruptly; they split or fade.
- Complements [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md) and [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md) as free, open-ended touch play.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 8.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the scene is built and the animation loop starts.
2. Initially displayed: one of six painted gradient backgrounds and **5 small bubbles** already floating at random positions.
3. Interactions: tap empty space (blow a big bubble), tap a bubble (split it), press and drag (small bubbles along the path).
4. The bubble fades in over 0.8 s and drifts upwards with a gentle sideways sway.
5. There is no completion state.
6. Bubbles keep fading out at the top; the child can blow more at any time.
7. Restart: leave and re-open the activity (a new background is chosen).
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back; the cleanup function stops the loop and removes the scene.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Blow | `pointerdown` on empty space creates a bubble with radius 46 to 62 (diameter 92 to 124 px) at the touch point, rising at 14 to 24 px/s. |
| Hit test | A bubble counts as touched when the distance to its centre is under `r + 8`; the nearest non-fading bubble wins. Bubbles themselves have `pointer-events: none`; all input goes to the scene. |
| Split | A touched bubble with `r > MIN_R * 1.2` (16.8) splits into 2 or 3 (50 % each); child radius is `0.66 * r` for 2 and `0.58 * r` for 3. Children get a small push (14 px/s) in different directions. The parent fades out over 1.6 s with a short 8 % scale pulse (`SPLIT_MS = 700`). |
| Small bubbles | Children with radius under 16.8 live 4 to 7 s and then fade. Touching a bubble that is already that small makes it fade away gently instead of splitting. |
| Drag trail | While the pointer is down, at most one small bubble (radius 14 to 22, rising 15.4 to 26.4 px/s) per 260 ms, only if the pointer is not on an existing bubble. |
| Motion | Each bubble: sideways sway amplitude 6 to 16 and sway speed 0.25 to 0.5 rad/s; rise speed capped at 26 px/s; a soft push back from the left/right edges. |
| Population limit | `MAX = 25` visible (non-fading) bubbles: when exceeded, the oldest fades out. A hard DOM bound of `MAX + 8` accelerates bubbles that are already fading. |
| Keep-out zones | A bubble that reaches the top (`y < r + 4`) or enters the area around the Back button or the playtime hourglass (measured from the DOM, plus 12 px padding) starts fading out. |
| Tint | Each bubble gets one of 5 RGB tints at random. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect between touch and visible result.
- Calm visual tracking of slowly moving objects.
- Fine-motor practice of tapping and dragging.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Any touch gives a reaction; nothing can fail.
- Bubbles split or fade; they never burst abruptly.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any developmental or calming effect. Nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events with pointer capture on the scene (touch, mouse, stylus). **There is no keyboard alternative**; the scene is a single `role="img"` element labelled "Bańki mydlane unoszące się w powietrzu".
- **Targets:** the whole screen is the target; split bubbles can be small (down to about 19 px diameter), but a miss simply blows a new big bubble.
- **Orientation:** the scene fills the viewport; background gradients are pure CSS and fill any portrait or landscape size without stretching.
- **Colour/contrast:** all six backgrounds use mid/deep tones so the pale bubbles with a white highlight stay visible.
- **Reduced motion:** the movement is driven by the `requestAnimationFrame` loop, not CSS animations, so it is still present under the global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule. (There is no reduced-intensity variant.)
- **Touch:** `touch-action: none`, `user-select: none`; `pointerdown` calls `preventDefault`.
- **Reading:** not required; a young child can use it independently.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Continuous slow motion of many bubbles; bubbles blown by rapid tapping can number up to 25 visible at a time.
- Rapid drag can create many small bubbles (limited to one per 260 ms).
- No end state; relies on the global playtime limit.
- No keyboard access (see section 6).
- No personal data is stored or sent.

## 8. Configuration

There is no external configuration; the constants at the top of [`js/banki.js`](../../js/banki.js) can only be changed in code.

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX` | Maximum visible bubbles and pool size | 25 |
| `MIN_R` | Smallest trail bubble radius; threshold for "small" is `MIN_R * 1.2` | 14 |
| `BIG_R` | Radius range of a tapped bubble | 46 to 62 |
| `FADE_IN`, `FADE_OUT` | Fade durations | 0.8 s, 1.6 s |
| `SPLIT_MS` | Parent split pulse | 700 ms |
| `GUARD_PAD` | Padding around keep-out zones | 12 px |
| `BACKS` | Six background CSS gradients (sunny hills, dusk, beach sea, starry night, sunrise meadow, underwater) | array |
| `TINTS` | Five bubble RGB tints | array |

Fallbacks: if the Back button or hourglass element is missing, that keep-out zone is skipped.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Backgrounds are CSS gradients set inline; bubbles are CSS-styled `div`s (radial gradients, inset shadows) defined by `.bm-b` in `css/style.css`. No images, fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Background:** one of 6 chosen with `Rand.pickOne(BACKS, 'banki-bg')` ([`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)), which never returns the same background as the previous launch within the same page session; not stored across reloads.
- **Bubbles:** radius, rise speed, sway phase/amplitude/speed, tint, and the number of children (2 or 3, 50 % each) are random per bubble (`Math.random`).
- **Initial bubbles:** 5, with random position (x 10 to 90 %, y 25 to 90 %), radius 16 to 30, rise 10 to 18 px/s.
- No weighted selection; no handling of an empty pool is needed (fixed arrays).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels or persistence.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No completion state, no failure. Feedback is the bubble motion itself: fade-in, a small scale pulse when splitting, fade-out when small, at the top or in a keep-out zone. No sound; no automatic next round.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/banki.js`](../../js/banki.js); returns `cleanup`, which sets a `dead` flag, cancels the frame, removes listeners and removes the scene.
- **Rendering:** DOM. Each bubble is a pooled `div.bm-b` positioned with `transform: translate(...) scale(...)` and `opacity`; `pool` recycles up to `MAX` removed elements.
- **State:** `bubbles[]` objects (`x`, `y`, `r`, `vy`, `vx`, phase, age, `fading`, `fade`, `split`, optional `life`).
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop `tick()` with `dt` capped at 0.1 s; stopped on `visibilitychange` when hidden and restarted when visible.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel` on the scene; `resize`, `orientationchange` (only re-measure the scene size); `visibilitychange`.
- **Keep-out zones:** `guards()` measures `.back` and `.hourglass` each frame with `getBoundingClientRect`.
- **Shared code:** `window.Rand.pickOne` for the background. No persistence, no analytics.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0` and uses CSS pixels relative to the scene; the origin is the top-left corner.
- `W` and `H` are the scene's client size and are re-read on resize and orientation change. Bubbles are not repositioned on resize; the soft push back from the edges (`W - r`) brings them back inside the new width.
- Backgrounds are gradients (no aspect-ratio dependency).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Rapid tapping | Population bounded (25 visible, hard DOM bound 33); oldest bubbles fade first. |
| Tab hidden | Loop stopped; resumes on return (`dt` is capped at 0.1 s so there is no catch-up). |
| Touch cancel | `pointercancel` clears the `down` flag. |
| Pointer capture unsupported | The `setPointerCapture` call is wrapped in `try/catch`. |
| Resize / orientation | Only `W` and `H` are updated (see section 15). |
| Back button / hourglass missing | Zone skipped. |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` stops everything. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; the 5 small bubbles are visible and float up; tap empty space; a big bubble appears and floats up.
- [ ] Split: tap a big bubble; it splits into 2 or 3 smaller ones; tap a medium child to split again; tap a very small bubble; it fades.
- [ ] Drag: press and drag slowly and quickly; small bubbles appear at a gentle rate and not over existing bubbles.
- [ ] Bubbles reaching the top fade out instead of disappearing abruptly; bubbles near the Back button or hourglass fade out.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: not applicable (every touch is valid); check taps near screen edges.
- [ ] Rapid tapping for 30 s: the number of bubbles stays bounded and the frame rate remains smooth.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: re-open the activity 10 times; the background changes each time and never repeats twice in a row.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate while bubbles are on screen; bubbles are not stuck outside the screen.
- [ ] Touch (Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad) and mouse (desktop): both work; no scrolling or zoom gestures interfere.
- [ ] Keyboard: confirm that there is no keyboard interaction (known limitation).
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tab and return; bubbles continue without jumping.
- [ ] Reduced motion: bubbles still move.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#40](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/40) reports a Node run against a DOM stub (400 rapid taps keep the DOM bounded, all bubbles are removed after fading, cleanup empties the scene) and lists manual device tests as pending. PR [#139](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/139) reports that 200 picks in Node reached all 6 backgrounds.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No keyboard or assistive-technology interaction; the scene is a single image role.
- Bubbles are not repositioned on resize or orientation change.
- `dragged` is assigned but never read (dead variable).
- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Overlap of the bubbles with the Back button and hourglass on devices with unusual safe areas (zones are measured at runtime, but device checks were pending in PR #40).
- Performance on slow devices with 25 bubbles (each has a box shadow and radial gradients).

## 19. Planned improvements

`None currently planned`.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Open-ended touch play: [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md), [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md), [Ogród Motyli](ogrod-motyli.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). The activity does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#31](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/31) / PR [#40](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/40): initial activity, including tiny bubbles fading on touch and keep-out zones measured from the Back button and hourglass.
- Issue [#114](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/114) / PR [#139](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/139): random background per launch (six scenes).

```
