## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/buzki.md`

```markdown
# Buźki

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Buźki |
| Internal ID | `buzki` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A big friendly face and a small random animal copy the same calm expression; touching the face, eyes, cheeks or mouth changes or animates it. |
| Category | Cause and effect, open-ended play (calm observation) |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse, keyboard activation of buttons) |
| CSS prefix | `bz-` |
| Source | [`js/buzki.js`](../../js/buzki.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section `/* Buźki */`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default (no `defaultOff`). Listed 28th in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

Buźki lets a young child explore facial expressions in a safe, slow and wordless way: one touch changes the whole face, small touch zones trigger a single gentle reaction. It supports the application's aim of calm, failure-free cause-and-effect play. It deliberately has no angry, sad or crying faces and no red, so every state is pleasant. It differs from the drag-based activities by being purely tap-driven, and the animal companion changes on every launch.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity from the menu (`#buzki`).
2. A large round yellow face shows the first expression (happy: open eyes, wide smile). A small animal head (random, see section 10) sits in a corner and shows the same expression.
3. The child can tap: the face or the animal (cycle the expression), the eyes (slow blink), either cheek (pink glow) or the mouth (smile or yawn).
4. The face and the animal respond together over about 1 s (expression change) or 1.5 s (eyes, cheeks, mouth effects).
5. There is no completion state and no goal. Every response returns to the current expression.
6. Nothing is restarted explicitly; re-opening the activity resets the face to the happy expression and picks a new animal.
7. About every 5 s, when nothing else is happening, the face blinks once by itself (0.8 s).
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

Expressions (parameters in `EXPR`; eye radii `ex`/`ey`, mouth half-width `mw`, smile depth `ms`, mouth opening `mo`):

| Order | Expression | Eyes (`ex` x `ey`) | Mouth (`mw`, `ms`, `mo`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | happy | 6.5 x 8 | 22, 8, 3 |
| 2 | sleepy | 7 x 3.2 | 8, -1, 3 |
| 3 | surprised | 9 x 12 | 9, -8, 16 |
| 4 | calm | 7 x 1.3 (closed) | 14, 5, 0.6 |

The cycle is happy -> sleepy -> surprised -> calm -> happy, started from happy.

| Touch zone | Action | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Whole face or whole animal (`bz-all`) | next expression | `CHANGE_S = 1` s ease (0.4 s under reduced motion) |
| Eyes (`bz-eyes`) | slow blink, eyes close to 8% of the height | `EFFECT_S = 1.5` s |
| Left or right cheek | cheek colour opacity rises from 0.3 to 0.9 | 1.5 s |
| Mouth | gentle smile (`mw 20, ms 8, mo 2`), or a yawn (`mw 12, ms 0, mo 16`) when the current expression is sleepy; strength 0.85 | 1.5 s |
| Automatic idle blink | one blink when nothing is changing | every `IDLE_BLINK_S = 5` s, lasts `BLINK_S = 0.8` s |

- **Input lock:** while an expression change or an effect is running (`busy()`), taps on any zone are ignored (no queueing).
- **Slow yawn:** while changing to *sleepy* (and not in reduced motion) the mouth opens and then closes (`+12` opening, `+4` width, `bump` curve).
- **Animal copy:** the same eye, cheek and mouth shapes are drawn over the animal head at the same relative positions, scaled by `k = min(0.85, max(0.62, 48 / (top * 2.5)))` where `top` is the animal's ear height.
- **No failure:** there are no wrong actions, scores or timers other than the idle blink.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (not measured)

- Early exposure to basic facial expressions in a calm context.
- Cause and effect: a touch produces a visible, gentle response.
- Independent, low-pressure play.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Four expressions that differ in eye and mouth shape rather than colour.
- Distinct reactions for eyes, cheeks and mouth.
- The animal always mirrors the face.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on emotional understanding or development. The code makes no such measurement.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** all touch zones are real `<button>` elements with `aria-label`s (`Buźka: zmień minę`, `Oczy`, `Lewy policzek`, `Prawy policzek`, `Buzia`, `<animal>: zmień minę`), so touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab then Enter/Space) work. Focus ring: 4 px `#8f7fd1`.
- **Target sizes:** hit areas are percentages of the face size `F`: eyes 64% x 26%, each cheek 24% x 20%, mouth 40% x 22%, whole face 100% x 100%; the animal is at least 64 px wide. In portrait `F = min(fw * 0.94, fh * 0.66)`; in landscape `F = min(fh * 0.98, fw * 0.6)`. For example, for a 640 x 360 landscape window with no safe-area insets, `F` is about 278 px, giving cheek zones of about 67 x 56 px (a calculation from the formulas, not a measurement). On smaller faces the cheek zones become smaller than 56 px (they reach 56 x 56 px only when `F` is at least about 280 px).
- **Orientation:** the layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange` (portrait: animal in the bottom-right corner; landscape: animal to the right of the face).
- **Colour:** expressions are told apart by shape; the pink cheek glow is an additional cue only.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Reduced motion:** expression changes and effects are driven from the rAF loop, so they are not disabled by the global CSS rule; under `prefers-reduced-motion` the change is shortened to 0.4 s and the yawn bump is skipped. Effects (blink, cheek glow, mouth) and the idle blink still run.
- **Touch behaviour:** `.bz` uses `touch-action: manipulation`; text selection disabled.
- **Independent use:** a young child can use it without reading; adult supervision is not required by the design.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The idle blink every 5 s and the animated mouth are the only unprompted motion; both are slow.
- Cheek hit areas can fall below 56 px on small screens (see section 6).
- The companion animal can partly overlap the face on very small portrait fields (see section 15); `Requires verification`.
- Touches during a change or effect are silently ignored, which may look unresponsive to a child who taps repeatedly.
- No personal data is collected.

## 8. Configuration

There is no external configuration; constants inside [`js/buzki.js`](../../js/buzki.js):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EXPR` | Four expression parameter sets | array of objects | see section 4 |
| `SMILE`, `YAWN` | Mouth shapes for the mouth effect | objects | `{20, 8, 2}`, `{12, 0, 16}` |
| `CHANGE_S` | Expression change time | s | `1` |
| `EFFECT_S` | Eyes, cheeks, mouth effect time | s | `1.5` |
| `BLINK_S` | Idle blink time | s | `0.8` |
| `IDLE_BLINK_S` | Pause before an idle blink | s | `5` |
| `EYE`, `MOUTH` | Colours | CSS colours | `#5b5675`, `#8a6a8f` |

These cannot be changed without editing the file; there is no fallback because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The face is an inline SVG (circle `#ffe9a8` with a highlight stroke, eyes, cheeks, mouth) built in `headSvg`; the animal head comes from `Animals.head(id, { bare: true })` in [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (shape only, without eyes, nose or mouth). The panda uses white eyes (`Animals.eyeColor`). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **What is random:** the companion animal, `Animals.pick(1)[0]`, chosen once per launch from the 13 shared animals (Miś, Króliczek, Kotek, Piesek, Myszka, Świnka, Lisek, Lew, Słoń, Panda, Żabka, Sowa, Koala).
- **Repetition:** `Animals.pick` uses `Rand.shuffle` and is independent per launch, so the same animal can appear on consecutive launches (no repeat prevention here; `Not implemented`).
- **Persistence:** none; the animal does not change while the activity is open.
- The face, expression order and timings are not random.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels, and nothing is stored between launches. The expression always starts at happy.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no formal completion state. The feedback for each touch is the visual response described in section 4; there is no score, sound, celebration or failure message. The interaction cycle is simply touch -> response -> idle.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/buzki.js`](../../js/buzki.js), registered by replacing the `mount` of the `buzki` registry entry; returns a cleanup function. The script is loaded before `app.js`.
- **State:** closure variables `cur` (expression index), `from` (parameters at the start of a change), `changeT`, `fx` (running effect `{type, t, d}`), `idleBlink`, `idleTimer`.
- **Rendering:** fixed DOM: `.bz-field` containing `.bz-face` and `.bz-cat`, each with one inline SVG and transparent buttons on top. `paint()` writes `rx`/`ry` of the eye ellipses, cheek opacity and the mouth path `d` on both heads each frame.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`, `dt` capped at 50 ms). When nothing animates the loop stops and `armIdle` sets a 5 s `setTimeout` to wake it for the next idle blink. The loop and timer are cancelled while the tab is hidden and resumed on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `click` on the buttons; `resize`/`orientationchange` for `layout`.
- **Randomization:** `Animals.pick(1)` ([`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js)).
- **Persistence and analytics:** none.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, clears the timer, removes three window/document listeners and the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.bz-field` is inset 64 px from the top (plus safe area) and 12 px elsewhere.
- Coordinates are CSS pixels inside the field; the face is positioned with `transform: translate`.
- **Portrait** (`fh >= fw`): face `F = min(fw * 0.94, fh * 0.66)` at the top; animal `C = max(64, min(fw * 0.4, fh - F - 12, 130))` in the bottom-right corner.
- **Landscape:** face `F = min(fh * 0.98, fw * 0.6)`; animal `C = max(64, min(F * 0.45, 130))` to the right of the face (16 px gap), at the bottom.
- Face and animal SVGs use a `0 0 100 100` viewBox; hit areas are percentages of the box, so they scale together. Eyes, cheeks and mouth on the animal are the same SVG parts laid over the animal head.
- Because `C` is floored at 64 px, in a very short portrait field the animal may overlap the face; `Requires verification`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable. |
| Rapid repeated taps | Ignored while an expression change or effect runs. |
| Resize/orientation change | `layout` repositions; animation state is kept. |
| Tab hidden | `frame` returns without scheduling; the idle timer is cleared; resumes on return. |
| Leaving mid-animation | Cleanup cancels the loop and timer. |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | `reduced()` returns `false`. |
| Touch cancellation | Not relevant: only `click` is used. |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#79](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/79) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM run; this documentation does not re-verify it.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: tap the face repeatedly (waiting for each change) and confirm the order happy, sleepy, surprised, calm, happy; the animal mirrors every change.
- [ ] Zones: tap eyes (blink), both cheeks (pink glow), mouth in happy (smile) and in sleepy (yawn).
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap during a change; the extra tap is ignored; tap the area between zones.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-open; the face is happy again.
- [ ] Randomization: open the activity several times and note that the companion animal varies, including the panda (white eyes).
- [ ] Idle: wait without touching for more than 5 s and watch one slow blink.
- [ ] Progression/completion: confirm there is no end state, score or level.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: face and animal fully visible; rotate while an effect runs; check small phones (320 x 568, 568 x 320).
- [ ] Touch and mouse: tap with a finger; click; Tab and press Enter/Space on each zone.
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab mid-change and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion: with the OS setting on, the change is quicker and the yawn animation is absent.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The animal companion is not prevented from repeating between launches.
- Taps during a running change are dropped rather than queued.

**Requires verification**

- Cheek hit-area size on small screens; face/animal overlap on very short portrait fields.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other activities with a random animal and gentle touch response: [Kąpiel Zwierzątek](kapiel-zwierzatek.md).
- Shared helpers actually used: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`, `Animals.eyeColor`). `Rand` is used indirectly through `Animals.pick`.
- Other activities that draw animals from the shared family: [Cienie](cienie.md).

## 21. Change history

- [#54](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/54) / PR [#79](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/79): activity added (originally with a fixed cat companion).
- Commit "Buźki: stop rAF loop when idle, wake via timer for idle blink" (review suggestion, merged with PR #79).
- [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): random animal companion from the shared family.
```

```markdown
# Cienie

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Cienie |
| Internal ID | `cienie` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Three grey animal shadows on top and the three matching coloured animals below; the child drags each animal onto its own shadow. |
| Category | Matching (shape/silhouette matching) |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop (pointer events); keyboard alternative: select an animal, then select a shadow |
| CSS prefix | `ci-` |
| Source | [`js/cienie.js`](../../js/cienie.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section `/* Cienie */`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`). Listed 27th in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

Cienie gives the child a calm matching task that relies on silhouette shape rather than on reading or colour: the shadows are all one grey, so the only cue is the outline. It reuses the layout approach of [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md) (PR #83) but with recognisable animals, and it stays consistent with the application's no-failure principle: a wrong drop simply floats back, with no message, shake, red colour or sound.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity from the menu (hash route `#cienie`); `mount` builds the board and picks the first set of animals at random.
2. Three grey shadows are shown in a row at the top; the three coloured animals are shown in a row at the bottom in a mixed order (no animal starts directly under its own shadow).
3. The child presses an animal and drags it. The animal follows the finger or pointer and is clamped so its centre stays inside the visible screen.
4. On release within 0.75 x the animal size (`S * 0.75`) of its own shadow, the animal glides into the shadow and stays there with a soft glow; the shadow dims to 30% opacity. On release anywhere else, the animal glides back to its home slot.
5. When all three animals are placed, the whole picture glows (about 3 s).
6. About 7 s after the third animal settled, the board fades out (0.6 s), a new set of three animals is loaded and the board fades back in (0.6 s).
7. The loop repeats indefinitely; there is no separate restart control. Leaving and re-opening the activity starts a fresh random set.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (source) |
|---|---|
| Shadows per round | 3, evenly spread at `fw * (i + 0.5) / 3`, vertical position `S / 2 + 4` (`layout`) |
| Animal size `S` | `max(64, min(140, fw / 3.6, fh * 0.3))` px |
| Snap distance | animal centre closer than `S * 0.75` to its own shadow centre (`up`) |
| Wrong drop | `sendHome`: glides back to the home slot; no feedback |
| Home slot | `fw * (slot + 0.5) / 3`, `y = max(fh - S/2 - 4, S * 1.6)` |
| Glide duration | `min(1400, 700 + distance * 0.8)` ms; 300 ms under reduced motion; 200 ms for a re-layout glide |
| Placed animal | `placed = true`, button disabled and `tabIndex = -1`, cannot be moved again in the round |
| Completion glow | `GLOW_S = 3000` ms |
| Next round | `NEXT_S = 7000` ms after all three are placed; fade `FADE_S = 600` ms each way |
| Input lock | pointer-down ignored while a round change is fading (`fadeDir !== 0`) |
| Multi-touch | each animal tracks its own `pointerId`, so several animals can be dragged at once |
| Mouse buttons | pointer-down with `button > 0` is ignored |
| Resize during a drag | the drag is cancelled and the animal returns home (`layout` -> `cancelDrag`) |

Timing values use the capped frame step (`dt` capped at 50 ms), so on a very slow device the sequence takes longer in wall-clock time.

Keyboard: `Enter`/`Space` on an animal button selects it (`aria-pressed`, outline `ci-selected`); activating a shadow button then snaps the animal if it is the right one, otherwise sends it home. Selecting a selected animal deselects it.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the code comments and README, not measured):

- Visual perception of silhouettes and shape discrimination.
- Hand-eye coordination through dragging.
- Calm, failure-free practice with immediate soft feedback.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Shadows are drawn in one colour (`#c4c0d4`) with no inner detail, so only the outline identifies the animal.
- The three animals in a round always have different silhouettes (see section 10).
- Correct placement fills the shadow with the animal and adds a glow; wrong placement only returns the animal.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about developmental benefit or learning effect. Nothing in the repository measures it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via Pointer Events (pointer capture); keyboard via the select-then-place flow above. The animal buttons have `aria-label` such as `kotek (Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz cień)`; the shadow buttons have `Cień: <name>`.
- **Target size:** animals and shadows are at least 64 x 64 px (`min-width/min-height: 64px`, size `S` up to 140 px).
- **Orientation:** the field fills the screen below the Back button (top offset `64px` plus safe area); layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange` and works in portrait and landscape.
- **Colour:** matching does not depend on colour (the shadows are grey and identical in colour); the coloured fill is only the reward.
- **Sound:** none (the application is silent).
- **Reading:** not required.
- **Reduced motion:** the glide, glow and fade are driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` loop that sets styles from JavaScript, so they are not removed by the global CSS rule. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` only the glide time is shortened to 300 ms (`reduced()`); the glow and fades still run.
- **Focus:** a 4 px outline (`#8f7fd1`) marks focused or selected items.
- **Touch behaviour:** `.ci`, `.ci-item` use `touch-action: none` so dragging is not turned into scrolling; text selection is disabled.
- **Limitations:** a child needs enough motor control to drag; the keyboard path needs two actions per match.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Whether every pair of silhouettes from different groups is easy to tell apart for a young child at the smallest size is not established in the repository (`Requires verification` on real devices).
- Fills of grey versus soft colours rely on low-saturation pastels; contrast of the grey shadow against the pale background (`#f3eefb` to `#e2f3dc` gradient) is low by design.
- A child may drag an animal around for a long time; there is no timeout or hint.
- The activity loops indefinitely with new rounds; there is no natural end other than leaving.
- No personal data is collected or stored.

## 8. Configuration

There is no external configuration; all values are constants inside [`js/cienie.js`](../../js/cienie.js). Tunable constants:

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SHADOW` | Shadow fill colour | CSS colour | `#c4c0d4` | top of IIFE |
| `GLOW_S` | Duration of the completion glow | ms | `3000` | top of IIFE |
| `NEXT_S` | Time from completion to the next round | ms | `7000` | top of IIFE |
| `FADE_S` | Fade time of a round change | ms | `600` | top of IIFE |
| `EXTRA` | Three hand-drawn animals (bird, fish, turtle) | array | 3 entries | top of IIFE |
| size formula | `S` between 64 and 140 px | px | see section 4 | `layout` |
| snap factor | Snap radius as a multiple of `S` | number | `0.75` | `up` |

The sets per round (3) are fixed by the DOM that `mount` builds. Invalid or missing values have no fallback because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything is inline SVG generated in JavaScript:

- 13 animals from the shared family (`Animals.head`, see [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js)), drawn with a small body (`body: true`); the shadow variant passes `shadow: '#c4c0d4'`.
- 3 hand-drawn full-body animals (bird `ptak`, fish `rybka`, turtle `żółw`) in `EXTRA`, drawn in a 100 x 100 box with placeholder `@@` replaced by the fill colour.
- Menu icon: inline SVG in the registry entry in `js/activities.js`.

No fonts, images or audio. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Pool:** 16 entries: the 13 shared animals plus bird, fish and turtle. Entries are grouped by silhouette group (`sil`): the shared family has 10 groups (for example `round` = bear, panda, koala; `point` = cat, fox), the extras add `bird`, `fish`, `turtle` (13 groups in total).
- **Selection (`nextSet`):** the pool is shuffled with `Rand.shuffle`; entries are taken in order, skipping any whose group is already in the set, until 3 are chosen. So a set never contains two animals of one silhouette group.
- **No immediate repeat:** the loop repeats until the set (compared by sorted ids) differs from the previous round's set. The same single animal may still appear in consecutive rounds, only the identical trio is excluded.
- **Mixing:** `rotation()` randomly returns slots `[1, 2, 0]` or `[2, 0, 1]`, so no animal starts under its own shadow.
- **First round:** a fresh random set on every launch; nothing is stored.
- **Terminating:** there are always at least 13 groups, so a 3-element set is always available; there is no empty-pool handling because the pool is a constant.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression: every round has three animals with a fixed layout and no change of difficulty. Nothing persists between rounds or sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Completion:** all three animals placed (`items.every(placed && mode === 'idle')`).
- **Feedback for a correct drop:** glide, the shadow dims to 30% opacity, the animal gets a soft glow (`drop-shadow` in the animal's own colour).
- **Feedback for a wrong drop:** the animal glides back; nothing else.
- **Celebration:** a warm radial glow (`.ci-glow`) over the whole board for about 3 s, plus extra glow on the animals.
- **Afterwards:** a new round fades in automatically; no input is needed.
- **Sound:** none.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/cienie.js`](../../js/cienie.js) replaces the `mount` of the registry entry whose `id === 'cienie'`; it returns a `cleanup` function. Script tag order in `index.html`: `cienie.js` is loaded before `app.js`.
- **State:** closure variables in `mount` (`set`, `slots`, `items`, `shadows`, `selected`, timers `doneT`, `fade`, `fadeDir`); per-animal state objects hold position, glide data and mode (`idle`, `drag`, `glide`).
- **Rendering:** a fixed DOM of three shadow `<button>` elements and three animal `<button>` elements inside `.ci-field`, each holding one inline SVG; positions are set through `transform: translate(...)`. A `.ci-glow` div carries the completion glow.
- **Animation:** a single capped-step (`dt <= 50 ms`) `requestAnimationFrame` loop `frame`; it runs only while something is moving (glide, glow, fade, completion timer) and is restarted by `start()`; it is cancelled when `document.hidden` and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel`/`lostpointercapture` on each animal; `click` with `detail === 0` (keyboard activation) selects; `click` on shadows places the selected animal; `resize` and `orientationchange` re-run `layout`.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.shuffle` from [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) and `Animals.LIST`/`Animals.head`.
- **Persistence:** none.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the animation frame, removes the `resize`, `orientationchange` and `visibilitychange` listeners and removes the board from the DOM.
- **Dependencies:** `window.Animals`, `window.Rand` (both loaded before the activity scripts).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The board `.ci` is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; the playing field `.ci-field` is inset 64 px from the top (plus `--safe-t`) and 12 px on the other sides (plus safe-area insets).
- All positions are measured in CSS pixels relative to the field (`fw` x `fh`, read from `getBoundingClientRect` in `layout`). Shadows, home slots and dragged animals share this one pixel coordinate space; there is no viewBox scaling of the layout.
- Item size `S` scales with the width and height of the field (section 4); each animal's SVG uses a `0 0 100 100` viewBox.
- Home slots sit in a row at the bottom; the shadows sit in a row at the top. In a very short landscape field the home row y is at least `S * 1.6`, keeping the animals below the shadows.
- During a drag the centre is clamped inside the window (`window.innerWidth/innerHeight`), so an animal cannot be lost off-screen.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable (no external assets). |
| Empty pool / too few groups | Not applicable; the pool is constant and has 13 silhouette groups. |
| Resize or orientation change | `layout` recomputes positions; a dragged animal is cancelled and sent home; gliding animals restart a 200 ms glide to the new target. |
| Tab hidden | The frame loop is cancelled and resumes on `visibilitychange`. |
| Rapid or multi-touch input | Each animal handles its own pointer; a placed animal cannot be grabbed; input is ignored during the round fade. |
| Touch cancellation | `pointercancel` and `lostpointercapture` end the drag like a release (snap or send home). |
| Synthetic or unsupported pointer capture | `setPointerCapture` and `releasePointerCapture` are wrapped in `try/catch`. |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | `reduced()` falls back to `false`. |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#83](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/83) reports `node --check` and a stubbed run; this documentation does not re-verify it.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: drag each of the three animals onto its own shadow; each glides in and fills the shadow.
- [ ] Completion: after the third animal, the glow appears for about 3 s and a new set fades in about 7 s after the last placement.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: drop an animal on a wrong shadow and on empty space; it floats back with no message.
- [ ] Restart/replay: play several rounds in a row; leave and re-open the activity to get a fresh set.
- [ ] Randomization: over many rounds check that no round shows two animals with a similar outline (for example cat and fox) and that the same trio never appears twice in a row.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that nothing changes in difficulty between rounds.
- [ ] Portrait: 320 x 568 up to a tablet; all six items visible, at least 64 px.
- [ ] Landscape: 568 x 320 and 1920 x 1080; shadows stay above the animals; rotate during a drag and during the glow.
- [ ] Touch: drag with one finger; try two fingers on two animals; try to drag a placed animal.
- [ ] Mouse: click-drag, right-click (ignored), keyboard Tab/Enter/Space select-and-place flow.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tabs during the 7 s timer and during a glide; the sequence resumes without a jump.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad (as required by the README).
- [ ] Reduced motion: enable the OS setting and confirm the glide is shorter and the activity still completes.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.
- Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The keyboard flow is the only non-pointer path; there is no arrow-key dragging.

**Requires verification**

- Visual distinguishability of all silhouette groups at the smallest size (64 px).
- Behaviour of the animation timers on very slow devices (they scale with the capped frame step).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned. (No open issue targets this activity; issue [#168](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/168) is this documentation task.)

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar drag-and-match layout: [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md) (PR #83 says Cienie uses the same proven layout); another matching game: [Pamięć](pamiec.md).
- Shared helpers: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.shuffle`) and [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.LIST`, `Animals.head`, with the `shadow` option used only here and in [Kąpiel Zwierzątek](kapiel-zwierzatek.md)).
- Other activities that draw animals from the shared family: Buźki ([buzki.md](buzki.md)), Kąpiel Zwierzątek.

## 21. Change history

- [#57](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/57) / PR [#83](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/83): activity added (originally with the CSS prefix `cn-`; commit "give Cienie its own ci- CSS prefix" renamed it after a review found a collision).
- [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): random animal pool from the shared family, silhouette groups, no repeated trio.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/co-nie-pasuje.md`

```markdown
# Co nie Pasuje?

> Documents the current implementation on `main`. Shared platform behaviour (no sound, global reduced-motion rule, menu configuration, playtime, absence of automated tests, analytics status) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Co nie Pasuje? |
| Activity ID | `co-nie-pasuje` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | Three large pictures: two of one kind (for example two fruits) and one different (for example a car). Touching the odd one makes it glow and bounce while the other two fade slightly, then the next set fades in. Touching a matching picture only wobbles it. |
| Category | Sorting / matching (odd one out) |
| Interaction type | Tap |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/co-nie-pasuje.js`](../../js/co-nie-pasuje.js), CSS prefix `cn-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity offers a simple categorisation game (find the picture that does not belong) without wrong-answer feedback. A matching picture only wobbles, the odd one gives a reward-free glow, so the child can try freely. It complements the counting and pattern activities with a visual-classification task.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the first set fades in (0.9 s).
2. Three pictures are shown in a row (landscape) or a column (portrait). The odd picture is at a random position.
3. The child touches a picture.
   - A matching picture wobbles once (0.7 s) and nothing else changes; the child can keep trying.
   - The odd picture glows and bounces (0.9 s); the two others dim to about 55% opacity.
4. The glow lasts 3 s, then the scene fades out (0.9 s) and a new set fades in (0.9 s).
5. There is no end screen; the activity continues with new sets. The child leaves with the Back button.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Pictures per set | 3 (2 of one category, 1 odd) |
| Sets | 10 fixed sets (`SETS`) |
| Pictures | 12 in 4 categories of 3 (`PICS`) |
| Wobble (matching) | 0.7 s (`WOBBLE`), rotation up to 7 degrees, decaying |
| Bounce (odd) | 0.9 s (`BOUNCE`), up to 16 units high |
| Glow | 3 s (`GLOW`), 0.5 s ramps; the other two pictures dim by up to 0.45 opacity |
| Fade between sets | 0.9 s out and 0.9 s in (`FADE`) |
| Touch handling | accepted only in phase `play`; ignored during glow, fade out and fade in |
| Odd position | random among the 3 slots |

Categories (`PICS`): 0 fruit (Jabłko, Gruszka, Banan), 1 vehicles (Samochód, Łódka, Samolot), 2 animals (Kotek, Kaczuszka, Rybka), 3 toys (Piłka, Klocek, Latawiec).

The 10 sets (`[category, picture, picture]` for the matching pair, `[category, picture]` for the odd one): fruit pairs (Jabłko+Gruszka, Gruszka+Banan, Jabłko+Banan), vehicle pairs (Samochód+Łódka, Łódka+Samolot), animal pairs (Kotek+Kaczuszka, Kaczuszka+Rybka, Kotek+Rybka) and toy pairs (Piłka+Klocek, Klocek+Latawiec), each with an odd picture from another category. Example: `[[0,0,1],[1,0]]` is Jabłko and Gruszka with Samochód as the odd one.

A correct touch is final for the set: after the odd picture is touched, further touches are ignored until the next set is shown. No score is kept.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**: visual perception and categorisation (shape, kind of object), attention, calm cause and effect, independent play without text.

**Directly observable behavior**
- Meaning is carried by silhouettes and pictures, not by colour alone (stated in the source header).
- A wrong guess has no negative signal; only a small wobble.
- The set changes only after the odd picture is found.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**
- Whether children learn categories or improve attention through this activity.
- Whether pairings such as Kaczuszka and Rybka (both animals) and Łódka and Latawiec (different categories) are unambiguous for a young child.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse, stylus and keyboard (each picture is a `<button>` with an `aria-label` of its Polish name, for example "Jabłko"); 4px focus outline; `touch-action: manipulation`.
- **Target size:** `--cn-s` is `min(28vw, 56dvh, 260px)` in landscape and `min(56vw, 22dvh, 260px)` when the viewport is not wider than tall; `min-width`/`min-height` 72px.
- **Orientation:** row in landscape, column in portrait (`@media (max-aspect-ratio: 1/1)`); the board is fluid (no fixed aspect ratio).
- **Colour:** each picture has a distinctive silhouette; the glow is a pale yellow circle behind the picture.
- **Reading:** none required.
- **Sound:** none.
- **Reduced motion:** state changes (glow, dimming, fades) are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so they still run under the global CSS rule. In addition the code reads `prefers-reduced-motion` once at mount (`noMotion`): when set, the wobble and bounce movement is omitted (the timing still runs, so touches are ignored for the same durations), leaving glow, dimming and fades.
- **Limitations:** the correct choice is not announced to assistive technology; the dimming of the others is visual only.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Only 10 fixed sets, so repetition appears after a short while (never twice in a row).
- Some pairs may be ambiguous in a child's mind (for example a boat and a fish both relate to water; a kite and an aeroplane both fly); the design intends category by object type but this is not validated.
- Touches are ignored for about 3 s plus fades after the odd picture is found, which may feel unresponsive to a child tapping repeatedly.
- No ending; the activity loops with new sets.
- Privacy: nothing is stored or transmitted.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in `js/co-nie-pasuje.js`.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Changeable without code change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WOBBLE`, `BOUNCE` | Matching-picture wobble and odd-picture bounce (s) | numbers | 0.7, 0.9 | No |
| `GLOW` | Time the glow shows before the next set (s) | number | 3 | No |
| `FADE` | Set fade out and fade in (s each) | number | 0.9 | No |
| `MAXDT` | Frame cap (s) | number | 0.05 | No |
| `PICS` | 12 pictures by category | nested array of `{label, svg}` | 4 x 3 | No |
| `SETS` | The 10 sets | array | see section 4 | No |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. All 12 pictures are inline SVG strings in `js/co-nie-pasuje.js` (100x100 viewBox, shared `STROKE` attributes and a shared glow circle `GLOWC`). No fonts, images or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **What is random:** the next set (`pick()` uses `Math.random()` over the 10 sets) and the slot of the odd picture (`Math.floor(Math.random() * 3)`).
- **Immediate repetition:** the next set is re-drawn until it differs from the current one (`do ... while (n === cur)`), so the same set never appears twice in a row. Across sets, repeats are allowed and there is no cycle through all sets. The odd slot can repeat.
- **Does not use `Rand`:** the shared helper `js/random.js` is not used here.
- **Persistence:** none; each visit starts with a random set (the very first set is also random).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. All sets are equivalent; no levels; nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Completion:** touching the odd picture ends the set.
- **Success feedback:** the odd picture glows and bounces; the other two dim.
- **Incorrect touch:** the touched matching picture wobbles; no other change.
- **After completion:** the next set fades in automatically after about 3.9 s (3 s glow plus 0.9 s fade out, then 0.9 s fade in). No sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** IIFE in [`js/co-nie-pasuje.js`](../../js/co-nie-pasuje.js) overriding `mount` for `co-nie-pasuje`.
- **Rendering:** DOM and SVG: a `.cn` root with a `.cn-row` containing three `<button class="cn-btn">` each with an SVG.
- **State:** `phase` (`in`, `play`, `glow`, `out`), `fade`, `glow`, `dim`, `cur` (current set), `oddIdx`, per item `{odd, t}`.
- **Animation:** single `requestAnimationFrame` loop `frame()` with capped dt, stops when idle and while the tab is hidden; `wake()` restarts it.
- **Events:** `click` on each button; `visibilitychange`.
- **Cleanup:** removes the listener, cancels the frame and removes the root.
- **Shared helpers:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The row is a flexbox centred in a container padded 56px at the top (Back button) plus safe areas.
- Size variable `--cn-s` (see section 6) is applied to the three buttons; each picture is a 100x100 SVG scaled to the button.
- Landscape: `flex-direction: row`, `gap: 4vw`. Viewport not wider than tall: column, `gap: 3dvh`, smaller `--cn-s`.
- There is no resize listener; the layout is CSS only. There is no shared coordinate system between pictures.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Rapid input:** touches are ignored outside the `play` phase; repeated touches on matching pictures simply restart the wobble.
- **Backgrounding:** loop cancelled while hidden and restarted on return.
- **Resize/orientation:** CSS only.
- **Leaving during animation:** cleanup cancels the frame.
- **Unhandled:** the reduced-motion preference is read once at mount.

## 17. Testing

There are no automated tests. Manual scenarios to perform:

- [ ] A set appears after the fade-in with two matching pictures and one odd picture.
- [ ] Touch a matching picture repeatedly: only a wobble; nothing else changes.
- [ ] Touch the odd picture: it glows and bounces, the others dim, and a new set fades in after about 4 s.
- [ ] Touch pictures during the glow and fades: nothing happens.
- [ ] Play 20 or more sets: the same set never appears twice in a row; the odd picture's slot varies.
- [ ] Check each of the 12 pictures renders correctly and is recognisable.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate between sets; small phone (320x568) and large tablet.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space).
- [ ] Switch tab during the glow and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion on at launch: no wobble or bounce, glow, dimming and fades still shown.
- [ ] Browsers required by the README: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#80](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/80) reports only `node --check`; it states that there was no browser in the sandbox and that manual tests (browsers, orientation, reduced motion) were pending.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**
- Only 10 sets and 12 pictures.
- No automated tests; manual tests were pending in PR #80.
- Reduced-motion preference is read once at mount.

**Requires verification**
- Whether all pairings are unambiguous for the target age.
- Layout of three 72px+ pictures in very short landscape viewports (for example 640x360).

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Same scene pattern (single rAF loop, glow, wait, cross-fade): [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md), [Ścieżka](sciezka.md), [Wzorki](wzorki.md).
- Related theme (finding what differs): [Cienie](cienie.md) (matching shadows).
- Shared helpers `js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not used.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#60](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/60) / PR [#80](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/80): activity added.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/deszczyk-i-tecza.md`

```markdown
# Deszczyk i Tęcza

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Deszczyk i Tęcza |
| Activity ID | `deszczyk` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Three clouds over a meadow: touching a cloud makes it rain gently, puddles ripple and swell, and after enough rain a soft rainbow fades in and out again. |
| Category | Cause and effect; observation |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse, keyboard) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default |
| Source | [`js/deszczyk.js`](../../js/deszczyk.js), styles with prefix `r-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A weather toy with a delayed, rewarding consequence: rain now, rainbow later, which shows a longer chain of cause and effect than a single tap-response.
- Calm, low-stimulation scenery (pastel sky, slow-falling drops).
- Complements [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md), whose night stars and rain were reworked in [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173) (merged) to look more natural.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 10.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the static scene is built (the animation loop is **not** running yet).
2. Initially displayed: a pale sky, a meadow, three puddles and three clouds.
3. Interactions: tap a cloud.
4. Response: that cloud rains for 5 s (a tap during rain restarts the 5 s); drops fall straight below it; those landing in a puddle produce a ripple; puddles swell a little while it rains and shrink back after.
5. After a total of 30 "cloud-seconds" of rain a rainbow fades in (4 s), stays (10 s) and fades out (4 s).
6. There is no formal end; the child can start rain again at any time, and the rainbow can reappear.
7. Restart: leave and re-open the activity (all counters reset).
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Rain duration | `RAIN_S = 5` s per tap. Tapping a raining cloud resets its timer to 5 s (it does not add up). |
| Drops | Each raining cloud spawns `DROPS_PER_S = 7` drops per second; a drop falls at `FALL = 0.2` board heights per second. Pool `MAX_DROPS = 60`; when the pool is full, new spawns are skipped silently. |
| Drop path | x = cloud x plus a random offset of up to 35 % of the cloud width either way; the drop starts 0.05 board heights below the cloud centre. |
| Landing | If the drop's x is within 40 % of a puddle's width of the puddle centre, it lands at the puddle's y and creates a ripple; otherwise it lands at a random ground y between 0.74 and 0.97 and disappears without a ripple. |
| Ripples | Pool `MAX_RIPPLES = 12`; lifetime `RIPPLE_S = 2.6` s; scale from 0.2 to 1 (smoothstep) and opacity from 0.7 to 0. A ripple is skipped if the pool is full. |
| Puddles | Scale by `1 + 0.18 * level`; `level` eases towards 1 while any cloud rains and back to 0 afterwards (rate about 0.25 per second, exponential). |
| Rainbow counter | `rainTotal` increases by `dt * (number of raining clouds)` only while no rainbow is showing. At 30 (`RAINBOW_AFTER_S`) the rainbow starts and the counter resets to 0. So one cloud needs 30 s of continuous rain, three clouds 10 s. |
| Rainbow | Fade in 4 s, hold 10 s, fade out 4 s (smoothstep, max opacity 0.85); 18 s in total. Rain during the rainbow does not count towards the next one. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect, including a delayed consequence (rain leads to a rainbow).
- Calm observation of slowly falling drops, ripples and a fading rainbow.
- Noticing that several clouds together make it happen faster.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Rain starts only on touch, stops by itself, and the rainbow only appears after enough rain.
- No failure, score or text.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claims about understanding of weather or causality. Nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** the clouds are native `<button>`s (labels "Chmurka 1" to "Chmurka 3"); they react to `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) and to keyboard-generated `click` (Enter/Space).
- **Targets:** each cloud is 30 to 36 % of the board width with `min-width: 96px`.
- **Layout:** the board is a square `min(94vw, 100dvh - 110px)` with a 60 px top margin, centred; works in portrait and landscape (a smaller board in landscape).
- **Colour:** nothing depends on colour; the rainbow is decorative.
- **Reduced motion:** every moving part (rain, ripples, puddle swelling, rainbow fades) is driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` loop, not CSS, so it still animates under the global rule. The activity has no reduced-intensity variant.
- **Touch:** `touch-action: none`, no text selection.
- **Reading:** not required. A young child can use it independently.
- **Limitations:** the clouds have no `aria-pressed` or raining state; a screen reader cannot tell whether it is raining.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- With all three clouds raining, the demand (21 drops/s, each falling for roughly 2.6 to 4 s) can exceed the pool of 60 drops, so some drops are skipped (computed from the constants; visual effect requires verification).
- Rainbow appears after real play only; a child who taps once may never see it (a single cloud needs 30 s of rain, so about 6 re-taps).
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.
- No privacy concerns; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/deszczyk.js`](../../js/deszczyk.js):

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `RAIN_S` | Rain time per tap | 5 s |
| `RAINBOW_AFTER_S` | Cloud-seconds of rain before the rainbow | 30 |
| `FADE_IN_S`, `HOLD_S`, `FADE_OUT_S` | Rainbow phases | 4, 10, 4 s |
| `MAX_DROPS`, `MAX_RIPPLES` | Pool sizes | 60, 12 |
| `DROPS_PER_S`, `FALL` | Drop rate per cloud; fall speed (board heights per second) | 7, 0.2 |
| `RIPPLE_S` | Ripple lifetime | 2.6 s |
| `CLOUDS` | Cloud `x, y, w` (fractions of the board) | (0.2, 0.17, 0.34), (0.52, 0.1, 0.36), (0.82, 0.2, 0.3) |
| `PUDDLES` | Puddle `x, y, w` | (0.24, 0.84, 0.24), (0.56, 0.92, 0.22), (0.8, 0.8, 0.2) |
| `GROUND_MIN`, `GROUND_MAX` | Landing range for drops outside puddles | 0.74, 0.97 |

Fallback: none needed (no external values).

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The cloud (`CLOUD_SVG`) and the rainbow (six stroked arcs, colours `#f7b6c2`, `#ffd3a8`, `#fff0a8`, `#bfe6b4`, `#b5dcf5`, `#c9b8f2`, `viewBox="0 0 200 110"`) are inline SVG; the meadow, puddles, ripples and drops are CSS shapes. No images, fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- The only randomness is in the rain itself: each drop's horizontal offset under its cloud, and its landing y when it does not hit a puddle (`Math.random`).
- Scene, cloud and puddle layout are fixed; there are no variants and nothing is stored.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. The rainbow counter is a short-lived internal state (in memory only) and resets when the activity is re-opened.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- There is no completion state. The rainbow is a delayed reward, not an end.
- Feedback: falling drops, ripples, puddles swelling; the rainbow fade in and out. No failure feedback, no sound.
- After the rainbow fades out the counter starts again from 0.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/deszczyk.js`](../../js/deszczyk.js); the cleanup function cancels the frame, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Rendering:** DOM. Fixed pools of 60 drop `div`s, 12 ripple `div`s, 3 puddles, 3 cloud buttons and one rainbow element are created at mount; drops and ripples are shown or hidden with `display`.
- **Loop:** `frame()` with `dt` capped at 0.05 s. It is started by a cloud tap and stops itself when nothing is active (no rain, drops, ripples, rainbow or puddle swelling). It pauses when the tab is hidden; long gaps are never replayed.
- **State:** per-cloud `rain` timer and drop accumulator; `rainTotal`, `bowState` (0 idle, 1 fade in, 2 hold, 3 fade out), `bowT`; `level` for puddles.
- **Events:** `pointerdown` (with `preventDefault`) plus `click` (when `detail === 0`) per cloud; `visibilitychange`.
- **Shared code:** none (the activity does not use `js/random.js` or `js/animals.js`).
- **Persistence and analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- A square board `.r-box` of side `min(94vw, 100dvh - 110px)`; all elements are placed with percentages of that square (clouds, puddles, drops, ripples, rainbow), so they always line up. The meadow extends beyond the square horizontally (`left/right: -100vw`).
- Drop positions are stored as fractions of the board; the rainbow occupies 4 % to 96 % of the width from 30 % of the height.
- Orientation changes need no JavaScript (CSS sizing only).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Rapid taps on clouds | Timer reset only; the pools bound the DOM. |
| Pool exhausted | New drops or ripples are skipped silently. |
| Tab hidden | Frame loop cancelled; on return `last` is reset, so the time hidden is not counted as rain or rainbow time. |
| Resize / orientation | CSS handles it; no JavaScript. |
| Leaving mid-rain | Cleanup cancels the frame and removes the scene. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; nothing moves; tap a cloud; it rains for about 5 s under that cloud only; puddles ripple and swell slightly and then shrink.
- [ ] Tap one cloud repeatedly for about 30 s; the rainbow fades in, holds and fades out.
- [ ] Tap all three clouds together; the rainbow appears after about 10 s.
- [ ] Rain during the rainbow does not trigger an immediate second rainbow.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the sky, meadow and puddles; nothing happens.
- [ ] Rapid tapping on all clouds; no slowdown, drops stay bounded.
- [ ] Restart: re-open the activity; the rainbow counter and puddles are reset.
- [ ] Randomization: drops fall at slightly different positions; confirm the layout is always identical.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate during rain; clouds and puddles stay aligned with the meadow.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard (Tab to each cloud, Enter/Space triggers rain, focus ring visible).
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab during rain and the rainbow; on return the motion resumes without catching up.
- [ ] Reduced motion: rain, ripples and rainbow still animate.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#38](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/38) reports that `node --check` passed and lists manual tests (including rapid tapping, orientation change and reduced motion) as pending. PR [#68](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/68) reports a stub-DOM mount without errors and lists the "all clouds rain" symptom on a Galaxy A33 as needing a device check.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No raining-state announcement for assistive technology.
- The rainbow threshold is time-based, so a casual single tap never produces a rainbow.
- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Pool saturation with three clouds raining (see section 7).
- Whether per-cloud rain is visually clear on small phones (the symptom in PR #68 was a device report).

## 19. Planned improvements

`None currently planned`.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Weather and sky: [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md) (its rain was reworked in #167 / PR #173, merged), [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md).
- Shared helpers: none used (`js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not used).
- The rAF loop pattern (capped time step, stops when idle, restarts on `visibilitychange`) is shared with other activities.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#29](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/29) / PR [#38](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/38): initial activity (rain, puddles, rainbow).
- Issue [#66](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/66) / PR [#68](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/68): drops fall below their own cloud; the rainbow counter counts cloud-seconds with a threshold of 30.
- Reviewer suggestion commit `0c0c4e8`: rain during the rainbow no longer counts towards the next one.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/dobranoc.md`

```markdown
# Dobranoc

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Dobranoc |
| Activity ID | `dobranoc` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A house at dusk: the child dims or relights four windows and tucks three random animals in or wakes them; when every light is off and every animal sleeps, stars and a sleeping moon fade in. |
| Category | Calming; cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse, keyboard) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default |
| Source | [`js/dobranoc.js`](../../js/dobranoc.js), styles with prefix `db-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A bedtime-themed, quiet activity: the only "goal" is a peaceful scene in which everything is switched off and asleep.
- All changes are reversible, so the child can play with the toggles endlessly with no wrong action.
- Complements the other calming/night activities ([Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md), [Nocne Niebo](nocne-niebo.md)) by adding a hands-on "put everything to bed" interaction.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 9.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the scene is built and painted once.
2. Initially displayed: a house with **four lit windows** and three **awake** animals in front of it, on a dusk-coloured sky.
3. Interactions: tap a window (dim or relight it) or tap an animal (tuck it in or wake it).
4. Response: the window fades over 1.5 s; the animal closes its eyes and a blanket fades in over 1.2 s.
5. Completion-like state: when all 4 lights are off and all 3 animals sleep, the "night" layer (stars and a sleeping moon) fades in over 4 s.
6. After that nothing happens automatically; any change reverses the state (the layer fades out over 2 s).
7. Restart: toggle things back, or leave and re-open (new random animals).
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Windows | 4 buttons (`WINDOWS`) at board positions (140,165), (260,165), (140,235), (260,235); size 64 units. Each toggles between lit (target 1) and dim (target 0); fade time `LIGHT_S = 1.5` s. |
| Animals | 3 buttons in fixed slots (52,238), (200,240), (348,238); size 72 units. Each toggles between awake (0) and asleep (1); fade time `SLEEP_S = 1.2` s with smoothstep easing; the open eyes fade out, the closed-eye arcs and a blanket fade in (the blanket also slides 10 units). |
| Night layer | Target is 1 only if every window target is 0 and every animal target is 1; otherwise 0. Fade in `GLOW_IN_S = 4` s, out `GLOW_OUT_S = 2` s, smoothstep. The layer holds a translucent blue overlay (opacity 0.38), 10 stars (radius 1.4 to 2.2 units) and a sleeping crescent moon. |
| Reversibility | A toggle mid-fade reverses from the current value, not from the end. |
| Automatic actions | None: only the child's taps change anything. |
| Labels | Polish `aria-label`s are updated on each toggle ("Okno N – zgaś światło" / "zapal światło"; "<animal> – obudź" / "połóż spać"). |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (a tap changes light and sleep state).
- A calm routine-themed play ("everything goes to sleep").
- Noticing a whole-scene goal made of several parts (all windows and all animals).

**Directly observable behavior**

- Every change is slow and reversible; the night layer appears only after every part is switched.
- No failure, score or text.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on bedtime routines or sleep. Nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** all 7 interactive elements are native `<button>`s using the `click` event, so touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space) work.
- **Target sizes:** windows are 16 % of the board width and animals 18 %, each with `min-width/min-height: 48px`. On a 4:3 board that is 64 and 72 board units; at a board width of 320 px a window is 51 px.
- **Layout:** the board is 4:3 (`aspect-ratio`), fitted into the viewport with top padding for the Back button; works in portrait and landscape.
- **State cues:** a lit window is yellow, a dim one is blue-grey (colour/brightness only; the mullions and frame are always visible); a sleeping animal shows closed-eye arcs and a coloured blanket (a shape cue besides colour). The ARIA labels announce the action, but the buttons have no `aria-pressed` state.
- **Reduced motion:** fades are driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (not CSS transitions), so they still run under the global reduced-motion rule.
- **Touch:** `touch-action: manipulation`, tap highlight removed.
- **Reading:** not required. A young child can use it independently.
- **Limitation:** hit areas of the middle animal and the two lower windows overlap slightly (see section 18).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The scene is dark and low-contrast by design (calming); the lit/dim difference of windows is subtle against the dusk house on some screens (requires verification).
- Relies on slow fades; with everything done there is no further activity, and the child must undo something to continue.
- No privacy concerns; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants at the top of [`js/dobranoc.js`](../../js/dobranoc.js).

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `LIGHT_S` | Window fade time | 1.5 s |
| `SLEEP_S` | Animal fade time | 1.2 s |
| `GLOW_IN_S`, `GLOW_OUT_S` | Night layer fade in / out | 4 s, 2 s |
| `WINDOWS` | Window centres in the 400x300 board | 4 positions |
| `WIN`, `ANI` | Button sizes in board units | 64, 72 |
| `SLOTS` | Animal slot positions and blanket colours (`#b9b3e0`, `#f7a8c9`, `#a9c9ef`) | 3 slots |
| `STARS` | Star positions and radii | 10 stars |

Fallback: none needed; the only dependency is `window.Animals`, which is not checked for being absent.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The house, sky gradient, windows, stars and moon are inline SVG (`sceneryHtml`, `windowSvg`, `glowSvg`); the animals are drawn by `window.Animals.head()` with `noEyes` plus the activity's own eyes and a body ellipse in the animal's fur colour (`js/animals.js`). No audio, images or fonts. The gradient id `db-sky` is defined in the inline SVG.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- On every launch `window.Animals.pick(3)` selects **3 unique animals** of the shared 13 and assigns them to the three fixed slots in the picked order. No `distinct` option, so similar silhouettes may appear together.
- Nothing is stored; there is no immediate-repetition guard between launches.
- Blanket colours, windows and stars are fixed.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels and nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- There is no formal completion state; the nearest equivalent is the "night" state (all lights off and all animals asleep), shown by the fading-in overlay with stars and a sleeping moon.
- No failure, score or sound. Any tap afterwards simply turns part of the scene back on, and the night layer fades out.
- No next round starts automatically.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/dobranoc.js`](../../js/dobranoc.js); the cleanup function cancels the frame, removes the `visibilitychange` and button listeners and removes the root element.
- **Rendering:** a `div.db-board` containing an SVG scene (`preserveAspectRatio="none"` inside a fixed 4:3 board), an SVG night layer in `.db-glow-wrap`, and 7 absolutely positioned buttons (percent-based `left`, `top`, `width`).
- **State:** `items[]` with `v` (progress 0 to 1), `t` (target 0 or 1), speed, `paint()` and `label()`; plus `glow` and `glowT`.
- **Loop:** `step()` moves each `v` towards `t` by `speed * dt` (`dt` capped at 0.05 s) and repaints; the loop stops itself when nothing is changing and is restarted by `kick()` on every tap. `visibilitychange` only resets the time base.
- **Events:** `click` on each button.
- **Shared code:** `Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`, `Animals.eyes`, `Animals.eyeColor`.
- **Persistence and analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The board is a fixed 400x300 coordinate system. Button positions are percentages (`x / 4`, `y / 3`, `size / 4`) of the board and are centred with `translate(-50%, -50%)`, so they always line up with the SVG scenery, which is stretched with the board.
- Board width is `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 4 / 3)`; the container has padding for the safe areas and 56 px at the top for the Back button.
- Portrait and landscape use the same layout (a smaller board in portrait).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Rapid repeated taps | Each tap flips the target; the progress reverses smoothly from where it is. |
| Tab hidden | The browser pauses `requestAnimationFrame`; `onVis` resets the time base so the hidden gap is not replayed. |
| Resize / orientation | Percent-based layout adjusts automatically; no JavaScript is needed. |
| Leaving mid-fade | Cleanup cancels the pending frame. |
| `window.Animals` missing | Not handled. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; four windows lit, three animals awake; tap each window; it dims over about 1.5 s; tap again; it relights.
- [ ] Tap each animal; it closes its eyes and a blanket appears; tap again; it wakes.
- [ ] Completion state: switch all 4 lights off and put all 3 animals to bed; stars and the moon fade in over about 4 s.
- [ ] Reversal: from the night state, wake one animal; the night layer fades out in about 2 s.
- [ ] Toggle quickly mid-fade; the animation reverses smoothly with no jump.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the house and sky (nothing happens).
- [ ] Restart/randomization: re-open the activity about 10 times; the three animals vary; none repeats within a scene.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate during a fade.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard (Tab to each of the 7 buttons, Enter/Space toggles, focus ring visible).
- [ ] Overlap: tap the strip between the lower windows and the middle animal; confirm which one reacts (see section 18).
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tab mid-fade; the animation continues without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion: the fades still run.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#43](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/43) reports a Node run against a DOM stub with a fake `requestAnimationFrame` (all 7 buttons present, tapping everything brings the glow to 1.0 within 4 s, undoing one light fades it to 0 and the loop stops, cleanup empties the container) and states that manual tests on devices were not possible. PR [#68](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/68) lists the moon crescent as needing device checks.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from the constants)**

- Hit boxes overlap: the middle animal spans x 164 to 236 and y 204 to 276 board units, while the lower windows span x 108 to 172 and x 228 to 292, y 203 to 267, so there are strips about 8 units wide where a tap lands on the animal (later in DOM order) instead of the window. The visible artwork inside the boxes may not overlap (requires verification).
- Buttons have no `aria-pressed`; state is only conveyed in the changing label.
- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Contrast of the lit versus dim window state on real devices.
- The moon crescent after the fix in #68 (listed as pending a device check there).

## 19. Planned improvements

`None currently planned`.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Night/calm activities: [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md), [Nocne Niebo](nocne-niebo.md).
- Activities using the same animal family: [Mały Pociąg](maly-pociag.md), [Zwierzątka na Farmie](zwierzatka-na-farmie.md), [Zabawa w Chowanego](zabawa-w-chowanego.md), [Cienie](cienie.md), [Buźki](buzki.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js). The activity does not use `js/random.js` directly (only through `Animals.pick`).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#34](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/34) / PR [#43](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/43): initial activity.
- Issue [#66](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/66) / PR [#68](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/68): moon redrawn as a single crescent path.
- Issue [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): the three animals are drawn at random from the shared family.
```
