## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/duze-i-male.md`

```markdown
# Duże i Małe

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Duże i Małe |
| Internal ID | `duze-i-male` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A big house and a small house are shown, with two big and two small animals waiting at the bottom. The child drags (or selects) each big animal to the big house and each small animal to the small house. |
| Category | Sorting / matching by size |
| Interaction type | Drag (pointer events); keyboard alternative (select an animal, then activate a house) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/duze-i-male.js`](../../js/duze-i-male.js), CSS block `/* Duże i Małe */` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (prefix `dm`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Introduces the concept of size (big and small) with a single, easily seen rule: big goes with big, small with small. Unlike the colour or shape sorting activities ([Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md), [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md)), the cue is size only, which is shown by the animals and the houses at the same time. It uses a "no wrong answers" model: an animal put in the wrong place gently floats back. Rounds repeat with different animals, so the activity can be replayed without becoming identical.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#duze-i-male`); `setRound()` and `layout()` run immediately.
2. A big house and a small house (in two different colours) stand side by side on the ground; four animals (two big, two small, of two animal types) wait in a row at the bottom in random order.
3. The child drags an animal. While dragging it follows the pointer and cannot leave the visible screen.
4. Released over its matching house, the animal glides into the house area and glows softly; released elsewhere (or over the other house) it glides back to its waiting place.
5. Placed animals stay in the house, are disabled (no longer draggable), and glow.
6. When all four are placed and idle, both houses glow (2 s); after 4 s the scene fades out (0.7 s), a new round with other animals is set up and fades in (0.7 s).
7. The cycle continues indefinitely; the houses keep the same colours for the whole visit.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (from `js/duze-i-male.js`) |
|---|---|
| Items per round | 4 animals: 2 big (size `B`) and 2 small (size `B / 2`); two animal types, each shown once big and once small |
| Correct target | Big animal -> big house, small animal -> small house (`it.house`) |
| Drop detection | Animal centre inside the house's box plus a 10% padding of the house width; if inside both, the nearer house centre wins |
| Wrong drop | Animal glides back to its resting spot |
| Glide duration | `min(1800, 800 + distance)` ms; 300 ms with reduced motion; 200 ms for re-layout glides |
| Glow | `GLOW_S = 2000` ms of house glow; `NEXT_S = 4000` ms until the next round; fade `FADE_MS = 700` ms each way |
| Input during fade or glow phases | New drags are ignored unless `phase === 'play'` and the animal is not already placed |
| Sound | None ([shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)) |

- Keyboard: Enter or Space on an animal (a `click` with `detail === 0`) selects it (`aria-pressed`, outline); activating a house then places it (correct house) or sends it home (wrong house).
- Placed animals are `disabled` and removed from the tab order (`tabIndex = -1`).
- The two animals of one pair sit left and right inside the house (offset `min(0.5 * size, 0.28 * house width)`).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (design intent, not measured):
- Comparing and sorting by size (big and small).
- Hand-eye coordination through dragging.
- Recognising animals and houses.

**Directly observable behavior:**
- The animal only stays when it is dropped at the matching house; otherwise it returns.
- Both houses glow when the round is complete, then a new set of animals appears.
- No scores, timers or error messages.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim that the activity teaches size concepts or has a developmental effect.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) with pointer capture and `touch-action: none`; keyboard alternative as above with a 4 px focus/selection outline (`#8f7fd1`).
- **Screen readers:** animals have Polish labels such as "Duży miś (Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz domek)"; houses are labelled "Duży domek" and "Mały domek"; `aria-pressed` shows the selection.
- **Target size:** big animals 96 to 180 px; small animals half of that (48 to 90 px); CSS minimum 48 px. Small animals therefore are 48 px on small screens, below the 56 px used by several other activities.
- **Orientation:** layout is computed in pixels from the field size (section 15) and re-run on `resize` and `orientationchange`; an active drag is cancelled and the animal returns home.
- **Size cue:** size, not colour, defines the correct house; house colours are decorative (two different colours per launch). Size is the only distinguishing cue, so a child who cannot judge relative size has no other hint.
- **Reduced motion:** glides, fades and glows are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with inline styles, so they still run under the global CSS rule; glides shorten to 300 ms. Fade between rounds still plays.
- **Reading:** none required; independent use is intended.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Small animals can be as small as 48 px; accidental misses are possible for small fingers (no penalty, they just return).
- The sorting rule is not announced or demonstrated; a child learns it by trying.
- Two different house colours but identical shapes: the houses differ only in size and colour (not a risk, but the house colour has no meaning).
- PR [#75](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/75) asked for close attention to small-landscape layouts such as 640x360.
- No privacy concerns; nothing stored or sent.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants are inside [`js/duze-i-male.js`](../../js/duze-i-male.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TYPES` | 8 animal drawings: id, Polish label, glow colour, SVG art (bear, rabbit, cat, duck, pig, mouse, frog, dog) | array | 8 entries | top of IIFE |
| `HOUSE_COLOURS` | 6 wall/roof/door/glow colour sets | array | 6 entries | top of IIFE |
| `GLOW_S` | Round-complete glow duration | ms | 2000 | top of IIFE |
| `NEXT_S` | Time from completion to the next round (fade starts) | ms | 4000 | top of IIFE |
| `FADE_MS` | Fade out and in duration | ms | 700 | top of IIFE |
| Layout numbers | Big size `B = clamp(min(0.28 fw, 0.2 fh), 96, 180)`, small `B / 2`, big house width `max(60, min(0.5 fw, ground))`, small house half of that, gap 6% of width | numbers | see `layout()` | `layout()` |

No fallback for invalid values because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Animals (`TYPES[].art`) and houses (`houseSvg`) are inline SVG strings drawn in the activity's own style; this activity does **not** use the shared animal family `js/animals.js`. Backgrounds are CSS gradients (`.dm` `#e6f2fb` to `#e2f3dc`; `.dm-glow` a radial yellow gradient). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, images or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | How | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| House colours | `Rand.pick(HOUSE_COLOURS, 2)`: two unique sets, first for the big house | 6 sets (30 ordered combinations) |
| Animal order for the visit | `Rand.shuffle` of the 8 animal types, once per launch | 8 types |
| Animals per round | Round `r` uses `pool[2r % 8]` and `pool[(2r+1) % 8]` | 4 rounds cover all 8 types, then the cycle repeats in the same order |
| Position of the four animals in the bottom row | `Rand.shuffle(order)` at every round | 4! orders |

- Immediate repetition: within the 4-round cycle no type repeats; the same two animals do not appear in consecutive rounds. The house colours are fixed for the visit.
- Nothing is stored; every time the activity is opened a new shuffle and colour pair are chosen (a fresh `mount`).
- There are no empty or invalid pools (fixed arrays).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. Every round has two big and two small animals; only the animal types change. Nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion: all four animals placed in their matching houses.
- Feedback: individual animals glow when placed; both houses plus a background radial glow when the round is complete.
- Failure: none; a wrong drop returns the animal. No sound.
- After about 4 s the next round starts automatically with a fade.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/duze-i-male.js`](../../js/duze-i-male.js), replacing `mount` of the `duze-i-male` registry entry; returns `cleanup`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `div.dm > div.dm-glow + div.dm-field`; the field holds 2 `button.dm-house` and 4 `button.dm-animal`, each with an inline SVG. Elements are moved with `transform: translate()`.
- **State:** per animal `{ big, k, type, x, y, hx/hy (home), tx/ty (target in house), sz, house, mode ('idle' | 'drag' | 'glide'), placed, glow }`; globals `round`, `pool`, `order`, `phase` (`play`, `out`, `in`), `doneT`, `doneGlow`, `fade`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown/move/up/cancel`, `lostpointercapture` per animal; `click` on animals (keyboard) and houses; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Animation:** one `frame()` loop (dt capped at 50 ms), smoothstep glides, which stops when idle and is restarted by `start()`; paused while the tab is hidden.
- **Randomization:** `window.Rand.pick` / `Rand.shuffle` (see section 10); `setRound()` assigns types and labels, `shuffleRest()` reshuffles the bottom row.
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js). **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** none from the activity itself (reported by `js/app.js`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the three listeners and removes the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.dm` is fixed full-screen; `.dm-field` is inset by the safe-area variables plus 64 px at the top and 12 px elsewhere. All positions are CSS pixels relative to the field.
- `layout()`: `B = max(96, min(180, min(0.28 fw, 0.2 fh)))`, `Sm = B / 2`; `ground = fh - 4 - B - 14` (the houses stand above the resting row); big house width `Hb = max(60, min(0.5 fw, ground))`, small house `Hb / 2`; the two houses are centred as a group with a gap of 6% of the width.
- The resting row is centred; gap between animals `clamp((0.96 fw - sum) / 3, 4, 28)`.
- Houses are square buttons whose SVG scales with them; animals and houses share the field's pixel coordinate space, so the drop test compares the animal centre with the house box directly.
- Resize or rotation recomputes everything; positions of placed animals are recomputed from their target positions.
- On very small fields the minimum sizes (96 px big animals, 60 px big house) take precedence over fitting, so content could overflow (requires verification).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | N/A (inline SVG); `Rand` is required and not guarded |
| Resize / rotation | `layout()` re-run; active drag cancelled and animal sent home |
| Backgrounding | Loop paused while hidden; completion timer only advances while visible |
| Multi-touch | Each animal tracks its own pointer; a second pointer on the same animal is ignored |
| Pointer cancel / lost capture | Treated as release (`up`) |
| Drop on the wrong house or between houses | Animal returns home |
| Dragging a placed animal | Not possible (button disabled) |
| Input during glow/fade | `down()` ignores input unless `phase === 'play'`; `onHouse` also checks the phase |
| Dragging outside the screen | Centre clamped to the visible window |
| Right mouse button | Ignored |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` cancels the frame |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#75](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/75) reports `node --check` only and lists browser tests as pending; PR [#144](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/144) reports `node --check`, a pool-size/unique-id check (8 animals, 6 colour sets) and that the new SVGs parse as XML, with no visual check. Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: drag a big animal to the big house; it settles inside and glows.
- [ ] Drag a small animal to the small house; same result.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: drop a big animal on the small house, and an animal on empty ground; it floats back each time.
- [ ] Completion: place all four; both houses glow, and after about 4 s a new round with different animals fades in.
- [ ] Restart: leave and reopen; house colours and animals differ (at least sometimes).
- [ ] Randomization: over four rounds the animal types do not repeat; the bottom-row order changes each round; two house colours always differ.
- [ ] Progression: confirm no difficulty change.
- [ ] Portrait (about 360x640): all items visible, small animals at least 48 px.
- [ ] Landscape (about 640x360): houses and the waiting row do not overlap or overflow.
- [ ] Touch: drag two animals at once with two fingers; rotate the device mid-drag.
- [ ] Mouse: left-button drag works; right button does nothing.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to an animal, Enter selects, Enter on a house places or returns it.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: glides are short, fades still run.
- [ ] Background the tab during the glow and return.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from code reading):**
- No automated tests.
- Small animals can be only 48 px, smaller than the 56 px used elsewhere.
- Animals and houses are drawn separately from the shared animal family, so the style differs from `js/animals.js` activities.
- Animal type order repeats identically after four rounds.

**Requires verification:**
- Layout on small landscape screens such as 640x360 (flagged in PR #75).
- Visual quality of the animal drawings added in PR #144 (no visual check was reported).

No open GitHub issue concerns this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Sorting/matching with the same "glow then new round" pattern: [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md), [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md), [Koraliki](koraliki.md).
- Shared helper used: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`, `Rand.shuffle`). [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) is **not** used.

## 21. Change history

- [#49](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/49) / [PR #75](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/75): activity introduced.
- [#120](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/120) / [PR #144](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/144): random animals (pool of 8) and house colours (6 sets); later `Rand.shuffle` for the animal row (commit `6d5e22d`).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/dzien-i-noc.md`

```markdown
# Dzień i Noc

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Dzień i Noc |
| Activity ID | `dzien-i-noc` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | Touching the sun slowly brings night with stars, touching the moon brings the day back, touching the sky sends a cloud drifting by. By day 2-3 birds cross the sky; at night a satellite or a plane sometimes drifts past and new stars slowly appear. |
| Category | Calming, observation, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap the sun/moon, tap the sky, tap a bird |
| Status | Implemented. Enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff` flag). |
| Source | [`js/dzien-i-noc.js`](../../js/dzien-i-noc.js), CSS classes `.dn`, `.dn-*` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A slow, predictable scene about the day-night cycle: one big button changes the whole sky with a smooth, unhurried transition. It supports calm, bedtime-like observation and has a very clear cause and effect relation (one touch, one gradual change). Compared with [Nocne Niebo](nocne-niebo.md) (connecting stars) and [Dobranoc](dobranoc.md) (a bedtime scene) it has no task, only a living sky with small optional surprises (birds, clouds, a passing plane or satellite).

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile (hash `#dzien-i-noc`); the scene starts in full day.
2. A light blue sky, three drifting clouds and a big sun (centre, 42 % from the top) are shown; after a moment 2-3 birds fly across.
3. The child can tap the sun, the sky or a bird.
4. Tapping the sun starts a 3.5 s transition to night: the sky darkens, the sun cross-fades into a smiling moon, stars appear, clouds fade and birds disappear. Tapping the moon reverses it. Tapping the sky adds a cloud; tapping a bird makes it fly a slow loop.
5. There is no completion state.
6. The activity keeps running and switching as often as the child wants.
7. There is no restart; the scene always begins as day.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Day/night transition | `TRANSITION_MS` = 3500 ms with smoothstep easing; 1200 ms (`REDUCED_MS`) under reduced motion; driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop that sets the CSS variable `--p` (0 = day, 1 = night) |
| Toggle target | `progress < 0.5` means day, so a tap goes to night (target 1); otherwise to day |
| Input lock | While the transition runs (`busy`), taps on the sun/moon **and on the sky** are ignored; bird taps still work |
| Sun/moon button | One `<button>`, size `clamp(150px, 38vmin, 320px)`, at 50 % / 42 %; its `aria-label` switches between "Słońce" and "Księżyc" at `progress >= 0.5` |
| Clouds | 3 ambient clouds are kept at all times (`AMBIENT`); max 7 in total (`MAX_CLOUDS`, oldest dropped); ambient speed 1.6-2.4 vw/s; removed beyond 105 vw; width 18-30 vmin; opacity falls from .95 to .40 as night comes |
| Cloud tap | Adds a cloud entering at -30 vw at the tapped height (y minus 8 %, clamped to 2-70 %) moving 3.2 vw/s |
| Birds | Flock of 2-3 (`flockSize`, chosen each launch), daytime only. Each crosses the screen in 20 s (+/- 15-25 %), in a lane that avoids the sun/moon box, with slow wing flapping (0.55-1 vertical scale, 1.2 flaps/s); when one leaves, the next enters after 0-1.5 s. The flock appears when day is fully reached (`progress < 0.05` and target day), and is removed once `progress >= 0.5` |
| Bird tap | A bird that is not already looping flies one 2.6 s loop away from the sun/moon; bird button at least 56 px (`clamp(56px, 9vmin, 72px)`) |
| Stars | 100 fixed stars (seeded generator, same layout each visit; 10 % bright 3-4 px, others 1.4-2.7 px, opacity 0.4-0.8) in the top 60 % of the screen; a new star is added every 15-30 s up to `STAR_CAP` = 160 and grows from 1 px in 8 s (`STAR_GROW_SECONDS`); they exist (hidden) by day too |
| Night flyer | At most one; only when night is reached (`progress >= 0.95`, target night), every 20-45 s; 50 % a steady white satellite (18 s crossing), 50 % a grey airplane dot with a red pulse (12 s crossing, 0.7 s cosine pulse); not touchable; removed when day returns |
| Scoring / failure | None |

Reduced motion: transition and bird/flyer/star motion are rAF-driven and still run (the transition is shortened to 1.2 s). Ambient clouds are **not** animated: the three initial clouds stay still, no new ones are generated, and a tap on the sky creates a static cloud that disappears after 6 s.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (touch the sun, the sky changes).
- Calm observation; the idea that day and night alternate.
- Spotting small events (a bird, a satellite or plane) in a quiet scene.

**Directly observable behavior**

- A 3.5 s smooth change between a day and a night scene with a sun/moon swap.
- Birds, clouds, stars and passing objects keep the scene alive without requiring input.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on bedtime routine, calming or understanding of time. None is measured or claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer (touch, mouse, stylus) via `pointerdown`; **keyboard** for the sun/moon button and birds through `click` events with `detail === 0` (Enter/Space). Clouds can only be added by pointer.
- **Screen readers:** the sun/moon button changes its label; birds are labelled "Ptaszek". Stars, clouds and the night flyer are hidden from assistive technology.
- **Layout:** full-screen, percent and viewport-unit based, works in portrait and landscape.
- **Targets:** sun/moon at least 150 px; birds at least 56 px; the sky is a large target.
- **Colour:** day and night are distinguished by brightness and the sun/moon icon shape, not hue alone.
- **Flashing:** the plane's red pulse is a smooth cosine with a period of 0.7 s (about 1.4 Hz) on a 3.5 px dot, below the usual 3 Hz flash threshold.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required. Independent use by a young child is possible.
- **Reduced motion:** see section 4; clouds do not drift.
- **Limitations:** the sun/moon button does not expose a pressed state; sky taps are ignored during the transition.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Night is dark (dark blue); a child may find the screen dim at bedtime, and a parent may prefer lower device brightness. Not a medical claim.
- No ending, so the playtime limit is the only stop (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).
- Stars keep being added while the activity stays open (up to 60 extra), so the night sky is slightly different after a long visit.
- Birds are hidden at night, so a child who touches the moon just after day returns may wait several seconds for birds.
- In very short landscape windows the bird lanes can collapse (computed: 640x360 leaves one lane of about 30 px at the bottom), so birds may overlap one another (requires verification in a browser).
- No personal data is involved.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/dzien-i-noc.js`](../../js/dzien-i-noc.js); layout and colours in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css).

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_CLOUDS`, `AMBIENT` | Cloud limits | 7, 3 |
| `TRANSITION_MS`, `REDUCED_MS` | Transition length | 3500, 1200 |
| `BIRD_SECONDS`, `LOOP_SECONDS` | Bird crossing and loop duration | 20, 2.6 |
| `STAR_ADD_MIN`, `STAR_ADD_MAX`, `STAR_GROW_SECONDS`, `STAR_CAP` | New-star interval (s), growth time, total cap | 15, 30, 8, 160 |
| `FLY_MIN`, `FLY_MAX`, `SAT_SECONDS`, `PLANE_SECONDS`, `BLINK_SECONDS` | Night flyer interval, crossing times and pulse | 20, 45, 18, 12, 0.7 |
| `flockSize` | Birds per launch | 2-3 (local variable) |
| Star seed | Fixed layout of the first 100 stars | 7 (`makeStars`) |

No fallback is needed because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external assets. Sun, moon, birds and clouds are inline SVG strings in the JS file; stars and the night flyer are CSS-styled elements. The menu icon is inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Flock size | Each launch | 2 or 3 uniformly (`Math.random`) |
| Bird direction, lane, speed (+/- 15-25 %), phase | Each bird spawn | Uniform |
| Respawn delay | When a bird leaves | 0-1.5 s |
| Cloud heights, widths, speeds, respawn offset | Each cloud | Ranges in section 4 |
| Added stars (position, size class, opacity) | Every 15-30 s | Uniform; about 10 % bright, about 25 % stay at 1 px, the rest 1.4-2.7 px |
| Night flyer type, direction, height (4-44 %), slope (+/- 6 %) and wait | Per flyer | 50 / 50 satellite or plane |
| Initial 100 stars | Never | Fixed seed (same every launch) |

It uses `Math.random` directly, not [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js); there is no "no immediate repeat" logic and nothing is stored.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. The only slow change is the growing number of stars (100 to at most 160) during a long visit; nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is the transition itself, a cloud appearing under a sky tap and a bird's loop. No sound and no celebration.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/dzien-i-noc.js`](../../js/dzien-i-noc.js).
- **Rendering:** DOM. `div.dn` with `.dn-night` (overlay whose opacity is `--p`), `.dn-stars`, `.dn-clouds`, the sun/moon button and bird buttons. Sun and moon are two SVG groups cross-faded by `--p`.
- **State:** `progress`, `target`, `busy`, `clouds`, `birds`, `respawn`, `growing`, `flyer`, `timers`.
- **Loops:** `step` (transition, started only on a toggle) and `cloudTick` (clouds, birds, flyer, stars; always running). Both stop when the tab is hidden; on return the clocks are reset and a toggle in progress resumes. `dt` is clamped (100 ms).
- **Events:** `pointerdown` and `click` on the scene (delegated), `visibilitychange` (also toggles `.paused`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels both frames, clears timers, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Dependencies:** none (does not use `Rand` or `Animals`).
- **Why rAF:** the transition and all motion are JavaScript-driven so they survive the global reduced-motion CSS rule.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

The scene is full-viewport. Most elements use percent or `vw`/`vmin` units: clouds translate in `vw`, star and flyer positions are percent (stars within the top 60 % of the screen), the sun/moon sits at 42 % height and scales with `vmin`. Birds are positioned in pixels per frame from the scene's client size. The bird lane calculation reserves the sun/moon box (same size formula, centred at 42 % height) so birds fly above or below it. There is no fixed aspect ratio.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Resize / rotation | Positions are recomputed from the current size each frame (birds) or are percent-based |
| Backgrounding | Both loops stop; the transition resumes with its progress kept |
| Rapid taps | Taps during a transition are ignored; clouds capped at 7 |
| Tap on the sun and moon at the same time | Not possible (one button) |
| Leaving mid-transition | Frames and timers cancelled |
| No room for bird lanes | Falls back to the top margin (birds may overlap the sun/moon in tiny viewports; requires verification) |
| Touch cancellation | `pointerdown` is used, so nothing is left pending |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#135](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/135) reports `node --check` and a numeric check of the bird lane geometry for 4 portrait and landscape sizes (0 overlaps with the sun/moon box) and notes that no browser was available, so a visual check on a device was recommended.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: tap the sun; the sky darkens over about 3.5 s, stars appear, the sun becomes a moon; tap the moon; day returns.
- [ ] Taps on the sun/moon and sky during the transition are ignored; bird taps still loop.
- [ ] Sky tap by day and at night adds a cloud that drifts across and leaves.
- [ ] Birds: 2-3 appear after day is reached; none overlap the sun; touching one makes a slow loop; they vanish when night begins.
- [ ] Night: wait 20-45 s after night is reached; a satellite or plane crosses; the plane's red pulse is calm.
- [ ] Wait 60 s: new stars appear one by one and grow.
- [ ] Restart: reopen; scene starts as day, the flock size varies between launches.
- [ ] Progression: none expected.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape (320x568, 360x640, 640x360, 1024x768): sun/moon centred, birds avoid it, nothing is cut off.
- [ ] Touch, mouse; keyboard (Tab to sun/moon and birds, Enter/Space).
- [ ] Background/foreground during the transition; it resumes smoothly.
- [ ] Reduced motion: transition about 1.2 s, clouds static, sky tap creates a static cloud that disappears after 6 s, birds still fly.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- The flock was reduced from 7-9 to 2-3 birds (fixed on `main`: item 3 of issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)); no flock-size limitation remains.
- Sky taps cannot add clouds by keyboard.
- Initial stars use no centring transform whereas added stars do (a sub-pixel inconsistency).
- The sun/moon button has no pressed state for assistive technology.
- Uses `Math.random` instead of the shared helper; no repeat avoidance.

**Requires verification**

- Bird lanes in very short landscape viewports (see section 7).
- Performance with up to 7 clouds, 3 birds and 160 stars on slow devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (the smaller flock from issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), item 3, is done, see section 21).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Nocne Niebo](nocne-niebo.md), [Dobranoc](dobranoc.md), [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md) (day/night weather), [Deszczyk i Tęcza](deszczyk-i-tecza.md).
- Pattern: a single rAF loop that writes a CSS custom property (`--p`) so motion survives the reduced-motion rule.
- Does not use [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) or [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#6](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/6) / PR [#13](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/13): initial activity; keyboard activation of the sun/moon added after review.
- Issue [#21](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/21): app review polish.
- Human requests on the PR: slowly growing stars, removed Big Dipper constellation, occasional satellite and plane.
- Issue [#111](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/111) / PR [#135](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/135): grey plane with red pulse, steady satellite, daytime bird flock.
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): daytime flock reduced from 7-9 to 2-3 birds.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/gdzie-jest-pilka.md`

```markdown
# Gdzie jest Piłka?

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Gdzie jest Piłka? |
| Internal ID | `pilka` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A ball, an open box on a table and a small bunny; the child moves the ball to four marked places (in, on, under, next to the box) and the bunny reacts. |
| Category | Exploratory (spatial concepts), cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap on a spot, or drag the ball; keyboard: Enter/Space on the ball |
| CSS prefix | `pk-` |
| Source | [`js/pilka.js`](../../js/pilka.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section `/* Gdzie jest Piłka? */`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default (no `defaultOff`). Listed 30th in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity introduces the position words in, on, under and next to through pictures only: the child sees the ball in four places relative to a box and a table, without any text. It is open-ended and failure-free (nothing is right or wrong), and it differs from the other activities by being about spatial relations rather than matching or counting. The bunny gives a small friendly reaction after each move.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#pilka`); one of six layouts is chosen at random (see section 10).
2. A 4:3 scene shows a wall, a table, an open cardboard box standing on the table, the pink ball on its start spot, four dashed marker circles with small symbols and the bunny near one edge.
3. The child can tap a marker (the ball moves there) or press the ball and drag it (on release it moves to the nearest marker).
4. The ball glides to the target; when it arrives, the bunny plays a reaction for about 2 s.
5. There is no completion state. Nothing happens by itself; the animation loop stops when idle.
6. Re-opening the activity chooses another layout (never the same as the previous launch).
7. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

Spots (scene units, scene 400 x 300; `cx` is the box centre of the chosen layout):

| Spot id | Polish label (aria) | Position | Symbol | Bunny reaction (2 s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | w pudełku | `(cx, 128)` | box with a dot inside | head tilts towards the box (14 deg) and body shifts 3 px |
| `on` | na pudełku | `(cx, 56)` | dot above a box | hops (up to 12 px, two hops) |
| `under` | pod stołem | `(cx, 240)` | dot below a line | crouches (4 px down, `scaleY` 0.92) and head tilts down (-16 deg) |
| `next` | obok pudełka | `(cx + side * 120, 156)` | dot beside a box | waves (arm rotates up to 30 deg, 3 cycles) |

Other rules:

- **Move:** the ball follows a critically damped spring (`OMEGA = 3.4`) towards the target, integrated in steps of at most 8 ms. Touching another spot mid-flight only changes the target, so the motion stays smooth. Arrival is declared when the distance is below 0.4 units and the speed below 1.5.
- **Drag:** pointer capture; the ball position is clamped to x 34..366 and y 34..280 scene units. On release `goTo(nearest spot)` runs, so the ball never stays between spots.
- **Same spot:** tapping the spot the ball is already on, or releasing the ball nearest to it, counts as an arrival, so the bunny reacts again.
- **During a drag:** taps on spots are ignored (`goTo` returns while a drag is active).
- **Bunny placement:** at `(34, 240)` when `cx >= 200`, otherwise at `(366, 240)`; the bunny does not receive input (`pointer-events: none`).
- **Reduced motion:** the ball does not glide; it fades out in 0.15 s, jumps to the target and fades in over 0.15 s (`FADE_S`); the bunny's reaction movement is skipped, although the 2 s reaction state still runs.
- Nothing is scored; there are no wrong places.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (not measured)

- Understanding positional concepts (in, on, under, next to) through pictures.
- Hand-eye coordination (drag) and cause and effect (tap, ball moves, bunny reacts).
- Calm independent exploration.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Each of the four places has its own marker symbol and its own bunny reaction.
- The same four places are available in every layout; only the box position, the side of "next to", the colours and the start place change.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Whether the activity improves understanding of spatial words. The activity contains no spoken or written words, so any link to language learning would depend on the parent.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus (pointer events); the four spots are `<button>`s with `aria-label` `Miejsce: <label>`; the ball is a button labelled `Piłka (Enter lub spacja: następne miejsce; przeciągnij na miejsce)`. Enter/Space on the ball (click with `detail === 0`) moves it to the next spot in the order in, on, under, next.
- **Target size:** spots 18% of the scene width and the ball 17.5%, each at least 56 x 56 px. Spot centres are 72 scene units apart for in/on, so markers do not overlap.
- **Orientation:** the scene keeps a 4:3 aspect (`w = max(240, min(fieldWidth, fieldHeight * 4/3))`) and is centred; it works in portrait and landscape, but on a narrow portrait screen it is small (width roughly the screen width).
- **Colour:** each spot has a different symbol, so place meaning does not depend on colour.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required (no text in the scene).
- **Reduced motion:** see section 4; motion is JS-driven, so the global CSS rule does not affect it.
- **Touch behaviour:** the ball has `touch-action: none` (dragging); the rest uses `touch-action: manipulation`.
- **Focus:** 4 px outline `#8f7fd1` on the spots and the ball.
- **Limitations:** the ball can be moved with the keyboard only in a fixed cycle; the bunny reactions are not announced to assistive technology.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The scene is a fixed small picture on narrow phones in portrait (the 4:3 scene is limited by width), so touch targets are near the 56 px minimum.
- The symbols in the dashed markers are abstract; a child may not link them to the words on their own (words are for the parent to say).
- Without any goal the activity may hold attention only briefly.
- No personal data is collected.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/pilka.js`](../../js/pilka.js):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `W`, `H` | Scene units | numbers | `400`, `300` |
| `LAYOUTS` | Six layouts (`cx`, `side`, `start`, `wall`, `top`, `leg`, `floor`) | array | see section 10 |
| `LABELS` | Polish labels of the spots | object | in/on/under/next |
| `OMEGA` | Spring stiffness (about 1.5 s to settle) | rad/s | `3.4` |
| `REACT_S` | Bunny reaction length | s | `2` |
| `FADE_S` | Reduced-motion fade half-time | s | `0.15` |
| `STROKE` | Marker colour | CSS colour | `#8f7fd1` |

No fallback for invalid values (nothing is read from outside). If `window.Rand` were missing, `LAYOUTS[0]` is used.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The scene (`sceneFor`), ball (`BALL`), bunny (`BUNNY`, 64 x 68 viewBox) and marker symbols (`SYMBOLS`) are inline SVG strings built in JavaScript. The background colours come from the chosen layout. The bunny is hand-drawn in this file, not the shared `Animals` family. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No unused assets.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **What is random:** one of six predefined layouts per launch: `Rand.pickOne(LAYOUTS, 'pilka')`, which never returns the layout used on the previous launch in the same page session (pools of 2 or more).
- **Layouts:**

| # | `cx` | `side` (next to) | Ball starts at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200 | +1 (right) | in | |
| 2 | 200 | -1 (left) | on | |
| 3 | 150 | +1 | next | |
| 4 | 250 | -1 | under | |
| 5 | 175 | +1 | under | |
| 6 | 225 | -1 | in | |

  Each layout has its own wall, table top, table leg and floor colours. The bunny stands on the left when `cx >= 200`, otherwise on the right.
- **Persistence:** none; the "last pick" memory of `Rand` lasts only for the page session.
- **Within a session:** the layout does not change while the activity is open.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels and nothing is stored.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is the ball's movement and the bunny's 2 s reaction on arrival. There is no score, sound or failure feedback. The interaction cycle is: choose a place -> ball moves -> bunny reacts -> idle.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/pilka.js`](../../js/pilka.js), registered on the `pilka` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **State:** `spot` (current spot index), ball position `x, y` and velocity `vx, vy`, target `tx, ty`, flags `moving`, `dragPid`, `react` (`{t, type}`), `fade` (reduced-motion cross-fade) and opacity `op`.
- **Rendering:** a `.pk-board` div sized in pixels holds a background SVG, four spot buttons, the bunny and the ball button, all positioned with percentages of the 400 x 300 scene (`pct(x, y)`). The bunny's parts (`pk-all`, `pk-head`, `pk-arm`) are animated through inline CSS `transform`.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop (`frame`, `dt` capped at 50 ms) that continues only while the ball is moving or the bunny reacts, and is cancelled when the tab is hidden and restarted on return.
- **Events:** `click` on spots; `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel`/`lostpointercapture` and `click` (keyboard) on the ball; `resize`/`orientationchange`.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.pickOne` ([`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)).
- **Persistence/analytics:** none.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the three listeners and the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Scene coordinate system: 400 x 300 units (`W`, `H`), SVG `viewBox 0 0 400 300` with `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"`. Spots, ball and bunny are HTML elements placed with `left/top` percentages of the board, so they stay locked to the artwork at every size.
- The board size is `w = max(240, min(fieldWidth, fieldHeight * 400/300))` by `w * 3/4`; the field is the screen minus 64 px at the top and 12 px on the other sides (plus safe areas).
- Pointer positions are converted with `toScene` (client rect to scene units), so dragging works at any scale.
- Ball/spot sizes are percentages of the board width with a 56 px minimum.
- If the field is narrower than 240 px the board is wider than the field (the `.pk` container clips overflow); `Requires verification`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable. |
| Missing `Rand` | Falls back to the first layout. |
| Redirect during a glide | Smoothly redirected (spring keeps velocity). |
| Drag started during a glide or reaction | Glide stops, the reaction is cancelled, the ball is picked up. |
| Resize/orientation change | `layout` resizes the board; scene units keep positions consistent. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted. |
| Pointer cancel / lost capture | Treated as release: the ball goes to the nearest spot. |
| Second pointer on the ball during a drag | Ignored (`dragPid !== null`). |
| Mouse buttons other than the primary | Ignored on pointer down. |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | `reduced()` is `false`. |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#85](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/85) reports a stub run checking per-frame step size after a redirect; PR [#152](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/152) reports a numeric check of the layouts. These are not re-verified here.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: tap each of the four markers and confirm the ball moves there and the bunny reacts as listed in section 4.
- [ ] Redirect: tap another marker while the ball is moving; the motion stays smooth.
- [ ] Drag: drag the ball between markers and onto empty space; it settles on the nearest marker; drag off the edge of the scene.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the ball, the bunny and the empty scene; nothing breaks.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: re-open the activity at least 6 times; layouts vary and the same one never appears twice in a row; the bunny and the "next to" marker are on sensible sides.
- [ ] Completion/progression: confirm there is no end state or level.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: 320 x 568, 568 x 320, tablet; markers and ball at least 56 px; rotate while the ball is moving.
- [ ] Touch and mouse: finger drag, mouse drag, keyboard Enter/Space on the ball and Tab through markers.
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab during a glide and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion: the ball fades instead of gliding.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- Tapping the current spot replays the bunny reaction (no "already here" state).
- Bunny reactions are not exposed to assistive technology.

**Requires verification**

- Usability of the 4:3 scene on narrow portrait phones.
- Overlap between the bunny and the "next to" marker in some layouts (PR [#152](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/152) reports a numeric check that the bunny stays outside the spots).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.
- No related activity documents are linked: the spring-style motion is implemented locally in this file.

## 21. Change history

- [#59](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/59) / PR [#85](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/85): activity added.
- [#126](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/126) / PR [#152](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/152): six random layouts per launch.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/hustawka.md`

```markdown
# Huśtawka

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Huśtawka |
| Activity ID | `hustawka` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A pastel garden with a big tree, grass and a swing hanging from a branch with a random animal sitting on it. Touching the swing or the animal pushes it gently. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, calm observation |
| Interaction type | Tap (swing seat, animal, tree) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |

Source: [`js/hustawka.js`](../../js/hustawka.js), CSS prefix `hs-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html). Introduced by issue #98 / PR [#161](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/161).

## 2. Business purpose

- A very simple cause-and-effect scene: each touch gives one small push, and repeated touches build up a slightly higher swing that settles by itself.
- The swing follows a slow pendulum (one swing takes 3.6 s), never jerks and is capped at 35 degrees, which keeps the motion calm.
- Complements [Karuzela](karuzela.md) and [Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md) in the playground group; it is the only one of the three whose motion decays by itself.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; `mount(container)` builds the scene.
2. The swing hangs at rest from the tree branch with one random animal on it.
3. The child can touch the swing seat, the animal, or the tree.
4. Seat or animal: one push (the animal also waves). Tree: the crown sways once.
5. There is no completion state; the swing returns to rest by itself about 14-15 s after the last push.
6. The child can push again at any time, also while it is swinging.
7. A new scene and a new random animal are created each time the activity is opened.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Push (seat or animal click) | `target` amplitude increases by `STEP` = 8 degrees, capped at `MAX_AMP` = 35 degrees. A push from complete rest resets the phase to 0, so the swing starts from the centre. |
| Amplitude | `target` drains at `DRAIN` = 2.7 degrees per second; the real amplitude `amp` eases toward it with rate `EASE` = 2 per second, so changes are smooth. |
| Swing angle | `theta = amp * sin(phase)`, `phase` advances by `OMEGA` = 2π / 3.6 per second (period `PERIOD` = 3.6 s). |
| Rest | When `amp < 0.08` and `target <= 0`: `amp`, `theta` and `phase` are zeroed and the loop stops when nothing else is animating. |
| Wave | A push through the animal sets a wave timer of `WAVE_T` = 1.6 s (raised paw moves up to 22 units and wiggles). A push through the seat does not wave. |
| Tree | Click on the tree button: the crown rotates up to 2.2 degrees about (93, 160) over `SWAY_T` = 2.6 s. Does not affect the swing. |
| Leaves | While `amp > LEAF_AMP` = 20 degrees, a pooled leaf is released at most every `LEAF_GAP` = 0.9 s, with at most `MAX_LEAVES` = 6 visible at once. Each leaf falls for 5-7 s with a sideways sway and rotation, fades in over 0.6 s and out over the last 1.2 s, then is hidden and reused. |

- No sound, scoring or failure state.
- Pushes made quickly are all accepted (no rate limit); the amplitude cap prevents runaway motion.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect: a touch gives a push that visibly lasts and fades.
- Calm observation of a slow pendulum and drifting leaves.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Several pushes in a row make the swing swing a bit higher (maximum 35 degrees).
- Without pushes the swing slowly settles to rest.
- Leaves appear only at larger amplitudes.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on rhythm perception, attention or calm is not established by the code and is not claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** `click` on `<button>` elements, so touch, mouse, stylus and keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space) work. No gestures.
- **Targets:** seat button `max(56, 100k)` x `max(56, 50k)` px; animal button `max(56, 60k)` x `max(56, 80k)` px; the tree button covers about 176 x 248 board units.
- **Labels:** "Huśtawka – pchnij" (seat), "<animal name> – pchnij i pomachaj", "Drzewo – pokołysz"; decorative SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible` outline 4px `#8f7fd1`.
- **Orientation:** the board has a fixed 400:300 aspect ratio, sized `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 400/300)`; works in portrait (smaller) and landscape.
- **Colour:** meaning is not carried by colour.
- **Reduced motion:** the swing, leaves, wave and sway are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop and therefore continue under the global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule; the activity has no separate reduced-motion variant (motion is slow and amplitude-limited).
- **Reading:** none required; a young child can use it independently.
- **Limitation:** the tree is a large invisible button over the left half of the scene, so a tap anywhere over the tree (including its crown and trunk) sways it; there is no visual hint that it is touchable.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Leaves have a fixed 18 px size (not scaled with the board).
- The ropes are a separate SVG layer (`.hs-ropes`) drawn from JavaScript each frame; their tops stay at fixed points on the branch and only the lower ends move with the seat.
- Visual check in a real browser is not documented.
- Random leaf placement uses `Math.random` and is not reproducible; this has no functional effect.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in [`js/hustawka.js`](../../js/hustawka.js) and require a code change. Nothing is stored; no fallback logic.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BW` x `BH` | 400 x 300 | Board units |
| `PX`, `PY`, `ROPE`, `ROPE_X` | 260, 112, 118, 26 | Pivot position, rope length and horizontal rope offset from the pivot (units) |
| `PERIOD` | 3.6 s | Swing period |
| `MAX_AMP`, `STEP` | 35, 8 degrees | Maximum amplitude, increment per push |
| `DRAIN`, `EASE` | 2.7 degrees/s, 2 per s | Target decay, amplitude easing rate |
| `LEAF_AMP`, `MAX_LEAVES`, `LEAF_GAP` | 20 degrees, 6, 0.9 s | Leaf threshold, pool size, spawn gap |
| `SWAY_T`, `WAVE_T` | 2.6 s, 1.6 s | Tree sway and wave durations |
| `MAX_DT` | 0.05 s | Frame time cap |
| `LEAF_COLS` | 6 colours | One fixed colour per pooled leaf |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Background (sky, cloud, hills, grass, tree trunk, branch), tree crown, seat SVG, rope SVG and leaves are inline SVG built in `scene()`, `crown()`, `swingSvg()`, the `.hs-ropes` markup in `mount()` and `leafSvg()`. The animal is built from `Animals.head(id, { body: true })` in `figure()`. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- One animal is chosen with `Animals.pick(1)[0]` on every `mount` (13 animals, uniform; see [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) and [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)). Not persisted; the same animal can come up twice in a row.
- Leaf parameters are random per leaf: start x 40-160, start y 70-120, duration 5-7 s, drift 10-36, sway 8-16, rotation 40-120 degrees. The pool has 6 elements, each with a fixed colour.
- Nothing else is random.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression or levels. The amplitude is a transient state only and is not stored.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- No completion state; open-ended.
- Feedback is visual only: swing motion, wave, tree sway, falling leaves.
- No failure; no sound; nothing starts automatically.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` assigned to the registry entry `hustawka`; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `.hs-board` with a background SVG (`viewBox 0 0 400 300`, including the crown group `.hs-crown`), a tree button, six pooled leaf spans and a fixed rope layer `.hs-ropes` (two lines `.hs-rl`/`.hs-rr` and two knobs at x = 260 +/- 26, y = 115) and one `.hs-swing` wrapper (seat SVG, seat button, animal button) that is rotated by CSS `transform: rotate()` about its top centre. In `paint()` the lower rope ends are set to the rotated seat positions (same pivot and angle), so the rope tops never move.
- **State:** `amp`, `target`, `phase`, `theta`, `swayT`, `waveT`, `sinceLeaf`, `leaves[]`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`/`paint`), capped dt, stops itself when idle and is restarted by `start()` on a touch; paused while the tab is hidden.
- **Events:** `click` on the seat, animal and tree buttons; `resize`/`orientationchange` call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the window/document listeners and removes the root node.
- **Dependencies:** `window.Animals`. No persistence or analytics integration. See [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board 400 x 300 units, scale `k = board.clientWidth / 400`.
- The swing wrapper is `max(56, 100k)` px wide, centred on the pivot (260, 112) units, and `(118 + 12) * k` px high; the seat SVG inside is 100 units wide.
- The animal button is anchored to the seat position (bottom at `ROPE * k + 6k`), the seat button is centred on the seat line.
- Leaves are positioned in board units times `k` in the board's pixel space; their 18 px size is not scaled.
- The tree button spans x 12-188, y 14-262 units, matching the drawn tree.
- On resize or orientation change `layout()` recomputes sizes; the swing continues from its current angle.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/orientation change: handled by `layout()`; motion state is kept.
- Backgrounding: loop paused while hidden and resumed with a fresh `last`; dt capped at 0.05 s.
- Rapid repeated pushes: bounded by the 35 degree cap; leaves are bounded by the 6-element pool.
- Push at rest: the phase is reset to 0 so the swing starts smoothly from the centre.
- Missing assets / empty pools: not applicable (inline SVG).
- Unsupported features: none specific; uses CSS transforms, SVG and `requestAnimationFrame`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#161](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/161) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation (12 pushes: maximum 34.1 degrees, at most 6 leaves, at most 1 degree per frame, back to rest and loop stopped about 14 s after the last push) and states that no browser was available.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: touch the seat once; the swing moves slowly, with one swing taking about 3.6 s, and settles after about 14-15 s.
- [ ] Touch the animal; it waves and the swing is pushed.
- [ ] Repeated pushes: tap about 6 times quickly; the swing rises but not above about 35 degrees and leaves begin to fall.
- [ ] Touch the tree; the crown sways once and the swing is unaffected.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no end state; the swing returns to rest on its own.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the sky or grass; nothing happens.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and re-enter; the swing is at rest, usually with a different animal.
- [ ] Randomization: enter several times; the animal varies; falling leaves differ in path.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate while swinging; the scene stays on screen and the swing continues.
- [ ] Highest amplitude: the rope tops stay on the branch and only the lower ends move with the seat.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard Tab and Enter/Space on seat, animal and tree.
- [ ] Background the tab while swinging and return; no jump.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: the swing and leaves still move.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; no documented real-device verification.
- Leaf size is fixed at 18 px.

**Requires verification**

- Appearance of the rope/branch attachment at the highest amplitude on real devices (fixed rope tops are implemented, but no real-device check is documented).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar scenes: [Karuzela](karuzela.md), [Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md), [Latawiec](latawiec.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`), which uses [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js). The animal sprite builder `figure()` is duplicated in `zjezdzalnia.js` and `hustawka.js`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue #98, PR [#161](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/161): activity added (commit ad2ff47).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) (closed) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173) (merged): ropes anchored at fixed points on the branch with only the lower end moving (`ROPE_X`, `.hs-ropes`).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/kapiel-zwierzatek.md`

```markdown
# Kąpiel Zwierzątek

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Kąpiel Zwierzątek |
| Internal ID | `kapiel` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | An animal spa in three gentle finger-drag stages: scrub off the mud, wash off the foam with a shower, then towel-dry the damp animal until the fur is fluffy. |
| Category | Cause and effect, open-ended play (gentle care) |
| Interaction type | Drag (rubbing); keyboard alternative: arrow keys and Enter/Space |
| CSS prefix | `kp-` |
| Source | [`js/kapiel.js`](../../js/kapiel.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section `/* Kąpiel Zwierzątek */`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default (appended last in the menu, no `defaultOff`). Listed 46th in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity offers a calm caring task with a clear, satisfying result: a muddy animal becomes clean, dry and fluffy and gets a small accessory. Rubbing with a finger is a very natural gesture for young children, nothing can go wrong and there is no text, score or failure. It differs from [Buźki](buzki.md) and [Cienie](cienie.md), which also use the shared animal family, by being a sequential three-stage task driven by continuous dragging.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#kapiel`); a random animal appears covered in brown mud (stage 1).
2. The child drags a finger over the animal. The mud is erased where the finger passes and soap bubbles rise from the finger.
3. When about 90% of the mud is gone, the rest fades by itself (0.5 s).
4. Stage 2: the animal is covered in white foam (fades in over 0.7 s). Dragging moves a shower stream that washes the foam off; droplets fall.
5. Stage 3: the animal is damp (slightly darker, with droplets) (fades in over 0.7 s). Dragging rubs it dry; a soft fur-coloured halo grows as it dries (the fur gets fluffy).
6. When the third stage is cleaned, a random accessory (bow, party hat, crown, flower, bow tie or star) fades in and the animal glows for about 3 s.
7. About 7 s after the third stage finished, the animal fades out (0.7 s), a new random animal fades in (0.7 s) and stage 1 starts again.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (constant) |
|---|---|
| Stages (internal `stage`) | 0 mud, 1 foam, 2 damp |
| Stage completion | `DONE_AT = 0.9`: the share of the stage layer removed (measured on a 32 x 42 downscaled copy of the layer) |
| Check frequency | every 0.12 s while the layer has changed |
| Rest fade | `REST_S = 0.5` s (instant under reduced motion) |
| Next layer fade-in | `IN_S = 0.7` s |
| Completion glow | `GLOW_S = 3` s; accessory fade-in `IN_S = 0.7` s |
| New animal | `NEXT_AT_S = 7` s after the last stage; `SWAP_S = 0.7` s fade out and in |
| Brush width (fraction of the animal box width) | `BRUSH = [0.11, 0.2, 0.17]`, never less than 44 CSS px |
| Bubbles/droplets | at most `MAX_BUBBLES = 28` pooled DOM nodes, life `BUBBLE_S = 1.6` s, one spawn per `SPAWN_GAP_S = 0.09` s |
| Stage 1 | rising bubbles (radius 0.03 to 0.07 of the stage width); a shower stream (`kp-shower`) is not shown |
| Stage 2 | shower stream from the top edge to the finger, falling droplets (radius 0.012 to 0.022); 6 extra bubbles when a stage ends |
| Stage 3 | the halo opacity equals the cleaned fraction; set to 1 when the stage ends |
| Input accepted | only in phase `play`; several pointers can rub at once |

The layer for each stage is a canvas of 256 x 336 logical pixels, clipped to the animal's silhouette: mud `#b99a7a` (46 random dirt blobs), foam `#ffffff` (46 bubbles with outlines), damp `#7c8fb8` at 38% opacity (70 small droplets). Erasing uses `destination-out` strokes. The blobs are placed with `Math.random`, so the pattern is different each time.

Keyboard: the animal box is focusable (`role="application"`); when focused a brush ring appears. Arrow keys move the brush by 0.07 of the box (position clamped to x 0.06 to 0.94, y 0.05 to 0.95) and erase along the move; Enter or Space advance the brush in a zig-zag (horizontal steps, 0.1 down at each edge, wrapping at the bottom).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (not measured)

- Practice of controlled, continuous finger movement (rubbing) and hand-eye coordination.
- Understanding a sequence of care steps (dirty, soapy, wet, dry).
- Cause and effect with immediate visual feedback.
- Calm, independent play.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Each stage visibly changes as the child rubs; the next stage starts automatically.
- The final state includes a glow and an accessory; nothing can fail.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on motor skills, hygiene knowledge or emotional development.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via pointer events with pointer capture; keyboard as described in section 4. The box has an `aria-label` that includes the animal name (`Zwierzątko do kąpieli: <name>. Strzałki przesuwają szczotkę, Enter lub spacja myje dalej.`).
- **Target size:** the whole animal (height up to 640 px, at least 160 px) is the touch surface; brush at least 44 CSS px wide.
- **Orientation:** the animal box is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange` (`h = clamp(min(fieldHeight * 0.96, fieldWidth * 0.96 * 84/64, 640), >= 160)`, width `h * 64/84`); progress is kept because stage layers use logical coordinates.
- **Colour:** progress is shown by the layer disappearing, not by colour alone; the three covers differ in texture (blobs, foam bubbles, droplets).
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required (no text on screen).
- **Reduced motion:** all effects are driven by the rAF loop; under `prefers-reduced-motion` only the 0.5 s rest fade becomes instant (the remaining layer disappears at once). The 0.7 s fade-ins, bubbles and glow still run.
- **Touch behaviour:** `touch-action: none` on the box, text selection disabled.
- **Focus:** 4 px box-shadow `#8f7fd1` on the focused box.
- **Limitations:** keyboard completion needs many key presses; the layers are drawn with random blobs, so a child may see small untouched patches that the 90% rule leaves to fade.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The activity has a fixed small animal with a rubbing gesture; very small hands on large tablets must cover a large area (brush width scales with the animal, up to 0.2 of the box width).
- Stage 2 shows a vertical stream and falling droplets while dragging, and stage 3 shows tiny droplets; motion is slow but continuous while touching.
- The accessory and animal are random; some accessories may look odd on some animals (`Requires verification`).
- A child may rub very quickly across the screen; the 90% threshold is checked every 0.12 s, so stages can end soon after fast scrubbing.
- No personal data is collected; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/kapiel.js`](../../js/kapiel.js):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LW`, `LH` | Logical size of the stage mask | px | `256`, `336` |
| `VX, VY, VW, VH` | Animal viewBox | numbers | `-32, -42, 64, 84` |
| `MAX_BUBBLES` | Pooled bubble/droplet nodes | number | `28` |
| `BUBBLE_S`, `SPAWN_GAP_S` | Bubble life and spawn spacing | s | `1.6`, `0.09` |
| `DONE_AT` | Cleaned share that ends a stage | 0 to 1 | `0.9` |
| `REST_S`, `IN_S` | Rest fade and fade-in times | s | `0.5`, `0.7` |
| `GLOW_S`, `NEXT_AT_S`, `SWAP_S` | Completion glow, time to the next animal, swap fade | s | `3`, `7`, `0.7` |
| `BRUSH` | Brush width per stage | fractions | `[0.11, 0.2, 0.17]` |
| `ACCESSORIES` | Six accessories (kokardka, czapeczka, korona, kwiatek, muszka, gwiazdka) | array | 6 entries |

No fallback because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The animal comes from [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.head(id, { body: true })`, drawn in a 64 x 84 viewBox with a small ground shadow). Mud, foam and damp covers are made from a silhouette SVG data URL loaded into an `Image` (`silhouette()`, cached in `SIL_CACHE` by animal id and colour) and drawn into the canvas with random blobs. The halo uses the same silhouette in the fur colour. Accessories are inline SVG strings. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Animal:** `Rand.pickOne(Animals.LIST, 'kapiel-animal')`: one of 13 animals (Miś, Króliczek, Kotek, Piesek, Myszka, Świnka, Lisek, Lew, Słoń, Panda, Żabka, Sowa, Koala), never the same as the previous pick for this key within the page session.
- **Accessory:** `Rand.pickOne(ACCESSORIES, 'kapiel-acc')`: one of 6, chosen when each animal is set up and not the same as the previous one.
- **Layer pattern:** random blob positions and sizes for each stage layer.
- **When:** the first animal at launch, then a new animal after each completed animal.
- **Persistence:** none.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No levels. Each animal always goes through the same three stages; the brush gets wider in stage 2 (0.2) and slightly narrower in stage 3 (0.17). Nothing is stored.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Stage completion:** at 90% cleaned the rest fades and the next cover fades in.
- **Final completion:** after stage 3 the accessory appears, the animal glows (`drop-shadow` `#ffe08a`) for about 3 s and a new animal replaces it about 7 s after the third stage finished.
- **Feedback during play:** bubbles, shower stream and droplets follow the finger; fur halo grows in stage 3.
- **Failure feedback:** none.
- **Sound:** none.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/kapiel.js`](../../js/kapiel.js), registered on the `kapiel` entry; returns a cleanup function. Loaded just before `app.js` in `index.html`.
- **State:** `animal`, `stage`, `phase` (`wait`, `play`, `rest`, `in`, `done`, `swap`), `baseline` (opaque pixel sum of the fresh layer), `pointers` (active drags), `dirty`, `token` (guards against stale async image loads), bubble pool `bubbles[28]`.
- **Rendering:** a `.kp-box` with an animal SVG, a blurred halo (`kp-halo`), the mask `<canvas class="kp-layer">`, an accessory layer, the shower, a keyboard brush ring and the bubble layer. The progress check draws the layer into a 32 x 42 canvas (`willReadFrequently`) and sums alpha.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop (`frame`, `dt` capped at 50 ms); `if (busy && !raf)` keeps a single loop when an image callback restarts it synchronously (fix in commit `c8b1d37`). The loop stops when idle and is cancelled when the tab is hidden.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.pickOne` ([`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)) and `Animals.LIST`.
- **Persistence/analytics:** none.
- **Cleanup:** sets `alive = false` (so late image callbacks do nothing), cancels the frame, removes the window and document listeners and the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Field: the screen minus 64 px at the top and 12 px elsewhere (plus safe areas), centred flex container.
- The animal box has a fixed aspect `64 : 84`; all internal layers (animal SVG, halo, canvas, accessory) fill the box (`inset: 0`).
- Mask and pointer coordinates use the logical 256 x 336 space (`toLogical` maps client coordinates through the box rectangle), so the same progress is valid at every size and orientation. Bubbles use fractions of the box (`x / LW`, `y / LH`, percentages in CSS).
- Brush radius is converted from CSS pixels to logical units so it is always at least 44 CSS px wide.
- The animal is scaled to fit, so on wide landscape screens it occupies the central part of the field.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Image not loaded (async) | Phase `wait` until the silhouette image fires `load`; cached images run the callback synchronously. |
| Image load error | Not handled: there is no `error` listener, so the activity would stay in `wait` (the loop keeps running). Practically unlikely for a data-URL SVG; `Requires verification`. |
| Stale callback after the animal changed or the activity was left | Ignored (`token` and `alive` checks). |
| Resize/orientation change | `layout` rescales the box; mask progress is kept. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return. |
| Multi-touch | Each pointer rubs independently. |
| Touch cancel / lost capture | Pointer removed; progress kept. |
| Rapid input | The progress check runs every 0.12 s while changes occur. |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | `reduced()` returns `false`. |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#171](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/171) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation (pointer drag and keyboard-only runs, with and without reduced motion) completing all three stages; it is not re-verified here.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: scrub the mud, shower off the foam and towel-dry; each stage ends after most of the cover is gone.
- [ ] Completion: after stage 3 the accessory appears, the animal glows for about 3 s and a new animal fades in after about 7 s.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: rub outside the animal, tap without dragging, leave a small patch untouched (the rest fades).
- [ ] Restart/replay: complete several animals; the animal and accessory change and the same animal does not repeat twice in a row.
- [ ] Randomization: check that all 13 animals and 6 accessories can appear and look acceptable.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is no level change besides the three stages.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: 320 x 568 up to 1920 x 1080; rotate in the middle of stage 2 and confirm the progress is kept.
- [ ] Touch: single finger and two fingers; mouse drag.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the animal, use the arrow keys and Enter/Space to finish all three stages.
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab during a stage and during the glow.
- [ ] Reduced motion: the rest fade becomes instant; effects still work.
- [ ] Performance: on a low-end device check that dragging stays smooth.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- No error handling for silhouette image load failure (section 16).
- Keyboard play needs many key presses.
- The final animal swap overrides phase `wait` with `swap`, so input may open at the end of the fade even if the new layer image has not finished loading (practically only on the very first load of an animal colour).

**Requires verification**

- Appearance of every accessory on every animal.
- Performance of canvas erasing and `getImageData` checks on low-end devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other activities using the shared animal family: [Buźki](buzki.md), [Cienie](cienie.md) (also uses the `shadow` option of `Animals.head`).
- Shared helpers: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`) and [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.LIST`, `Animals.head`).
- Another activity with a washing theme: [Myjnia](myjnia.md) (not compared in detail here).

## 21. Change history

- [#169](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/169) / PR [#171](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/171): activity added.
- Commit `c8b1d37`: keep a single rAF chain in `frame()` when a cached silhouette callback restarts it (review suggestion).

```
