## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/karuzela.md`

```markdown
# Karuzela

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Karuzela |
| Activity ID | `karuzela` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A pastel merry-go-round with a striped roof, bunting and four random animals. It turns in place when touched. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, calm observation |
| Interaction type | Tap (start/stop), drag around the carousel (turn by hand), tap an animal |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |

Source: [`js/karuzela.js`](../../js/karuzela.js), CSS prefix `kz-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html). Introduced by issue #96 / PR [#159](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/159).

## 2. Business purpose

- Offers a slow, predictable "ride" the child can start and stop, and a manual way to turn it, giving a direct cause-and-effect loop without any goal.
- The motion is deliberately gentle: one full turn takes 18 s, speed changes are eased over 2-3 s, and the direction never reverses.
- Complements the other playground scenes ([Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md)) with a continuous rotating motion rather than a single triggered action.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; `mount(container)` builds the scene and starts the animation loop.
2. The carousel stands at rest, with four randomly chosen animals on seats and gently swaying bunting.
3. The child can touch the carousel body, drag around it, or touch an animal.
4. Tap on the carousel: it eases up to full speed over 2 s. Tap while it turns (or coasts): it eases to a stop over 3 s. Dragging turns it with the finger. Tapping an animal makes it hop or wave once.
5. There is no completion state; the activity is open-ended.
6. Nothing ends or resets; the cycle (rest, turn, stop) can repeat indefinitely.
7. Re-entering the activity creates a new scene with a new random animal selection.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Interaction | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tap on the carousel body (`.kz-hull`) at rest | Ramp to full speed `WMAX` = 2π/18 rad/s over `T_UP` = 2 s (smoothstep easing), then keeps turning. |
| Tap while ramping up or coasting | Ramp down to rest over `T_DOWN` = 3 s. Tap during a ramp-down starts a new ramp-up from the current speed. |
| Drag (pointer moves 10 px or more from the press point) | Mode `drag`: the turn angle follows the finger; per frame it never advances faster than `WMAX`; if the finger gets more than 0.6 rad ahead the grip is shifted. |
| Release after a drag | Forward momentum only: speed = clamp(estimated speed, 0, `WMAX`); decays exponentially with `COAST_TAU` = 0.9 s; below 0.003 rad/s it rests. A reverse drag leaves it at rest. |
| Tap on an animal | A reaction of `REACT_S` = 1.8 s: seats 0 and 2 hop up to `HOP` = 8 px; seats 1 and 3 raise a paw (rotation up to about 40 degrees). Ignored while that animal is already reacting. Rotation is unaffected. |
| Pointer cancel | Ends the gesture; if dragging, speed is set to 0 and the carousel rests. |

- Angle `th` grows in one direction only. Seats sit on an ellipse (x = sin, depth = cos) and always stay upright.
- Drag sensitivity: `angleDelta` converts horizontal finger movement to angle; touching in the front half (below the orbit centre) turns forward, in the back half the sign flips; a dead zone keeps the factor at least 0.5 in magnitude.
- Seat bobbing: up to `BOB` = 4 px up or down (8 px range), scaled by current speed, with a per-seat phase.
- Perspective: seat scale = 0.92 + 0.12 cos(angle); each animal is also drawn lower toward the front: a vertical offset `FRONT_DROP * seatPx * (1 + cos) / 2` (`FRONT_DROP` = 0.08, i.e. 0 at the back and 8% of the animal's height at the very front, smooth in the angle); front seats (cos > 0) get a higher z-index (5 vs 3).
- Bunting: 9 flags rock by up to 5 degrees with a 6 s period, independent of the ride.
- No sound, no scoring, no failure state. See also [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect: touching the carousel starts and stops it.
- Calm visual observation of slow, regular motion.
- Hand-eye coordination through dragging.

**Directly observable behavior**

- A tap changes speed smoothly (2 s up, 3 s down) rather than instantly.
- A drag follows the finger but cannot exceed full speed or reverse.
- Animals respond to touch without disturbing the ride.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on attention, calm or development is not established by the code and is not claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via pointer events (`pointerdown/move/up/cancel` with pointer capture on the scene). Keyboard: the carousel body and each animal are `<button>` elements; Enter/Space produce a `click` with `detail === 0`, which toggles the ride or triggers the animal reaction. Dragging has no keyboard equivalent.
- **Targets:** seats are `max(56, 68 * k)` px square (`k` = board scale); the carousel body button covers 340 x 250 board units.
- **Labels:** the body button has `aria-label` "Karuzela – uruchom lub zatrzymaj"; each seat has "<animal name> na karuzeli"; decorative SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible` outline 4px `#8f7fd1`.
- **Orientation:** works in portrait and landscape; the board is rescaled on `resize` and `orientationchange`.
- **Colour:** meaning is not carried by colour; animals are distinguished by shape and name.
- **Reduced motion:** the ride is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so it keeps working under the global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule (which only disables CSS animation/transition). The activity therefore does not reduce its motion for users with that setting; the speed is already slow.
- **Reading:** none required; a young child can use it independently.
- **Limitations:** the scene sets `touch-action: none` and `user-select: none`, so the scene cannot be scrolled or zoomed by touch; no screen-reader description of the current rotation state.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Continuous motion: the carousel can turn indefinitely once started (there is no auto-stop). Speed is low (18 s per turn) and there is no flashing.
- A drag that starts on an animal turns the carousel; only a short tap triggers the animal reaction (accidental drag vs tap threshold is 10 px).
- On very small or very wide-and-short screens seats are at least 56 px, so they can overlap when the board is scaled down (`k` is clamped at 0.3). Not verified on real devices.
- Visual check in a real browser is not documented (see section 17).

## 8. Configuration

The activity has no external configuration; the constants are inside [`js/karuzela.js`](../../js/karuzela.js) and cannot be changed without editing code. Nothing is read from storage; there is no fallback logic.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `WMAX` | 2π/18 rad/s | Full speed (one turn in 18 s) |
| `T_UP` / `T_DOWN` | 2 s / 3 s | Time to reach full speed / to stop |
| `COAST_TAU` | 0.9 s | Momentum decay after a drag |
| `BOB` | 4 px | Seat bob amplitude (8 px range) |
| `HOP`, `REACT_S` | 8 px, 1.8 s | Animal reaction height and length |
| `MAX_DT` | 0.05 s | Frame time cap |
| `BW` x `BH` | 400 x 300 | Board units |
| `FRONT_DROP` | 0.08 | Extra drop of an animal at the front-most point, as a fraction of its height |
| `CX`, `ORB_R`, `ORB_Y`, `ORB_D` | 200, 118, 214, 20 | Orbit centre x, radius, feet baseline y, depth amplitude |
| `N`, `SEAT` | 4, 68 | Seat count; seat box in board units |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything is inline SVG generated in `mount` (background, roof with 8 alternating stripes, platform, pole, bunting) and animal heads from [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.head(id, { body: true })`). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- On every `mount`, `Animals.pick(4, { distinct: true })` selects 4 unique animals from the 13-animal pool, preferring one per silhouette group (falls back to plain unique picks if there are too few groups). See [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) and [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.shuffle`).
- The pick is not stored; each visit gets a new selection and the same animal can recur between visits (no cross-visit repetition prevention).
- Seat order and positions are fixed (90 degrees apart); paws are attached to odd seats only.
- Nothing else is random.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression, levels or difficulty. Nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- No completion state; open-ended.
- Feedback is visual only: smooth speed changes, animal hop or wave, bobbing, swaying bunting.
- No failure or retry; no sound; nothing starts automatically.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in an IIFE; assigned to the registry entry whose `id === 'karuzela'`. Returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** DOM plus several SVG layers inside `div.kz`: `.kz-bg` (hill and grass, sized in pixels), `.kz-flags`, `.kz-base`, `.kz-hull` button, four `.kz-seat` buttons, `.kz-top` (pole and roof, above seats).
- **State:** closure variables: `th` (angle), `om` (angular speed), `mode` (`rest | ramp | coast | drag`), ramp parameters, `react[4]`, bunting phase `ph`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`) with capped dt, updating transforms in `place()` each frame. It is cancelled while `document.hidden` and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** pointer events on the scene and `pointerdown` on the hull and seats (`down(e, src)`); `click` with `detail === 0` for keyboard activation; `resize`/`orientationchange` call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes all listeners (including window/document ones) and removes the scene node.
- **Dependencies:** `window.Animals`, and `window.Rand` indirectly. No persistence, no analytics integration. See [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Logical board 400 x 300 units; scale `k = max(0.3, min(W/400, 0.9*H/300))`; board centred horizontally (`ox`) and slightly above centre vertically (`oy`).
- Base, roof/pole (`.kz-top`) and flags SVGs are positioned and sized in pixels from the board; seats are positioned with `transform: translate(...)` computed from the orbit in board units times `k`, anchored by the animal's feet (`FEET` = 83/86 of the seat box).
- The hill and grass background uses a pixel viewBox (`0 0 W H`), with the grass band as the bottom 12% of the height.
- Portrait and landscape both use the same fit rule; `layout()` is re-run on resize and orientation change, and the next frame redraws.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/orientation change: `layout()` recomputes everything; a ride in progress continues.
- Backgrounding: the loop stops and restarts on return with a fresh `last`, so the large time gap is not applied.
- Frame hitches: dt capped at 0.05 s.
- Touch cancellation: ends the gesture and rests the carousel if dragging.
- Multiple fingers: only the first pointer is tracked (`g` is set while a gesture is active; other `pointerdown` events are ignored).
- Repeated taps: toggling uses the current speed as the ramp start, so there are no jumps.
- Missing assets / empty pools: not applicable (inline SVG; `Animals.pick` always has 13 animals). `Animals.head` returns an empty string for an unknown id (not reachable here).
- `setPointerCapture` failures are caught and ignored.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#159](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/159) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation at 800x500 and 360x640 (period 18.0 s, ramp/stop, reverse drag settles at rest, animal reaction) and states it was not checked in a real browser.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: tap the carousel; it reaches steady speed in about 2 s and one turn takes about 18 s.
- [ ] Stop: tap again; it stops smoothly over about 3 s and never reverses.
- [ ] Tap an animal while turning: seats 1 and 3 wave a paw, seats 2 and 4 hop; the rotation does not change.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no end state and the ride can run for several minutes.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: drag in the opposite direction; the carousel does not reverse and rests after release.
- [ ] Drag fast across the carousel; it never exceeds full speed and coasts to a stop in about 3 s.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and re-enter; scene is at rest with (usually) different animals.
- [ ] Randomization: enter several times; four different animals each time, no duplicates within a scene.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none and nothing persists after reloading.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape on a phone and a tablet; rotate while turning; seats stay at least 56 px and the scene stays on screen.
- [ ] Touch: single-finger tap and drag; a second finger is ignored.
- [ ] Mouse: click, drag, hover cursor.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the carousel and animals, Enter/Space toggles the ride or the reaction.
- [ ] Background the tab while turning and return; no jump in angle.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: the carousel still turns and animals still react.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; no documented real-device verification.
- No keyboard way to turn the carousel by hand.
- Touching the carousel never auto-stops it.

**Requires verification**

- Seat overlap and drag feel on very small portrait screens and on real touch devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned. (The depth-dependent vertical offset of the animals is done, see issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), pull request [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173).)

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other playground scenes: [Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md), [Latawiec](latawiec.md), [Wiatraczki](wiatraczki.md) (also a rotating, touch-started motion).
- Shared helpers: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`), which uses [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js).
- The single `requestAnimationFrame` loop with capped dt and `visibilitychange` restart is the common pattern for these scenes.

## 21. Change history

- Issue #96, PR [#159](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/159): activity added (commit 69c94ef).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): fixed on `main`; animals sit lower toward the front of the carousel (`FRONT_DROP`).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/kolejka-linowa.md`

```markdown
# Kolejka Linowa

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Kolejka Linowa |
| Internal ID | `kolejka` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)); source file `js/kolejka.js`, CSS prefix `kl-` |
| Description | A small gondola with a bear and a rabbit glides along a cable between a valley station and a peak station on a pastel mountain with three pine trees and drifting clouds. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap / click (real buttons, so Enter and Space also work) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Kolejka Linowa is the mountain member of the vehicle group. Unlike the looping vehicles it travels back and forth on a straight line with two stations, which gives a clear "from here to there" structure: the child can send the gondola to either station, where a door opens, or let it shuttle on its own with a 3 s pause at each end. All speed changes are smooth, the gondola can never leave the cable, and nothing can go wrong.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#kolejka`); `mount` builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The scene shows a mountain with a snow cap, a valley station at the lower left (at 20 % of the width) and a peak station at the upper right (80 %), a cable between them, three pine trees on the grass, three clouds drifting slowly, and the gondola waiting at the **valley station** with the door closed.
3. The child can touch the gondola hull, a station, the bear or the rabbit in the windows, or a tree.
4. Touching the gondola while it waits starts it (2 s ramp) towards the other station; it pauses 3 s at each station (the door opens, then closes before departure) and keeps shuttling. Touching it while it moves brakes it to a halt on the cable, where it sways gently; touching it again continues in the same direction. Touching a station sends the gondola there (braking first if it is heading away) and it waits with the door open. Touching an animal makes it wave (2.6 s). Touching a tree makes it sway once (2 s).
5. There is no formal completion state.
6. The shuttle continues until the child stops it or sends it to a station.
7. The activity does not reset itself and nothing is randomised (section 10).
8. The child leaves with Back (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Cruise speed | `VC = 1/12` cable fractions per second; a full trip takes about 13.5 to 14 s including the ramps |
| Acceleration ramp | `RAMP = 2` s (smoothstep) |
| Braking | the gondola brakes over a distance of at most one second of travel (`D = min(v·1.0, remaining)`), duration `T = 2·D/v` (about 2 s at cruise speed); it also brakes automatically before the end station |
| Pause at a station while shuttling | `DWELL = 3` s |
| Door open / close | `DOOR_S = 1.2` s |
| Door hold after touching the current station | `HOLD_S = 1.5` s |
| Sway while stopped on the cable | `SWAY_MAX = 3.2` deg, period 4.5 s; amplitude eases in and out at 2 deg/s |
| Animal wave | `WAVE_S = 2.6` s |
| Tree sway | `TREE_S = 2` s (7 deg decaying, 1.5 cycles) |
| Frame step cap | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |
| Clouds | 3, crossing the scene in 150, 120 and 180 s respectively |

Details:

- **Position model.** The position is a fraction `p` of the cable (0 = valley station, 1 = peak station), so the gondola always stays on the cable and keeps its relative place after a resize or rotation. It never reverses in the middle of a trip.
- **Gondola touch** (`onCar`): while moving it stops (`brakeStop`) and cancels any destination and the shuttle mode; while a delayed departure is waiting for the door it cancels it; during a station pause it ends the shuttle and leaves the door open; otherwise it starts the shuttle (`loop = true`), leaving a station in the direction of the other one or continuing in the current direction from the cable.
- **Station touch** (`onStation`): when the gondola is already at that station, the door opens for 1.5 s and closes and nothing else changes; otherwise the gondola goes there; if it is moving towards it, it continues; if away from it, it first brakes and then returns; if the door is open it closes first and then departs. Touching a station while the gondola is already slowing down keeps the slow-down and carries on to the destination.
- **At arrival** the door opens; when in shuttle mode the pause starts (`dwellT`), the door closes during the last 1.2 s of the 3 s pause and the gondola departs towards the other station.
- **Animals:** a touch is ignored while that animal is already waving. **Trees:** a touch is ignored while that tree is already swaying.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is JS-driven; see section 6. **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touching the gondola or a station changes its movement.
- Calm observation of slow, predictable movement between two places.
- Understanding "from one place to another" through two clearly marked stations.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- The gondola changes speed only through 2 s ramps and brakes smoothly.
- The door opens and closes visibly (1.2 s) at the stations.
- Animals wave and trees sway on touch.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on attention, spatial understanding or planning. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) and `click` with `event.detail === 0` for keyboard activation. The hull, the two stations, both animals and the three trees are real `<button>` elements with Polish `aria-label`s and can be reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space.
- **Touch handling.** `.kl` uses `touch-action: none`; no drag gesture. The gondola container has `pointer-events: none`; only the hull and the animal buttons capture touches.
- **Target sizes.** Gondola width `g = clamp(0.22·min(W, H), 136, 190)` px; the hull covers 132/160 x 108/150 of the gondola; animal buttons 56 x 56 px; stations `1.5·g` wide; trees `tw = clamp(0.1·min(W, H), 56, 96)` px wide, spaced at least `tw + 4` px apart.
- **Orientation.** Layout recomputed on `resize`/`orientationchange`.
- **Colour.** Nothing depends on colour alone; the two stations differ in position (and the labels in `aria-label`).
- **Reduced motion.** The gondola, door, sway, waves, tree sways and clouds are driven by the rAF loop and keep running under the global reduced-motion rule. No CSS animations are used by this activity. The motion is slow, but it is not reduced for users who asked for reduced motion.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Limitations:** the animals' windows and the hull overlap (animals sit on top of the hull button); station and gondola can overlap at the stations, where the hull is the target above the station button (z-index 8 vs 5).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Accidental interactions:** at a station the gondola covers part of the station, so a touch there may hit the gondola instead of the station; the effect (start or stop) is harmless.
- **Unclear ending:** the activity never ends.
- **Visual stimulation:** low; the sway is at most 3.2 degrees and slow.
- **Performance:** one always-running rAF loop; the SVG scene is redrawn only on resize.
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/kolejka.js`](../../js/kolejka.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VC` | Cruise speed (cable fractions/s) | number | `1/12` |
| `RAMP` | Time to get up to speed (s) | number | 2 |
| `DWELL` | Pause at a station while shuttling (s) | number | 3 |
| `DOOR_S` | Door open/close time (s) | number | 1.2 |
| `HOLD_S` | Door hold after touching the current station (s) | number | 1.5 |
| `SWAY_MAX` | Sway amplitude while stopped on the cable (deg) | number | 3.2 |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 |
| `WAVE_S`, `TREE_S` | Animal wave and tree sway durations (s) | number | 2.6, 2 |
| `cloudU`, `cloudSpd`, `cloudY` | Cloud start positions, speeds (per s), heights | arrays | 3 entries each |

There is no fallback because there is no external input.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The gondola (with the bear and rabbit), the stations, trees and clouds are inline SVG strings in the JS file; the mountain, snow cap, hills and cable are SVG paths whose geometry is computed in `layout()`; the sky gradient is CSS (`.kl-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css)). The two animals are drawn locally by `animalSvg`, not from `js/animals.js`. No audio, fonts or data files. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

None. The scene, animals (bear and rabbit), tree positions and cloud positions are the same on every launch.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. No levels or difficulty, and nothing persists between sessions. The gondola starts waiting at the valley station on every launch.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is visual only: smooth speed changes, the door opening and closing at stations, the gentle sway when stopped on the cable, waving animals and swaying trees. No sound, no celebration, no automatic restart.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/kolejka.js`](../../js/kolejka.js), assigned to the `kolejka` registry entry; loaded before `js/app.js`. No shared helper is used.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG. The land and cable are full-scene SVG overlays; stations, trees and the gondola are positioned with inline `transform`; the door is an SVG rectangle scaled horizontally.
- **State:** closures: `p` (cable fraction), `dir`, `v`, `ramp`, `plan` (braking), `loop`, `dest`, `dwellActive`/`dwellT`, `door`/`doorTarget`, `pulse`, `goAfterDoor`, `swayAmp`, `waves[]`, `tsT[]`.
- **Control functions:** `startMove`, `depart`, `brakeStop`, `finishPlan`, `arrive`, `onCar`, `onStation`.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop `frame` with a capped dt; paused while hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `bind()` registers `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the rAF, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Persistence/config/analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; `W`/`H` come from `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`.
- **Units:** CSS pixels. All SVG overlays use a `viewBox` of `0 0 W H` (1 unit = 1 px), so the land, the cable and the HTML elements share one coordinate space. The gondola is `cx = xv + p·(xp - xv)`, `cy = ya + p·(yb - ya)`, i.e. along the cable line from the valley station `(xv, ya)` to the peak station `(xp, yb)`.
- **Layout rules:** `xv = max(0.75·g + 8, 0.2·W)`; `xp = min(W - 0.75·g - 8, 0.8·W)`; the ground occupies the bottom 13 % of the height; the peak station is at `max(34, 0.09·H) + 0.25·g`; the mountain summit is placed just above the peak station.
- **Trees:** at 50 %, 73 % and 93 % of the width, pushed apart so the hit boxes never overlap.
- Tested sizes: Not currently documented.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Backgrounding:** the loop pauses while hidden and resumes without a jump.
- **Resize:** the gondola keeps its cable fraction and everything is recomputed.
- **Rapid input:** the state transitions in `onCar`/`onStation` handle repeated touches (PR [#157](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/157) reports 30 rapid touches in a simulation); animal and tree reactions ignore touches while running.
- **Edge of the cable:** `p` is clamped to [0, 1] and braking starts automatically before the end stations.
- **Touch cancel / missing assets / invalid config:** not applicable.
- **Unhandled:** no fallback without `requestAnimationFrame`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#157](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/157) reports a node run against a stub DOM covering trip time, monotonic motion, stop and sway amplitude, restart, station touches (docked, from mid-cable, reversing), 30 rapid touches and cleanup, and asks for a device check of the portrait and landscape layout.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Kolejka Linowa; the gondola waits at the valley station with the door closed; touch it; it glides up to the peak station in about 14 s.
- [ ] At the peak station the door opens for about 3 s, closes, and the gondola travels back; the shuttle continues.
- [ ] Touch the moving gondola; it stops on the cable in about 2 s and sways gently; touch again; it continues in the same direction.
- [ ] Touch the opposite station while the gondola moves away from it; the gondola brakes and turns back to that station.
- [ ] Touch the station where the gondola is waiting; the door opens for about 1.5 s and closes.
- [ ] Touch the bear and the rabbit (waves) and each tree (one sway); repeat quickly; nothing stacks.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch the mountain, clouds and sky; nothing happens.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no completion state.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-enter; the gondola waits at the valley station again.
- [ ] Randomization and progression: confirm that nothing varies and nothing persists.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate while the gondola moves and while it waits; the gondola stays on the cable and the stations and trees are fully visible and do not overlap.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab through stations, gondola, animals and trees; Enter/Space).
- [ ] Background the tab during a trip; return without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled: the gondola, door and clouds still move.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The motion ignores the reduced-motion preference by design.
- The two animals are drawn locally rather than from `js/animals.js`.

**Requires verification**

- Overlap of the gondola and the station buttons at the stations (which element receives the touch) on different viewports.
- Layout on very short or very narrow viewports (geometry is computed from `min(W, H)` and the ground height).
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Kolejka Linowa; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Mała Łódka](mala-lodka.md) and [Autobusik](autobusik.md) (stop at a place), [Traktor](traktor.md), [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md), [Balon](balon.md).
- Shared helpers: none used (`js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not referenced).
- Shared pattern: rAF loop with a capped dt; position stored as a fraction so it survives resizing.

## 21. Change history

- [#94](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/94) / PR [#157](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/157): Kolejka Linowa activity added (single commit `6db0e60`, no later changes to `js/kolejka.js`).
```

```markdown
# Kolorowe Kształty

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Kolorowe Kształty |
| Activity ID | `ksztalty` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Soft coloured shapes are dragged onto matching dashed outlines. Pictures start as 2x2 shapes and become 3x3 after three finished pictures; every picture has fresh random shapes, colours and positions. |
| Category | Matching |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop (touch, mouse, stylus); keyboard alternative (select, then choose outline) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default |
| Source | [`js/ksztalty.js`](../../js/ksztalty.js), styles with prefix `ks-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

Not to be confused with [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md), a separate tracing activity.

## 2. Business purpose

- A shape-matching activity with no wrong answers: a shape released anywhere but on its own outline drifts back, with no negative feedback.
- Practises matching by form (outline and shape have the same form), with colour as an additional but independent attribute.
- Variety through random shapes, colours and positions, and a gentle step up from 4 to 9 pieces, so the activity can be replayed without repeating the same picture.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 11.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the first picture (2x2) is built.
2. Initially displayed: a grid of 4 dashed outlines (targets) and a grid of 4 coloured shapes (to drag). In portrait the outline grid is above and the shapes below; in landscape they are side by side (outlines left, shapes right).
3. Interaction: drag a shape onto its matching outline. Keyboard: press Enter/Space on a shape, then activate an outline.
4. Response: released near its own outline (within 0.75 shape sizes), the shape glides in, glows and stays (outline dims to 35 % opacity). Anywhere else, or on another outline, it glides back to its start position.
5. Completion: when all shapes are placed, a soft whole-picture glow fades in.
6. After 4 s the next picture is built automatically (new shapes, colours and positions).
7. After 3 completed pictures the grid becomes 3x3 (9 shapes) for the rest of the visit.
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back. Re-opening starts again at 2x2.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Pieces per picture | `g * g`: 4 (g = 2) or 9 (g = 3). |
| Shapes | 9 shapes (`SHAPES`): kółko (circle), kwadrat (square), trójkąt (triangle), gwiazdka (star), serduszko (heart), romb (diamond), sześciokąt (hexagon), owal (oval), krzyżyk (cross). A picture uses `g * g` **different** shapes. |
| Colours | 9 colours (one defined per shape, but used independently): pink `#f7a8c9`, blue `#a8d8f0`, yellow `#ffd98a`, light yellow `#fff0a0`, rose `#f7b0b8`, lilac `#c9b8f2`, green `#bfe6b4`, orange `#ffc9a0`, mint `#a8e0d6`. A picture uses `g * g` **different** colours, randomly paired with the shapes. |
| Placement | The outline for shape *i* is at target-grid cell *i*; the shape *k* starts at a different cell of the shape grid (random permutation with no fixed point, so no shape starts "under" its own outline's slot). |
| Drop test | On release, the distance from the shape centre to its own outline centre must be below `0.75 * S` (S = shape size in px); otherwise the shape returns. Dropping on a different outline does not accept it. |
| Glide | Returning or snapping takes `min(1400, 700 + distance * 0.8)` ms with smoothstep; 300 ms when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set; 200 ms when re-laid out after a resize. |
| Drag limits | The shape centre is clamped inside the visible screen; only the primary pointer button (or touch) starts a drag; one pointer per shape (multi-touch on different shapes works). |
| Placed shapes | Disabled (not draggable or focusable), glow fades in over about 250 ms, outline opacity 0.35. |
| Whole-picture glow | A radial glow over the screen fades in (about 500 ms) when every shape is placed and idle. |
| Next picture | `RETURN_AFTER = 4000` ms after the last shape settles; the timer only advances while the page is visible. |
| Progression | `WIN_AFTER = 3` completed pictures at 2x2, then 3x3. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Visual discrimination and matching of forms.
- Hand-eye coordination through dragging.
- Noticing that colour and form are separate properties (colour is randomly paired with shapes).

**Directly observable behavior**

- A shape only stays where its own outline is; every other release returns it softly.
- Colour is not a reliable cue for the match (random pairing), so form decides.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning shapes or colours. Nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events with pointer capture (touch, mouse, stylus), `touch-action: none`. Keyboard: shapes are native buttons; Enter/Space selects (`aria-pressed`, visible selection outline), then Enter/Space on an outline places it there (wrong outline sends the shape home). Tap-to-select is keyboard-only: a plain tap on a shape without dragging returns the shape home.
- **Labels (Polish):** outlines "Miejsce na <shape>", shapes "<shape> (Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz miejsce)".
- **Target sizes:** shape size `S = clamp(min(cell width, cell height) * 0.82, 56, 140)` px, and CSS `min-width/min-height: 56px`.
- **Orientation:** portrait (field height >= width): outlines above, shapes below; landscape: side by side; re-laid out on `resize` and `orientationchange`.
- **Colour:** a match is made by form; outlines carry the same dashed form and colour as their shape. Colour is not required.
- **Reduced motion:** the glides, glow and all state changes run from a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so they still work under the global rule (the glides are shorter, 300 ms).
- **Reading:** not required; the labels are for assistive technology only.
- **Limitation:** a very small screen can make the grid cells smaller than the 56 px minimum, so shapes may overlap (requires verification).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Dragging requires some motor control; keyboard alternative exists but a mouse or touch tap-select does not.
- The glow and re-layout every 4 s after completion are the only automatic changes; they replace all shapes at once (DOM is rebuilt).
- No end; relies on the global playtime limit.
- No privacy concerns; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/ksztalty.js`](../../js/ksztalty.js):

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `SHAPES` | Shape definitions (id, Polish label, colour, glow, SVG path) | 9 |
| `COLORS` | Colour list derived from `SHAPES` | 9 |
| `WIN_AFTER` | Completed 2x2 pictures before 3x3 | 3 |
| `RETURN_AFTER` | Delay before the next picture | 4000 ms |
| Drop radius | Fraction of shape size | 0.75 (in `up()`) |
| Shape size limits | `Math.max(56, Math.min(140, ...))` | 56 to 140 px |
| Frame cap | `Math.min(now - last, 50)` | 50 ms |

Fallback: none needed.

## 9. Assets

No external assets. All shapes and outlines are inline SVG (`viewBox="0 0 100 100"`) generated by `shapeSvg()` from path templates (filled with stroke width 12 for shapes; translucent white fill with a dashed 4-wide stroke for outlines). Glow is a CSS radial gradient and `drop-shadow` filter. No images, fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Per picture:** `Rand.pick(SHAPES, n)` selects `n` unique shapes; `Rand.pick(COLORS, n)` selects `n` unique colours (`js/random.js`, in memory only); pairing is by position. Outline slots follow the order of the shapes; start slots are a random permutation with no fixed point (re-drawn until none matches).
- **Pool sizes:** 9 shapes and 9 colours; for 3x3 all of each are used (only the pairing and positions vary).
- There is no guard against the same combination appearing in consecutive pictures; nothing is stored between launches.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

- Start: 2x2 (4 pieces). After 3 completed pictures: 3x3 (9 pieces) for the remainder of the visit.
- No further levels; re-opening the activity resets to 2x2 (the counters are in memory only).
- Difficulty changes only through the piece count.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion state: all shapes placed; feedback is a soft glow over the screen, with no text or sound.
- Wrong drops: shapes glide back; no red, shake or message.
- After 4 s the next picture starts automatically; there is no end screen.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/ksztalty.js`](../../js/ksztalty.js); it sets `container.style.display = 'block'` and does not restore it (the stage is emptied by `app.js` on exit). The cleanup function cancels the frame, removes the global listeners and removes the board.
- **Rendering:** DOM buttons with inline SVG, moved with `transform: translate`; one `div.ks-glow` overlay; rebuilt for each picture by `newRound()`.
- **State:** `g`, `completed`, `defs[]` (shape, colour, outline), `items[]` (position `x, y`, home `hx, hy`, target `tx, ty`, mode `idle | drag | glide`, `placed`, `glow`), `selected`, `doneT`, `doneGlow`.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`) that stops when idle and is restarted by `start()` (glide, resize, `visibilitychange`); the time step is capped at 50 ms.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture` per shape; `click` (keyboard, `detail === 0`) on shapes; `click` on outlines; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Shared code:** `window.Rand` (`pick`, `shuffle`).
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** `Analytics.levelStart` / `levelComplete` / `complete`.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.ks-field` is positioned below the Back button (top `safe + 64px`, 12 px other margins) and measured in pixels with `getBoundingClientRect`.
- Cell size: `cw = rw / g`, `ch = rh / g`, where the field is split in two regions (top/bottom in portrait, left/right in landscape); items are centred in their cells. Outlines and shapes use the same pixel coordinate space (the `ks-field`), so a shape placed on an outline is exactly on it.
- Re-layout on resize: positions recomputed; active drags are cancelled and sent home; placed shapes stay on their outlines.
- The shape size is recomputed per layout and passed to CSS as `--ks-s`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Release outside any outline or on another outline | The shape glides home. |
| Resize or rotation during a drag | The drag is cancelled safely and the shape is sent home. |
| Pointer cancel or lost capture | Treated as a release (`up`). |
| Multi-touch | Several shapes can be dragged at once; one pointer per shape. |
| Tab hidden | The loop is cancelled; the post-completion timer only counts visible time; restarted on return. |
| Drag off-screen | The shape centre is clamped inside the viewport. |
| Synthetic pointer without capture support | `setPointerCapture` is wrapped in `try/catch`. |
| Selecting a placed shape via keyboard | Ignored (placed shapes are disabled). |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; 4 shapes and 4 outlines (2x2); drag each shape onto its outline; it glides in and glows.
- [ ] Completion: place all shapes; the screen glows softly; after about 4 s a new picture appears.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: drop a shape on another outline, on empty space, and near-but-off the outline; it always glides back with no message.
- [ ] Tap a shape without dragging; it returns home.
- [ ] Progression: finish 3 pictures; the 4th has 9 shapes (3x3); re-open the activity; it starts at 2x2 again.
- [ ] Randomization: over several pictures, shapes, colours (all different within a picture) and positions change; no shape starts at its own outline's slot.
- [ ] Restart: leave in the middle of a picture and re-open; a new picture starts.
- [ ] Portrait: outlines above, shapes below; landscape: side by side; rotate during a drag and after placing shapes.
- [ ] Small screens (for example 320x568 and 360x640): shapes are at least 56 px and do not overlap.
- [ ] Touch (Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad), including dragging two shapes at once; mouse (desktop).
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to a shape, Enter/Space, then Tab to an outline and Enter/Space; wrong outline returns the shape.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tab during the glow; the 4 s timer pauses.
- [ ] Reduced motion: glides still occur (shorter).
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#141](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/141) reports a stub-DOM simulation that dragged every shape onto its outline over 6 pictures (4, 4, 4, 9, 9, 9 items, colours unique per picture) and states that portrait and landscape visuals were not device-tested. PR [#41](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/41) reports a Node DOM-stub check of the original version.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- Tap-to-select works only from the keyboard; mouse and touch require dragging.
- All shapes are rebuilt (DOM replaced) at the start of each picture; there is no transition between pictures.
- 3x3 is the maximum; there is no further progression.
- `container.style.display` is set and not restored.
- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Overlap of shapes on very small screens when the cell size is below 56 px.
- Visual quality of portrait and landscape layouts on devices (not device-tested in PR #141).

## 19. Planned improvements

`None currently planned`.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other matching or shape activities: [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md), [Wzorki](wzorki.md), [Puzzle](puzzle.md), [Cienie](cienie.md), [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`, `Rand.shuffle`). The activity does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#33](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/33) / PR [#41](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/41): initial activity (3 shapes).
- Issue [#66](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/66) / PR [#68](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/68): 9 shapes in two 3x3 grids, stacked in portrait and side by side in landscape.
- Issue [#115](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/115) / PR [#141](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/141): random shapes and colours per picture and 2x2 to 3x3 progression.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/kolorowe-kubeczki.md`

```markdown
# Kolorowe Kubeczki

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Kolorowe Kubeczki |
| Internal ID | `kubeczki` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Three pastel cups and six soft balls (two per colour). The child drags each ball into the cup of the same colour; colours also differ by a pattern (plain, dots, stripes). |
| Category | Sorting / matching by colour |
| Interaction type | Drag (pointer events); keyboard alternative (select a ball, then activate a cup) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/kubeczki.js`](../../js/kubeczki.js), CSS block `/* Kolorowe Kubeczki */` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (prefix `kc`) |

## 2. Business purpose

A colour-matching game with a small, fixed workload (six balls, three cups) and no wrong-answer feedback: a ball put in a cup of another colour floats back. Each colour is also marked with a pattern on both the cup and its balls, so the activity does not rely on colour vision alone. The colour set changes between launches. It complements the size-based sorting of [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md) and the shape-based [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md).

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#kubeczki`); a random colour/pattern combination is picked and the scene is laid out.
2. Three cups stand in a row at the top; six balls (two per colour) wait in the bottom area in shuffled places (one row of six, or two rows of three on narrow screens).
3. The child drags a ball. It follows the pointer and cannot leave the visible screen.
4. Released over its own cup, or anywhere above it (in the column of the cup's width, up to the top of the screen), the ball glides into the cup (smaller); released elsewhere or above another colour's cup it floats back to its waiting place.
5. When all six balls are in their cups (and nothing moves) the three cups glow for 2 s.
6. After 4 s the balls drift out of the cups to the bottom area in a new order.
7. The activity then continues with the same colours; there is no end.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (from `js/kubeczki.js`) |
|---|---|
| Cups | 3, each with a colour name, colour, glow colour and a pattern (`plain`, `dots`, `stripes`) |
| Balls | 6: ball `k` belongs to cup `k % 3` (two per cup) |
| Accept area | Ball centre within `0.5 * C` horizontally of the cup centre and anywhere above the cup's lower edge (`y < cup.y + 0.5 * C`, up to the top of the screen), and the ball's own cup: a column above the cup, not a square |
| Wrong drop | Ball glides home; no message |
| Placed balls | Disabled (not draggable); scaled to `min(1, 0.42 * C / B)` and nested left/right in the cup (offset `0.18 * C`) |
| Glide duration | `min(1600, 800 + distance * 0.9)` ms; 300 ms with reduced motion; 200 ms for re-layout glides; a ball snapped into a cup glides for at most 700 ms, so it falls in briefly even when released high above the cup |
| Glow | `GLOW_S = 2000` ms on the cups |
| Reset | `RESET_S = 4000` ms after completion: new shuffle of home slots (must differ from the previous), balls leave the cups |
| Sound | None ([shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)) |

- Keyboard: Enter or Space (a `click` with `detail === 0`) on a ball selects it (`aria-pressed`, outline); activating a cup then places it (own cup) or sends it home (other cup). Placed balls leave the tab order.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (design intent, not measured):
- Matching and sorting by colour, supported by pattern as a second cue.
- Hand-eye coordination through dragging.
- Calm repeatable play with immediate, gentle feedback.

**Directly observable behavior:**
- A ball stays only in a cup of its own colour and pattern.
- Cups glow when all balls are sorted, then the balls drift back out in a new order.
- No scores, timers or error messages.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about colour learning or developmental effect.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) with pointer capture and `touch-action: none`; keyboard alternative as above with a 4 px outline (`#8f7fd1`).
- **Screen readers:** cups are labelled "Kubeczek <colour>" and balls "Piłeczka <colour> (Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz kubeczek)"; `aria-pressed` marks the selected ball.
- **Non-colour cue:** every colour has a distinct pattern (plain, dots, stripes), always three distinct colours and three distinct patterns in each of the eight combinations.
- **Contrast:** soft pastel colours with a white translucent outline; contrast against the background (`#f6f0fb` to `#e3f1ea`) is low by design and has not been measured (requires verification).
- **Target size:** balls `B` between 64 and 120 px (CSS minimum 64 px); cups up to 190 px (minimum 72 px).
- **Orientation:** one row of six balls when `fw / 6 >= 84`, otherwise two rows of three; recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion and glow are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with inline styles, so they still run under the global CSS rule; glides shorten to 300 ms.
- **Reading:** none required.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Reliance on colour is mitigated by patterns, but the patterns are subtle (white 75% opacity marks on pastel fills).
- Some colour names occur in different combinations (for example both pink and blue appear in several sets); within one launch they are always distinct.
- No privacy concerns; nothing stored or sent.
- PR [#76](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/76) listed layout at 360x640 portrait/landscape (balls at least 64 px) and Safari checks as not yet done.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants are inside [`js/kubeczki.js`](../../js/kubeczki.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COMBOS` | Eight predefined sets of three cups (label, colour, glow colour, pattern) | array | 8 entries | top of IIFE (built by `combo()`) |
| `GLOW_S` | Cup glow duration | ms | 2000 | top of IIFE |
| `RESET_S` | Time from completion to the balls drifting out | ms | 4000 | top of IIFE |
| Layout numbers | `B` clamp 64-120, `C` clamp 72-190, per-row breakpoint `fw / 6 >= 84` | numbers | see `layout()` | `layout()` |

No fallback for invalid values because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external files. Cups (`cupSvg`) and balls (`ballSvg`) are inline SVG generated from the chosen combination, with pattern overlays drawn in white. The background is a CSS gradient. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, images or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | How | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| Colour/pattern combination | `Rand.pickOne(COMBOS, 'kubeczki')`: never the same combination as the previous pick of this key in the same page session | 8 combinations |
| Waiting slot of each ball | `shuffled(6)` at mount; reshuffled (must differ from the previous order) at every reset | 6! orders |

- The combination is chosen once per `mount`, so it persists during a visit and changes (never repeating the previous one) when the activity is re-opened in the same page session. After a page reload the "last pick" memory is lost.
- Nothing is stored. The pool is a fixed array, so empty/invalid pools cannot occur.
- Ball `k` always belongs to cup `k % 3`; only the waiting positions vary.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. Every round has three cups and six balls; nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion: all six balls placed and idle.
- Feedback: a coloured drop-shadow glow on the three cups for 2 s (eased in about 400 ms). Individual placement is shown by the ball gliding into the cup and shrinking.
- Failure: none; a wrong drop returns the ball. No sound.
- After 4 s the balls leave the cups in a new order and play continues automatically.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/kubeczki.js`](../../js/kubeczki.js), replacing `mount` of the `kubeczki` registry entry; returns `cleanup`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `div.kc > div.kc-field` with 3 `button.kc-cup` and 6 `button.kc-ball`, each containing an inline SVG. Elements are moved with `transform: translate() scale()`.
- **State:** per ball `{ cup, slot, x, y, s (scale), hx/hy (home), tx/ty/ts (target), nest, mode, pid, placed }`; per cup `{ c, x, y, count, glow }`; globals `order`, `selected`, `doneActive`, `doneT`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown/move/up/cancel`, `lostpointercapture` per ball; `click` on balls (keyboard) and cups; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Animation:** one `frame()` loop (dt capped at 50 ms), smoothstep glides, restarted by `start()` and stopped when nothing is moving; paused while hidden.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.pickOne` for the combination, local `shuffled()` for the ball slots (uses `Math.random` directly).
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js). **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** none from the activity itself (reported by `js/app.js`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the three listeners and removes the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.kc` is fixed full-screen; `.kc-field` is inset by the safe-area variables plus 64 px at the top and 12 px elsewhere. All coordinates are CSS pixels relative to the field (`fw` x `fh`).
- Cups: centred at `x = fw * (i + 0.5) / 3`, `y = C / 2 + 6` (top of the field). Balls rest at the bottom: one row of six (`x = fw * (col + 0.5) / 6`) or two rows of three, `hy = fh - B/2 - 6 - (rows - 1 - row) * (B + 8)`.
- `B = max(64, min(120, fw / per * 0.86, fh * (0.3 or 0.2)))`, `C = max(72, min(fw / 3 * 0.86, fh - rows * (B + 10) - 24, 190))`; both are exposed as CSS variables `--kc-b` and `--kc-c`.
- Cups, balls and drop areas share the field's pixel space; a ball's scale (placed state) is a transform and does not change its layout box.
- Resize or rotation re-runs `layout()`; dragged balls go home, glides continue to the new targets.
- On very short screens the minimum sizes (64 px balls, 72 px cups) take precedence over fitting (requires verification).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | N/A (inline SVG); `Rand` is required and not guarded |
| Resize / rotation | `layout()` re-run; active drag cancelled and ball sent home |
| Backgrounding | Loop paused while hidden; completion timers advance only while visible |
| Multi-touch | Each ball tracks its own pointer; a second pointer on the same ball is ignored |
| Pointer cancel / lost capture | Treated as release |
| Wrong cup or empty area | Ball returns home |
| Dragging outside the screen | Centre clamped to the visible window |
| Right mouse button | Ignored |
| Drag during the post-completion drift-out | Allowed, the balls are not yet placed; the drift-out can be interrupted by dragging (requires verification of the visual result) |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` cancels the frame |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#76](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/76) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM run of the keyboard flow (all six balls placed, glow, auto-reset to a new order); PR [#146](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/146) reports `node --check` and a check that all eight combinations have three distinct colours and patterns, with no browser available. Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: drag a ball into the cup of its colour; it shrinks into the cup.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: drag a ball to another cup and to empty ground; it floats back each time.
- [ ] Completion: all six sorted; the cups glow for about 2 s and the balls drift out in a new order after about 4 s.
- [ ] Restart: leave and reopen several times; the colour/pattern combination changes and does not repeat consecutively.
- [ ] Patterns: in every combination the three cups and their balls are told apart by pattern as well as colour.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that nothing changes between rounds.
- [ ] Portrait (about 360x640): two rows of three balls, all at least 64 px, no overlap with the cups.
- [ ] Landscape (about 640x360): one row of six, no overlap.
- [ ] Touch: drag two balls at once with two fingers; rotate mid-drag.
- [ ] Mouse: left-button drag works; right button does nothing.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to a ball, Enter selects, Enter on a cup places or returns it.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: glides are short, glow still shown.
- [ ] Background the tab during the glow and return.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from code reading):**
- No automated tests.
- The accept area is the column above the cup (its full width, from the cup's lower edge up to the top of the screen), not the cup outline; the cups sit at the top of the field, so this column is small in height.
- `Rand.pickOne` memory only lasts for the current page session.
- The waiting-slot shuffle uses its own `Math.random` code rather than `Rand.shuffle`.

**Requires verification:**
- Pastel contrast and pattern visibility on low-quality screens.
- Layout on short landscape screens.

No open GitHub issue concerns this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned. (Accepting a ball released anywhere above its cup is done, see issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173).)

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Sorting activities: [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md), [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md), [Koraliki](koraliki.md).
- Shared helper used: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) is **not** used.

## 21. Change history

- [#47](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/47) / [PR #76](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/76): activity introduced.
- [#121](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/121) / [PR #146](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/146): random colour and pattern combinations (8 sets).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): fixed on `main`; a ball released anywhere above its own cup is accepted and falls in with a glide of at most 700 ms.

```

```markdown
# Koparka

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Koparka |
| Activity ID | `koparka` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | The child drives an excavator with a finger: the arm scoops sand from a pile and tips it into a dump truck. The arm follows smoothly and cannot break. |
| Category | Control skill; cause and effect; open-ended play; calming |
| Interaction type | Finger/mouse drag anywhere on the screen, keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/koparka.js`](../../js/koparka.js), styles with prefix `kg-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A precise-movement activity with a multi-part arm and a safe, failure-free model; issue [#182](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/182).
- Differs from the other vehicle activities ([Traktor](traktor.md), [Autobusik](autobusik.md)) by direct control of an arm with three joints and a scoop-lift-drop sequence.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; an excavator (base, boom, arm, bucket) rests on the left, a sand pile lies in the middle and a dump truck waits on the right.
2. Interactions: the child drags a finger anywhere; the bucket glides to the finger.
3. Dragging the bucket through the sand fills it (sand grows in the bucket and the pile sinks). The bucket then carries the sand with its opening tilted up.
4. Releasing over the truck bed (generous zone around it, white outline while dragging over it) moves the bucket above the bed, tips it for 0.9 s and the sand falls into the truck.
5. After 3 scoops the truck wobbles (0.6 s), drives off to the right (1.3 s) and an empty truck of another colour drives in (1.5 s, about 4 s in all); the pile refills gently in the meantime.
6. Releasing anywhere else lowers the bucket to a rest pose by the base; carried sand stays in the bucket. The rounds repeat without end. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Follow | The bucket moves toward the finger with a damped glide (rate 9 per second), capped at 60% of the screen width per second. |
| Arm | Two links (boom 0.36, arm 0.30 of the scene width) solved by inverse kinematics, elbow up; the arm end is always computed from the elbow, so the parts stay connected. |
| Working area | The bucket stays inside the scene, above the ground, in front of the base and between a minimum and a maximum distance from the boom foot (0.14 and 0.97 x 0.66 of the scene width); a finger outside the area is clamped to it. |
| Scoop | Moving the bucket (while the finger is down or a key was just used) through the pile for 0.17 scene widths fills it; the pile drops by 0.12 of its height per scoop and never below 0.64, then refills during the truck swap. |
| Tip | The bucket glides to the point above the bed (at most 1.4 s), rotates to 115 degrees, sand drops for about 0.5 s, the load in the truck grows by a third. |
| Truck swap | After 3 scoops: wobble, exit, new truck, entry, settle (total about 4 s); tipping is not accepted until the truck has settled. |
| Elsewhere | A release that is not over the truck, or a cancelled drag, lowers the bucket to rest; nothing breaks or fails. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Text, faces, sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Fine control of movement and of a following object; cause and effect (scoop, carry, tip).

**Directly observable behavior**

- The bucket follows the finger smoothly and the arm bends so it stays connected; sand moves from the pile to the truck.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events on the whole stage (touch, mouse, stylus), so the touch area is the full screen; the bucket does not have to be grabbed.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to the bucket (a 56 px or larger button follows it, visible 4 px focus ring); arrow keys move it by 3.5% of the scene width per press; Enter or Space starts a scoop when the bucket is in the sand (it fills in 0.6 s) and tips it when it is full and over the truck bed.
- **Label (Polish):** "Koparka. Strzałki ruszają łyżką, Enter lub spacja nabiera piasek albo wysypuje go na ciężarówkę."; the SVG is decorative.
- **Non-colour cues:** the bed outline while a full bucket is over the truck; sand shape and pile height show the state.
- **Reduced motion:** all movement is driven from JavaScript (one rAF loop), so it behaves the same under `prefers-reduced-motion`; no end state exists only in a CSS keyframe.
- **Text:** none.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Visual quality (arm proportions, bucket shape, falling sand, truck wobble) has not been checked on a device (sections 17 and 18).
- The excavator is small on a narrow portrait screen (the scene is as wide as the screen).
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/koparka.js`](../../js/koparka.js): `SPEED` (0.6), `FOLLOW` (9), `DIG_LEN` (0.17), `SCOOP_DROP` (0.12), `SCOOPS_PER_TRUCK` (3), `KEY_SCOOP_S` (0.6), `POUR_S` (0.9), `BACK_S` (0.35), `WOBBLE_S`, `OUT_S`, `GAP_S`, `IN_S`, `SETTLE_S`, `REFILL_S`, the bucket angles and `TRUCK_COLORS`. Changing them needs a code edit.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything (sky, ground, pile, truck, excavator, sand) is inline SVG created by `js/koparka.js`; the menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

None. Trucks cycle through three colours in a fixed order; falling sand grains have a small random sideways spread.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A truck is full after 3 tipped scoops. Feedback: sand in the bucket and the truck, a falling stream, a wobble and a new truck. No failure state. The activity is open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/koparka.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant: 'scoop' })` when a scoop is filled, `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant: 'tip' })` when a full bucket is tipped and `Analytics.complete()` when a truck is full. All calls are wrapped so that nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. The activity is not in the module's `COMPLETABLE` list (it repeats endlessly), so exit-before-completion is not defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/koparka.js`](../../js/koparka.js) overrides `mount` of the `koparka` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.kg > svg.kg-svg (sky and ground, pile, truck, excavator and bucket, sand grains) + button.kg-bucket`; the SVG `viewBox` equals the pixel size of the stage and its elements are updated every frame.
- **State:** bucket position `T` glides toward the aim point `G`; scoop progress, a filled flag, a tip phase (`goto`, `pour`, `back`) and a truck phase (`wait`, `wobble`, `out`, `gap`, `in`, `settle`).
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, guarded by `!raf`, cancelled while the tab is hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`; it stops when nothing moves and restarts on input; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.kg` is fixed full-screen; all positions are pixels recomputed in `layout()` on `resize` and `orientationchange`. The scene width is `min(width, 1.4 x height)`, centred; every size is a fraction of it, so the arm geometry keeps its proportions in portrait and landscape (320 x 568 to 1920 x 1080).
- The ground line is at `min(76% of the height, 50% of the height + 0.45 x scene width)`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Finger outside the working area | The aim point is clamped to the nearest reachable point. |
| Very fast finger | The bucket speed is capped at 60% of the screen width per second. |
| Release elsewhere / cancelled drag | The bucket lowers to rest; carried sand stays. |
| Release over the truck while it is driving | Treated as elsewhere; the bucket rests with its sand. |
| Pile low | Never below 0.64 of its height, and it refills during every truck swap. |
| Resize / orientation | Layout recomputed; the bucket position is re-clamped. |
| Leaving mid-round | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag through the sand; sand grows in the bucket and the pile sinks.
- [ ] Release over the truck; the bucket moves above the bed, tips and the load grows.
- [ ] After 3 scoops the truck wobbles, leaves and an empty one arrives in about 4 s; the pile is full again.
- [ ] Release elsewhere; the bucket lowers to rest.
- [ ] Drag to the screen corners; the arm stays connected and the bucket stays in the working area.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the bucket, arrows, Enter/Space over the sand and over the truck.
- [ ] Rotate the device mid-round.
- [ ] Leave and reopen ten times quickly.
- [ ] Small screens (320 x 568, 568 x 320) and 1920 x 1080; reduced motion.

The PR for issue [#182](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/182) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM (arm connectivity, clamping, speed cap, three scoops and the truck swap, ten open/close cycles); no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel of the arm, bucket and falling sand, and the layout on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned. A separate issue covers a construction-site scene with several machines.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Traktor](traktor.md), [Autobusik](autobusik.md), [Myjnia](myjnia.md).
- No shared component is used besides `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#182](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/182): initial activity.

```
