## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/koraliki.md`

```markdown
# Koraliki

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Koraliki |
| Internal ID | `koraliki` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Eight big pastel beads in different shapes wait in a bowl; the child drags them onto a string to make a necklace. |
| Category | Coordination / open-ended play with a soft completion |
| Interaction type | Drag (pointer events); keyboard alternative (select a bead, then activate the string) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/koraliki.js`](../../js/koraliki.js), CSS block `/* Koraliki */` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (prefix `kr`) |

## 2. Business purpose

A simple threading game with no wrong answers: any bead can go on the string in any order. It gives a drag-and-drop activity with a tangible goal ("all eight on the string") and a gentle reward, without sorting rules. It sits between the single-tap activities (for example [Zabawa w chowanego](zabawa-w-chowanego.md)) and the sorting activities with correct targets ([Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md), [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md)): the only decision is where the bead is dropped, and a bead released away from the string simply returns.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#koraliki`); the scene is laid out and drawn immediately.
2. Eight beads rest in a bowl at the bottom (shuffled spots); a string with a knot on the left and an open end with a hook on the right is shown above.
3. The child drags a bead (touch, mouse or stylus). While dragging it follows the pointer and is kept within the visible screen.
4. On release within about 0.9 bead sizes of the string the bead glides to the next free place on the string; otherwise it glides back to its bowl spot.
5. A bead on the string can be dragged off again; the remaining beads close the gap.
6. When all eight beads are on the string (and nothing is moving) the necklace glows for 3 s; 4 s after completion started (1 s after the glow has faded) the beads leave the string, glide back to the bowl in a new order, and the activity is ready again.
7. Taking a bead off during this wait cancels the sequence.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (from `js/koraliki.js`) |
|---|---|
| Beads | `N = 8`: pink circle, blue square, green hexagon, purple diamond, yellow star, red heart, orange oval, mint flower |
| Drop test | Bead centre within `0.9 * S` of the string polyline (`nearString`, segment distance) |
| Slot on the string | Order of threading; slot `i` = i-th bead on the string; no choice of position |
| Glide duration (drop/return) | `min(1300, 600 + distance * 0.9)` ms; 300 ms when reduced motion is requested; 200 ms for re-layout glides |
| Completion glow | `GLOW_MS = 3000` ms, then `WAIT_MS = 4000` ms total before beads return |
| Bead size `S` | 56 to 84 px (see section 15) |
| Dragging limits | Bead centre clamped to keep the whole bead on the screen |
| Failure | None: a missed drop returns the bead; nothing is counted |

- A new bead is only accepted on the string when fewer than 8 are threaded (`string.length < N`), otherwise it returns home.
- Keyboard: Enter/Space (a `click` with `detail === 0`) on a bead in the bowl selects it (`aria-pressed`, visible outline); activating the "Nitka" button threads the selected bead; Enter on a threaded bead sends it home.
- Sound: none ([shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (design intent, not measured):
- Hand-eye coordination by dragging beads to a target line.
- Shape and colour recognition (eight distinct shapes in distinct colours).
- Cause and effect and a calm sense of accomplishment from the glow.

**Directly observable behavior:**
- Beads follow the finger, snap smoothly onto the string, and return when missed.
- The completed necklace glows softly and the beads are redistributed.
- No scores, timers or failure messages exist.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about motor skill, concentration or developmental benefit; the repository contains no such evidence.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) with per-bead pointer capture, `touch-action: none`; keyboard alternative described in section 4 using native `<button>` elements and a 4 px `:focus-visible` outline (`#8f7fd1`).
- **Screen readers:** beads have Polish `aria-label`s such as "Koralik: różowe kółko (Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz nitkę)" that change when the bead is on the string; `aria-pressed` marks the selected bead; the string button is labelled "Nitka (wybierz koralik, potem nitkę)". The glow is not announced.
- **Target size:** beads are 56 to 84 px (`min-width/min-height: 56px`); the string drop zone is the whole row height.
- **Orientation:** works in portrait and landscape; narrow screens use two string rows and a 4x2 bowl (section 15). Layout is recomputed on resize/orientation change; an active drag is cancelled and the bead returns home.
- **Colour:** each bead has a different shape as well as colour, so colour is not the only cue. No decision depends on colour.
- **Reduced motion:** the global rule does not affect it because all movement and glow come from a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with inline styles; glides shorten to 300 ms with `prefers-reduced-motion`. The glow is still shown (opacity/drop-shadow changes).
- **Reading:** none required. Independent use by a young child is the design aim.
- **Limitations:** the glow overlay and bead drop-shadows are not accessible to screen readers; the bead position on the string cannot be chosen.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Very short two-row screens (about 568x320 landscape or narrow phones) can make the bowl and the second string row touch because beads stay at least 56 px; PR [#72](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/72) flagged this for a manual check on a small phone.
- The 3 s glow and 4 s wait are fixed; a child who is still playing is not affected because touching a bead cancels the sequence.
- No colour-only reliance. No privacy concerns: nothing stored or sent.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants are inside [`js/koraliki.js`](../../js/koraliki.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | Number of beads / string slots | number | 8 | top of IIFE (the shapes list `DEFS` has 8 entries; changing `N` alone is not supported) |
| `GLOW_MS` | Glow duration | ms | 3000 | top of IIFE |
| `WAIT_MS` | Time after completion before beads return | ms | 4000 | top of IIFE |
| `DEFS` | Label, colour, glow colour and SVG path per bead | array | 8 entries | top of IIFE |
| Layout numbers | margin `m = 12`, `extra = 78`, pitch `1.04 * S`, S range 56-84, drop radius `0.9 * S` | numbers | see `layout()` and `nearString()` | functions |

No fallback for invalid values because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external files. Beads are inline SVG built by `beadSvg(def)` (shape path plus a white centre dot and a highlight). The bowl, string, knot and hook are SVG drawn into `.kr-deco` by `drawDeco()` (bowl `#fbe7c8`, string `#c9a0c0`). The background is a CSS gradient (`#fdf0d5` to `#e6e0f7`) and the glow is a CSS radial gradient on `.kr-glow`. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, images or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- Bowl spot per bead: `shuffled(N)` at mount (Fisher-Yates over 8 indices).
- After each completed necklace: a new shuffle that must differ from the previous order (up to 20 attempts, `shuffled(N, avoid)`; after 20 failures the same order could in principle be kept, which has probability near zero).
- A bead sent home (dropped away from the string or taken off) returns to its own bowl spot; spots change only after a completed necklace.
- The shuffle uses its own `Math.random` code, not `window.Rand`. Nothing is stored; a new random order is created each time the activity is opened.
- There are no value pools beyond the fixed eight beads.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. Every round has eight beads and the same rules; nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion: eight beads on the string with all beads idle.
- Feedback: soft warm glow behind the string (`.kr-glow` radial gradient) and a coloured drop-shadow on each bead, easing in over about 450 ms; glow lasts 3 s.
- After 4 s in total the beads glide back to the bowl in a new order and the activity continues automatically.
- Failure: none; a missed drop returns the bead. No sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/koraliki.js`](../../js/koraliki.js), replacing `mount` of the `koraliki` registry entry; returns `cleanup`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `div.kr > div.kr-glow + div.kr-field`; the field holds an SVG `.kr-deco` (bowl, string, knot, hook), 8 `button.kr-bead` and one transparent `button.kr-string` that covers the string rows (used for keyboard threading).
- **State:** per bead `{ def, el, home, onString, mode ('idle' | 'drag' | 'glide'), pid, x, y, glide fields }`; global `string` (ordered beads on the string), `slots`, `homes`, `pts` (string polyline), `selected`, `doneT`, `doneGlow`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown/move/up/cancel` and `lostpointercapture` per bead; `click` for keyboard; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Animation:** one `frame()` loop (dt capped at 50 ms) using smoothstep glides; it keeps running only while something is moving or glowing and is restarted by `start()`. It is paused when the tab is hidden.
- **Completion logic:** `string.length === N` and all beads idle starts `doneT`; at `GLOW_MS + WAIT_MS` the beads are released with a new order.
- **Dependencies:** none (no `Rand`, no `Animals`). **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** none from the activity itself (reported by `js/app.js`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the three window/document listeners, removes the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.kr` is fixed full-screen; `.kr-field` is inset by the safe-area variables, 64 px at the top and 12 px on the other sides. All coordinates are CSS pixels relative to the field's top-left (`fw` x `fh` from `getBoundingClientRect`).
- `layout()` chooses one string row if `(fw - 2*12 - 78) / (8 * 1.04) >= 56`, otherwise two rows of four. Bead size `S = max(56, min(84, row size, height-based size))`.
- The bowl is one row of eight if the width allows (`fw - 24 >= 9 * clamp(sw, 56, 84)`), otherwise 4x2. It sits at the bottom of the field.
- The string polyline `pts` is knot, each slot, open end; on two rows an extra cubic curve joins slot 4 to slot 5 in the drawing. The drop test uses the straight segments of `pts`.
- Beads, string, bowl and decoration share the field's coordinate space (SVG `width/height/viewBox` set to `fw x fh`). The global `.stage svg` rule (120 px) beats the `width`/`height` attributes, so `drawDeco()` also sets the SVG's size inline (`deco.style.width/height = fw/fh px`), and the `.stage .kr-deco` rule sets `width: 100%; height: 100%`; the string and bowl therefore fill the play area instead of shrinking to 120 px at the top-left (issues [#130](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/130) and [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)).
- On resize every bead is re-placed at its target; active drags are cancelled and the bead returns home.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | N/A (inline SVG) |
| Resize / rotation | `layout()` and `start()`; dragged bead returns home, glides continue to the new target |
| Backgrounding | Loop paused when hidden; restarted on return; completion timers only advance while visible |
| Rapid or multi-touch input | A bead ignores a second pointer while it already has one (`pid`); each bead captures its own pointer, so several beads can be dragged at once |
| Pointer cancel / lost capture | Handled as release (`up`): the bead is threaded if near the string, otherwise returns |
| Release while string full | Bead returns home (the 8-slot string cannot take a ninth) |
| Dragging out of the screen | Bead centre clamped to the visible window |
| Right mouse button | Ignored (`e.button > 0`) |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` cancels the frame; state is local |
| Synthetic pointers | `setPointerCapture` wrapped in `try/catch` |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#72](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/72) reports a stub-DOM run in Node at four viewport sizes (threading 8 beads in order, glow then return in a new order, far drop returns home, simultaneous pointers/cancel leave no stuck bead, node count constant) and lists manual tests as pending; PR [#155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155) reports `node --check` only and asks for a visual check. The script is not in the repository. Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: drag a bead onto the string; it glides to the next free place.
- [ ] Drag a bead and release far from the string; it glides back to its bowl spot.
- [ ] Drag a threaded bead off; the others close the gap.
- [ ] Completion: thread all eight; the glow shows for about 3 s and the beads return in a different order after about 4 s.
- [ ] Take a bead off during the wait; the sequence is cancelled.
- [ ] Restart: leave and reopen; the bowl order is different.
- [ ] Randomization: order differs after each completed necklace.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that nothing changes between rounds.
- [ ] Portrait (about 360x640): two string rows, beads at least 56 px, bowl not overlapping the second row.
- [ ] Landscape (about 640x360 and 568x320): one or two rows; check the bowl and string do not collide.
- [ ] Touch: two fingers dragging two beads at once; no bead gets stuck.
- [ ] Mouse: drag with the left button; right button does nothing.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to a bead, Enter selects it, Enter on "Nitka" threads it, Enter on a threaded bead removes it.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: glides are short (about 300 ms) and the glow still appears.
- [ ] Background the tab during the glow and return; the sequence resumes.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from code reading):**
- No automated tests.
- The bead's position on the string cannot be chosen; beads always go to the next free slot in drop order.
- Bead shuffle does not use the shared `Rand.shuffle`.

**Requires verification:**
- Overlap of bowl and second string row on very short screens (flagged in PR #72).
- Behaviour of the transparent string button for assistive technology (it covers the whole string area and has a label asking the user to select a bead first).

No open GitHub issue concerns this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other drag-to-target activities with a soft glow on completion: [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md), [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md), [Wieża z Klocków](wieza-z-klockow.md), [Puzzle](puzzle.md).
- The "select then activate target" keyboard pattern is shared in spirit with those activities (see their documents).
- Shared helpers (`js/random.js`, `js/animals.js`) are **not** used by this activity.

## 21. Change history

- [#62](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/62) / [PR #72](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/72): activity introduced; moved to the end of the activity list after review (commit `a1024e0`).
- [#130](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/130) / [PR #155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155): layout fix so the string and bowl SVG fill the field.
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): fixed on `main`; the inline size in `drawDeco()` makes the string and bowl fill the play area.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/kulkowy-tor.md`

```markdown
# Kulkowy Tor

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#217](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/217)
- Planned activity id: `kulkowy`
- Planned CSS prefix: `mt-`

## 1. Overview

Kulkowy Tor (`kulkowy`, module `js/kulkowy.js`, CSS prefix `mt-`): a soft red ball is dropped from the top and rolls down four ramps; the child turns the ramps to change where it goes. The ball ends in a basket with a friendly bear or on a cushion at the bottom edge.

## 2. Business purpose

Gentle cause and effect with simple, scripted physics where the child changes the path; unlike Ścieżka (follows a drawn line) the child shapes the route. No failure: the ball always finds a safe way down and starts again.

## 3. Activity flow

1. Four ramps are shown with a small arrangement chosen at random on every start. 2. The child touches a ramp to turn it (left, flat, right, left, ...) and touches the big ball button to drop a ball. 3. The ball falls from the hatch, follows the ramps it meets and reaches the basket or the cushion in about 4.5-5.7 s. 4. In the basket the bear catches it and waves; on the cushion the ball squashes, fades and reappears at the top after 1 s and falls again. 5. After three balls in the basket the track glows for 3 s and the ramps move to a new arrangement.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Board | 400x360 units scaled to the screen; ramps at (200,72), (95,152), (305,152), (200,232); half length 65 units (130 long), tilt 22 degrees |
| Turn | Each touch cycles left, flat, right, left; the turn takes 0.4 s (smoothstep) and can be restarted at any time |
| Drop | Big button (72 px) releases a ball at x=190 above ramp 1; ignored while a ball is in play (at most one ball) |
| Speed | One constant speed of 80 units/s for falling and sliding (22% of the board height per second, cap is 40%); every one of the 81 arrangements arrives in 4.5-5.7 s |
| Sliding | The ball follows the ramp's current target: left or right slides to that end; flat slides to the nearer end (x below the ramp centre = left). Turning a ramp under the ball sends it the other way, so it never gets stuck |
| Landing | A falling ball lands on the first ramp whose span contains its x; leaving an end it falls on and meets the next ramp or the floor |
| Basket | Opening x 250-342; the ball dropping in counts as one caught ball; the bear raises both paws and waves for 1.6 s |
| Cushion | Anywhere else on the bottom edge; squash 0.3 s, fade-out from 0.7 s, back at the top at 1 s (0.3 s fade-in), then it falls again by itself |
| Round | Three balls in the basket light the three picture pips; the track glows (static drop-shadow) for 3 s and the ramps turn to a new random arrangement, different from the one they were left in and from the previous starting arrangement |

No score, no failure, no stored data, no text on screen.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

Cause and effect, planning a path in advance, comparing three positions of an object, patience while watching a motion.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

Ramps are focusable buttons (width = ramp length, at least 56 px high, ramps at least 80 px long down to 568x320); Tab goes through ramps 1-4 and then the drop button, Enter/Space activates. The tilt of the ramp is the non-colour cue; aria labels give the ramp number and position in Polish. The drop button is 72 px and shows a ball. Ramps and button are click-based, so two fingers cannot break the state.

## 7. Risks and limitations

Only checked with a node stub DOM and XML-style review of the markup; no real browser or device test was possible, so visual proportions (bear, basket) still need a manual look. Constant speed makes falling look floaty.

## 8. Configuration

None; there is no setting. The activity is enabled by default and appended at the end of the menu list.

## 9. Assets

Inline SVG scene (sky, hatch, ramps, cushion, basket, bear, pips) built in `scene()`; menu icon in `js/activities.js`. No sound, no external files.

## 10. Randomization and variants

The starting arrangement of the ramps is random on every mount and after every third basket ball (never equal to the arrangement just left nor to the previous starting arrangement).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None: the same rules throughout.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A ball in the basket: bear waves 1.6 s, one more pip fills. Third ball: glow for 3 s and new arrangement. Cushion: soft squash and the ball returns to the top.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Each ramp turn: `track('interaction', {variant: 'ramp1'..'ramp4'})`; each drop: `track('interaction', {variant: 'ball'})`; each ball in the basket: `complete()`. Automatic re-drops from the cushion and arrangement changes after a round are not reported.

## 14. Technical implementation

`mount` builds the DOM, attaches the root with `container.appendChild(root)`, and returns a cleanup that cancels the rAF loop and removes the resize, orientation and visibility listeners and the root. One rAF loop (dt capped at 0.05 s, stopped when idle or hidden, restarted on `visibilitychange`) advances the ramp angles, the ball state machine (`enter`, `fall`, `slide`, `cushion`, `basket`), the glow timer and the bear's wave. All final states are drawn by the loop, so reduced motion does not disable them.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Board aspect 400/360 sized by CSS (`.mt-board`); portrait stacks board over the drop button, landscape puts the button to its right. `layout()` only repositions the transparent ramp buttons from the board width, so rotation or resize keeps every state. SVG sizing uses `.stage .mt-svg` and `.stage .mt-dropsvg`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

Rotation and resize during any state: only button positions are recomputed. Tab hidden: loop pauses, dt cap prevents a jump. Fast repeated touches on a ramp: each touch restarts the 0.4 s turn from the current angle. Second drop while a ball is in play: ignored. Ramp turned under the ball: the ball reverses; a falling ball landing in the swept band of a rising ramp lands on it.

## 17. Testing

Manual scenarios: (1) Open the activity: four ramps in a random arrangement, drop button visible below (portrait) or at the right (landscape). (2) Touch ramp 1: it turns in 0.4 s through left, flat, right. (3) Touch drop: one ball falls; touching again meanwhile does nothing. (4) Set ramp 1 right, ramp 3 left, ramp 4 right and drop three times: bear catches, pips fill, then the track glows 3 s and the ramps move. (5) Leave ramps on a cushion route: ball returns to the top after 1 s. (6) Tab through ramps and the drop button, use Enter/Space. (7) Rotate the device in the middle of a fall. (8) Enable reduced motion and repeat 2-4. Automated check used in development: a node stub-DOM harness ran all 81 arrangements (arrival 4.5-5.7 s) and a three-ball round.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

Interpretation: after the cushion the ball is dropped again automatically (the issue says it 'starts again'). A flat ramp always sends a ball entering left of the centre to the left, so ramp 1 flat always leads left. No real-device verification.

## 19. Planned improvements

None planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

Ścieżka (a different mechanic: follows a line), Wiatraczki (same single-rAF-loop pattern).

## 21. Change history

Initial implementation (issue #217).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/latarka.md`

```markdown
# Latarka

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Latarka |
| Activity ID | `latarka` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A dark pastel room is explored with a torch: a soft beam follows the finger and reveals three hidden animals and three hidden toys. |
| Category | Control skill; cause and effect; discovery; calming |
| Interaction type | Finger/mouse drag or tap anywhere, keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/latarka.js`](../../js/latarka.js), styles with prefix `fl-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- Revealing hidden things by moving a light; issue [#212](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/212).
- Differs from [Chowany](zabawa-w-chowanego.md) (taps on hiding places) and [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md) (only draws) by discovery with a moving light.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; a dark room (about 85% dim) shows only a soft round beam in the middle.
2. Touching or dragging moves the beam with a soft lag. Crossing the screen takes at least 1.6 s.
3. An animal or toy that is more than half inside the beam fades in (0.45 s). An animal waves (a small tilt), a toy bounces once (1.2 s).
4. A revealed item stays visible while lit and fades out 2 s after the light has left it (0.6 s fade).
5. When all six were revealed at least once, the room lights up slowly (3 s), then darkens again (1.5 s) with a new random arrangement. There is no end. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Darkness | Overlay alpha 0.85 outside the beam, transparent inside 45% of the radius, full darkness at the radius. |
| Beam | Radius `max(90 px, 18% of the shorter side)`; damped follow (rate 6/s) with speed capped at width / 1.6 s. |
| Items | 3 random animals (`Animals.pick(3)`) and 3 of 6 toys (ball, block, car, drum, star, boat), at random places below the Back button row, spaced at least 1.25 item sizes apart when room allows. Item size `clamp(17% of the shorter side, 64, 110)` px. |
| Layout | New on every launch and every new room, never identical to the previous layout in this page session. |
| Reveal | 25 sample points of the item disc; more than half inside the beam lights it. |
| Action | One wave / bounce each time an item is lit from dark. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. No text; the room is decorative. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Smooth control of a following object; cause and effect (light reveals); object permanence in a playful setting.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The beam follows the finger smoothly; items appear when lit and fade later.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events on the whole room (touch, mouse, stylus); a second finger is ignored. A mouse moves the beam on hover.
- **Keyboard:** Tab focuses the room (visible focus ring); arrows move the beam by 8% of the width; Enter or Space reveals what is under the beam.
- **Labels (Polish):** "Latarka. Strzałki przesuwają światło, Enter lub spacja pokazuje to, co jest w świetle."; items are decorative.
- **Non-colour cues:** meaning is carried by the pictures (animal faces, toy shapes); colour is not needed.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion (beam, fades, wave, bounce, glow) comes from one JavaScript loop, so every state is reached; nothing is faster than 2 tilts per second, no flashing.
- **Text:** none. Items are 64 px or larger.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Look and feel (beam softness, darkness level, toy drawings) has not been checked on a device.
- The loop runs while something moves or fades and rests when the beam has settled and nothing is changing; input, resize and returning to the tab restart it.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/latarka.js`](../../js/latarka.js): `DIM`, `FOLLOW`, `CROSS_S`, `LIGHT_S`, `HOLD_S`, `FADE_S`, `GLOW_S`, `DARKEN_S`, `ACT_S`, `KEY_STEP`, `SAMPLES` and the `TOYS` table.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Animals come from `window.Animals`; toys are inline SVG in `js/latarka.js`; the menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Animals via `Animals.pick(3)`, toys shuffled from 6, positions random with a spacing rule. The layout key of the previous room is remembered for this page session only, so two rooms in a row are never identical.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

Feedback: fade-in, wave or bounce, and the room glow. Completion: all six items revealed at least once in a room; the room lights up for 3 s and a new one follows. Open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Reports to `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). Beam moves are not reported. `track('interaction', { variant })` is called on the first reveal of each item in a room, with the item id (animal id or toy id) as variant. `complete()` is called once for each fully lit room. All calls are wrapped so nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. Data stays on the device; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/latarka.js`](../../js/latarka.js) overrides `mount` of the `latarka` entry; returns a cleanup function that cancels the frame and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Rendering:** `div.fl > div.fl-dark (two radial gradients driven by CSS variables --fl-x, --fl-y, --fl-r, --fl-a) + div.fl-items > div.fl-item`.
- **State:** beam and aim points, item list (fraction position, lit level, hold timer, revealed flag, action timer), phase (`play`, `glow`, `darken`).
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s; it rests when the beam has settled in the play phase and no item is fading or acting, and restarts on pointer/key input, resize and `visibilitychange` (cancelled while the tab is hidden). Nothing is lit or reported before the first input of a room.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.fl` is fixed full-screen. Items keep fractional positions inside the area below the Back button row, so rotation and resize keep state (beam and aim points are rescaled). Beam radius and item size follow the shorter side.
- Works from 320 px wide down to 568 x 320, portrait and landscape.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Resize / orientation | Layout recomputed; the beam and items keep their state. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| Fast repeated touches | The aim point changes; the beam speed stays capped. |
| Two fingers | The second pointer is ignored. |
| Beam stays over an item | It stays lit. |
| Leaving mid-room | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag across the room; the beam lags softly and crossing takes at least 1.5 s.
- [ ] Move the beam over an item until it is half covered; it fades in, waves or bounces once.
- [ ] Move the light away; the item stays 2 s and then fades.
- [ ] Reveal all six; the room lights up for 3 s and a new arrangement follows.
- [ ] Reopen several times; the layouts differ.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab, arrows (8% steps), Enter/Space.
- [ ] Rotate mid-room; use two fingers; hide and show the tab.
- [ ] 320 x 568, 568 x 320, reduced motion.

The PR for issue [#212](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/212) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM (six items, all reveal events, one `complete()`, new room); no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Chowany](zabawa-w-chowanego.md), [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md), [Cienie](cienie.md).
- Uses `window.Animals`, `window.Rand` and `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#212](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/212): initial activity.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/latawiec.md`

```markdown
# Latawiec

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Latawiec |
| Activity ID | `latawiec` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A pastel sky with a hill, a random animal holding the kite string, a randomly designed kite (six shapes) with a ribbon tail of 5 bows and three clouds. The kite follows the child's finger softly. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, coordination |
| Interaction type | Touch/drag in the sky (follow), tap the animal |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |

Source: [`js/latawiec.js`](../../js/latawiec.js), CSS prefix `lw-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html). Introduced by issue #99 / PR [#162](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/162).

## 2. Business purpose

- Gives direct, continuous control: the kite goes where the finger goes, but always with a soft lag and a speed limit, so it never jumps (crossing the screen takes at least 3 seconds).
- When the finger is lifted the kite does not stop abruptly; it drifts and settles into a slow figure-eight, so the scene stays alive without input.
- It is the only scene in the playground group ([Karuzela](karuzela.md), [Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md)) that tracks a finger position continuously.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; `mount(container)` builds the scene and starts the loop immediately.
2. The kite hovers in a slow figure-eight near the upper middle of the sky; three clouds sit in the sky and the animal stands on the hill.
3. The child can touch or drag anywhere in the scene (except on the animal), or tap the animal. Keyboard users can move the kite with the arrow keys.
4. While a finger is down the kite follows it on a damped spring, the tail follows the kite's earlier path, and clouds the kite touches puff aside. Tapping the animal makes it wave.
5. There is no completion state.
6. When the finger is lifted, the kite drifts on and settles into the figure-eight around its position within about 4 s.
7. A new scene with a new animal is created each time the activity is opened.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Steering | Only the first pointer steers (`pid`); a second finger is ignored while the first is down. Pressing on the animal button does not steer. |
| Target clamping | The finger target is clamped to the kite bounds x 28-372, y 36-140 board units (`KX0`, `KX1`, `KY0`, `KY1`). The kite therefore stays in the upper part of the board. |
| Motion | Damped spring: `v += (SK * (target - pos) - SD * v) * dt` with `SK` = 6 and `SD` = 4.4; speed capped at `VMAX` = 110 board units per second; position clamped to the bounds (velocity zeroed at the walls). |
| Release | The hover centre is set to the position plus half the velocity (clamped so the figure-eight fits); the figure-eight amplitude fades in smoothly over `SETTLE` = 4 s. |
| Figure-eight | x amplitude `HA` = 26, y amplitude `HB` = 11 units, period 10 s (`HW` = 2π/10). |
| Tilt | The kite rotates with horizontal speed (up to 18 degrees) plus a slow 3 degree wobble, smoothed. |
| Tail | 5 bows, bow i samples the kite's position history at lag `i * 0.22` s (`LAG`), offset i * 15 units below the kite, plus a small sinusoidal wave; all points are clamped inside the board (8-unit margin). History is kept for `BOWS * LAG + 0.5` s. |
| String | A quadratic curve from the animal's right paw (about (51, 221)) to the kite, with the control point sagging 20 units below the midpoint. |
| Clouds | Three clouds at (84, 52, scale 1), (236, 38, 0.85), (334, 92, 1.05). When the kite centre is closer than `46 * scale` units, the cloud moves 46 units sideways (away from the kite, clamped to x 40-360) and swells by about 10% for 1.2 s. It returns once the kite is more than 100 units away horizontally from the cloud's home position. |
| Animal | Tap: waves for `WAVE_T` = 1.6 s. |
| Keyboard | On the kite button, ArrowLeft/Right move the hover centre by 50 units and ArrowUp/Down by 35 units (clamped); ignored while a pointer drag is active. |

No sound, scoring or failure state.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect and hand-eye coordination: the kite follows the finger.
- Calm observation: the tail, string and clouds respond slowly.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Movement is rate-limited and smoothed, so fast finger movement does not produce fast kite movement.
- After release the kite settles into a slow figure-eight.
- Clouds step aside when the kite touches them.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on motor control, tracking or attention is not established by the code and is not claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) on the whole scene; one finger only. Keyboard: the kite button (`aria-label` "Latawiec – strzałki przesuwają latawiec") accepts arrow keys; Enter/Space have no effect. The animal button supports click, Enter and Space.
- **Targets:** the whole sky is a touch area; the kite button is `max(56, 56k)` px square and follows the kite; the animal button is `max(56, 60k)` x `max(56, 64k)` px.
- **Labels:** the animal button is labelled "<name> – pomachaj"; the SVG scene is `aria-hidden`.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible` outline 4px `#8f7fd1` on both buttons.
- **Orientation:** the board keeps its 400:300 ratio and is sized `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 400/300)`, so it works in portrait (smaller) and landscape.
- **Colour:** the kite and bows use several colours (the kite's colour set is random) but nothing depends on colour.
- **Reduced motion:** motion is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop and is not disabled by the global rule; there is no separate reduced-motion variant (motion is slow and speed-capped).
- **Reading:** none required; suitable for a young child to use independently.
- **Limitations:** the scene sets `touch-action: none`; the keyboard only moves the kite in steps and has no way to "drag".

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The loop never stops while the activity is open (it re-requests a frame every time, unlike Zjeżdżalnia and Huśtawka), so it continuously uses CPU on slow devices; it is paused only while the tab is hidden.
- A child may drag over the whole screen quickly; this is safe because the speed is capped.
- The kite area is limited to the upper part of the board (y up to 140 of 300 units).
- Visual check in a real browser is not documented.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in [`js/latawiec.js`](../../js/latawiec.js) and require a code change. Nothing is stored; no fallback logic.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BW` x `BH` | 400 x 300 | Board units |
| `KX0`, `KX1`, `KY0`, `KY1` | 28, 372, 36, 140 | Kite centre bounds |
| `VMAX`, `SK`, `SD` | 110 units/s, 6, 4.4 | Speed cap, spring stiffness, damping |
| `HA`, `HB`, `HW`, `SETTLE` | 26, 11, 2π/10, 4 s | Figure-eight amplitudes, angular speed, settle time |
| `BOWS`, `LAG` | 5, 0.22 s | Tail bows and lag per bow |
| `AX`, `AY`, `AS` | 70, 234, 0.9 | Animal feet position and scale |
| `CLOUDS` | 3 entries | Cloud x, y, scale |
| `BOW_COLS` | 5 colours | Bow colours |
| `WAVE_T`, `MAX_DT` | 1.6 s, 0.05 s | Wave length, frame time cap |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The sky, sun, clouds, hills, grass, animal, string, tail, bows and kite are inline SVG produced by `scene()`; the animal uses `Animals.head(id, { body: true })`. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- One animal per `mount` from `Animals.pick(1)[0]` (13 animals, uniform; see [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js), [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)). Not persisted; the same animal can repeat.
- One kite per `mount`, built from three independent random picks with `Rand.pickOne` (keys `latawiec-design`, `latawiec-colours`, `latawiec-pattern`; the same pick is not repeated twice in a row within one page session): six designs (diamond, dragon, airplane, butterfly, star, heart) x five colour sets (`PALETTES`) x four patterns (`plain`, `quarters`, `stripes`, `dots`; the second or third colour of the set is laid over the main one and clipped to the kite outline). Not persisted. Tail, physics and touch targets do not depend on the design.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression or levels. Nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- No completion state; open-ended.
- Feedback is visual only: the kite, tail, string, clouds and the animal's wave.
- No failure; no sound; the loop runs continuously.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` assigned to the registry entry `latawiec`; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** one SVG (`viewBox 0 0 400 300`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`) inside `.lw-board`, updated every frame through attributes (`transform`, path `d`); two transparent `<button>`s (animal and kite) sit on top for accessibility and focus.
- **Kite look:** `DESIGNS`, `PALETTES`, `PATTERNS` and `kiteSvg(design, palette, pattern)` build the kite group inside `scene(def, kite)`; picked once in `mount`.
- **State:** kite `x, y, vx, vy, tilt`; hover centre `cx, cy`, phase `th`, `tFree`; `dragging`, `pid`, target `tx, ty`; `hist[]` position history; per-cloud `{ ox, side, away, pulse }`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`/`paint`) with capped dt. It starts in `mount`, continues forever and is cancelled only while `document.hidden`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel` on the root element (pointer coordinates converted with `getBoundingClientRect` to board units); `click` on the animal; `keydown` on the kite button; `resize`/`orientationchange` call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes window/document listeners and removes the root node (root listeners go with the node).
- **Dependencies:** `window.Animals`. No persistence or analytics integration. See [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board 400 x 300 units, scale `k = board.clientWidth / 400`; everything (scene, kite, tail, string, clouds) lives in the one SVG space, so scaling needs no recomputation.
- Pointer positions are converted to board units with the current `getBoundingClientRect` and clamped to the kite bounds, so the kite stays fully on screen after orientation change.
- The animal button is placed from board units (`AX`, `AY`) times `k`; the kite button follows the kite at `max(56, 56k)` px.
- Tail points are clamped to 8 units inside the board edges.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/orientation change: `layout()` repositions the buttons; kite state is in board units and is unaffected.
- Backgrounding: the loop is cancelled while hidden and restarted with a fresh `last`; dt capped at 0.05 s.
- Touch cancellation: `pointercancel` is treated like release (kite drifts on and settles).
- Second finger: ignored while a pointer is active; arrow keys are ignored during a drag.
- Pointer leaves the board: the target is clamped to the bounds.
- Missing assets / empty pools: not applicable (inline SVG, 13 animals).
- Pointer capture is not used, so if a pointer is released outside the window the `pointerup` may not arrive on the root (see section 18).

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#162](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/162) reports `node --check` and a node stub-DOM simulation covering hover, drag speed cap, off-screen drag, multi-pointer (second finger ignored), release settling, fast zigzag drag and cloud puff/return, and states it was not checked in a real browser or on a device.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: touch and drag across the sky; the kite follows with a soft lag, never jumping, and the tail waves along its earlier path.
- [ ] Fast drag across the full width; the kite's speed stays capped.
- [ ] Release: lift the finger; the kite drifts and settles into a slow figure-eight within about 4 s.
- [ ] Touch in the lower part of the screen; the kite stays in the upper area.
- [ ] Cloud: steer the kite into each cloud; the cloud puffs aside and returns after the kite leaves.
- [ ] Tap the animal; it waves for about 1.6 s and the kite is not steered.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no end state.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: use two fingers; the second is ignored.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and re-enter; a fresh scene, usually with a different animal.
- [ ] Randomization: enter several times; the animal and the kite (shape, colours, pattern) vary.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape on phone and tablet; rotate while the kite is flying; the kite remains fully visible.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard: Tab to the kite button and use the arrow keys; Tab to the animal and press Enter.
- [ ] Release the pointer outside the browser window or board; the kite should not remain stuck in follow mode.
- [ ] Background the tab and return; no jump.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: the kite still flies.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; no documented real-device verification.
- The kite design (six shapes, five colour sets, four patterns) is random per start and not stored; the former single-design limitation is fixed on `main` (issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)).
- The kite's clip path uses the fixed id `lw-kclip`; this is harmless because only one Latawiec scene is mounted at a time.
- The animation loop never idles.

**Requires verification**

- `setPointerCapture` is not used; whether a pointer released outside the window leaves the kite in follow mode (`dragging` stays true until a `pointerup`/`pointercancel` is delivered to the root) has not been tested.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (the random kite design from issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) is done, see section 21).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar scenes: [Karuzela](karuzela.md), [Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md); [Wiatraczki](wiatraczki.md) also reacts to a sliding finger.
- Shared helper: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`), which uses [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js).
- Reference for the damped-spring follow: the "smooth redirect" convention used by other vehicle activities (not linked here because those documents are separate).

## 21. Change history

- Issue #99, PR [#162](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/162): activity added (commit b13a2e7).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): random kite per launch (six designs, five colour sets, four patterns); tail, physics and targets unchanged.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/literki.md`

```markdown
# Literki

> Documents the current implementation on `main`. Shared platform behaviour (no sound, global reduced-motion rule, menu configuration, playtime, absence of automated tests, analytics status) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Literki |
| Activity ID | `literki` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | One big letter (capital and small, for example "Aa") on a soft card with a drawn picture of something that starts with it. Touching the picture wiggles it and shows its Polish word for about 3 s; touching the letter makes it glow; arrows or a swipe move to the next or previous letter. |
| Category | Exploratory (letters) |
| Interaction type | Tap and swipe |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/literki.js`](../../js/literki.js), data [`js/literki-data.js`](../../js/literki-data.js), CSS prefix `lt-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A parent-and-child letter picture book: the child sees large letters with friendly pictures, and the parent can read the word shown under the picture. It is the only activity in the application that introduces the Polish alphabet. There are no scores or wrong answers.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the first letter of a random order is shown at once (no fade-in).
2. The card shows the letter (for example "Aa") and a picture (for example an arbuz for A).
3. The child can touch the picture, touch the letter, press an arrow, or swipe the card horizontally.
4. Picture: it wiggles (0.8 s) and its word appears below it for about 3 s, then fades out (0.5 s).
5. Letter: it glows softly for 1 s.
6. Arrow or swipe: the card slides out and the next (or previous) letter slides in (0.5 s in total). The picture shown is a random one of the letter's pictures.
7. After the last letter of a round, going forward starts a new random round. Nothing changes on its own; there is no completion state.
8. The child leaves with the Back button.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Letters | 32 (Polish alphabet): A Ą B C Ć D E Ę F G H I J K L Ł M N Ń O Ó P R S Ś T U W Y Z Ź Ż |
| Pictures per letter | 2, or 3 for ten letters (B, D, G, J, K, L, O, P, S, T); 74 pictures in total |
| Slide | 0.5 s (`SLIDE_S`); card fades out for the first half and in for the second half; the letter is swapped at the midpoint; slide offset 60 px |
| Wiggle | 0.8 s (`WIGGLE_S`), up to 7 degrees |
| Word display | visible 3 s (`WORD_S`) after 0.25 s fade-in, 0.5 s fade-out (`WORD_FADE_S`) |
| Glow | 1 s (`GLOW_S`), `drop-shadow` up to 22 px |
| Swipe | horizontal movement over 60 px between `pointerdown` and `pointerup` on the card; left goes next, right goes previous |
| Input during a slide | ignored (`go()` returns while a slide is running); picture and letter touches are still accepted |
| Order | all 32 letters once per round in random order, then a new random round |

Words with a flag `c: 1` do not start with the letter (there is no suitable native word); they are shown as "<word> · <letter> w słowie" ("letter in the word"). The 10 flagged pictures are: Ą (ząb, wąż), Ć (kość), Ę (gęś, ręka), Ń (słoń, koń), Ó (żółw), Y (mydło, tygrys). Ą, Ę, Ń and Y therefore have only such words; Ć and Ó have one normal word each (ćma, ósemka).

Going back from the first letter of a round wraps to the last letter of the same round order.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**: early exposure to letter shapes and to the words that start with them (with a parent reading the word), visual perception, calm independent exploration.

**Directly observable behavior**
- The letter is large (110-220px), shown as capital and small; the word is small and meant for the parent.
- The child controls the pace; nothing changes by itself.
- The word is shown only after touching the picture.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**
- Whether the activity helps letter recognition or reading readiness.
- Whether words with the "w słowie" notation (letter inside the word) are understandable for a parent and not confusing.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse, stylus (buttons plus pointer-event swipe) and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space on the arrows, letter and picture buttons; there are no arrow-key shortcuts). 4px focus outlines.
- **Target size:** arrows 60 x 60px; letter button at least 96px (font size `clamp(110px, 30vmin, 220px)`); picture button `clamp(96px, 30vmin, 200px)` square.
- **Orientation:** the card is a row in landscape and a column in portrait (`@media (orientation: portrait)`); the card is at most 720 x 520px.
- **Colour:** letters are lilac on a white card; pictures are recognisable by shape.
- **Reading:** reading is not required for the child; the word text is for a parent. It has `aria-live="polite"`, and the letter and picture have labels ("Litera A", "Obrazek: arbuz").
- **Sound:** none; the activity does not pronounce letters or words.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so it still runs under the global CSS rule. In addition the code reads `prefers-reduced-motion` on every frame: when set, the slide is replaced by a fade without the 60px offset and the wiggle is skipped.
- **Limitations:** swipes starting on a button may also trigger its click if the pointer ends on the same button (see section 18); text is in Polish only.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- No audio, so the child cannot hear a letter unless a parent reads it.
- The "w słowie" words (for example ząb for Ą) may confuse a parent who expects the word to start with the letter.
- Letter shapes depend on the system font (`font-family: inherit`); some fonts draw "ą", "ę" or "ń" differently.
- Accidental swipes can change the letter while the child intends to tap.
- Privacy: nothing is stored or transmitted.

## 8. Configuration

No runtime configuration; the letters and pictures are data in [`js/literki-data.js`](../../js/literki-data.js) and timings are constants in `js/literki.js`.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location | Changeable without code change? | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window.LiterkiData` | Letters: `{u, l, pics: [{w, c?, svg}]}` | array | 32 letters | `js/literki-data.js` | Data edit only (no UI) | `[]` if missing (see section 16) |
| `SLIDE_S`, `WIGGLE_S`, `WORD_S`, `WORD_FADE_S`, `GLOW_S` | Timings (s) | numbers | 0.5, 0.8, 3, 0.5, 1 | `js/literki.js` | No | None |
| Swipe threshold | Minimum horizontal distance | number | 60 px | `sup()` | No | None |

## 9. Assets

No external image files. The 74 pictures are inline SVG strings in `js/literki-data.js` (100x100 viewBox, the app's own style), one `w` (Polish word) per picture and an optional `c` flag. The file is about 26 KB and is loaded by a script tag before `js/literki.js`. The arrow icons are inline SVG in `js/literki.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Letter order:** `Rand.shuffle(LETTERS)` at launch and again at the start of each new round; each letter appears once per round. When a new round starts, its first letter is never the letter just shown (the first element is rotated to the end if equal).
- **Picture:** `Rand.pickOne(L.pics, 'literki-' + L.l)` on each showing; with 2 or 3 pictures per letter, the picture differs from the last one shown for that letter within the page session (the memory is in-process and per letter).
- **Pool sizes:** 32 letters; 2 pictures per letter, 3 for B, D, G, J, K, L, O, P, S and T (extra pictures: butelka, drzewo, gwiazda, jajko, klucz, liść, oko, parasol, serce, truskawka).
- **Persistence:** none; a new order on every launch.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. The child moves freely forwards and backwards; the order is random, not progressive. Nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no completion state and no failure. Feedback: wiggle and word for the picture, glow for the letter, slide for navigation. No sound. When a round ends, the next forward step simply starts a new random round.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches inside the stage; `js/literki.js` additionally calls `levelStart(0, letter)` for each letter shown and `track('interaction', { variant: letter })` when the picture or the letter is touched, so the letters shown and touched are recorded. Recorded: starts, active time, replays, quick exits, touches and the letter variants. It is open-ended, so no completion or level is defined. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** IIFE in [`js/literki.js`](../../js/literki.js) overriding `mount` for `literki` (via `forEach` over `window.ACTIVITIES`); it reads `window.LiterkiData`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `.lt-field` with two arrow buttons and `.lt-card` containing the letter button (`.lt-letter`, text "Aa"), the picture button (`.lt-pic`, an SVG) and `.lt-word`. `show(i)` rewrites the texts and the SVG.
- **State:** `order` (shuffled letters), `idx`, and timers `slide`, `wiggle`, `wordT`, `glow`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop `frame()` with capped dt (0.05 s), started by `start()` and stopped when idle or hidden.
- **Events:** `click` on arrows, picture and letter; `pointerdown`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel` on the card for the swipe; `visibilitychange`.
- **Randomization:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`shuffle`, `pickOne`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the `visibilitychange` listener and the root.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.lt-field` is absolutely positioned with 64px at the top (Back button) and safe-area insets, a flex row with arrows on each side of the card.
- The card is `flex: 1 1 auto`, `max-width: 720px`, `max-height: 520px`; landscape is a row (letter, picture), portrait a column.
- Sizes use `vmin` clamps (letter 110-220px, picture 96-200px, word 1.1-1.6rem).
- Letters and picture SVGs are scaled by CSS; there is no board coordinate space.
- No resize handler is needed (CSS only).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Quick repeated arrow touches:** ignored while a slide is running (one letter per slide).
- **Touch cancel:** `pointercancel` clears the swipe start.
- **Backgrounding:** loop stopped while hidden and restarted on return.
- **Reduced motion:** read every frame.
- **Missing data:** if `js/literki-data.js` fails to load, `LETTERS` is `[]` and `show(0)` would fail (`order[idx]` undefined, causing a script error at mount). This is not handled.
- **Unhandled:** a swipe that starts and ends on the same button also triggers that button's click (see section 18).

## 17. Testing

There are no automated tests. Manual scenarios to perform:

- [ ] Open the activity: a letter with a picture is shown; the word is hidden.
- [ ] Touch the picture: wiggle and a word below for about 3 s, then fade; the word for a flagged picture shows "letter w słowie".
- [ ] Touch the letter: soft glow for about 1 s.
- [ ] Use the next and previous arrows through all 32 letters of one round and wrap past the end; the first letter of the new round is not the last letter shown.
- [ ] Swipe left and right over 60 px on the card; short movements do nothing.
- [ ] Double-tap an arrow quickly: only one letter change.
- [ ] Leave and re-enter: the order is different; the letters Ą, Ę, Ń, Y show words flagged with "w słowie".
- [ ] See all pictures of several letters by revisiting them (including a 3-picture letter such as B); the picture varies and does not repeat directly.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; very small phone; large tablet.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space).
- [ ] Switch tab while the word is shown and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: no wiggle, slide becomes a fade.
- [ ] Browsers required by the README: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#86](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/86) reports `node --check` and a Node stub-DOM run (stepping through letters with wrap-around, quick double tap on an arrow advancing one letter, word displayed about 3 s, glow); it lists touch, swipe and Safari checks as untested. PR [#142](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/142) reports that all 64 SVGs parse as XML and that a Node script confirms 32 letters, at least 2 pictures each, and that every non-flagged word starts with its letter; no browser test.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**
- No automated tests; device checks were pending in the PR descriptions.
- Each letter has 2 pictures, ten letters have 3; Ą, Ę, Ń and Y have only words that contain, not start with, the letter.
- No audio.
- No handling when `LiterkiData` is missing.
- Swipe is bound to `pointerdown`/`pointerup` on the whole card, so a drag that starts and ends on the same button may both swipe and trigger the button (code reading; behaviour in browsers not verified).

**Requires verification**
- Whether horizontal swipes are ever stolen by the browser (`touch-action: manipulation` allows panning).
- Appearance of the letters in the fonts available on each device.

Item 6 of issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) (at least 2 pictures per letter, 3 where a good Polish word exists) is done on `main` via PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173); the random picture on each showing was already implemented.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (the third pictures from issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), item 6, are done, see section 21).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`shuffle`, `pickOne`). `js/animals.js` is not used.
- Data file: [`js/literki-data.js`](../../js/literki-data.js) (used only by this activity).
- Another browse-and-touch activity with no score: [Co nie Pasuje?](co-nie-pasuje.md) (different mechanics, no shared code).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#63](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/63) / PR [#86](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/86): activity added (12 letters).
- Issue [#118](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/118) / PR [#142](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/142): full Polish alphabet, random order and random pictures.
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): third pictures for ten letters (74 pictures in total).

```
