## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/lodz-podwodna.md`

```markdown
# Łódź Podwodna

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Łódź Podwodna |
| Internal ID | `podwodna` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)); source file `js/podwodna.js`, CSS prefix `pd-` |
| Description | A yellow submarine with a bear in its round window hovers in a pastel sea among four slow fish, three clumps of seaweed and rising bubbles. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, observation |
| Interaction type | Tap / click (real buttons; the sand also uses the touch position) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Łódź Podwodna is the underwater member of the vehicle group. Besides the usual "start / slow down" interaction it adds a vertical dimension (the submarine can settle on the sand and lift off again), fish that react to touch by circling the submarine, and bubbles the child can pop. The submarine starts hovering rather than moored, so the first touch is already a choice between swimming and resting. Nothing can go wrong: there is no score, and the submarine never swims backwards.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#podwodna`); `mount` builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The scene shows a blue sea gradient, a sand strip at the bottom, three seaweed clumps, four fish swimming back and forth at different heights and the submarine **hovering** near the left (at 6 % of the width), bobbing gently. Bubbles start to rise from it.
3. The child can touch the submarine hull, the bear in the window, the sand, a fish or a bubble.
4. Touching the hull makes the submarine swim (2 s ramp) or slow to a hover. Touching the sand makes it glide down to rest on the sand at the touched horizontal position; touching it while resting lifts it back to cruising height (2.2 s). Touching a fish makes it swim once around the submarine (7 s). Touching a bubble pops it (0.5 s fade). Touching the bear makes it wave (2.6 s).
5. There is no formal completion state.
6. The cycle repeats for as long as the child plays.
7. The activity does not reset itself and nothing is randomised (section 10).
8. The child leaves with Back (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Loop time at cruise speed | `CROSS_S = 24` s (`V = 1/24` loop fractions per second); the visible width is crossed in about 14 to 18 s |
| Start / slow-down ramp | `RAMP_S = 2.0` s (smoothstep) |
| Bob | `BOB = 4` px each way (8 px peak-to-peak), period 3.6 s, tilt up to 1.2 deg; both fade to 0 as the submarine settles on the sand |
| Sand glide duration | `T = clamp(2.5 + |Δf|·L/W·3, 2.5, 6)` s, a cubic Hermite from the current speed |
| Lift-off | 2.2 s, no horizontal movement |
| Bear wave | `WAVE_S = 2.6` s |
| Fish circling | `CIRCLE_S = 7` s, blended in and out over 1.3 s each; ellipse radii `max(0.7·bw, FS)` by `max(0.8·bh, FS)` |
| Bubbles | pool `MAX_BUBBLES = 10`; one spawned every `BUBBLE_EVERY = 1.0` s; life `BUBBLE_LIFE = 4.5` s; rise 55 px/s; sideways wobble ±10 px; pop `POP_S = 0.5` s |
| Fish | 4, speeds 22, 28, 25 and 20 px/s, lanes at 12 %, 23 %, 68 % and 77 % of the water height; colours pink, blue, orange and green |
| Seaweed | 3 clumps at `SEAWEED_X = [0.1, 0.46, 0.86]` of the width |
| Frame step cap | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |

Details:

- **Hull touch** (`onSub`): while resting it lifts off; while lifting it is ignored; otherwise a stopped or slowing submarine accelerates and a moving one slows to a hover.
- **Sand touch** (`onSand`): the target is the touched x (clamped so the submarine stays on screen); if the target lies behind the submarine it travels forward past the right edge and wraps (`fwd = 1`), so it never moves backwards (commit `ea2fe47`). A keyboard activation (no pointer coordinates) rests the submarine at the centre of the screen.
- **Resting submarine:** the horizontal position is kept on resize as a fraction of the free width.
- **Bubbles** are only created while the submarine is swimming or hovering, not while it rests or glides down; a bubble spawn is skipped if all ten are in use. A touched bubble fades and scales up 1.5x during `POP_S`.
- **Fish** move in a ping-pong between the screen edges with a slight vertical wave; touching an already circling fish is ignored; fish flip to face their direction of travel.
- **Reduced motion:** the submarine, fish, bubbles and wave are driven by the rAF loop; the seaweed sway is a CSS animation and stops; see section 6. **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touch to swim, rest, lift, pop, circle.
- Calm observation of slow underwater motion.
- Exploring several targets without failure.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- The submarine changes speed over 2 s and glides to the sand over 2.5 to 6 s.
- A fish circles the submarine once for 7 s after a touch.
- Bubbles are created once per second while the submarine is up and pop softly when touched.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on attention, fine motor skills or understanding of cause and effect. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) and `click` with `event.detail === 0` for keyboard activation. The hull, the bear window, the sand and the fish are real `<button>` elements with Polish `aria-label`s and are reachable with Tab. The bubbles are buttons with `tabindex="-1"` and are therefore **not** keyboard reachable.
- **Touch handling.** `.pd` uses `touch-action: none`; no drag gesture. The submarine container has `pointer-events: none`; only the hull, window and (bubble buttons while a bubble is alive, class `pd-on`) capture touches.
- **Target sizes.** Sand strip height `max(56, 0.16·H)` px across the full width; window button `max(56, 0.24·bw)` px; fish `FS = clamp(0.11·min(W,H), 56, 84)` px; bubble hit box 56 x 56 px around a 24 px visible bubble; hull is 90 % x 70 % of the submarine.
- **Orientation.** Layout is recomputed on `resize`/`orientationchange`; a resting or hovering submarine keeps its relative horizontal position.
- **Colour.** Fish colours are decoration; nothing depends on colour alone.
- **Reduced motion.** The movement of the submarine, fish and bubbles is drawn from the rAF loop and keeps running under the global reduced-motion rule. The seaweed sway (`pd-sway`, a 6 s CSS keyframe animation) is purely decorative and is disabled by the global rule, so the seaweed stands still for such users; no state depends on it.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Limitations:** bubbles cannot be popped by keyboard; a keyboard user cannot choose where the submarine rests.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Accidental interactions:** the sand strip spans the full width at the bottom; a touch near the sand always sends the submarine there.
- **Moving targets:** fish and bubbles move continuously, which may be harder to hit for a very young child (the hit boxes are at least 56 px).
- **Unclear ending:** the activity never ends.
- **Performance:** one always-running rAF loop updating the submarine, 4 fish and up to 10 bubbles per frame.
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/podwodna.js`](../../js/podwodna.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S`, `V` | Loop time (s) and cruise speed | number | 24, `1/24` |
| `RAMP_S` | Start / slow-down ramp (s) | number | 2.0 |
| `BOB` | Bob amplitude (px) | number | 4 |
| `VB_W`, `VB_H` | Submarine viewBox size | number | 240, 130 |
| `WAVE_S`, `CIRCLE_S`, `POP_S` | Bear wave, fish circle, bubble pop durations (s) | number | 2.6, 7, 0.5 |
| `MAX_BUBBLES`, `BUBBLE_LIFE`, `BUBBLE_EVERY` | Bubble pool, life, spawn interval | number | 10, 4.5, 1.0 |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 |
| `SEAWEED_X` | Seaweed positions (fractions of the width) | array | `[0.1, 0.46, 0.86]` |
| `FISH` | Fish colours, lane, speed, phase | array of 4 objects | 4 entries |

There is no fallback because there is no external input.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The submarine, bear, fish and seaweed are inline SVG strings in the JS file (the bear is drawn locally by `bearSvg`); the sea gradient, sand (with pebble dots) and bubbles are CSS (`.pd-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css)). No audio, fonts or data files. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

None. The scene, the four fish (colours, lanes, speeds, start phases), the seaweed and the starting position are fixed. The only variation is derived deterministically: bubble start position and sway phase cycle through a sequence (`bubSeq`), so no random function is used.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. No levels or difficulty, and nothing persists between sessions. The submarine starts hovering at cruise height on every launch.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is visual only: swimming and hovering, a glide to and from the sand (the bob fades out when resting), a fish circling, a popping bubble, a waving bear. No sound, no celebration, no automatic restart.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/podwodna.js`](../../js/podwodna.js), assigned to the `podwodna` registry entry; loaded before `js/app.js`. No shared helper is used.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG; the submarine, fish and bubbles are moved with inline `transform`; there are 10 pooled bubble buttons.
- **State:** closures: `f` (loop fraction), `v`, `yk` (0 = cruising, 1 = resting on the sand), `ramp`, `glide` (`{f0, v0, f1, pc1, fwd, cur, y0, y1, t, T}`), `waveT`, per-fish `ph`/`circ`/`th0`, per-bubble `t`/`pop`.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop `frame` with a capped dt; `glide` is a cubic Hermite in `f` (`fNew`) combined with an eased `yk`; fish ping-pong with phase `ph` in [0, 2); paused while hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `bind()` registers `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the rAF, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Persistence/config/analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; `W`/`H` come from `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`.
- **Units:** CSS pixels. The submarine's left edge is `f·L - bw` with `L = W + bw` and `bw = min(clamp(0.42·W, 200, 340), 0.55·H)`; its vertical position interpolates from `cruiseTop = 0.45·H - bh/2` to `restTop`, which seats the hull in the sand. The fish and bubbles share the same pixel space; fish lanes use fractions of the water height (`H - 0.8·sandH`).
- **Resting position** is stored as a fraction of the free width (`pc`) and restored after a resize.
- **Seaweed:** positioned by fractions of the width and anchored `0.5·sandH` above the bottom.
- Tested sizes: Not currently documented (PR [#156](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/156) reports a stub simulation at four portrait and landscape viewports).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Backgrounding:** the loop pauses while hidden and resumes without a jump.
- **Resize:** a stationary submarine is re-placed from its stored fraction; an ongoing glide is retargeted (`glide.f1` is recomputed).
- **Rapid input:** a fish already circling ignores touches; a bubble that is not alive or already popping is ignored; a second hull touch during a lift-off is ignored.
- **Full bubble pool:** a spawn is skipped.
- **Sand touch behind the submarine:** it sails on and wraps (never backwards).
- **Touch cancel / missing assets / invalid config:** not applicable.
- **Unhandled:** no fallback without `requestAnimationFrame`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#156](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/156) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation at 4 viewports (no backward steps, bob 8 px peak-to-peak, rest and lift positions, fish never off-screen, at most 5 bubbles alive, a pop removes the bubble, no bubbles at rest); a later commit (`ea2fe47`) changed the sand glide so it never travels backwards.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Łódź Podwodna; the submarine hovers near the left and bubbles rise; touch the hull; it swims forward and loops round.
- [ ] Touch the swimming submarine; it slows to a hover in about 2 s.
- [ ] Touch the sand to the right of and to the left of the submarine; it glides down at that position and never moves backwards.
- [ ] Touch the resting submarine; it lifts off in about 2.2 s and bubbles start again.
- [ ] Touch each fish; it circles the submarine once (about 7 s) and returns to its path; touch the same fish while circling; nothing extra happens.
- [ ] Pop several bubbles; rapid popping does not leave stuck bubbles.
- [ ] Touch the bear; it waves.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch open water and seaweed; nothing happens.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no completion state.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-enter; the submarine hovers at the left again.
- [ ] Randomization and progression: confirm that nothing varies and nothing persists.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate while swimming, resting and during a glide; the submarine and fish stay on screen and the resting submarine stays in the sand.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab to the hull, window, fish and sand; Enter/Space; confirm that bubbles are not reachable by keyboard).
- [ ] Background the tab while swimming; return without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled: the submarine, fish and bubbles still move; the seaweed stands still.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- Bubbles are not reachable by keyboard (`tabindex="-1"`); a keyboard activation of the sand always rests the submarine at the screen centre.
- The seaweed animation is CSS-based and stops under reduced motion; the rest of the motion ignores that preference by design.
- The bear in the window is drawn locally, not with `js/animals.js`.

**Requires verification**

- Layout of the submarine, sand and fish on very short or very wide viewports.
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Łódź Podwodna; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Mała Łódka](mala-lodka.md) (loop-fraction model), [Autobusik](autobusik.md), [Traktor](traktor.md), [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md), [Balon](balon.md).
- Shared helpers: none used (`js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not referenced).
- Shared pattern: rAF loop with a capped dt.

## 21. Change history

- [#95](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/95) / PR [#156](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/156): Łódź Podwodna activity added.
- Commit `ea2fe47`: the sand glide never travels backwards (reviewer optional suggestion).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/lustro.md`

```markdown
# Lustro

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#213](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/213)
- Planned activity id: `lustro`
- Planned CSS prefix: `lu-`

## 1. Overview

Lustro (`lustro`, module `js/lustro.js`, CSS prefix `lu-`): a big outline of a butterfly, a house or a tree is split by a soft dashed centre line. The child paints with a finger on either half and the same line appears at once on the other half, mirrored, in the same colour and width.

## 2. Business purpose

Gentle introduction to symmetry through free drawing: every picture comes out symmetrical and pretty. It fills the gap between Malowanie Światłem (fading light) and Rysuj Kształty (tracing): paint stays on the picture.

## 3. Activity flow

1. One outline (random from a shuffled bag of three) is shown with a row of six colour dots (one chosen at random) and a sponge button. 2. The child paints on either half; each stroke is mirrored over the centre line and clipped to the outline. 3. When about 70% of the outline is painted the picture glows for 3 s, then fades out (0.3 s) and the next outline fades in (0.5 s) on a clean canvas. 4. The sponge button wipes the picture with a 0.5 s fade. The activity never ends by itself.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Outlines | butterfly, house, tree, each drawn in a 100x100 unit space symmetrical about x = 50; bag of three shuffled, each once before repeats (the first of a new bag is never the one just shown) |
| Board | square, at least 300 px on a 320 px wide portrait phone and 304 px on 568x320 landscape (at least 60% of the shorter side) |
| Brush | width max(14 px, 5% of the board); round caps; same colour and width on the mirrored side |
| Colours | six dots (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple), 56 px, each with its own white pattern (stripes, dots, zigzag, checks, waves, cross); the chosen dot has a thick ring; the first colour is random |
| Wipe | round 56 px sponge button; 0.5 s fade of the paint, then empty canvas; ignored while the picture glows |
| Clip | paint is clipped to the outline path and never leaves it |
| Goal | painted area measured on a 40x40 grid of the cells inside the outline (a cell counts when the brush centre passes within half the brush width; the mirror counts too); at 70% the glow starts |
| Glow | 3 s static warm drop-shadow, painting ignored; then 0.3 s fade-out, new outline, 0.5 s fade-in |
| Pointers | only the first pointer paints; other fingers are ignored until it lifts |

No score, no failure, no stored data, no text on screen.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

Symmetry (what is done on one side appears on the other), cause and effect, colour choice, fine motor control with a finger.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

The board is focusable: arrows move a brush ring (3% of the board per press), Enter or Space paints while held (arrows then draw a line), colour dots and the sponge button are reachable by Tab (Enter/Space selects). The pattern on each colour dot and the ring on the chosen dot are the non-colour cues. All targets are at least 56 px; aria labels are in Polish.

## 7. Risks and limitations

Checked only with a node stub DOM (stroke flow, coverage, glow, bag, wipe, two pointers) and syntax checks; no browser or device run was possible, so the real proportions of the outlines, the clip and the glow still need a manual look. The 70% goal (raised from 40%, which came too early) needs real covering of the picture; a very small outline may still fill quickly for a child who scribbles.

## 8. Configuration

None; no setting. Enabled by default and appended at the end of the menu list.

## 9. Assets

Inline SVG outlines as path strings in `OUTLINES` (the butterfly's left half is generated by mirroring its right half), a canvas for paint, menu icon in `js/activities.js`. No sound, no external files.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Outline order: shuffled bag of three. Starting colour: random on every mount.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None: the same rules throughout.

## 12. Completion and feedback

At 70% painted: glow for 3 s, then the next outline on a clean canvas. Sponge: fade and clean canvas.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Each stroke start (touch or Enter/Space): `track('interaction', {variant: 'butterfly' | 'house' | 'tree'})`; each glow-and-next picture: `complete()`. Wipes and colour changes are not reported. Open-ended.

## 14. Technical implementation

`mount` builds the DOM, attaches the root with `container.appendChild(root)` before `layout()` and returns a cleanup that cancels the rAF loop, removes the window and document listeners and the root. Strokes are kept as arrays of points relative to the board plus colour and relative width; `clipAndRedraw()` resizes the canvas, clips it to the scaled outline path (`Path2D`) and replays every stroke (and its mirror), so rotation or resize loses nothing. Fast drags are filled with points every 1% of the board so the line and the coverage grid have no holes. A single rAF loop (dt capped at 0.05 s, running only while a fade or the glow is active, paused while the tab is hidden) drives the wipe, glow and outline fades through inline opacity, so it also works under prefers-reduced-motion.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Portrait: board over the controls (4 + 3 grid of 56 px buttons); landscape: board left, controls in a 3-column grid on the right, 72 px left padding keeps the Back button uncovered. Board size is pure CSS (`min(width, height minus reserved)`); SVG sizing uses `.stage .lu-svg` and `.stage .lu-dotsvg`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

Rotation and resize: the canvas is replayed from relative strokes. Tab hidden: the current stroke ends and the loop pauses. Two fingers: second pointer ignored. Very fast touches: each pointer-down starts one stroke, gaps are filled. Focus lost with a key held: the stroke ends. Painting while the glow runs: ignored. A cap of 6000 points per picture prevents unbounded growth.

## 17. Testing

Manual scenarios: (1) Open: one outline with a dashed centre line, six dots, a sponge; one dot is chosen. (2) Draw on the left half: the mirrored line appears at the same moment on the right, in the same colour; draw across the outline edge: paint stays inside. (3) Pick another colour and draw: the new colour is used, the old paint stays. (4) Rotate the device: the picture stays, redrawn. (5) Touch with two fingers: only the first paints. (6) Tab to the board, move with arrows, hold Enter and press arrows: a mirrored line is drawn. (7) Fill about 70%: the picture glows for 3 s, then a different outline fades in clean; repeat three times: all three outlines appear before one repeats. (8) Press the sponge: the paint fades in 0.5 s. (9) Settings, Statystyki: strokes counted as touches, glow-and-next pictures as completions.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

The brush width is computed when a stroke starts (at least 14 px at that time); after rotating to a smaller board it is clamped to 14 px. No eraser, saving or sharing (out of scope). No real-device verification.

## 19. Planned improvements

None planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

Malowanie Światłem (free painting with fading marks), Rysuj Kształty (tracing), Cienie (silhouettes).

## 21. Change history

Initial implementation (issue #213).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/magiczny-ogrod.md`

```markdown
# Magiczny Ogród

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Magiczny Ogród |
| Activity ID | `ogrod` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A meadow with a random weather and time of day. Touching the lawn grows a flower or a mushroom from a seed; touching the drifting cloud gently clears the garden. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap on the lawn and on the cloud (keyboard Enter/Space also supported) |
| Status | Implemented. Enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff` flag). |
| Source | [`js/ogrod.js`](../../js/ogrod.js), CSS classes `.garden`, `.g-*` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A small "plant and watch it grow" scene where each touch produces a pleasant, slowly unfolding result and the whole garden can be wiped with one touch, so the child can start again at any time without anything being "lost". It complements the quieter observation scenes ([Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md), [Akwarium Artura](akwarium-artura.md)) by letting the child place objects where they want. Since issue #109 the weather and time of day vary per launch, so the same garden does not look identical every visit.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile (hash `#ogrod`); `mount` builds the garden as DOM nodes.
2. A random combination of weather (sunny, cloudy, rain, breeze) and time (day, night) is shown: sky, lawn (bottom 45 % of the screen) and a small cloud drifting across the sky.
3. The child can tap the lawn or the cloud.
4. A tap on the lawn plants a seed at that point; the seed fades, a stem grows, leaves pop out and the bloom opens (about 4 s). A tap on the cloud makes all plants fade out.
5. There is no completion state; the garden is open-ended.
6. After a clear, the lawn can be planted again immediately after about 0.9 s.
7. A new weather is chosen only on the next launch.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Plant kinds | 7 (`KINDS`): four flowers (four-petal, tulip, daisy, round pom-pom) and three mushrooms (spotted, flat wide cap, tall pointed cap); kind chosen uniformly at random per tap |
| Plant colours | Flowers: 6 pastels (`PASTELS`); mushrooms: 5 cap colours (`CAPS`); colour chosen at random |
| Plant size | Scale `--s` random 0.8-1.2; box `60 x 100` units times `1.4 * s`, i.e. about 67-101 px wide and 112-168 px tall (height is capped at 30 vh) |
| Anchor | Plant is bottom-centred on the tap point; position stored in percent of the garden |
| Max live plants | 20 (`MAX_PLANTS`); planting a 21st fades the oldest |
| Max fading nodes | 6 (`MAX_FADING`); beyond that, nodes are removed immediately instead of fading |
| Fade | `FADE_MS` = 900 ms, then the node is removed by a `setTimeout` (never by `transitionend`) |
| Growth timeline | Seed shown 0-3.6 s; stem grows 0.5-2.5 s; leaves pop 1.8-3.0 s; bloom pops 2.6-4.2 s (CSS keyframes) |
| Cloud | Drifts left to right in 80 s, linear, infinite (CSS); width `clamp(120px, 26vw, 240px)` plus 12 px padding as extra tap area; at 12 % height |
| Cloud tap | All live plants fade; planting is locked for 900 ms (`locked`) |
| Taps on the sky | Ignored (the plant layer and sky do not take input) |
| Keyboard | Lawn and cloud are `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`; Enter/Space plants at a random spot (x 10-90 %, y 60-96 %) or clears the garden |
| Weather layers | See table below |

| Weather | Layers |
|---|---|
| sunny | Sun orb (a pale moon-like orb at night) |
| breeze | Orb plus 4 white wind streaks crossing in 7 s |
| cloudy | Two cloud banks |
| rain | Two cloud banks plus 30 rain drops at random horizontal positions, each falling linearly and endlessly with its own random duration of 0.9 to 1.4 s and a random negative start delay (the CSS default of 1.1 s is overridden per drop) |
| night (any weather) | 40 twinkling stars (4 s cycle) at random positions (x 2-98 %, y 2-48 % of the garden), about 10 % of them bigger and brighter (3-4 px, opacity 0.9) and the rest small (1.4-2.7 px, opacity 0.4-0.8), dark blue sky and lawn, white glow around plants |

Decorative layers have `pointer-events: none`.

Reduced motion: the global rule disables CSS animations and transitions. For this activity that means plants appear fully grown at once (the final state is defined in the base CSS and the seed is hidden by a dedicated rule), clearing removes plants instantly (the removal timer still runs), the cloud stays still at the left edge but is still tappable, rain drops (which start above the screen) are not visible, wind streaks stay still at the left edge and stars do not twinkle. This is derived from reading the CSS and should be confirmed in a browser (see section 17).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (touch, plant appears and grows).
- Calm observation of slow growth and weather.
- Freedom to place objects where the child chooses; recognising flowers vs mushrooms.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Each tap yields one of 7 plant shapes in a random colour, at the tap position.
- A single cloud tap clears everything and the child can start again.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on attention, creativity or development. None is measured or claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer (touch, mouse, stylus) and **keyboard** (Tab to lawn or cloud, Enter or Space). A visible focus outline is defined for the lawn and cloud.
- **Screen readers:** garden `role="group"` with `aria-label="Ogród z kwiatami"`; lawn labelled "Trawnik – posadź roślinę", cloud "Chmurka". Plants and weather are not announced.
- **Orientation:** the garden fills the viewport; plants are positioned in percent so they stay on the lawn after rotation. In short landscape the 30 vh height cap shrinks plants.
- **Targets:** the whole lawn (bottom 45 %) is one target. The cloud is at least about 144 px wide (120 px plus padding) and moves slowly (80 s per crossing).
- **Colour:** meaning does not depend on colour. Contrast is not a requirement for the decorative scene.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required. Independent use by a young child is possible.
- **Motion intensity:** slow; rain and wind are continuous but gentle (see section 7).
- **Limitations:** a child who taps on the sky gets no response; the cloud is the only way to clear.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Continuous rain and wind animation run for as long as the activity is open.
- Cloud tap clears all plants, which may surprise a child who wanted to keep them (the cloud is drawn as a decoration, not a button).
- Up to 20 plants of up to 168 px height can crowd the lawn; they overlap freely.
- Night stars and rain drops are random per launch (positions, sizes, durations and delays), so no two launches look the same.
- No personal data is involved.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/ogrod.js`](../../js/ogrod.js); styling and timings in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css).

| Name | Purpose | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_PLANTS` | Live plants | 20 | `js/ogrod.js` |
| `MAX_FADING` | Simultaneously fading plants | 6 | `js/ogrod.js` |
| `FADE_MS` | Fade-out time and lock after a clear | 900 ms | `js/ogrod.js` and `.g-plant` transition in CSS (must be kept in sync by hand) |
| `PASTELS`, `CAPS` | Flower / mushroom colours | 6 / 5 | `js/ogrod.js` |
| `KINDS` | Plant shapes | 7 | `js/ogrod.js` |
| `WEATHERS` x times | Scene combinations | 4 x 2 = 8 | `js/ogrod.js` (`COMBOS`) |
| Growth keyframes (`g-seed`, `g-grow`, `g-pop`), `g-drift` 80 s, `g-fall` 1.1 s, `g-gust` 7 s, `g-twinkle` 4 s | Animation timings | see section 4 | `css/style.css` |

## 9. Assets

No external assets. Plants, cloud and weather elements are inline SVG strings built in `js/ogrod.js` and CSS-drawn shapes (stars, drops, wind streaks, sun/moon orb, cloud banks). The menu icon is inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | When | Pool | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weather and time of day | Each mount | 8 combinations (`COMBOS`) | `Rand.pickOne(COMBOS, 'ogrod-weather')`: never the same as the previous launch in the same page session; falls back to a plain random pick if `window.Rand` is missing; not stored |
| Night stars | Each mount (night only) | 40 stars | `Math.random`: position, size (about 10 % bright), opacity and twinkle delay |
| Rain drops | Each mount (rain only) | 30 drops | `Math.random`: position, duration 0.9-1.4 s, start delay |
| Plant kind | Each tap | 7 | Uniform (`Math.random`), repetition allowed |
| Plant colour | Each tap | 6 (flowers) or 5 (mushrooms) | Uniform, repetition allowed |
| Plant scale | Each tap | 0.8-1.2 | Uniform |
| Keyboard planting position | Each key press | x 10-90 %, y 60-96 % | Uniform |

The pool is never empty. Choices are in memory only.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression, levels or persistence.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback: the seed appears, grows into a plant in about 4 s; clearing fades all plants out in 0.9 s. No sound, no celebration, no scoring. Planting is possible again after the 0.9 s lock.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/ogrod.js`](../../js/ogrod.js).
- **Rendering:** DOM. A `div.garden` contains `.g-sky`, a weather layer `.g-wx` (from `weatherHtml`), the lawn, a plant layer and the cloud. Each plant is a `div.g-plant` with an inline SVG.
- **Animation:** CSS keyframes and a transition; no JavaScript animation loop. Removal and the planting lock are driven by `setTimeout` (collected in `timers`).
- **State:** closure variables `live` (plants, oldest first), `fading`, `locked`, `timers`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown` and `keydown` on lawn and cloud; `visibilitychange` toggles `.paused` to pause CSS animations while the tab is hidden.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.pickOne` for weather, `Math.random` elsewhere.
- **Cleanup:** removes listeners, clears timers and removes the garden node.
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (optional).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

The garden is `position: fixed; inset: 0`. Sky is the top 55 %, lawn the bottom 45 % (`inset: 55% 0 0 0`). Plants are positioned with `left`/`top` in percent of the garden, so after a resize or rotation they keep their relative position on the lawn. The cloud is positioned at 12 % height and moves with a `translateX` from -120 % of its width to `100vw + 20px`. Night stars are placed in percent (x 4-95 %, y 3-42 %); the sun/moon orb is at 9 % from the right and 8 % from the top. Plants are bottom-anchored with `translate(-50%, -100%)`. There is no aspect-ratio correction beyond the 30 vh height cap.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable |
| Missing `Rand` | Falls back to `Math.random` for the weather choice (no "no repeat") |
| Resize / rotation | Percent positions keep plants on the lawn |
| Rapid taps | Capped at 20 live plants; excess oldest plants fade or are removed |
| Tap during a clear | Ignored for 900 ms (`locked`) |
| Backgrounding | CSS animations are paused (`.paused`); planting and fade timers keep running |
| Cleanup during fade | Timers are cleared and the garden node removed |
| Touch on the sky | Ignored |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#133](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/133) is the random-weather change; no test report was found in it.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: tap the lawn several times; plants grow in about 4 s at the tapped spots.
- [ ] All 7 plant kinds appear after many taps; none is cut off at screen edges when tapping near them.
- [ ] Completion: not applicable; confirm there is no end state.
- [ ] Tap the cloud: all plants fade within 1 s; taps during that second do nothing; planting works afterwards.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the sky or between plants; nothing breaks.
- [ ] Rapid taps: plant more than 20; the oldest fade away and the page stays responsive.
- [ ] Restart: reopen the activity repeatedly; weather and time vary and are not identical twice in a row (8 combinations: 4 weathers x day/night).
- [ ] Progression: confirm nothing changes over time (none expected).
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate with plants on the lawn; plants stay on the lawn and the weather fills the screen.
- [ ] Touch: finger taps on lawn and cloud. [ ] Mouse: clicks. [ ] Keyboard: Tab, Enter and Space on lawn and cloud.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tab during rain and return; animations resume.
- [ ] Reduced motion: enable the OS setting; plants appear fully grown, cloud and rain behave as described in section 4 (verify the cloud remains reachable and the clear still works).
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- The former fixed-formula night stars and evenly spaced, uniform-speed rain drops (synchronised waves) are fixed on `main` (items 1 and 2 of issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)): stars and drops are now random per launch.
- `FADE_MS` in JavaScript and the 0.9 s opacity transition in CSS are separate constants.
- The cloud is the only way to clear the garden and looks like decoration.

**Requires verification**

- Reduced-motion appearance described in section 4 (static cloud at the left edge, no visible rain).
- Overlap and crowding of plants on small screens.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (random night stars and more natural rain from issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) are done, see section 21).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Deszczyk i Tęcza](deszczyk-i-tecza.md) (rain look), [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md) (stars), [Ogród Motyli](ogrod-motyli.md) (garden theme), [Akwarium Artura](akwarium-artura.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#4](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/4) / PR [#11](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/11): initial activity (the core `js/ogrod.js` was added in a follow-up commit after review; percent-positioned plants and keyboard activation were added at a human request).
- Issue [#21](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/21): app review polish.
- Issue [#109](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/109) / PR [#133](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/133): random weather and day/night.
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): random night stars (40, mixed sizes) and random rain (30 drops, random positions, durations and delays).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/mala-lodka.md`

```markdown
# Mała Łódka

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Mała Łódka |
| Internal ID | `lodka` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)); source file `js/lodka.js`, CSS prefix `ld-` |
| Description | A small sailboat with a bear and a rabbit aboard floats along a calm river with soft waves, a little jetty and three ducks. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap / click (real buttons, so Enter and Space also work) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Mała Łódka is the river member of the vehicle group. It repeats the "start, slow down, go to a destination" pattern of [Autobusik](autobusik.md) with a single destination (the jetty), plus gentle side interactions (ducks that nod and send out a ripple ring, animals that wave). The boat starts moored, so the child sees a calm still scene first and chooses when to set sail. Nothing can go wrong: the boat never moves backwards and there is no score.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#lodka`); `mount` builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The boat starts **moored** at the jetty on the right of the river. Sun, clouds, two moving wave bands, a river bank, three ducks and the bear and rabbit aboard are visible.
3. The child can touch the boat hull, the jetty, a duck or an animal aboard.
4. Touching the boat sets sail (2.2 s ramp) or, if it is sailing, slows it to a halt where it is (2.2 s). Touching the jetty makes the boat sail on and glide in to moor there; touching a duck makes it nod and a ripple ring spread; touching an animal makes it wave.
5. There is no formal completion state.
6. The boat keeps looping (leaves on the right, re-enters from the left) until the child stops it or moors it.
7. The activity never resets by itself; there is nothing to randomise (see section 10).
8. The child leaves with Back (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Loop time at cruise speed | `CROSS_S = 26` s (`V = 1/26` loop fractions per second); the boat crosses the visible width in about 15 s or more |
| Start / slow-down ramp | `RAMP_S = 2.2` s (smoothstep) |
| Gliding into the mooring | braking starts when the remaining distance `D <= 1.5·v`; duration `T = 2·D/v` (about 3 s at cruise speed) |
| Boat bob | `BOB = 3` px each way (6 px peak-to-peak), period 3.4 s; tilt up to 1.2 deg |
| Duck nod | `NOD_S = 2.2` s (rotation up to 12 deg, dip of 4 px) |
| Animal wave | `WAVE_S = 2.4` s (rotation up to 14 deg) |
| Ripple ring | `RING_S = 2.6` s; pool `MAX_RINGS = 6`; the oldest ring is recycled when all are in use |
| Frame step cap | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |
| Ducks | 3, at `DUCK_POS = [[0.18, 0.74], [0.5, 0.85], [0.8, 0.76]]` (fractions of width and height); the middle duck is mirrored |
| Animals | 2 (bear, rabbit), at 20 % and 50 % of the boat width |

Details:

- **Boat touch** (`onBoat`): if the boat is stopped or is in a slow-down, it sets sail; otherwise (sailing or gliding to the jetty) it slows to a halt where it is and cancels any mooring request.
- **Jetty touch** (`onJetty`): ignored when already moored and still. Otherwise `target` is set (the last intent counts); a stopped boat starts sailing; a slowing boat accelerates again. If the jetty is too close to brake gently (`D < 1.25·v`) the `skip` flag makes the boat go round once (until `D > 0.9`) before mooring.
- **Never backwards:** braking uses a polynomial profile whose distance equals the remaining distance, and speed is clamped at 0.
- **Moored boat touched:** it sets sail again.
- **Ducks:** each duck keeps a small idle bob (2 px, period 3.8 s); touching starts a nod and a ring at the duck.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is JS-driven; see section 6. **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touch to sail, stop, moor, make a duck nod.
- Calm observation of slow, smooth movement on water.
- Independent play without failure.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- Ramps and gliding are slow (2.2 s, about 3 s); waves and bob are small (6 px peak-to-peak).
- Ducks and animals respond to touch with short, soft reactions.
- The boat can be stopped anywhere and always sails forwards.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on attention or fine motor skills. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) and `click` with `event.detail === 0` for keyboard activation. The hull, the jetty, the animals and the ducks are real `<button>` elements with Polish `aria-label`s, reachable with Tab and activated with Enter or Space.
- **Touch handling.** `.ld` uses `touch-action: none`; no drag gesture. The boat container has `pointer-events: none` so only the hull and the animals (inside it) capture touches.
- **Target sizes.** Duck buttons `DS = clamp(0.11·H, 56, 76)` px square (fixed to at least 56 px in review, commit `3aa7cb3`); animals `AS = clamp(0.24·bw, 56, 72)` px; hull is the lower half of the boat (96 % of its width, 50 % of its height); jetty height at least 56 px.
- **Orientation.** Layout recomputed on `resize`/`orientationchange`; the moored boat is always fully on screen (`cm = max(bw/2, jetty x - 0.4·bw)`).
- **Colour.** Nothing depends on colour alone.
- **Reduced motion.** Boat, waves (background position), ducks, animals and rings are updated by the rAF loop through inline styles, so the global CSS rule does not stop them. The wave bands scroll continuously (`ph = clock·9` px/s). The motion is slow, but it is not reduced for users who asked for reduced motion.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Limitations:** on very short screens the two animal buttons (centres 0.3·bw apart) overlap by a few pixels (reported as an optional review suggestion on PR [#132](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/132) and not applied).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Accidental interactions:** the hull button covers the lower half of the boat and the animal buttons sit on top of it; touches on the animals never move the boat.
- **Unclear ending:** the activity never ends.
- **Hidden state:** a jetty touch just after the boat has passed makes the boat sail a whole loop (up to about 26 s) before mooring.
- **Visual stimulation:** two scrolling wave bands run continuously, even when the boat is moored.
- **Performance:** one always-running rAF loop with a handful of nodes.
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/lodka.js`](../../js/lodka.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S` | Seconds per loop at cruise speed | number | 26 |
| `V` | Cruise speed (loop fractions/s) | number | `1 / CROSS_S` |
| `RAMP_S` | Start / slow-down ramp (s) | number | 2.2 |
| `NOD_S`, `WAVE_S`, `RING_S` | Duck nod, animal wave, ring durations (s) | number | 2.2, 2.4, 2.6 |
| `MAX_RINGS` | Ripple ring pool size | number | 6 |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 |
| `VB_W`, `VB_H` | Boat viewBox size | number | 200, 160 |
| `BOB` | Boat bob amplitude (px) | number | 3 |
| `AN_X` | Animal centres across the boat width | array | `[0.2, 0.5]` |
| `KINDS`, `NAMES` | Animals aboard and their labels | arrays | `['bear','rabbit']`, `['Miś','Króliczek']` |
| `DUCK_POS` | Duck positions (fractions of the scene) | array | 3 entries |

There is no fallback because there is no external input.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The boat, ducks, jetty and the two animals are inline SVG strings (the animals are drawn locally by `animalSvg`, not from `js/animals.js`); the two wave bands are generated data-URL SVGs (`waveUrl`) used as repeating backgrounds; the sky, sun, clouds, water, bank and rings are CSS (`.ld-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css)). No audio, fonts or data files. One dead element exists in `jettySvg()` (a circle with radius 0).

## 10. Randomization and variants

None. The scene, the two animals (bear and rabbit) and the three duck positions are fixed on every launch.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. No levels, no difficulty and nothing persists between sessions. The boat starts moored on every launch.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is visual only: sailing, slowing, gliding to the jetty and mooring, duck nods, expanding ripple rings, waving animals, the continuous boat bob and wave scrolling. No sound, no celebration, no automatic restart.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/lodka.js`](../../js/lodka.js), assigned to the `lodka` registry entry; loaded before `js/app.js`. No shared helper is used.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG; the boat, ducks and rings are positioned with inline `transform`; wave bands are `<div>`s with repeating SVG background images whose `background-position-x` is updated each frame.
- **State:** closures. Boat: `f` (loop fraction), `v`, `ramp`, `brake`, `target`, `skip`, `moored`. Ducks: `nod`; animals: `wave`; rings: `t`, `age` (pool of 6).
- **Animation:** one rAF loop `frame` with a capped dt, paused while hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `bind()` registers `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()` (a brake in progress is dropped and the boat re-accelerates from its current speed, no snap).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the rAF, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Persistence/config/analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; `W`/`H` come from `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`.
- **Units:** CSS pixels for placement; boat position is the loop fraction `f` over a path `L = W + bw` (boat left = `f·L - bw`), so speed and mooring stay valid after resizing. Boat width `bw = min(clamp(0.42·W, 200, 300), 0.55·H)`; waterline `wl = 0.56·H`.
- **Jetty and mooring:** the jetty is `jw = clamp(0.28·W, 100, 220)` wide at the right edge; mooring fraction `fm = (cm + bw/2)/L`.
- **Ducks and rings:** ducks use fractions of the scene; rings are placed at the touched duck.
- Tested sizes: Not currently documented.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Backgrounding:** the loop pauses while hidden and resumes without a jump.
- **Resize during gliding:** the brake is re-planned from the current speed.
- **Rapid input:** repeated jetty touches are ignored once `target` is set; duck and animal reactions ignore touches while already running; touching the duck while all six rings are in use recycles the oldest ring.
- **Jetty too close:** handled by `skip`.
- **Touch cancel / missing assets / invalid config:** not applicable.
- **Unhandled:** no fallback without `requestAnimationFrame`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#132](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/132) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation in node (start moored, sail, monotonic motion, halt, resume, glide to the jetty and moor at the exact spot, bob range 6 px, ring cap of 6), and asks for a device check in portrait and landscape and after rotation.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Mała Łódka; the boat is moored at the jetty; touch the hull; it sets sail gently and crosses the width in about 15 s or more.
- [ ] Touch the sailing boat; it slows to a halt where it is; touch again; it sails on.
- [ ] Touch the jetty while sailing; the boat glides in and moors without reversing.
- [ ] Touch the jetty just after the boat has passed; it moors on the next loop.
- [ ] Touch the jetty while moored; nothing happens.
- [ ] Touch each duck (nod and a ripple ring); tap one duck rapidly more than six times; no ring is stuck.
- [ ] Touch the bear and the rabbit (wave).
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch water, sky and bank; nothing happens.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no completion state.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-enter; the boat is moored again.
- [ ] Randomization and progression: confirm that nothing varies between visits and nothing persists.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate while sailing, gliding and moored; the boat stays on screen and the moored boat is not cut off by the jetty.
- [ ] Short landscape screen: check that the animal buttons do not interfere with each other.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab through the jetty, hull, animals and ducks; Enter/Space).
- [ ] Background the tab while sailing; return without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled: boat, waves and ducks still move.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The motion ignores the reduced-motion preference by design.
- On very short screens the two animal buttons overlap by a few pixels (review suggestion on PR #132, not applied).
- A dead element (zero-radius circle) remains in `jettySvg()`.
- The animals are drawn locally rather than from `js/animals.js`.

**Requires verification**

- Appearance of the jetty and boat overlap on different aspect ratios (flagged as a manual check in the PR).
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Mała Łódka; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Autobusik](autobusik.md) (same loop-fraction and brake model), [Traktor](traktor.md), [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md), [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md), [Balon](balon.md).
- Shared helpers: none used (`js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not referenced).
- Shared pattern: rAF loop with a capped dt; position as a loop fraction.

## 21. Change history

- [#88](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/88) / PR [#132](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/132): Mała Łódka activity added; the review's blocking finding (duck targets under 56 px tall) was fixed in commit `3aa7cb3`.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/malowanie-swiatlem.md`

```markdown
# Malowanie Światłem

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Malowanie Światłem |
| Activity ID | `malowanie` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A dark canvas. Touching and dragging paints soft glowing coloured marks that drift and fade away after a few seconds. |
| Category | Drawing, open-ended play, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Touch, drag, mouse drag; keyboard (arrows and Enter/Space) |
| Status | Implemented. Enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff` flag). |
| Source | [`js/malowanie.js`](../../js/malowanie.js), `.paint-canvas` focus style in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A free-drawing activity with no permanent result: whatever the child paints disappears by itself, so there is nothing to keep, clean or get wrong, and the screen returns to calm darkness. It gives the child direct control (the mark appears exactly under the finger) and is the only fully free "draw anything" activity, in contrast with [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md) which asks the child to trace given shapes.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile (hash `#malowanie`); `mount` creates one full-screen canvas.
2. A dark purple canvas (`#2b2748`) is shown; nothing else.
3. The child can touch, drag or (with a keyboard) use the arrow keys, Enter and Space.
4. Each touch point and each 22 px of drag leaves a soft glowing disc in the next colour of a cycle; discs drift slowly in a random direction and fade out in 3-5 s.
5. There is no completion state; the canvas goes dark again when nothing is touched.
6. There is no "clear" button; marks vanish by themselves.
7. Reopening the activity starts with a blank canvas.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Mark spacing while dragging | `SPACING` = 22 px of pointer travel between marks |
| Marks per move event | At most 3 (`Math.min(floor(d / 22), 3)`), spread evenly along the segment since the last painted point |
| Maximum marks | `MAX` = 150; adding more removes the oldest |
| Mark radius | 40-75 px (random per mark) |
| Mark life | 3000-5000 ms (random) |
| Mark drift | Random direction, 6-14 px/s |
| Opacity | `0.5 * sin(min(t * 8, 1) * pi / 2) * (1 - t)^2` where `t` = age / life: fades in over the first 12.5 % of life, then fades out quadratically |
| Blending | Additive (`globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`) with a radial gradient from the mark colour to transparent |
| Colours | 6 (`#f7a8c9` pink, `#c9b8f2` lilac, `#a8d8f0` light blue, `#ffd98a` yellow, `#a9dcb4` green, `#ffb7a5` coral), used in a fixed rotating order (`colorIdx++ % 6`), starting with pink on every launch |
| Multi-touch | Each pointer is tracked separately (`pointers` map); pointer capture is requested on the canvas |
| Mouse hover | Does not paint; only while a button or finger is down |
| Keyboard | The canvas is focusable (`tabindex="0"`); arrows move a light spot by 30 px (starting at the centre, clamped to the canvas) and paint a mark at each press; Enter or Space paints at the current spot |
| Frame step | Capped at 50 ms |
| Failure / scoring | None |

The animation runs in one `requestAnimationFrame` loop that stops when no marks are left and restarts when a new mark is added, so it is not affected by the global reduced-motion CSS rule (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). There is no slower variant for reduced motion; marks still drift and fade at the same speed.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Free expression and cause and effect (finger movement leaves a visible trail).
- Fine-motor and hand-eye coordination through dragging.
- Calm, forgiving play without a result to protect.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Marks appear where touched, in colours that change one after another, and drift away.
- Drag speed does not change the spacing of marks much: marks are placed every 22 px or more.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on creativity, motor skills or calm. None is measured or claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via pointer events; **keyboard** support (see section 4) with a visible focus outline (`.paint-canvas:focus-visible`).
- **Screen readers:** the canvas has `role="img"` and a Polish `aria-label` describing the keyboard controls; painted marks are not exposed.
- **Orientation:** full viewport (`position: absolute; inset: 0` inside a relative container); resized on `resize` and `orientationchange`.
- **Targets:** there are no buttons; the whole canvas is the target.
- **Colour:** colour carries no meaning. The marks are bright additive lights on a dark background.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required. Independent use by a young child is possible.
- **Visual intensity:** soft glows that fade; overlapping additive marks can look bright when many are close together (see section 7). No flashing.
- **Limitations:** a keyboard user has no visible cursor except the marks themselves; there is no way to choose a colour.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Overlapping additive marks add up and can approach white in busy areas.
- A fast scribble is limited to 3 marks per move event, so very fast strokes look dotted rather than continuous.
- Up to 150 radial gradients are created and drawn every frame, which may be slow on low-end devices (requires verification).
- The result cannot be saved or cleared on demand; it always fades (by design).
- On resize the existing marks keep their pixel positions (they are not rescaled).
- No personal data is involved and nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/malowanie.js`](../../js/malowanie.js).

| Name | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX` | Maximum marks on screen | 150 |
| `SPACING` | Pointer travel between marks | 22 px |
| `COLORS` | Colour cycle | 6 hex colours |
| `STEP` (inside the keyboard handler) | Keyboard movement | 30 px |
| Radius, life, speed ranges and the 0.5 alpha | Mark appearance | literals in `addMark` and `draw` |
| Canvas background | Dark purple | `#2b2748` (inline style) |

There is no fallback or validation; values are not read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external assets. Everything is drawn on one `<canvas>` with radial gradients; the background colour is set inline. The menu icon is inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | Rule |
|---|---|
| Mark radius (40-75 px), life (3-5 s), drift direction and speed (6-14 px/s) | `Math.random()` per mark |
| Colour | Not random; fixed cycle through 6 colours, starting with pink every launch |

[`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) is not used and nothing is stored. There are no pools that can be empty.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. Nothing is persisted between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is immediate: the mark appears under the finger (or at the keyboard light spot) and fades after 3-5 s. No sound, no celebration.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/malowanie.js`](../../js/malowanie.js).
- **Rendering:** a single `<canvas class="paint-canvas">` styled inline (absolute, `touch-action: none`); the container is set to `position: relative; display: block` and restored on cleanup. Device pixel ratio capped at 2.
- **State:** `marks` (plain objects with position, velocity, radius, life, age, colour), `pointers`, `colorIdx`, keyboard spot `kx, ky`.
- **Loop:** `frame` ages and moves marks and calls `draw`; it re-arms itself only while marks exist (`start()` is called from `addMark`); it is cancelled when the tab is hidden and restarted when it becomes visible again and marks remain.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`, `keydown` on the canvas; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Cleanup:** stops the loop, clears marks, removes window/document listeners, restores container styles and empties the container.
- **Dependencies:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

The canvas fills its container (the stage). Logical drawing units are CSS pixels: `w` and `h` come from the canvas client size and the context is scaled by `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`. Pointer positions are converted with `getBoundingClientRect`, so touch positions and drawn marks share one pixel space. Marks do not scale with the screen size (radius 40-75 px on every device), so on a small phone they are relatively large. After a resize the canvas is redrawn at the new size; existing marks are not moved.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable |
| `setPointerCapture` failing | Wrapped in `try/catch` and ignored |
| Resize / orientation change | Canvas resized and redrawn; marks keep their positions |
| Backgrounding | Loop is cancelled; on return it restarts and marks continue (no age jump because `last` is reset) |
| Rapid or very fast input | At most 3 marks per move event; total capped at 150 |
| Touch cancellation | `pointercancel` and `lostpointercapture` remove the pointer |
| Keyboard key repeat | Each repeat adds a mark; the cap of 150 applies |
| Leaving during animation | Cleanup stops the loop and empties the container |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). No test report was found in the activity's PRs ([#15](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/15) and the keyboard commit).

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: tap once; a soft disc appears under the finger, drifts and fades within about 5 s.
- [ ] Drag slowly and quickly; a trail of marks follows the finger; very fast strokes look dotted but nothing freezes.
- [ ] Colours: successive marks cycle through the 6 colours starting with pink.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: none possible; confirm hovering a mouse without pressing does not paint.
- [ ] Multi-touch: draw with two or three fingers at once.
- [ ] Limit: scribble for 10 s; the app stays responsive and marks fade out afterwards; the screen returns to plain dark.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and reopen; the canvas is empty and the cycle starts with pink.
- [ ] Progression: none expected.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate during painting; the canvas fills the screen and touches line up with marks.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and stylus input.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the canvas (visible outline); arrows move the spot by 30 px and paint; Enter and Space paint in place; the spot stays inside the canvas.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tabs mid-fade; marks resume without jumping.
- [ ] Reduced motion: confirm marks still drift and fade (JavaScript-driven).
- [ ] Performance: on a low-end device draw continuously and watch for stutter.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No colour choice and no clear button (by design).
- Motion is not reduced for `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Mark size is fixed in pixels and not scaled to the screen.
- Fast strokes are limited to 3 marks per event.
- The keyboard light spot has no visible cursor of its own.

**Requires verification**

- Rendering performance with 150 simultaneous gradients on low-end devices.
- Brightness build-up of overlapping additive marks on very bright screens.

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md) (tracing), [Bańki Mydlane](banki-mydlane.md) (touch-created soft visuals), [Akwarium Artura](akwarium-artura.md) (canvas with one rAF loop).
- Does not use [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) or [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#8](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/8) / PR [#15](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/15): initial activity.
- Commit `72b4d31`: keyboard operability (arrows move and paint, Enter/Space paint) and a focus outline.

```
