## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/maly-pociag.md`

```markdown
# Mały Pociąg

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Mały Pociąg |
| Activity ID | `pociag` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A little train with three random animals in its wagons runs along a track; the child starts and stops it, sends it to the station, or makes an animal nod. |
| Category | Cause and effect; open-ended play; observation |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse, or Enter/Space on the focusable elements) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/pociag.js`](../../js/pociag.js), styles with prefix `tp-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

## 2. Business purpose

- Offers a slow, predictable cause-and-effect toy: one tap on the train makes it ease into motion, the next tap eases it to a stop, so the child sees the result of their own action.
- Complements the other vehicle activities (for example [Autobusik](autobusik.md) and [Traktor](traktor.md)) with a train that runs on a looping track and has a stopping point (the station).
- The three wagon animals come from the shared animal family, so the scene looks different on each launch.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 7.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; `mount()` builds the scene and starts a `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. Initially displayed: sky, sun, hills, a track, a station in the centre, and the train **parked** in the centre of the screen (in front of the station), with three random animals in three coloured wagons. A little steam puff is released every 2.4 s even while parked.
3. Interactions: tap the train (start/stop), tap the station (go to the station and stop there), tap an animal in a wagon (nod).
4. Response: the train ramps its speed over 2 s; a station tap plans a smooth stop at the station; an animal nods for 1.8 s.
5. There is no completion state.
6. Nothing ends or resets; the cycle repeats as long as the child plays.
7. Restart: leave and re-open the activity; a new random trio of animals is drawn and the train is parked again.
8. Exit: the Back button (or browser Back); `app.js` calls the cleanup function returned by `mount`.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Train tap | If the train is moving (cruising, accelerating or on its way to the station) it ramps down to 0 over `RAMP_S = 2` s; otherwise it ramps up to cruise speed over 2 s. Smoothstep easing, no sudden speed changes. |
| Cruise speed | `CROSS_S = 22` s per full loop (`V = 1/22` loop fractions per second). The loop length is the screen width plus the train width, so the train leaves on the right and re-enters on the left. |
| Station tap | Only has an effect while the train is not parked. It plans a cubic Hermite curve from the current speed to a standstill at the station position (train centred on screen). Duration `T = max(2.5 s, 1.2 * D / V)`, capped at `2.85 * D / v` so the train never reverses; if that would mean braking in under 2.5 s the train drives one more lap. |
| Station tap on a stopped, non-parked train | Because "not parked" is all that is checked, a train that was stopped by a train tap away from the station starts moving and drives to the station. |
| Station tap on a parked train | Ignored. |
| Train tap during a station approach | Cancels the plan and ramps to a stop from the current speed. |
| Animal tap | Nod lasting `NOD_S = 1.8` s (rotation up to 14 degrees, vertical offset up to 3 board units); a tap on an animal that is already nodding is ignored. Animal taps do not toggle the train. |
| Wheels | The five wheels rotate according to the distance travelled (`odo`). |
| Steam | Pool bounded by `MAX_PUFFS = 5`; each puff lives `PUFF_S = 3.2` s; one puff every 1.1 s while moving and every 2.4 s while stopped. |
| Time step | Capped at `MAX_DT = 0.05` s; the loop stops while the tab is hidden and restarts on `visibilitychange`. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (tap, train responds).
- Calm observation of slow, smooth motion.
- Early hand-eye coordination through tapping targets of different sizes.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Every state change is eased over about 2 s; there are no abrupt starts or stops, and the train never moves backwards.
- No wrong action exists, no score and no text.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about the effect of the activity on attention, language or other development. Nothing in the code can establish this.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) on `pointerdown`; the train (`role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`) reacts to Enter/Space; the station and the animal hit areas are native `<button>` elements that react to keyboard-generated clicks (`click` with `detail === 0`).
- **Labels (Polish):** train "Pociąg – ruszaj lub zatrzymaj", station "Stacja – zatrzymaj pociąg na stacji", animals "<name> w wagonie". The scene is a `role="group"` labelled "Mały pociąg".
- **Target sizes:** the animal buttons are 22 % of the train width by 66 % of its height with `min-width/min-height: 48px`; the train is `min(80 % of width, 560 px, 160 % of height)` wide; the station is 60 % of the train width.
- **Orientation:** layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`; the track sits at 72 % of the height.
- **Colour:** no meaning depends on colour; wagon colours are decorative.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion (movement, wheels, nodding, steam) is driven by the `requestAnimationFrame` loop, not CSS animations, so it still plays under the global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule.
- **Touch:** `touch-action: none` and `user-select: none` on the scene.
- **Reading:** not required. A young child can use it independently.
- **Limitations:** the animal buttons overlay the train; a press on an animal nods it and does not start the train.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Continuous gentle motion of the whole scene (the train crossing the screen) and a repeating steam puff, including while parked.
- The activity has no ending; it relies on the global playtime limit.
- An accidental tap on the train area stops or starts the train (no confirmation, which is intentional).
- On small screens the wagon animals become small; the touch area keeps a 48 px minimum.
- No privacy concerns: nothing is stored, no network calls.

## 8. Configuration

There is no external configuration; everything is a constant at the top of [`js/pociag.js`](../../js/pociag.js). Changing them requires editing the code.

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S` | Seconds for a full loop at cruise speed | 22 |
| `V` | Cruise speed (loop fractions per second) | `1 / CROSS_S` |
| `RAMP_S` | Duration of start and stop ramps | 2 s |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame time cap | 0.05 s |
| `MAX_PUFFS`, `PUFF_S` | Steam pool size and lifetime | 5, 3.2 s |
| `NOD_S` | Animal nod duration | 1.8 s |
| Wagon colours | `#f7a8c9`, `#a9d6f2`, `#ffd98a` (inline in `trainSvg`) | fixed |

Fallback for missing or invalid values: Not applicable (no external values). The only dependency is `window.Animals` (loaded before the activity script); there is no check for it being absent.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything is inline SVG and CSS: the train, wheels and station (`trainSvg`, `stationSvg`), the hills (`hillsSvg`), and the sun, ground and track (CSS). The wagon animals are heads from `window.Animals.head()` ([`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js)). The activity tile icon is an inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No audio, fonts or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- On every launch `window.Animals.pick(3)` selects three **unique** animals from the shared family of 13 (no `distinct` option, so similar silhouettes can occur together). The selection is not stored and there is no immediate-repetition guard between launches.
- Nothing else is random except the horizontal drift of each steam puff (6 to 12 units).
- Layout, wagon colours and animal positions in the train (wagon 1, 2, 3) are fixed.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels, scores or persistence; the train always starts parked in the centre.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no formal completion state and no failure. Feedback is purely the train's movement, wheel rotation, steam and the nodding animal. After a station stop the train simply waits until tapped again. No sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/pociag.js`](../../js/pociag.js) replaces the `mount` of the `pociag` registry entry; it returns a cleanup function that cancels the frame request, removes all listeners and removes the scene.
- **Rendering:** DOM plus inline SVG. The train is one `div` moved with a CSS `transform` each frame; wheels and animals are SVG groups whose `transform` attribute is set from JavaScript; steam puffs are pooled `div`s released above the chimney (at 91% of the train width).
- **State:** `f` (train position as a fraction of the loop; 0 = just off the left edge, 1 = just off the right edge), `v` (speed), `ramp`, `plan` (station approach), `parked`, `odo` (distance for the wheels), `nods[]`, `puffs[]`.
- **Layout:** `layout()` sets CSS variables `--tw`, `--th`, `--ty`; loop length `L = W + tw`; the station position is `fs = (tw + (W - tw) / 2) / L`. Because speed and positions are fractions of the loop, resizing or rotating keeps them valid; a moving station plan is re-planned from the current speed.
- **Events:** `pointerdown` (with `preventDefault`) plus `click` for keyboard activation (`detail === 0`); `keydown` Enter/Space on the train; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Randomization:** `Animals.pick(3)`.
- **Persistence and analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; the track is at `0.72 * H`; the train is `tw = min(0.8 * W, 560, 1.6 * H)` wide and `th = tw / 4` high.
- The train SVG uses `viewBox="0 0 400 100"` (three wagons 92 wide at x = 4, 104, 204; locomotive from x = 304 to 386, drawn facing right: the tall cab block at x 304 to 350 sits at the back next to the carriages, the boiler at x 326 to 386, the chimney at x 356 to 372 and the headlight at x 360 at the front). Animal heads are centred in each wagon. The station SVG is `viewBox="0 0 200 120"`.
- Moving elements use pixels (translate in px); the train position uses loop fractions, so changing the screen size does not move the stopping point away from the station.
- Portrait and landscape both work; no aspect-ratio-specific layout exists. Extremely wide, low screens are limited by the `1.6 * H` rule.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Resize / orientation change | `layout()` recomputes; a parked train is re-centred, a moving train continues, an active station approach is re-planned. |
| Tab hidden | Frame loop cancelled; restarted on return with a fresh time base, so time spent hidden is not replayed. |
| Rapid taps | Each tap restarts a ramp from the current speed; no abrupt change. |
| Station tap exactly at the station | Snaps to parked when the remaining distance is under 0.002 and the speed under 5 % of cruise. |
| Missing `window.Animals` | Not handled (script would throw on mount). |
| Touch cancel | Not specifically handled; taps are handled on `pointerdown`, so there is nothing to cancel. |
| Leaving the activity | Cleanup removes listeners and cancels the loop. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios to run (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; the train is parked in the centre; tap it; it eases into motion within about 2 s and leaves at the right edge and re-enters on the left.
- [ ] Tap the train again while moving; it eases to a halt without moving backwards.
- [ ] Station: tap the station while moving; the train slows smoothly and stops centred on the station; tap the station again while parked (nothing happens).
- [ ] Station tap just after the train passed the station (it should drive another lap rather than brake abruptly).
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap empty sky or ground; nothing happens.
- [ ] Animals: tap each animal; it nods once; tap it again while nodding (ignored); the train does not start.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-open the activity repeatedly; the animals vary and the train is parked each time.
- [ ] Randomization: over about 20 launches, check that all 13 animals can appear and that no duplicates occur within a train.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that there is none (nothing changes over time).
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: layout, train size, station placement and animal buttons; rotate during travel and during a station approach.
- [ ] Touch (Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad): tap accuracy on animals, no scrolling or zooming.
- [ ] Mouse (desktop): clicks work; right button also triggers (no button filter).
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the train, station and animals; Enter/Space activate them; focus outline visible.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tab during travel; on return, motion continues smoothly with no jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion: enable the OS setting; the train, wheels, steam and nodding still move.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad (as required by the README).

PR [#39](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/39) reports a Node run against a DOM stub (train starts parked, ramps up, never moves backwards while stopping, station stop lands exactly on the station) and lists manual device tests as pending.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- Steam is released continuously even while the train is parked.
- No keyboard or screen-reader state: the train button does not announce whether it is moving.
- The animal pool allows visually similar animals in the same train (no `distinct`).
- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Behaviour of the animal hit areas versus the train area on very small screens (48 px minimum).
- Visual fit of larger animals (Słoń trunk, Lew mane) in the wagons; PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137) lists it as a pending manual check.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned. (The locomotive direction fix is done, see issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173).)

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other vehicle activities: [Autobusik](autobusik.md), [Traktor](traktor.md), [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md), [Mały Samolot](maly-samolot.md).
- Shared animals: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`); the same family is used by [Dobranoc](dobranoc.md), [Zwierzątka na Farmie](zwierzatka-na-farmie.md), [Zabawa w Chowanego](zabawa-w-chowanego.md), [Cienie](cienie.md) and [Buźki](buzki.md).
- The rAF loop pattern (capped time step, restarts on `visibilitychange`) is shared with several other activities.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#30](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/30) / PR [#39](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/39): initial activity (including reviewer-suggested refinements).
- Issue [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): wagon animals drawn at random from the shared animal family.
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): fixed on `main`; the locomotive now faces the direction of travel (chimney and headlight at the front, steam puffs released above the chimney at 91% of the train width).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/maly-samolot.md`

```markdown
# Mały Samolot

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Mały Samolot |
| Internal ID | `samolot` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A little propeller plane with an animal pilot on a runway among hills and clouds; touching the plane makes it take off and fly slowly, touching it again lands it. |
| Category | Cause and effect, open-ended play, observation |
| Interaction type | Tap (plane, clouds, pilot); keyboard: Enter/Space on the plane, native activation of cloud and pilot buttons |
| CSS prefix | `sa-` |
| Source | [`js/samolot.js`](../../js/samolot.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section `/* Mały Samolot */`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default (no `defaultOff`). Listed 32nd in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity lets a child control a plane with single taps and watch a slow, smooth flight. It supports calm observation and simple cause and effect (tap, take off; tap, land) and adds small surprises (the plane circles a touched cloud, the pilot waves). Motion is deliberately slow (about 15 s to cross the screen) and the plane never moves backwards. Each launch looks different through random plane colour, airport, weather and pilot, which keeps the activity fresh without any score or goal.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#samolot`). The scene is built with a random plane colour, airport, weather and pilot (section 10).
2. The plane is parked on the runway at 30% of the screen width; three clouds drift slowly in the sky.
3. **Tap the parked plane:** it takes off and flies a slow loop (an ellipse) around the sky.
4. **Tap the flying plane:** it descends and lands on the runway in about 4 s.
5. **Tap the plane while it is landing:** a go-around; it climbs again.
6. **Tap a cloud while flying:** the plane curves toward it, circles it once and returns to its loop. **Tap a cloud while parked:** the cloud just drifts a little to the side (2.6 s).
7. **Tap the pilot:** the pilot waves a paw for 2.4 s (does not toggle the plane).
8. There is no completion state; the activity runs until the child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (constant) |
|---|---|
| Crossing time at cruise | `CROSS_S = 15` s per screen width (cruise speed `sc = W / 15` px/s) |
| Landing time | `LAND_S = 4` s (cubic Hermite curve from the current position and velocity to the runway) |
| Flight path | ellipse centred at (W/2, 0.4H), radii `rx = 0.34W` (landscape) or `0.3W` (portrait), `ry = 0.22H`; the plane follows a look-ahead point on it |
| Direction | the plane never flies backwards: its heading is rate-limited and smoothed; take-off direction follows the way the plane is facing |
| Turn rate limit | `Om = sc / Rt`, where `Rt = max(min(W, H) * 0.12, pw * 0.3, sc / 0.7)` |
| Cloud orbit | radius `R = 1.15 * Rt`; ends after one full sweep (`2 pi`) or after 40 s; the last tapped cloud wins |
| Landing direction | lands in the current direction; if there is little room ahead it turns around and lands the other way |
| Soft trail | at most `MAX_PUFFS = 8` puffs, one every `PUFF_EVERY = 0.55` s, life `PUFF_S = 2.6` s, only when the plane is moving faster than 0.3 x cruise |
| Pilot wave | `WAVE_S = 2.4` s |
| Cloud nudge (tap while parked) | `NUDGE_S = 2.6` s, displacement up to `min(W * 0.03, 26)` px |
| Propeller | spin eases with speed (up to about 1.1 revolutions per second), blur disc opacity up to 0.28 |
| Weather | decoration only: sunny (nothing extra), cloudy (greyer sky and clouds), rain (`RAIN_N = 26` drops), snow (`SNOW_N = 22` flakes); drawn in a non-interactive layer below the clouds and plane |

The plane is a kinematic body (position, heading, speed) and is flipped vertically (`scale(1, sy)`) when it flies left so it is never shown upside down.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (not measured)

- Cause and effect: one tap changes what the plane does.
- Calm visual tracking of a slowly moving object.
- Imaginative play (animal pilot, weather, airports).

**Directly observable behavior**

- Different taps have distinct, gentle consequences (take off, land, circle a cloud, wave).
- Random scenery changes between launches without changing the controls.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any developmental effect of watching or steering the plane.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus (the plane, clouds and pilot react on `pointerdown`, so the response is immediate); keyboard: the plane is focusable (`tabindex="0"`, `role="button"`, `aria-label` `Samolot – wzlatuj lub ląduj`) and Enter/Space toggles it; the clouds (`Chmurka 1 – samolot poleci wokół niej` and so on) and the pilot (`<animal> pilot – pomachaj`) are real buttons. The scene is a `role="group"` with the label `Mały samolot`.
- **Target size:** the plane box is `pw x ph` with `pw = clamp(min(W * 0.42, H * 0.5), 170, 320)` and `ph = pw / 2`; clouds are `clamp(W * 0.2, 96, 190)` px wide (at least 96 x 56); the pilot button is at least 56 x 56 px.
- **Orientation:** layout and the flight ellipse are recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`; the flight state is rescaled.
- **Colour:** controls do not depend on colour; the plane colour and weather are decoration.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Reduced motion:** the flight, propeller, trail, wave and cloud drift are driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` loop and the code contains no `prefers-reduced-motion` check, so **they continue under reduced motion**. Only the CSS rain/snow animation (`sa-fall`) is disabled by the global rule; the drops and flakes then stay at their random start positions. Motion is slow by design (about 15 s per screen crossing).
- **Touch behaviour:** `.sa` has `touch-action: none`; text selection disabled.
- **Focus:** 4 px outline `#8f7fd1` on the plane, clouds and pilot button.
- **Limitations:** a parked plane partly overlapping a cloud button hides that cloud from touch (the plane has a higher z-index); the flashing-like propeller effect is described in section 7.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The propeller blur oscillates (`scaleY` follows `|cos|` of the angle) at up to roughly 2.2 cycles per second at full speed (a figure computed from the code, not measured); `Requires verification` against accessibility guidance on flashing.
- The animation loop never stops while the activity is open (even when the plane is parked, the clouds drift), which uses CPU/battery for as long as it is open (it is paused while the tab is hidden).
- Weather particles (rain 26, snow 22) fall continuously and are the only part of the motion that respects reduced motion.
- The activity has no ending; a child may fly indefinitely.
- No personal data is collected; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/samolot.js`](../../js/samolot.js):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S` | Seconds to cross the screen width at cruise | s | `15` |
| `LAND_S` | Landing duration | s | `4` |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap | s | `0.05` |
| `MAX_PUFFS`, `PUFF_S`, `PUFF_EVERY` | Trail size, life and interval | number, s, s | `8`, `2.6`, `0.55` |
| `WAVE_S`, `NUDGE_S` | Pilot wave and cloud nudge | s | `2.4`, `2.6` |
| `PLANES`, `AIRPORTS`, `WEATHERS`, `PILOTS` | Content pools | arrays | 6, 3, 4, 6 entries |
| `RAIN_N`, `SNOW_N` | Weather particle counts | number | `26`, `22` |
| `CF` | Cloud centres as screen fractions | array | `[0.2,0.3] [0.5,0.27] [0.8,0.35]` |

No fallback because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files; everything is inline SVG and CSS built in JavaScript: the plane (`planeSvg`, 200 x 100 viewBox) with the pilot head, clouds (`cloudSvg`, 160 x 90), hills (`hillsSvg`, 1000 x 200, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`), airport buildings (tower, hangar, terminal, 120 x 100), CSS sun, runway, ground and weather particles. The pilots are drawn locally in this file; they do not use the shared `Animals` family. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No unused assets.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Chosen once per launch, independently, with `Rand.pickOne` (never the same value as the previous pick for the same key within the page session):

| Pool | Key | Size | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plane colours | `samolot-plane` | 6 | pink, mint, yellow, lilac, orange, blue (body, wing and tail colours) |
| Airports | `samolot-airport` | 3 | tower, hangar, terminal (each with its own runway, ground and hill colours) |
| Weather | `samolot-weather` | 4 | sunny, cloudy, rain, snow |
| Pilots | `samolot-pilot` | 6 | Miś, Zajączek, Kotek, Piesek, Myszka, Lisek |

That gives 432 combinations. The scene does not change while the activity is open. Rain and snow particles get random positions, delays and durations at build time. Nothing is persisted.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels and nothing is stored.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is the plane's motion (take off, landing, circling), propeller spin, trail, cloud nudge and pilot wave. No score, sound or failure feedback. The interaction cycle is: tap -> plane responds -> keep flying or park.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/samolot.js`](../../js/samolot.js), registered on the `samolot` entry; returns a cleanup function. The activity does not set `container.style.display`; the `.sa` scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`.
- **State:** plane state `st` (`parked`, `flying`, `landing`), position `x, y`, heading `psi`, speed `spd`, turn rate `om`, facing `face`, vertical flip `sy`, `orbit`, `land` (Hermite plan), `propA`/`propW`, `puffs`, `waveT`, `cloudNudge[3]`, `clock`.
- **Rendering:** a DOM scene (sun, hills SVG, weather layer, ground, airport SVG, runway, three cloud buttons, trail layer, plane `div` with an inline SVG and the pilot button). Plane and clouds are moved with `transform`; the propeller and the paw are animated through SVG `transform` attributes.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`, `dt` capped at 50 ms). It keeps requesting frames while the tab is visible (no idle stop), and is cancelled when `document.hidden` and restarted on return. The `sa-fall` CSS keyframe animation is used only for weather particles.
- **Events:** `pointerdown` (and `click` with `detail === 0` for keyboard) for the plane, clouds and pilot via `bindTap`; pilot and clouds stop propagation so they do not toggle the plane; `keydown` (Enter/Space) on the plane; `resize`/`orientationchange`/`visibilitychange`.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.pickOne` ([`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)); particle positions with `Math.random`.
- **Persistence/analytics:** none.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes all tap listeners (collected in `offs`), keydown, window and document listeners, removes remaining puffs and the scene.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene covers the whole screen (`position: fixed; inset: 0`, not inset below the Back button). Coordinates are CSS pixels in the scene (`W = clientWidth`, `H = clientHeight`).
- Static layers use percentages and CSS variables: runway at `--ry = 0.86 H`, plane parked at `yC = runY - ph * 0.43`, airport on the right (`right: 4%`, width `clamp(70px, 16vw, 130px)`), sun at the top right, hills in the bottom 50%.
- Moving elements (plane, clouds, trail) are positioned with `transform: translate` in the same pixel space; on resize the plane position is scaled by the new/old size ratio and an ongoing landing plan is rescaled.
- Cloud positions are screen fractions (`CF`) with a small sinusoidal drift (up to `min(W * 0.012, 10)` px horizontally and 4 px vertically) and are kept at least `R + 10` px from the top.
- Plane, cloud and runway sizes derive from `W` and `H`, so portrait and landscape work; no fixed viewBox is shared between layers (each SVG has its own viewBox).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable. |
| Rapid taps on the plane | Each tap changes state (parked, flying, landing, go-around); no lock. |
| Tap during landing | Go-around: the plane resumes flying from its current velocity. |
| Cloud tapped while parked or landing | The cloud nudges aside (2.6 s); the plane is not affected. |
| Little room to land ahead | The plane turns around and lands the other way. |
| Resize/orientation change | State is rescaled (`layout`). |
| Tab hidden | The loop is cancelled; on return `last` is reset and `dt` is capped, so there is no jump. |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | Not used. |
| Leaving mid-flight | Cleanup removes listeners, puffs and the scene. |
| Touch cancellation | Not relevant (taps act on `pointerdown`). |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#102](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/102) reports `node --check` and a stubbed-DOM simulation (take-off, 60 s loop, cloud orbit, landings at varied phases, relanding, cleanup) with no jumps and landings ending parked; PR [#151](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/151) describes the random scenery. These are not re-verified here.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: tap the parked plane to take off, watch a full loop, tap to land (about 4 s).
- [ ] Go-around: tap the plane while landing; it climbs again.
- [ ] Clouds: tap each cloud while flying (plane circles once and resumes) and while parked (cloud drifts aside); tap a second cloud mid-orbit.
- [ ] Pilot: tap the pilot while flying and parked; the paw waves for about 2.4 s and the plane state does not change.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the sky, the runway and the airport; nothing happens or breaks.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: re-open the activity about 10 times and check that plane colour, airport, weather and pilot vary and none repeats twice in a row.
- [ ] Progression/completion: confirm there is no end state or level.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: 320 x 568, 568 x 320, tablet; rotate while flying and while landing; the plane stays on screen.
- [ ] Touch and mouse: finger, mouse, keyboard (Tab to the plane, Enter/Space; Tab to clouds and pilot).
- [ ] Weather: observe rain and snow scenes for a minute and confirm the particles stay behind clouds and plane.
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab mid-flight and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion: confirm that the flight still runs and the rain/snow stops falling.
- [ ] Performance: leave the activity open for several minutes on a low-end device.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The frame loop never idles while the tab is visible.
- Flight and propeller motion are not reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion` (only rain and snow stop).
- The plane overlaps and hides a cloud button when they coincide.
- The pilots are drawn locally and are not the shared animal family.

**Requires verification**

- Propeller oscillation rate against flashing guidance (section 7).
- Behaviour of the landing curve on extreme aspect ratios.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other vehicle activities: [Mały Pociąg](maly-pociag.md), [Balon](balon.md), [Latawiec](latawiec.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- [#90](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/90) / PR [#102](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/102): activity added (bear pilot, fixed scenery).
- [#127](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/127) / PR [#151](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/151): random plane colour, airport, weather and pilot animal.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/mieszanie-kolorow.md`

```markdown
# Mieszanie Kolorów

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Mieszanie Kolorów |
| Activity ID | `mieszanie` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Red, yellow and blue paint blobs are dragged into a big pot; two different colours blend into a new one. |
| Category | Cause and effect; combining; open-ended play; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop (touch, mouse), keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/mieszanie.js`](../../js/mieszanie.js), styles with prefix `mx-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |
| Issue | [#211](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/211) |

## 2. Business purpose

- The first activity where the child combines things to make something new; colour otherwise appears only in sorting ([Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md)).
- Every mix is a happy surprise: no wrong answers, no failure.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile and sees a big glass pot on a warm background and a wooden shelf with three paint blobs.
2. Drag a blob over the pot (the pot gets a white outline) and release: it flies in (0.25 s) with a soft splash ring.
3. The first blob colours the pot. A second **different** blob blends the pot colour over 1.5 s into the mix.
4. The result blob (same pattern as the mix) rises above the pot and glows for 3 s; then the pot empties over 1 s and the next round starts.
5. When all three different mixes have been made once, a friendly animal in the matching colour sits beside the pot for that 3 s glow (fox, frog or bunny), and the set starts counting again.
6. Every new mixed colour is remembered: a blob in that colour appears on a second shelf (below the pot row in portrait, a column at the right edge in landscape) and can be dragged into the pot like the three basic ones. The shelf keeps the last 4 created colours; the oldest is replaced. Mixing any two different blobs gives a colour (the average of the two) with its own white mark; the three basic pairs give orange, green and purple. Memory lives only while the activity is open.
7. The rounds repeat without end. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Blobs | Red (1 dot), yellow (2 dots), blue (3 dots), each at least 72 px; the shelf blob reappears (fade 0.5 s) after a drop, so each can be used any number of times. |
| Mixes | red + yellow = orange (stripes), yellow + blue = green (zigzag), red + blue = purple (ring). |
| Same colour twice | The pot just stays that colour with a small glow (1 s); no result, no `complete()`. A different colour dropped afterwards mixes with it. |
| Drop target | The pot plus a 16 px margin and the space above its opening. A blob released elsewhere, or while the pot is mixing, glowing or emptying, drifts back in 0.5 s. |
| Saved colours | Up to 4 (`SAVED_MAX`), 56-64 px, newest last; a colour already on a shelf or within 24 (summed RGB difference) of one is not added again. Mixed colours get one of six white marks (square, triangle, diamond, cross, wave, smile) so colour is not the only cue. |
| Animal | Appears only when the three different mixes have each been made since the start or since the last animal. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. No text on screen. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect and drag-and-drop with a finger.
- Noticing that colours combine into new ones.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Two different blobs always produce the matching colour and pattern, and a mix is never wrong.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- Blobs are `button`s with Polish `aria-label`s; Tab moves between them and Enter or Space drops the focused blob into the pot (keyboard alternative to dragging).
- Colour is never the only cue: dots on the basic blobs, and stripes, zigzag or ring on the mixes and animals.
- Targets: blobs 72-100 px; the pot is at least 30% of the screen width.
- Reduced motion: every state is driven by one rAF loop, so all states are reached; motion is slow (no turn faster than one per second, no flashing).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Rendering was not checked in a real browser by the implementing agent (only syntax and a stub-DOM simulation); see section 17.
- On a 568x320 screen the result blob rises close to the top edge (not over the Back button).

## 8. Configuration

None. Texts are only the Polish `aria-label`s.

## 9. Assets

Everything is inline SVG (blobs, pot, three animals) drawn in `js/mieszanie.js`; the menu icon is in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

None; the mixes are deterministic (the three basic pairs are fixed, every other pair gives the average colour).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None.

## 12. Completion and feedback

Each finished mix is a completion (`complete()`); feedback is the colour blend, a glowing result blob and, after a full set, an animal. The activity never ends by itself.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

`js/app.js` records start and end and the module counts touches. `js/mieszanie.js` additionally calls `window.Analytics.track('interaction', { variant })` on each drop accepted by the pot (a blob released over the pot while it is mixing, glowing or emptying just drifts back and is not counted) with the blob colour (`red`, `yellow`, `blue`, `orange`, `green`, `purple`, or `mixed` for any other) and `complete()` for each mix. Nothing else is stored; the saved colours are not persisted.

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/mieszanie.js`](../../js/mieszanie.js) overrides `mount` of the `mieszanie` entry; returns a cleanup function (listeners, rAF, root).
- **Rendering:** `div.mx > shelf + glow + pot svg + result blob + animal + splash + button.mx-blob per basic and saved colour`; the root is attached with `container.appendChild(root)` before layout.
- **State:** pot phase `open`, `mix`, `glow`, `empty`; numeric tweens for the fill level and the liquid colour (kept as `[r,g,b]`, never re-parsed from strings); blob modes `home`, `drag`, `back`, `fly`.
- **Loop:** one capped-dt (0.05 s) rAF loop, stopped when idle and while the page is hidden.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.mx` is fixed full-screen; positions are pixels recomputed in `layout()` on `resize` and `orientationchange`; the pot state, level and colour are kept.
- Saved blobs are 56-64 px: a row above the shelf when the height is at least 400 px, otherwise a column at the right edge (the basic blobs and the pot are centred in the remaining width).
- Blob size is 72 px when the height is under 400 px, otherwise `min(width / 3.6, 100)` (at least 80). Pot width is `min(50% of the width, available height x 1.18)`, never below 31% of the width where height allows.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Rotation or resize | Layout recomputed; the pot colour, level and phase are kept. |
| Tab hidden and shown | The loop pauses and resumes; timers are time-stepped, not wall-clock. |
| Very fast repeated touches | Drops are handled in order; a drop while the pot is busy drifts back. |
| Two fingers | The second pointer is ignored while one blob is dragged. |
| Analytics missing or failing | Ignored. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag red then yellow into the pot: it turns orange over 1.5 s, an orange striped blob glows for 3 s, the pot empties over 1 s.
- [ ] Repeat for yellow + blue (green) and red + blue (purple), then check that an animal appears beside the pot during the third glow.
- [ ] Drop red twice: the pot stays red with a small glow and no result appears.
- [ ] Release a blob next to the pot: it returns in 0.5 s.
- [ ] Tab to a blob and press Enter or Space: it is dropped into the pot.
- [ ] Make several mixes and check the new colours appear on the second shelf, can be dragged into the pot, and the fifth new colour replaces the oldest.
- [ ] After a keyboard drop, focus stays on the blob (Tab is not needed again).
- [ ] Rotate the device in the middle of a mix and check nothing is lost; hide and show the tab.
- [ ] With reduced motion enabled, check that all states are still reached.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; the stub-DOM simulation used during development is not part of the repository.

**Unverified**

- Visual appearance on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md) (colour sorting).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#211](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/211): initial activity.
- PR #243 review follow-up: remembered mixed colours (second shelf), keyboard focus kept after a drop, metrics only for accepted drops.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/moj-dzien.md`

```markdown
# Mój Dzień

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Mój Dzień |
| Activity ID | `mojdzien` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), appended last) |
| Description | Four tiles (a sun, a bowl, a ball and a moon) each play a 6 s scene of one random animal's day: waking up, eating, playing, sleeping. |
| Category | Daily routine; cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse, keyboard) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default |
| Source | [`js/mojdzien.js`](../../js/mojdzien.js), styles with prefix `md-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |
| Issue | [#220](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/220) |

## 2. Business purpose

- Shows the order of a day (morning, meal, play, night) in pictures, without clock numbers or text; Dobranoc covers only the evening.
- Calm and without failure: tiles can be touched in any order.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The activity opens with a calm animal in daylight and four tiles in a row at the bottom.
2. Touching a tile starts that scene (6 s); the sky blends to the time of day over 1 s.
3. Touching any tile during a scene restarts or replaces it; only one scene runs at a time.
4. A scene counts as seen as soon as it is started (a scene cut short still counts); the finale follows when the scene playing after all four were seen reaches its end; the final frame stays until the next touch.
5. When all four have been seen, the tiles glow for 3 s and the animal waves; then a different animal and a new set begin.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Scene | Tile picture | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | sun | Animal asleep in bed, opens its eyes, sits up, stretches with raised arms, yawns; the sun rises. |
| Meal | bowl | Animal leans to the bowl and eats; the food gets lower. |
| Play | ball | A ball bounces and the animal hops side to side after it. |
| Night | moon | Sun sets, moon and stars fade in, the animal closes its eyes, is covered by a blanket and "z" signs rise. |

- Scene length `DUR = 6` s, finale `FINALE = 3` s, pose blend between scenes 0.35 s, sky blend 1 s.
- Sky colours (top, bottom): morning `#b9dff5/#ffe0bd`, meal `#9fd3f3/#e4f3fb`, play `#a9d9f0/#fff0c4`, night `#2f3b78/#6f66ae`.
- "Seen" means the scene was started, so a scene cut short by another touch still counts; the finale starts when a scene plays to its end after all four have been seen. The set resets at the finale.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

- Sequence of a day, linked to familiar actions (waking, eating, playing, sleeping); no scoring.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- Tiles are native buttons (at least 72 px; four in a row from 320 px width); Tab to a tile, Enter/Space plays it. Polish `aria-label`s: Rano, Posiłek, Zabawa, Noc.
- Meaning is carried by four different pictures (not colour); focus ring is a white outline plus a purple halo.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Poses are drawn from the shared animal heads with simple arms; scene art was verified only with a stub DOM, not in a real browser.

## 8. Configuration

None; constants at the top of `js/mojdzien.js`.

## 9. Assets

All drawn inline in SVG; the animal head comes from `window.Animals`. No sound, no images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

One random animal per launch (`Animals.pick(1)`), never the same as the previous one; a new animal after each full set.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None.

## 12. Completion and feedback

When the fourth distinct scene ends: glow on all tiles for 3 s (box-shadow and 5% scale, driven from the rAF loop) and the animal waves; then a new set starts.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

`track('interaction', { variant })` on every scene start (variant `morning`, `meal`, `play`, `night`); `complete()` when a set of four has been seen.

## 14. Technical implementation

- One SVG scene (200x150, `meet`) plus a tile row. Every pose is a pure function of scene time (`pose(kind, t)`) painted from one capped-dt rAF loop, so reduced motion does not disable anything; the loop stops when the scene is held.
- Sky gradient, glow and pose blending are interpolated in JS. `mount` returns a cleanup that cancels rAF and removes listeners and DOM.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

`.md` is fixed full screen with 56 px reserved at the top for Back; the sky fills the remaining height and the tile row (max 424 px, 320 px when the height is under 420 px) sits at the bottom. State lives in JS, so rotation and resizing keep it.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

Fast repeated touches restart the scene without stacking; a hidden tab restarts the rAF clock (dt capped at 50 ms); multi-touch is just several clicks; analytics errors are swallowed.

## 17. Testing

Manual scenarios:

1. Open the tile: four tiles, a standing animal.
2. Touch each tile once: scene runs about 6 s, sky changes; final frame stays.
3. Touch a tile three times quickly: it restarts, nothing duplicates.
4. See all four: tiles glow 3 s, the animal waves, then a new animal.
5. Tab to a tile and press Enter / Space.
6. Rotate the device mid-scene: nothing resets.
7. Enable reduced motion: scenes still play.

A node stub-DOM simulation covered: restart, completion count (one per set), glow on and off, cleanup and no NaN in painted values.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

Not checked on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

[Dobranoc](dobranoc.md), [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md); `window.Animals`, `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

Added by issue #220.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/myjnia.md`

```markdown
# Myjnia

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Myjnia |
| Internal ID | `myjnia` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A muddy vehicle or animal stands in a car wash with soft foam clouds. Dragging a finger over it scrubs the mud away and releases soap bubbles; when it is clean it glows softly and a new muddy one fades in. |
| Category | Cause and effect / open-ended play (scrubbing) |
| Interaction type | Drag / scrub (pointer events); keyboard alternative (arrow keys move a brush, Enter or Space scrubs along a zig-zag) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/myjnia.js`](../../js/myjnia.js), CSS block `/* Myjnia */` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (prefix `mj`) |

## 2. Business purpose

A scrubbing game with an immediate, visible effect: the child's gesture removes mud and produces bubbles, and the clean drawing underneath appears. It has no targets or rules to learn, so it suits the youngest users, and the soft bubbles and glow give a calm reward. The variety of six vehicles, six colours and six animals (in a repeating pattern of two vehicles and one animal) keeps replay interesting. The animals are drawn in the activity's own style; the dog appears more often than the others. A related animal-only washing activity is [Kąpiel Zwierzątek](kapiel-zwierzatek.md).

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#myjnia`); the first item (always a vehicle) is built and shown covered with mud.
2. The item stands in a 5:3 box in the middle of the screen on a light-blue background with three foam clouds.
3. The child drags a finger (or mouse) over the item. Mud is erased along the whole path, and soap bubbles rise from the touch point.
4. When about 90% of the mud is gone, the remaining mud fades (1.2 s) and the item glows softly for 3 s; six extra bubbles float up.
5. At 7 s after reaching 90% the item fades out (0.7 s), a new muddy item is built and fades in (0.7 s).
6. The sequence continues indefinitely: vehicle, vehicle, animal, vehicle, vehicle, animal, ...
7. The child leaves with the Back button (see [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (from `js/myjnia.js`) |
|---|---|
| Item sequence | Item `n` (0-based) is an animal when `n % 3 === 2`, otherwise a vehicle: V V A V V A ... |
| Vehicles | 6 types (samochód, autobus, ciężarówka, furgonetka, traktor, kamper) x 6 body colours |
| Animals | 6 (słoń, świnka, krowa, hipopotam, piesek, owieczka), each with its own colours |
| Mud mask | Canvas with logical size `LW x LH = 480 x 288` (5:3), mud drawn on the item's silhouette in `#b99a7a` with 46 random darker/lighter blotches |
| Brush | Round-cap stroke, at least 44 CSS px wide (`brushLogical = max(44, 0.11 * boxW)` converted to logical units) |
| Completion threshold | `DONE_AT = 0.9`: remaining mud at most 10% of the starting mud, measured every 0.12 s while the mask has changed |
| Mud fade | `FADE_MUD_S = 1.2` s (immediate with reduced motion) |
| Glow | `GLOW_S = 3` s, with 0.5 s ease in and out |
| Next item | `NEXT_AT_S = 7` s after completion, with `SWAP_S = 0.7` s fade out and 0.7 s fade in |
| Bubbles | Pool of `MAX_BUBBLES = 28`; at most one spawn every `SPAWN_GAP_S = 0.09` s while scrubbing; life `BUBBLE_S = 1.8` s; radius 2-4.5% of the box width; rise 18% of the box height; fade out |
| Input | `pointerdown`/`move` erase in phases `play` and `done`; ignored while swapping |
| Failure | None; mud never returns while the item is on screen |
| Sound | None ([shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)) |

- Keyboard: the box is focusable (`tabindex="0"`, `role="application"`, label such as "Brudny pojazd: autobus. Strzałki przesuwają szczotkę, Enter lub spacja szoruje dalej."). Arrow keys move the brush by 0.07 of the box (limits 0.04-0.96 horizontally, 0.06-0.94 vertically) and scrub; Enter/Space moves it one step along a zig-zag, going down 0.12 at each edge and wrapping to the top. A ring shows the brush position while the box has focus.
- Several pointers can scrub at the same time (each has its own stroke state).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (design intent, not measured):
- Cause and effect (a gesture changes the picture).
- Gross and fine motor coordination through scrubbing.
- Recognition of vehicles and animals.

**Directly observable behavior:**
- Mud disappears exactly where the finger passes and stays gone.
- Bubbles appear while scrubbing; a clean item glows and is replaced by a new one.
- No scores, timers or error messages.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about motor development or learning.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) with pointer capture on the box and `touch-action: none`; keyboard alternative as above with a 4 px focus ring (`#8f7fd1`).
- **Screen readers:** the box has a Polish `aria-label` naming the current item (vehicle or animal); progress and completion are not announced.
- **Target size:** the whole box is the interaction area (width `max(120, min(0.96 * field width, 0.9 * field height * 5/3, 680))` px); the brush is at least 44 px wide.
- **Orientation:** the box scales with the field in both orientations; the canvas is in logical coordinates, so cleaned areas are kept on resize or rotation.
- **Colour:** mud and drawings are decorative; nothing depends on colour.
- **Reduced motion:** the mud fade, glow, bubbles and item swap are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with inline styles, so they still run under the global CSS rule; with `prefers-reduced-motion` the mud disappears immediately (no 1.2 s fade). The brush is not slowed.
- **Reading:** none required.
- **Limitations:** the glow and the bubbles carry no non-visual cue; there is no sound.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The canvas coverage measure (`getImageData` on a 48x29 downscale) and the 90% threshold depend on real canvas behaviour; PR [#82](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/82) says they were not checked in a real browser.
- Very small leftover mud patches are ignored once 90% is reached (by design).
- Bubble spawning is limited to 28 simultaneous bubbles and every 90 ms, so continuous scrubbing is bounded in cost.
- Mud blotches are re-randomised for each item, so appearance varies (not a risk).
- No privacy concerns; nothing stored or sent.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants are inside [`js/myjnia.js`](../../js/myjnia.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LW`, `LH` | Logical size of the mud mask | px | 480, 288 | top of IIFE |
| `VB` | Width of the vehicle drawing viewBox (200 x 120) | number | 200 | top of IIFE |
| `MAX_BUBBLES`, `BUBBLE_S`, `SPAWN_GAP_S` | Bubble pool size, life, spawn spacing | number, s, s | 28, 1.8, 0.09 | top of IIFE |
| `DONE_AT` | Fraction of mud removed to finish | number | 0.9 | top of IIFE |
| `FADE_MUD_S`, `GLOW_S`, `NEXT_AT_S`, `SWAP_S` | Mud fade, glow, time to next item, swap fade (s) | numbers | 1.2, 3, 7, 0.7 | top of IIFE |
| `DOG_WEIGHT` | Selection weight of the dog (others are 1) | number | 3 | before `pickAnimal` |
| `COLOURS` | 6 vehicle body colours | array | 6 entries | top of IIFE |
| `VEHICLES`, `ANIMALS` | Drawings as arrays of `{ d (path), fill }` | arrays | 6 + 6 entries | top of IIFE |

No fallback for invalid values because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external files. All vehicles and animals are inline SVG path data (`VEHICLES`, `ANIMALS`), used both for the clean SVG layer (`svgFor`) and, via `Path2D`, for the mud silhouette drawn on the canvas. Foam clouds and the background are CSS (radial gradient, linear gradient `#d8ecfb` to `#cfe3ee`). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. This activity does **not** use the shared animal drawings of [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js). No fonts, images or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | How | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| Vehicle type | `Rand.pickOne(VEHICLES, 'myjnia-vehicle')`: never the same as the previous vehicle | 6 |
| Vehicle colour | `Rand.pickOne(COLOURS, 'myjnia-colour')`: never the same as the previous colour | 6 |
| Animal | `pickAnimal()`: weighted choice, dog weight 3 and others 1, excluding the animal shown previously | 6 |
| Mud blotches | `Math.random` positions and shades, 46 blotches per item | - |

- The no-repeat memory (`Rand`'s last pick, and `lastAnimal`) lives for the page session, so it also applies across re-opening the activity; it is reset by a page reload.
- Because the dog is excluded right after it appears, its long-run share is about 30% (about 2.1 times each other animal) rather than a flat 3/8, as PR [#165](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/165) notes; the dog never appears twice in a row.
- The V V A pattern is fixed (animals every third item); only the contents vary. Nothing is stored.
- Pools are fixed arrays, so empty pools cannot occur.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. The only recurring structure is the V V A pattern; nothing becomes harder, and nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion: at least 90% of the mud removed.
- Feedback: remaining mud fades, the item glows softly (yellow drop-shadow `#ffe08a`) for 3 s and six extra bubbles float up.
- After 7 s the next item replaces it automatically.
- Failure: none. No sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/myjnia.js`](../../js/myjnia.js), replacing `mount` of the `myjnia` registry entry; returns `cleanup`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `div.mj > div.mj-field` with three `div.mj-foam` clouds and `div.mj-box` containing `div.mj-clean` (the clean SVG), `canvas.mj-mud` (480 x 288), `div.mj-brush` (keyboard ring) and `div.mj-bubbles` (28 pooled `div.mj-bub`).
- **Mud mask:** `drawMud()` fills the item's paths in `#b99a7a` on the canvas, adds blotches with `source-atop`, and records `baseline` (sum of alpha on a 48 x 29 downscale). `erase()` strokes with `destination-out`. `remaining()` re-measures the downscale.
- **State:** `item` (label, shapes, `animal`), `seq` (item counter), `phase` (`play`, `done`, `swap`), `phaseT`, `mudOp`, `glow`, `boxOp`, `swapDir`, `pointers` (last point per pointer), `kx`/`ky`/`kdir` (keyboard brush), `bubbles`.
- **Events:** `pointerdown/move/up/cancel`, `lostpointercapture`, `keydown`, `focus`, `blur` on the box; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Animation:** one `frame()` loop (dt capped at 0.05 s) that stops when idle; paused while hidden. The coverage check runs every 0.12 s only when the mask changed.
- **Randomization:** `Rand.pickOne` and the local weighted `pickAnimal()`.
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js). **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** none from the activity itself (reported by `js/app.js`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame and removes the window/document listeners and the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.mj` is fixed full-screen; `.mj-field` is a flex container inset by the safe-area variables plus 64 px at the top and 12 px elsewhere; the box is centred.
- The box is 5:3: width `max(120, min(0.96 * fw, 0.9 * fh * 5/3, 680))`, height `0.6 * width`.
- Coordinates: the mud canvas has fixed logical size 480 x 288 and is stretched to the box by CSS; pointer positions are converted with `toLogical()` (client coordinates relative to the box, scaled to 480 x 288). The vehicle and animal drawings use a 200 x 120 viewBox and are drawn onto the canvas with scale `480 / 200`, so the clean SVG layer and the mud silhouette share one coordinate space. Bubbles and the keyboard brush use percentages of the box.
- Resize or rotation only changes the box size and the brush width; the canvas contents are kept, so cleaned areas stay in place.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | N/A (inline SVG); `Rand` is required and not guarded |
| Resize / rotation | `layout()`; canvas unaffected (logical coordinates) |
| Backgrounding | Loop paused while hidden; timers advance only while visible |
| Multi-touch | One stroke per pointer id (`pointers`) |
| Pointer cancel / lost capture | Stroke ended (`up`) |
| Fast drags | Continuous round-cap stroke from the previous point, so no gaps |
| Input while swapping | `down` and `move` ignored; `pointers` is cleared when the swap begins; keyboard moves the brush but does not erase |
| Canvas read-back unavailable | Not handled (`getImageData` is assumed to work; requires verification) |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` cancels the frame |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#82](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/82) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM/stub-canvas run (multi-point drag, keyboard zig-zag, done phase, swap and return to play) and states that real canvas pixels were not verified; PR [#150](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/150) reports a node harness checking the V V A pattern over 60 items, 18 distinct labels/colours over 300 picks and that all generated SVGs parse as XML; PR [#165](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/165) reports 60,000 simulated picks with no consecutive dogs and all animals appearing. These scripts are not in the repository. Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: drag a finger over the first item; mud disappears where touched, bubbles rise, and the clean drawing shows.
- [ ] Fast drags leave no gaps; two fingers scrub at once.
- [ ] Completion: scrub until about 90% clean; the rest of the mud fades, the item glows for about 3 s, and after about 7 s a new muddy item fades in.
- [ ] Sequence: items follow vehicle, vehicle, animal, vehicle, vehicle, animal; vehicle types and colours do not repeat consecutively.
- [ ] Randomization: over many animals the dog appears most often (about 30%) and never twice in a row.
- [ ] Restart: leave and reopen; the sequence starts again with a vehicle.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that nothing changes with time.
- [ ] Portrait (about 360x640): the box fills about 96% of the width; the brush is at least 44 px.
- [ ] Landscape (about 640x360): the box fits the height; rotate mid-wash and check that cleaned areas stay in place.
- [ ] Touch and mouse: scrub with both; right button has no special effect.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the box, arrow keys move the visible brush ring and scrub; Enter/Space follows the zig-zag; focus ring visible.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: the mud vanishes at once at 90%; bubbles and glow still appear.
- [ ] Background the tab during the glow and return.
- [ ] Verify the 90% threshold feels right on a phone and in Safari (canvas read-back).
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from code reading):**
- No automated tests.
- The animals are drawn separately from the shared animal family, so their style differs from activities that use `js/animals.js`.
- The no-repeat memory (`Rand` last picks and `lastAnimal`) lasts across re-opening during a page session.
- The dog's effective share (about 30%) is lower than a flat weight-3 selection would give (3/8).
- In the comment block of `frame()`, a stale remark refers to `setVehicle`, which is now `setItem` (documentation debt, no behavioural effect).

**Requires verification:**
- Behaviour of the coverage measure on real devices and browsers (PR #82).
- Visual quality of the tractor, sheep and other drawings added in PR #150.

No open GitHub issue concerns this activity (issues #124 and #163 are closed).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Related washing activity: [Kąpiel Zwierzątek](kapiel-zwierzatek.md) (animal-only scrub, rinse and dry; issue [#169](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/169)).
- Other activities with a "glow then next round" cycle: [Koraliki](koraliki.md), [Puzzle](puzzle.md), [Wieża z Klocków](wieza-z-klockow.md).
- Shared helper used: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) is **not** used.

## 21. Change history

- [#56](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/56) / [PR #82](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/82): activity introduced (3 vehicles).
- [#124](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/124) / [PR #150](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/150): 6 vehicle types, 6 colours, 6 animals and the V V A sequence.
- [#163](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/163) / [PR #165](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/165): the dog appears more often (weight 3), never twice in a row.
```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/nakarm-pieska.md`

```markdown
# Nakarm Pieska

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Nakarm Pieska |
| Activity ID | `nakarm` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A hungry dog of a random breed is fed by dragging foods from a random table of six to it; unsuitable ones are gently refused. |
| Category | Cause and effect; open-ended play; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop (touch, mouse), keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/nakarm.js`](../../js/nakarm.js), shared drawings in [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js), styles with prefix `nk-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A dog activity with a caring, drag-and-drop mechanic and no wrong answers, different from washing ([Myjnia](myjnia.md), [Psia Myjnia](psia-myjnia.md)), racing ([Wyścig Piesków](wyscig-pieskow.md)) and fetching ([Aport](aport.md)); issue [#179](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/179).
- Uses the shared dog drawings of [Rasy Piesków](rasy-pieskow.md) (`window.Dogs`, issue [#175](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/175)).
- Gives a parent the Polish breed name, shown small under the dog.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; a dog of a random breed (not the one of the previous launch) sits next to an empty bowl.
2. Initially displayed: a sky strip, a green yard with the dog and bowl, and a wooden table at the bottom with six pictures drawn at random (4 dog-friendly, 2 unsuitable; section 10), in one row of six when the screen is at least 468 px wide, otherwise two rows of three.
3. Interactions: drag an item to the dog or the bowl; keyboard alternative in section 6.
4. Response: a dog-friendly item flies to the bowl or mouth (0.3 s) and is eaten (1.5 s chew), then a heart rises and the dog wags (1 s). An unsuitable item makes the dog shake its head (0.9 s) and drifts back to the table in 0.5 s.
5. After 3 different items: the dog yawns (1 s, head tilt only; its body size never changes), lies down with a soft glow (3 s), walks off to the left (0.5 s); a new breed walks in (0.7 s) and a newly dealt table fades in (0.5 s).
6. The rounds repeat without end. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Items | Six per round: 4 dog-friendly and 2 unsuitable (pool in section 10). Each friendly item can be given once per round; it disappears when eaten. A refused item is not accepted and can be given again. |
| Drop target | The dog (button plus 12 px margin, including its name) or the empty bowl (plus 14 px margin). While a dragged item is over a target and the dog is waiting, both get a white 5 px outline and a yellow glow. |
| Drift back | An item dropped elsewhere, while the dog is busy, or an unsuitable item, glides back to its table slot in 0.5 s (smoothstep); this includes unsuitable items. |
| Dog busy | The dog only accepts items while waiting; during chewing, wagging, shaking, yawning, lying and the breed change an item dropped on it simply drifts back. |
| Round | 3 different friendly items (all three) fill the dog. The count is never shown. |
| Faces | Only `dg-calm` and `dg-happy` (happy mouth shown while chewing and yawning); no angry or sad face exists. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (an item given to the dog is eaten) and dragging and dropping with a finger.
- Matching pictures of food to a dog; noticing different dog breeds.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Friendly items are eaten, unsuitable ones are refused, with feedback in both cases and no negative expression.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus). The items are native `<button>` elements.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to an item (visible 4 px focus ring), Enter or Space gives it to the dog (it flies from the bowl; an unsuitable item drifts back after a head shake).
- **Labels (Polish):** each item, named in Polish ("Kość. Przeciągnij do pieska lub naciśnij Enter, aby go poczęstować.", ...) and the dog ("Piesek: Labrador."); the SVG is decorative.
- **Target sizes:** items are `clamp(72, min(W/(columns+0.4), 30% of H / rows), 100)` px square (6 columns at W >= 468 px, else 3 columns x 2 rows); the bowl is at least 64 x 56 px; the drop zone is larger than the drawing.
- **Layout:** the yard starts 56 px from the top (below the Back button); the table height is the rows of items plus 40 px; portrait and landscape from 320 x 568 to 1920 x 1080 (at 568 x 320 items are about 89 px in one row).
- **Non-colour cues:** the outline around the dog and bowl; items differ by shape, not only colour.
- **Reduced motion:** all movement is driven from JavaScript (one rAF loop), so it behaves the same; the glow, lying pose and positions are set from state, not from a CSS keyframe.
- **Text:** none except the small parent-facing breed name.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Visual quality (dog size, head tilt and shake, glow, heart) has not been checked on a device (sections 17 and 18).
- The head movements pivot around an approximate head centre derived from the ear pivot of the shared drawing; on some breeds it may look slightly off.
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/nakarm.js`](../../js/nakarm.js): `CHEW_S` (1.5), `WAG_S` (1.0), `SHAKE_S` (0.9), `YAWN_S` (1.0), `LIE_S` (3.0), `OUT_S` (0.5), `IN_S` (0.7), `BACK_S` (0.5), `FLY_S` (0.3), `FADE_S` (0.5), `ROUND_ITEMS` (3), `YARD_TOP` (56), `N_OK` (4), `N_BAD` (2) and the `KINDS` pool. Changing them needs a code edit.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The dog is inline SVG built by `Dogs.draw(id)`; items, bowl, heart, sky and the menu icon are inline SVG.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- Breed: uniformly from the 8 in `Dogs.LIST`; the first breed of a launch differs from the last one shown (module variable `lastBreed`) and each new breed differs from the previous one.
- Items: before each round (including the first) 4 dog-friendly foods are drawn from 9 (bone, dog food, water, meat, sausage, biscuit, chicken leg, fish, rice bowl) and 2 unsuitable ones from 5 (carrot, chocolate, onion, grapes, cake), shuffled over the six grid slots. The set differs from the previous round's (order ignored); nothing is stored.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A round is complete when the dog has eaten 3 different items. Feedback: happy chew, heart, tail wag; a head shake for an unsuitable item; yawn, lying with a soft glow and a new breed at the end. No failure state. The activity is open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/nakarm.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant: breedId })` on each give attempt (an item dropped on the dog or bowl, or given by keyboard) and `Analytics.complete()` when the dog is full. All calls are wrapped so that nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. The activity is not in the module's `COMPLETABLE` list (it repeats endlessly), so exit-before-completion is not defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/nakarm.js`](../../js/nakarm.js) overrides `mount` of the `nakarm` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.nk > svg.nk-sky + yard + table + glow + button.nk-dog (art + name) + bowl + heart + six button.nk-item`.
- **State:** dog phase `wait`, `eat`, `wag`, `shake`, `yawn`, `lie`, `out` or `in` with a phase timer; items with mode `home`, `drag`, `back`, `fly` or `gone`.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, guarded by `!raf`, cancelled while the tab is hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`; it stops when the dog waits and nothing else moves, and restarts on the next interaction; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.nk` is fixed full-screen; all positions are pixels inside it, recomputed in `layout()` on `resize` and `orientationchange` (items at rest return to their slots; the dog group is centred).
- Dog width is `min(52% of the width, (yard height - 42) x 1.2, 220 px)`; the dog and the bowl sit on the same baseline at the bottom of the yard.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Drop in the middle of nowhere | The item drifts back to the table in 0.5 s. |
| Drag cancelled by the system | The item drifts back. |
| Item given while the dog is busy | It drifts back and is still available. |
| Leaving mid-round | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| Resize / orientation | Layout recomputed; resting items return to their slots. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |
| `window.Dogs` missing | Not handled. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag the bone, food and water to the dog and to the bowl; each is eaten (1.5 s), a heart and wag follow.
- [ ] Drag an unsuitable item (e.g. the carrot) to the dog; it shakes its head and the carrot returns in 0.5 s.
- [ ] Drop an item in empty space; it returns smoothly.
- [ ] After the third item: yawn, lying with a glow (3 s), a new breed (never the same) and a different random table (4 + 2).
- [ ] The outline shows while dragging over the dog or bowl.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to each item, Enter/Space.
- [ ] Rotate the device mid-round.
- [ ] Leave and reopen ten times quickly.
- [ ] Small screens (320 x 568, 568 x 320) and 1920 x 1080.
- [ ] Reduced motion: eating, glow and the breed change still work.

The PRs for issues [#179](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/179) and [#207](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/207) report a Node simulation with a stub DOM; no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel of the head tilt and shake, glow and heart, and the layout on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Aport](aport.md), [Psia Myjnia](psia-myjnia.md), [Wyścig Piesków](wyscig-pieskow.md), [Myjnia](myjnia.md), [Rasy Piesków](rasy-pieskow.md).
- Shared component: [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js) (`Dogs.LIST`, `Dogs.draw`).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#179](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/179): initial activity.
- Issue [#207](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/207): pool of 14 foods, 6 random items per round.

```
