## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/naklejki.md`

```markdown
# Naklejki

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#221](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/221)
- Activity id: `naklejki`
- CSS prefix: `st-`

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Naklejki |
| Activity ID | `naklejki` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Twelve stickers are dragged from a tray and placed freely on a meadow, sea or sky scene; each placed sticker moves gently. |
| Category | Free creative play; dragging; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop (touch, mouse) with a keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/naklejki.js`](../../js/naklejki.js), styles with prefix `st-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- The first activity with free placing and no target: every other dragging activity has a goal. Issue [#221](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/221).
- The picture is always nice: nothing can be wrong, scored, saved or erased by accident.

## 3. Activity flow

1. A scene (meadow, sea or sky, chosen at random) fills most of the screen; below it (portrait) or to its right (landscape) is a tray of twelve stickers, each 64 px (96 px once placed in the scene).
2. The child drags a sticker onto the scene and lets go. It appears with a short pop and then keeps a gentle loop (sway, float, twinkle, ...).
3. The same sticker can be placed again and again, up to 20 stickers on the scene. When 20 are placed the tray fades and gets a dashed outline, and further drops simply return to the tray.
4. Dragging a placed sticker moves it; letting go on the tray removes it; tapping it makes it wiggle once.
5. The round button at the top right (56 px) starts a new scene: stickers fade out and the background cross-fades to the next one over 0.8 s.
6. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Stickers | sun, flower, fish, cloud, bird, house, tree, boat, star, butterfly, heart, balloon (same tray for every scene). |
| Limit | 20 stickers on the scene; a drop above the limit returns to the tray. |
| Drop outside the scene | The sticker flies back to the tray (new) or to its old place (placed) in 0.26 s. |
| Tap | A tap (under 6 px of movement) on a placed sticker wiggles it once; a tap on a tray sticker does nothing. |
| Scene order | The three backgrounds are shuffled; each is shown once before any repeats, and the first scene of a new launch differs from the last one shown in the same page session. |
| New scene | Stickers fade for 0.8 s while the next background cross-fades in, then the stickers are removed. The button is ignored while this runs. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is stored. |
| Text | None on screen; Polish screen-reader labels only. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits:** creative composition, cause and effect (place, it comes alive), fine motor control of drag and drop, early naming of everyday pictures.

**Directly observable behavior:** every placed sticker moves in its own gentle way; the child can build any picture.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on creativity or vocabulary.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- Input: touch, mouse, keyboard. Tray stickers and placed stickers are buttons (Tab). On a tray sticker Enter/Space places it in the centre of the scene and moves the focus to it; on a placed sticker arrows move it (5% of the free range per press), Enter/Space wiggles it and Delete/Backspace removes it.
- Targets: tray stickers are 64 px and placed stickers 96 px, the new-scene button 56 px; the scene starts 72 px below the top so the fixed Back button is never covered.
- Colour is not the only cue: every sticker has its own shape; the "full" state is shown by a faded tray with a dashed outline.
- Reduced motion: the loops and the pop are CSS animations that the global rule disables; every state (placed, removed, new scene) is still reached through timers and base styles. Every loop is 1.4 s or longer (nothing flashes; the sun turns once per 14 s).
- Only the first pointer drags; a second finger is ignored.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Tested only with stub-DOM simulations in this environment (no browser), see section 17.
- Placed stickers can overlap or stack exactly (keyboard placement always uses the centre); the last placed is on top.
- Pictures are simple inline SVG and not checked on real devices.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of `js/naklejki.js`: `SIZE` (96, placed sticker), `MAX` (20), `FADE_MS` (800), `TAP_PX` (6), `STEP` (0.05), `RETURN_MS` (260) and the `KINDS` list (picture, Polish label, loop motion).

## 9. Assets

No asset files: stickers are inline SVG in `js/naklejki.js`, backgrounds are CSS gradients, the menu icon is in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

The first scene and the scene order (shuffled, each once per cycle, no repeat across the cycle boundary); the animation delay of every placed sticker so the loops are out of step. Nothing persists.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No completion; the activity stays open-ended. Feedback: a pop on placing, a wiggle on touching, a fly-back when a drop is not accepted.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Reports to `window.Analytics` (see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status)):

- `track('interaction', { variant: '<sticker id>' })` for each placement from the tray (drag-drop or keyboard); moving, wiggling, removing and new scenes are not reported.
- No `complete()`.

Calls are wrapped in try/catch; nothing is stored by the activity.

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` overrides `mount` of the `naklejki` entry; the root is attached with `container.appendChild` before anything is measured; it returns a cleanup function that removes listeners and timers.
- **Rendering:** `div.st > div.st-scene (two background layers + div.st-items)`, `div.st-tray` of twelve buttons, `button.st-new`. Placed stickers are `button.st-item` with three nested spans (pop, wiggle, loop) so the animations do not fight. SVG sizing uses `.stage .st-svg`.
- **Model:** each sticker is `{kind, fx, fy}` with `fx, fy` in 0..1 of the free range (`left = (100% - 96px) * fx`), so no resize code is needed.
- **Drag:** a pointerdown on a sticker arms a drag; after 6 px a fixed-position ghost copy follows the pointer (the placed original is hidden); on release the ghost centre decides: scene = place/move, tray = remove, elsewhere = fly back.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Pure CSS: portrait puts the tray (4 x 3 grid, 270 px wide) under the scene, landscape (aspect ratio 1:1 or wider) puts it at the right. Positions are fractions of the scene, so rotation keeps every sticker visible and in place relative to the scene.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Rotation or resize: layout is CSS only; a drag in progress is judged at release with fresh measurements.
- Tab hidden and shown: CSS animations pause by themselves; timers are short (0.8 s).
- Very fast repeated touches: the new-scene button and new drags are ignored while a scene change runs; the 20 limit is checked at every placement.
- Two fingers: the second pointer is ignored; `pointercancel` restores a hidden sticker.

## 17. Testing

Manual scenarios:

1. Drag each of the twelve tray stickers onto the scene; each pops and starts its loop.
2. Place the same sticker five times; place 20 in total, then try a 21st: it returns to the tray and the tray looks faded.
3. Drop a sticker on the tray: it returns. Drag a placed sticker to the tray: it disappears (the tray is no longer faded).
4. Tap a placed sticker: one wiggle.
5. Press the round button six times, waiting 1 s between presses: all three backgrounds appear once in each group of three; the stickers are gone.
6. Rotate the device with stickers placed: all stay in view.
7. Keyboard: Tab to a tray sticker, Enter (placed in the centre, focus moves to it), arrows move it, Delete removes it.
8. Touch with two fingers: the second is ignored.

A Node stub-DOM simulation (drops, second pointer, tray return, the 20 limit, removal, wiggle, keyboard, scene order, cleanup) was run during development; there is no automated test suite in the repository.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

No renderer was available to the author; the look of the pictures and the layout at 320 px and 568x320 need a check on a real device.

## 19. Planned improvements

None agreed; erasing, saving and scoring are out of scope.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

Other free-drag activities: [Kolorowe Kształty](kolorowe-ksztalty.md), [Ubierz Misia](ubierz-misia.md). Reuses `window.Rand` and `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Implemented from issue [#221](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/221).

```

---

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/nalej-wody.md`

```markdown
# Nalej Wody

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#218](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/218)
- Activity id: `nalej`
- CSS prefix: `nw-`

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Nalej Wody |
| Activity ID | `nalej` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A jug is dragged sideways and tilts to pour a thin stream into glasses of three different heights; bigger glasses fill more slowly. |
| Category | Volume and flow; dragging; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag and hold (touch, mouse) with a keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/nalej.js`](../../js/nalej.js), styles with prefix `nw-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- The first activity that shows volume and flow over time; [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md) only counts objects. Issue [#218](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/218).
- No text, wrong answers, scores or spilling mess.

## 3. Activity flow

1. A jug (96 px wide or more) hangs in the top row, a small pitcher stands at the right edge, and three glasses of different heights and colours stand on the table.
2. The child holds the jug and drags it sideways. The jug turns to face the direction of travel. While it is held with its spout over the opening of a glass that is not full, it tilts (up to 40 degrees) and a thin stream falls into the glass; the water rises.
3. Moving the jug away, releasing it, filling the glass or emptying the jug stops the stream at once; water never lands outside a glass.
4. Over the pitcher the jug refills by itself (no holding needed); the jug shows its water with a level line and tick marks, and the pitcher gets a dashed outline when the jug is nearly empty.
5. A full glass sparkles with four stars for 2 s.
6. When all three glasses are full they glow and a small animal toasts for 3 s (the jug fades out); the glasses then empty over 2 s and come back with new random heights and colours.
7. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Fill rate | Percent of the glass height per second: 25 (smallest glass), 15 (medium), 10 (tallest). A glass fills in 4 s, 6.7 s and 10 s. |
| Sizes | The three heights are `big` (0.90-1.00 of the maximum height), then each next one is 0.68-0.75 of the previous (so every glass is at least 25% shorter than the next taller one, ratio at least 1.33). The three colours come from a pool of 8 and are always distinct. Order on the table is random. |
| Pouring | Needs the jug held (pointer down, or Enter/Space held), the spout within 34% of the glass width of the glass centre, the glass not full, water in the jug and the tilt past 55% of its maximum. |
| Jug water | The jug drains 6% per second of pouring (about 16 s of pouring per fill) and refills 60% per second over the pitcher. |
| Pitcher | At the right edge; the jug refills whenever its centre is within the pitcher. Over the pitcher the jug never pours. |
| Facing | The spout points the way the jug last moved (changes only while the jug is level, a turn takes 0.5 s). |
| Finale | All three full: glow and a toasting animal for 3 s, 2 s of emptying, then 0.6 s fade-in of a new set; the jug is refilled. Touches are ignored in between. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is stored. |
| Text | None on screen; only a Polish screen-reader label on the jug. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits:** seeing that bigger containers take longer to fill, cause and effect (hold, tilt, flow), fine motor control of a slow horizontal drag.

**Directly observable behavior:** three glasses fill at different, fixed speeds; the water level always rises smoothly.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on understanding of volume or time.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- Input: touch, mouse, keyboard. The jug is a `<button>` (Tab). Arrow Left/Right move it (260 px per second while held); Enter or Space pours while held down.
- The jug is at least 96 px wide; the field starts 64 px below the top so the Back button is never covered, also when the jug is tilted.
- Colour is not the only cue: the glasses differ in height, the full state shows stars and a rising water level, the jug level has a line and tick marks, a nearly empty jug is signalled by a dashed pitcher outline.
- Reduced motion: all movement is driven from one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (no CSS animation), so every state is reached; the jug never turns faster than 0.8 turn per second and nothing flashes (sparkles pulse at 0.8 Hz).
- Only the first pointer drags; a second finger is ignored.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Dragging across a glass while holding pours into it for as long as the spout is over it, as the issue requires; a child may start several short pours.
- The jug cannot pour into a glass from outside the screen edge: the jug is turned so that its spout always reaches every glass.
- Tested only with stub-DOM simulations in this environment (no browser), see section 17.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of `js/nalej.js`: `RATE` (0.25, 0.15, 0.10), `DRAIN` (0.06), `REFILL` (0.6), `TILT_MAX` (40 degrees), `KEY_SPEED` (260), `SPARK_S` (2), `TOAST_S` (3), `EMPTY_S` (2), `START_GAP` (400 ms) and the `COLORS` list.

## 9. Assets

No asset files: jug, pitcher, glasses, stream and stars are inline SVG built in `js/nalej.js`; the animal head comes from `window.Animals`; the menu icon is in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Glass heights, order on the table and colours (new each set); the animal for the toast. Nothing persists.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None: always three glasses.

## 12. Completion and feedback

Completed when all three glasses are full. Feedback: sparkles per glass, then glow, a toasting animal and new glasses. No failure.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Reports to `window.Analytics` (see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status)):

- `track('interaction', { variant: 'small' | 'medium' | 'large' })` at each pour start (the stream begins), where the variant is the rank of the glass by height; at least 400 ms pass between two starts into the same glass.
- `track('interaction', { variant: '<size>-full' })` for each filled glass.
- `complete()` once per full set.

Calls are wrapped in try/catch; nothing is stored by the activity.

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` overrides `mount` of the `nalej` entry; the root is attached with `container.appendChild` before layout; returns a cleanup function that removes listeners and the rAF.
- **Rendering:** `div.nw > div.nw-field > svg.nw-svg` (glasses, pitcher, stream, rebuilt by `build()` on layout), `button.nw-jug` (SVG with a water group counter-rotated so the water stays level), `div.nw-toast`. SVG sizing uses `.stage .nw-jsvg` / `.stage .nw-tsvg`.
- **Model:** jug position is a fraction `fx` of its travel range, facing `dir` with an eased turn `f`; the spout (pivot) is at `X + f * 42 s`. Glasses keep a relative height, colour, level and sparkle timer, so resize and rotation keep all state.
- **Loop:** one capped-dt (50 ms) rAF loop; it stops when nothing changes and restarts on input or when the tab becomes visible.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Field = viewport minus 64 px at the top and 12 px elsewhere (plus safe areas). Scale `s` = min(width / 320, height / 300) limited to 1-1.35. Maximum glass height = min(42% of the field height, 50% of its width, height minus 156 px - 78 s), at least 60 px; glasses sit in three equal slots on the ground line; the spout row is as high as the maximum glass allows (70 px minimum from the field top). Works from 320 px wide down to 568 x 320 in both orientations; rotation re-runs `layout()` without losing state.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/rotation: layout is recomputed, levels, jug position and sparkles are kept.
- Tab hidden: held pointer and keys are released and the loop stops; it restarts when visible.
- Fast repeated touches: only one pointer is tracked; pour starts are throttled per glass.
- Second finger: ignored; `pointercancel` and lost capture release the jug.
- Finale: input is ignored and held state is cleared when the toast starts.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests in the repository. Done in this environment: `node --check`, and a node stub-DOM simulation (fake rAF, pointer events on the jug) at 296x244, 296x492 and 544x320 that measured fill times (4.0 s, 6.9 s, 10.1 s), refilling at the pitcher, the three pour/full events, `complete()` and the new set after the finale. Manual scenarios to run in a browser:

1. Drag the jug over each glass and hold: the jug tilts, a stream falls, the water rises at the rates in section 4; release: the stream stops.
2. Hold over a full glass: no tilt and no stream.
3. Pour until the jug is empty: the stream stops; the pitcher gets a dashed outline; drag over the pitcher: the level line rises.
4. Fill all three: glow, toasting animal 3 s, glasses empty over 2 s, new heights (at least 25% apart) and colours.
5. Keyboard: Tab to the jug, arrows move it, hold Enter/Space to pour.
6. Rotate the device mid-pour and mid-finale; hide and show the tab; touch with two fingers.
7. Reduced motion on: every state is still reached.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

- Visual check in a real browser is still needed (no renderer here).
- The jug can pour into a glass it merely passes over while held.

## 19. Planned improvements

None agreed.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

[Rozmiar](rozmiar.md) (size ordering), [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md). Uses `window.Rand`, `window.Animals` and `window.Analytics`; nothing shared was added.

## 21. Change history

- Initial implementation ([#218](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/218)).

```

---

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/nocne-niebo.md`

```markdown
# Nocne Niebo

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Nocne Niebo |
| Activity ID | `niebo` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | Glowing stars in a night sky. Touching every star connects them into a simple shape (a "constellation"); when all stars are lit the shape glows and a "Dalej" button leads to the next shape. |
| Category | Observation, drawing-like connecting, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap (click) on star buttons, then tap "Dalej" |
| Status | Implemented. Enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff` flag). |
| Source | [`js/niebo.js`](../../js/niebo.js), CSS classes `.night`, `.n-*` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A gentle "connect the dots" activity without numbers, errors or scores: each touched star lights up and the lines appear by themselves. It gives the child a small, achievable goal (light all stars) with a clear and calm payoff (the shape glows, a short praise message appears), and teaches by example that a set of points forms a recognisable picture (a car, a bear, a house...). It differs from [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md) and [Ścieżka](sciezka.md) in that nothing has to be traced; each star is a single tap. Since issue #110 there are 10 shapes shown in random order.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile (hash `#niebo`); the 10 shapes are shuffled and the first one is built.
2. The sky shows faint dim star dots and a faint dashed ghost outline of the shape.
3. The child taps stars in any order.
4. A tapped star lights up; each edge whose two ends are both lit draws itself (0.9 s).
5. When the last star is lit, the interior of the shape glows softly (1.6 s), the lines glow, the message "Brawo, Artur!" fades in and the "Dalej" button becomes active.
6. Tapping "Dalej" fades the sky out (0.8 s), builds the next shape and fades it in. After the 10th shape the order is reshuffled and play continues without end.
7. There is no separate restart; "Dalej" is the only way to move on.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Number of shapes | 10: samochód (car), miś (bear), domek (house), kot (cat), ryba (fish), drzewo (tree), serce (heart), łódka (boat), gwiazda (star), latawiec (kite) |
| Stars per shape | car 10, bear 8, house 7, cat 8, fish 9, tree 11, heart 8, boat 7, star 10, kite 6 |
| Edges | A closed outline through the first `ring` stars (7-11), plus optional `extra` edges (bear 2, boat 3, kite 2) |
| Valid input | Tap any unlit star, in any order. Re-tapping a lit star does nothing |
| Line drawing | An edge draws (stroke-dashoffset transition, 0.9 s) as soon as both of its stars are lit |
| Success | All stars of the shape lit (`active.every(Boolean)`) |
| Success feedback | `.done` class: polygon fill `rgba(255,233,168,.18)` fading in over 1.6 s, glow on lines; "Brawo, Artur!" message; "Dalej" enabled |
| Next shape | "Dalej" disables itself, fades the sky for `FADE_MS` = 800 ms, builds the next shape, fades in, and input is accepted again 800 ms later (`busy` flag) |
| Order | Every shape once in random order; when used up it is reshuffled and the first of the new round is never the last of the previous round |
| Failure / retry | None; there are no wrong taps |

Reduced motion: state changes are defined in base CSS rules (`.n-line.on` has `stroke-dashoffset: 0`, `.done .n-fill` has the fill colour), so under the global rule the lines and fill simply appear instantly; the star pulse (3.6 s, scale 1.18) and the fade transitions are removed. The 800 ms delays are JavaScript timers and still run.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Visual perception and recognition of simple shapes.
- Attention and hand-eye coordination (finding and tapping every star).
- Calm, goal-oriented play with immediate positive feedback.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The ghost outline shows where lines will go; lit stars are brighter and pulse slowly.
- The result is a recognisable shape that fills with a soft glow.
- The child does not need to read; the praise text is short and not required to proceed.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on visual-spatial skills or shape recognition. None is measured or claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via `click`; **keyboard** (Tab to each star, Enter/Space) because stars are real `<button>` elements; "Dalej" is also a button. Focus outlines are defined for stars and "Dalej".
- **Screen readers:** every star has the same label "Gwiazdka" and no lit/unlit state (`aria-pressed` is not used); the message region has `aria-live="polite"`. The shape cannot be identified without sight.
- **Targets:** star buttons are 56 x 56 px (`min-width` and `min-height` 48 px); the visible dot is 22 px. Spacing between stars is small in some shapes: the closest pair is 10 units apart in Domek (12 in Samochód, 14 in Drzewo, 16 in Ryba, 20 or more in the others). On a 300 px sky (320 px wide phone) 10 units are 30 px, so neighbouring 56 px buttons overlap there (computed from the data, see section 18).
- **Sky size:** a square `min(94vw, 100dvh - 76px)`, centred; portrait and landscape both work, with a smaller sky in short landscape.
- **Colour:** lit and unlit stars differ by brightness and glow, not hue alone; the ghost outline is a dashed non-colour cue.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** only the praise text, not required. Independent use by a young child is feasible.
- **Motion:** slow pulse and fades only; no flashing.
- **Limitations:** no accessible name distinguishing stars; praise text includes the name "Artur" (it is the product's named user, see README) and is not configurable.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- A child can tap stars at random and complete the shape without understanding the shape (by design: no failure).
- When all stars are lit, "Dalej" is the only progression; a child who does not press it sees a static scene.
- Shapes are small polygons; some (kite, boat) have fewer stars and are easier than others (tree has 11).
- In Domek, Samochód, Drzewo and Ryba some stars are closer together than the 56 px button size on small screens (about 30, 36, 42 and 48 px on a 300 px sky), so a tap can hit the neighbouring star instead of the intended one; the result is harmless (no wrong answers) but can be confusing.
- No personal data is involved.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. The shape data is the `SHAPES` array in [`js/niebo.js`](../../js/niebo.js): each entry has `name`, `ring` (number of stars in the closed outline), `extra` (additional edges as index pairs) and `pts` (star coordinates, 0-100 on both axes). New shapes can be added by appending to `SHAPES` without changing logic. Timing constant `FADE_MS` = 800 is in the same file; the line draw time (0.9 s), fill time (1.6 s) and pulse (3.6 s) are in CSS. There is no validation of the data; invalid indices would break the build step.

## 9. Assets

No external assets. The sky background is a CSS radial gradient, the shape is inline SVG (lines and polygon built at runtime) and stars are `<button>` elements with a CSS pseudo-element dot. Menu icon: inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **What:** the order of the 10 shapes.
- **When:** at mount, and again whenever the 10 are used up.
- **How:** `Rand.shuffle(SHAPES)` (Fisher-Yates, from [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)); every shape appears once per round; if the first shape of a new round equals the last shown, it is rotated to the end.
- **Persistence:** none; every launch starts with a new random order, so a launch may begin with the same shape as the previous launch.
- **Pool:** fixed 10; an empty pool cannot happen.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No difficulty progression: shapes are served in random order regardless of their star count (6-11). Nothing is stored between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

Completion state exists per shape: all stars lit. Feedback is visual only (glowing lines and interior, message "Brawo, Artur!"). After completion nothing happens automatically; the child presses "Dalej" for the next shape. There is no overall end, no score and no sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/niebo.js`](../../js/niebo.js).
- **Rendering:** a `div.night` containing `div.n-sky` (square) with an SVG (`viewBox 0 0 100 100`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`) for ghost lines, glowing lines and the fill polygon, plus `button.n-star` elements positioned in percent. The SVG paths are rebuilt per shape in `build()`.
- **State:** `order`, `index`, `active[]`, `busy`, `timers`.
- **Events:** one delegated `click` listener on the sky (closest `.n-star`), `click` on "Dalej", `visibilitychange` (toggles `.paused`, pausing the CSS pulse).
- **Animation:** CSS transitions on `stroke-dashoffset`, fill and opacity; line length is passed as `--len`.
- **Cleanup:** clears timers, removes listeners and the scene node.
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.shuffle`).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Star and line coordinates share one square space of 0-100 units: stars are placed at `left/top` in percent of `.n-sky`, lines in the SVG viewBox 0-100. The sky is a square with side `min(94vw, 100dvh - 76px)` (with a `100vh` fallback), centred with 64 px top padding for the Back button. The "Dalej" button is placed at the bottom-right corner with safe-area insets; the praise text is at the top of the screen. Because the sky is a square, shapes are never distorted by the aspect ratio of the device.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing `Rand` | `reshuffle()` throws; the activity would not start |
| Resize / rotation | Percent layout; the sky is resized by CSS |
| Tapping during the fade | Ignored (`busy`) |
| Tapping "Dalej" twice | Second tap ignored (`busy`, disabled) |
| Tapping a lit star | No effect |
| Backgrounding | Pulse paused; JS timers continue |
| Leaving during a fade | Timers are cleared |
| Touch cancellation | `click` is used, so a cancelled touch simply does not activate a star |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#136](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/136) states that node spacing on short landscape screens was not browser-tested.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; the first shape's ghost outline and stars appear; tapping a star lights it and draws edges to lit neighbours.
- [ ] Completion: light all stars of a shape in a random order; the interior glows, "Brawo, Artur!" and an active "Dalej" appear.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the same star repeatedly, tap between stars; nothing breaks.
- [ ] Restart / next: press "Dalej"; the next shape appears after a fade; a double tap on "Dalej" does not skip a shape.
- [ ] Randomization: play 11 shapes; all 10 appear once per round and the first of round two differs from the tenth.
- [ ] Every one of the 10 shapes (car, bear, house, cat, fish, tree, heart, boat, star, kite) completes with all edges drawn and looks recognisable; the bear's two extra edges, the boat's three and the kite's two are drawn.
- [ ] Progression: none expected; confirm.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape (including 320x568 and a short landscape such as 640x360): check that every star of Domek, Samochód, Drzewo and Ryba can be lit deliberately, and note which neighbour is hit when buttons overlap.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space on stars and "Dalej").
- [ ] Background/foreground during a fade; return and continue.
- [ ] Reduced motion: lines and glow appear instantly; "Dalej" still works.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- Closest star pairs (computed from `SHAPES`): Domek 10 units, Samochód 12, Drzewo 14, Ryba 16; with a 56 px button this overlaps below a sky of about 560 px (Domek) to 350 px (Ryba) wide, i.e. on all phones.
- The README describes touching stars "in turn", but the code accepts any order.
- All stars share the label "Gwiazdka"; lit state is not exposed to assistive technology.
- `window.Rand` is required, no fallback.
- The praise text contains a fixed name and is not configurable.

**Requires verification**

- Which star receives the tap where 56 px buttons overlap (later DOM order is likely on top); PR #136 notes that spacing on short landscape screens was not browser-tested.
- Whether all 10 shapes are recognisable to a young child.

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md), [Ścieżka](sciezka.md), [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md) (night sky).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.shuffle`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#5](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/5) / PR [#12](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/12): initial activity; a later fix drew lines with real path lengths because the first approach did not connect stars.
- Issue [#110](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/110) / PR [#136](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/136): 10 shapes in random order.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/od-jajka-do.md`

```markdown
# Od Jajka do…

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#214](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/214)
- Activity id: `odjajka`
- CSS prefix: `oj-`

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Od Jajka do… |
| Activity ID | `odjajka` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A touch-driven life-cycle story: one big picture changes stage by stage (egg to chick to hen, egg to caterpillar to cocoon to butterfly, seed to sprout to flower to apple tree). |
| Category | Observation; cause and effect; calming |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse), keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/odjajka.js`](../../js/odjajka.js), styles with prefix `oj-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A story-over-time activity: the child's touch moves a small living thing through change, unlike [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md) which only changes the sky; issue [#214](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/214).
- Nothing can go wrong: no wrong steps, no negative states, no text.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; one of the three cycles is shown at its first stage (egg, egg on a leaf or seed).
2. Initially displayed: a pastel picture that only sways slowly, and a row of four dots under it (right of it in landscape); the first dot is marked as current.
3. Touching the picture moves to the next stage with a 1.5 s cross-fade and grow-in and a small happy wiggle. Touching a dot of an already reached stage jumps to that stage; dots of stages not reached yet are inactive.
4. At the fourth (last) stage the picture glows for 3 s and a little bunny waves; the picture no longer advances.
5. After 7 s (3 s glow + 4 s) the picture fades out (0.6 s) and the next cycle fades in at its first stage.
6. Cycles come in a shuffled order, each once before any repeats; the first cycle of a launch differs from the first one of the previous launch. There is no end; exit with the Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Cycles | `chick`, `butterfly`, `flower`; 4 stages each, drawn as inline SVG groups in one pastel style. |
| Advance | A click on `.oj-pic` at stage 1-3 moves one stage on. At stage 4 it does nothing. Nothing advances by itself within a cycle. |
| Morph | Each stage group fades in/out over 1.5 s (opacity) and grows from 92% to 100%. Rapid touches simply continue the fades. |
| Wiggle | 0.7 s rotate/scale of the picture button, restarted on each advance or jump. |
| Sway | The picture rotates between -1.5 and +1.5 degrees (with a 1.5% scale) every 3 s, alternating, all the time. |
| Dots | Four 56 px buttons with a 28 px visible dot. Current = larger with a ring; reached = solid; not reached = dashed outline and disabled. |
| Finale | On entering stage 4 (by touch or by dot): glow 3 s, bunny waving until the next cycle, fade-out starts at 6.4 s, next cycle at 7 s. Jumping back to an earlier stage cancels the finale. |
| Order | `window.Rand.shuffle` of the 3 cycles; a new shuffle after the third, never starting with the cycle just shown; a fallback to an unshuffled list when `Rand` is missing. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits:** calm observation of change over time, cause and effect (touch moves the story), a first sense of sequence (stage dots).

**Directly observable behavior:** every touch moves exactly one stage; the dots show how far the story has come; the order of cycles is shuffled.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on understanding of life cycles or of sequence.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- Input: touch, mouse, keyboard. The picture and the dots are real `<button>` elements: Tab to the picture and Enter/Space advances; Tab to a reached dot and Enter/Space jumps. Focus is shown with a 4 px outline.
- The picture button fills the area between the Back button and the dots (at least 70% of a 320x568 or 568x320 screen; the drawing itself is a square of at least 50%); dot targets are 56 px.
- Layout: portrait = picture above, dots in a row below; landscape = picture in the middle, dots in a column on the right; the top-left 56 px Back button is never covered (picture starts 64 px from the top in portrait and 72 px from the left in landscape).
- Colour is not the only cue: the current dot is larger with a ring, reached dots are solid, others dashed; the stage itself is carried by the picture.
- Reduced motion: the global rule removes all animations and transitions, so stages switch instantly; the stage, glow and bunny states are defined in base CSS classes and are all still reached; sway and wiggle simply do not play. Nothing flashes and nothing turns faster than 1.5 degrees per 3 s (the bunny's arm swings once per second).
- No reading is required; a young child can use it independently.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Very low risk: slow motion, soft colours, no failure.
- A child who keeps touching reaches the finale in three touches, so the story can be short; the finale then runs on its own.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Tunable constants at the top of `js/odjajka.js`: `FIN_GLOW` (3000 ms), `FIN_NEXT` (7000 ms), `FADE_OUT` (600 ms), `WIGGLE` (700 ms). Stage fade (1.5 s), sway (3 s) and glow timing are in the `oj-` rules in `css/style.css`.

## 9. Assets

No asset files: everything (three cycles with four stages each, the bunny helper, the glow) is inline SVG built in `js/odjajka.js` on a 300x300 viewBox, plus the menu icon in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

The order of the three cycles (see section 4); no other randomness. Nothing persists between launches except the remembered first cycle of the previous launch (page session only, in memory).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None: four stages per cycle, no levels.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A cycle is complete when its last stage is shown. Feedback: a soft glow and a waving bunny; then the next cycle fades in automatically. No failure and no score.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`), see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status). `js/app.js` records start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/odjajka.js` additionally calls:

- `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant: '<cycle>-<stage>' })` on each advance by touching the picture (variant e.g. `chick-2` = the stage reached, 1-4; cycles `chick`, `butterfly`, `flower`). Jumps via the dots are not reported.
- `Analytics.complete()` once per cycle when its last stage is first reached (a jump back and forward in the same cycle does not report it again).

Calls are wrapped in try/catch and skipped when `window.Analytics` is missing. Nothing is stored by the activity.

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/odjajka.js`](../../js/odjajka.js) overrides `mount` of the `odjajka` entry; the root is attached with `container.appendChild(root)` before anything else; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.oj > button.oj-pic (svg.oj-svg with background, glow, 4 × g.oj-st, bunny) + div.oj-dots > 4 × button.oj-dot`. The SVG is rebuilt per cycle by `build()`.
- **State:** `cur`, `reached`, `done` (completion already reported), the shuffled `order` and index, and a list of pending timers.
- **Animation:** CSS transitions and keyframes only; classes `oj-fin`, `oj-glow-on`, `oj-help`, `oj-out` on the root drive the finale. Timers use `setTimeout`.
- **Cleanup:** clears every timer and removes the root; no document-level listeners exist.
- **Persistence:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Pure CSS: the picture button and the dots are placed with `position: absolute` and an `@media (orientation: landscape)` rule; the SVG scales into the button with `preserveAspectRatio` meet (viewBox 300x300, CSS `.stage .oj-svg` so the global 120 px SVG rule does not apply). Because state lives in the closure and no pixel values are computed, rotation or resize never loses it.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Rotation / resize | CSS only; the stage and pending finale continue. |
| Tab hidden and shown | Timers keep running; the finale simply continues or has completed. |
| Very fast repeated touches | Each touch advances one stage at most up to stage 4; later touches do nothing. |
| Two fingers | Each tap is a normal click; extra taps at stage 4 are ignored. |
| Dot of a stage not reached | Disabled. |
| Jump away during the finale | Timers are cancelled, glow and bunny removed. |
| `window.Rand` or `window.Analytics` missing | Unshuffled order / calls skipped. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Launch several times: the first cycle varies; three cycles in a row show each once.
- [ ] Touch the picture: it changes in 1.5 s with a small wiggle; four touches are never needed (3 touches reach the last stage).
- [ ] Do nothing: nothing advances; the picture sways slowly.
- [ ] Touch dots: reached dots jump, unreached dots do nothing; the current dot is clearly larger.
- [ ] At the last stage: 3 s glow, bunny waves, after 7 s the next cycle fades in.
- [ ] Jump back during the finale: the glow stops and the cycle stays.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab, Enter/Space on the picture and on the dots.
- [ ] Rotate in the middle of a morph and during the finale; the Back button is never covered at 320x568 and 568x320.
- [ ] Enable reduced motion: stages switch without animation, the finale glow and bunny still appear.
- [ ] Hide the tab at the last stage and return.
- [ ] Check in Statystyki that advances and completions are counted.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Requires verification:** appearance of the drawings and the 1.5 s cross-fade on real devices (no renderer was available while building).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

[Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md) (change over time without a story), [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md) (growth by touch). Uses the shared `window.Rand` ([`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)) and `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- [#214](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/214) initial implementation.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/ogrod-motyli.md`

```markdown
# Ogród Motyli

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Ogród Motyli |
| Activity ID | `motyle` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A garden of five swaying flowers. Touching a flower makes the butterfly fly slowly to it along a smooth curve; if left alone it flies to another flower by itself. |
| Category | Open-ended play, observation, cause and effect |
| Interaction type | Tap a flower (five large buttons) |
| Status | Implemented. Enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff` flag). |
| Source | [`js/motyle.js`](../../js/motyle.js), CSS classes `.m-*` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A very simple, forgiving activity for the youngest child: five big targets, every tap does something visible and gentle, and nothing can be wrong. The butterfly's flight is deliberately slow and smooth, even when the child taps another flower in mid-flight, so the scene stays calm. Since issue #112 the flower colours and the butterfly's colouring vary per launch.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile (hash `#motyle`); the scene is built with five flowers and a butterfly resting on the first flower (top left).
2. A pale cream-to-green background shows the five flowers with different petal counts.
3. The child can tap any flower.
4. The tapped flower sways for 2.2 s and the butterfly flies to it along a curved path; the curve bends one way and the other on alternating flights.
5. There is no completion state.
6. After arriving the butterfly rests; if no flower is tapped for 10-15 s it flies to a different flower by itself.
7. A new colour combination appears on the next launch.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Flowers | 5 at fixed positions (fractions of the play square): (0.22, 0.24) 6 petals, (0.74, 0.22) 8, (0.48, 0.50) 5, (0.22, 0.70) 7, (0.76, 0.68) 6 |
| Tap on the flower the butterfly is on or heading to | The flower sways but no flight starts; the idle timer restarts |
| Tap on another flower | Butterfly redirects immediately, keeping its position and velocity; the pull direction is rotated by `TURN` = 0.55 rad, with the sign alternating on each flight (`dir = -dir`) |
| Flight model | Damped spring toward the target: `OMEGA` = 2.2 (critically damped, so no overshoot in the straight case); integration step capped at 0.05 s |
| Arrival | Distance below 0.006 and speed below 0.03 (in play-square fractions); position snapped to the flower |
| Idle flight | After 10-15 s at rest (`IDLE_MIN` 10, `IDLE_MAX` 15) it flies to a random other flower; hidden time is not counted |
| Sway | 2200 ms (`SWAY_MS`), rotation `7 deg` (`SWAY_AMP`) damped sine with two oscillations, around a point 150 % below the flower |
| Wings | Wing scale `0.6 + 0.4 * cos(phase)`; phase speed 4.5 pi rad/s in flight (2.25 flaps/s), 1.8 pi rad/s at rest (0.9 flaps/s) |
| Tilt | Butterfly rotated by velocity, clamped to +/-15 deg |
| Failure / scoring | None |

All motion is JavaScript-driven in one `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so it is **not** affected by the global reduced-motion CSS rule (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)); there is no slower variant for users who prefer reduced motion.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (touch a flower, the butterfly comes).
- Calm visual tracking of a smoothly moving object.
- Recognising that flowers differ in shape (petal count 5, 6, 7, 8) as well as colour.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The butterfly always moves smoothly, even when redirected.
- Flowers have different petal counts, so they stay distinguishable even if colours look alike.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on attention, tracking or development. None is measured or claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer (`pointerdown`) and **keyboard**: the flowers are real `<button>` elements (`aria-label` "Kwiatek 1" to "Kwiatek 5"); Enter/Space fires `click` with `detail === 0`, which is handled. A focus outline is defined.
- **Screen readers:** flower buttons are labelled by number only; the butterfly is `aria-hidden`.
- **Targets:** each flower is 22 % of the play square wide and at least 72 px. The butterfly is not a target (`pointer-events: none`).
- **Layout:** the play square is `min(94vw, 100dvh - 110px)` with a 60 px top margin, centred; portrait and landscape both work, with smaller flowers (but not under 72 px) on short screens.
- **Colour:** colours are decorative; petal count provides a non-colour cue. Pastel petals on a pale background have modest contrast; PR [#138](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/138) asked a reviewer to check it.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required. Independent use by a young child is possible.
- **Motion:** slow; no flashing. Not reduced under the OS setting (see section 4).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Some colour sets put similar pastel colours on neighbouring flowers; the petal counts help but are subtle (5-8).
- No ending; the butterfly continues to fly by itself every 10-15 s, which can run for as long as the playtime limit allows.
- Reduced-motion users still see the full flight and wing animation.
- On short landscape screens the play square shrinks, so flowers may sit close together (requires verification in a browser).
- No personal data is involved.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/motyle.js`](../../js/motyle.js).

| Name | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `OMEGA` | Spring stiffness of the flight | 2.2 |
| `TURN` | Rotation of the pull vector (curve) | 0.55 rad |
| `SWAY_MS`, `SWAY_AMP` | Flower sway length and amplitude | 2200 ms, 7 deg |
| `IDLE_MIN`, `IDLE_MAX` | Rest before an automatic flight | 10 s, 15 s |
| `FLOWERS` | Position and petal count per flower | 5 entries |
| `FLOWER_SETS` | Petal and core colour pairs per flower | 6 sets |
| `BUTTERFLY_SETS` | Upper and lower wing colours | 6 sets |

There is no validation; the five-entry layout is assumed by all colour sets.

## 9. Assets

No external assets. Flowers and the butterfly are inline SVG built at runtime (`flowerSvg`, `butterflySvg`); the background is a CSS gradient. The menu icon is inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | When | Pool | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flower colour set | Each mount | 6 sets of 5 petal/core pairs | `Rand.pickOne(FLOWER_SETS, 'motyle-flowers')`: never the same set as the previous launch in the same page session |
| Butterfly colouring | Each mount | 6 wing colour pairs | `Rand.pickOne(BUTTERFLY_SETS, 'motyle-butterfly')`, chosen independently of the flowers, no immediate repeat |
| Automatic flight target | Every 10-15 s of rest | The other 4 flowers | Uniform; the idle delay is also random |
| Flight curve side | Each flight | 2 | Alternates, not random |

The first flower the butterfly sits on is always flower 1. Choices are in memory only, so after a page reload the same set can come again. The helper is called as the global `Rand` (no `window.` and no fallback), so [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) must be loaded first, which `index.html` ensures.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. Nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is the sway of the touched flower and the butterfly flight. No sound, no celebration.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/motyle.js`](../../js/motyle.js).
- **Rendering:** DOM and SVG. `div.m-scene` contains `div.m-box` (the play square) with five `button.m-flower` (each wrapping an SVG) and one `div.m-butterfly`.
- **State:** butterfly position `px, py` and velocity `vx, vy` in play-square fractions, `rest` (target flower index), `flying`, `dir`, `idle`, per-flower `swayT`.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`) updates the flight, wing scale (SVG `transform` attribute folding toward the body axis), tilt, sway and idle timer; it stops while the tab is hidden and restarts on return (`last` reset, so the butterfly does not jump).
- **Events:** `pointerdown` and `click` (keyboard only, `detail === 0`) per flower; `visibilitychange`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes listeners and the scene.
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Flowers and the butterfly share one coordinate space: fractions (0-1) of the square `.m-box`, which is `min(94vw, 100dvh - 110px)` wide, square (`aspect-ratio: 1`), centred with a 60 px top margin. Flowers are placed with percent `left`/`top` (centred with `translate(-50%, -50%)`), and the butterfly with percent `left`/`top` of the same box, so both stay aligned in any size or orientation. A flower is 22 % of the square (minimum 72 px); the butterfly is 13 % (minimum 48 px) and the sway is applied to the SVG inside the button, so the hit area does not move.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable |
| Missing `Rand` | `ReferenceError` at mount; no fallback (unlike [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md)) |
| Resize / rotation | Everything is fractional, so layout follows |
| Backgrounding | Loop stops; idle time is not counted; on return no jump |
| Rapid or repeated taps | Redirects smoothly with kept velocity; repeated taps on the same flower only sway it |
| Touch cancellation | `pointerdown` only, nothing left pending |
| Leaving during flight | Frame cancelled |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#138](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/138) reports `node --check js/motyle.js` only, with no browser in the sandbox, and asks to review contrast of the colour sets.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: tap each of the five flowers; the butterfly flies to each one smoothly and the flower sways.
- [ ] Redirect: tap a second flower mid-flight; no sudden jump, direction changes smoothly.
- [ ] Tap the flower the butterfly is on: it sways, nothing else happens.
- [ ] Idle: wait 10-15 s; the butterfly flies to another flower by itself.
- [ ] Completion: none; confirm no end state.
- [ ] Randomization: reopen about 7 times; the flower colour set and butterfly colouring change and no set repeats twice in a row.
- [ ] Contrast: each of the 6 flower sets and 6 butterflies is visible on the background.
- [ ] Progression: none expected.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape (including 640x360): five flowers visible, at least 72 px, no overlap with the butterfly's resting place.
- [ ] Touch, mouse, keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space).
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch away for 30 s; the butterfly resumes without a jump or an immediate idle flight.
- [ ] Reduced motion: confirm the butterfly still flies (it is JavaScript-driven).
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- Motion is not reduced for `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Colour sets may combine similar pastels on neighbouring flowers; only the petal count (5-8) is a non-colour cue.
- Flowers have only a number as accessible name.
- `Rand` is used without a fallback.

**Requires verification**

- Contrast of all colour sets on the background (PR #138).
- Flower spacing on short landscape screens.

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar calm scenes: [Magiczny Ogród](magiczny-ogrod.md), [Akwarium Artura](akwarium-artura.md), [Latawiec](latawiec.md) (smooth spring flight).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#7](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/7) / PR [#14](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/14): initial activity; later fixes made flowers keyboard-activatable and folded the butterfly's wings toward the body axis.
- Issue [#21](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/21): app review polish.
- Issue [#112](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/112) / PR [#138](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/138): random flower and butterfly colour sets.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/pamiec.md`

```markdown
# Pamięć

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Pamięć |
| Internal ID | `pamiec` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A gentle memory game of large picture cards: turn over two cards at a time and find the matching pairs. |
| Category | Memory (matching) |
| Interaction type | Tap |
| CSS prefix | `pm-` |
| Source | [`js/pamiec.js`](../../js/pamiec.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section `/* Pamięć */`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default (no `defaultOff`). Listed 29th in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

Pamięć is the classic find-the-pair card game adapted for a very young child: it starts with only three pairs, never punishes a miss and adds a pair after every completed game up to ten pairs. It is the one activity that explicitly grows in difficulty, and it complements the purely open-ended activities with a short goal-oriented game. The game state is kept in memory only, so each visit begins gently again.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#pamiec`); `deal()` creates game 1: 6 face-down cards (3 pairs).
2. All cards show the same lilac back with a dotted border and a small pattern.
3. The child taps a card; it turns over in about 0.6 s and shows a picture.
4. The child taps a second card. When both are fully open the game compares them.
5. **Match:** both cards glow and stay open. **No match:** after 1.5 s both cards turn back (0.6 s) with no shake, colour or message.
6. When every pair is found, all cards glow for about 3 s. About 7 s after the last match the cards turn back, fade softly while a new deal is made (0.8 s) and the next game starts with one more pair.
7. After 10 pairs (20 cards) the next games stay at 20 cards.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)); leaving resets the progression.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (source) |
|---|---|
| Cards in game `n` (n = 0, 1, 2, ...) | `2 * min(MAX_PAIRS, START_PAIRS + n)` = 6, 8, 10, ... 20 (`START_PAIRS = 3`, `MAX_PAIRS = 10`) |
| Flip time | `FLIP_S = 0.6` s (0.36 s under reduced motion) |
| Mismatch wait | `BACK_AFTER_S = 1.5` s counted from when both cards are fully open |
| Completion glow | `GLOW_S = 3` s (ramps over 0.5 s), card glow on matched cards |
| Next game | `NEXT_AT_S = 7` s after the last match, then cards close and `SHUFFLE_S = 0.8` s shuffle fade |
| Valid touch | only in phase `play`; the card must be face down and not mid-flip; at most 2 cards open at once |
| Invalid touch | open or matched card, a card mid-flip, a third card, any touch outside phase `play` -> ignored silently |
| Comparison | by picture key; two different cards of the same key are a pair |

A matched card stays face up (`matched = true`) with a glow (`drop-shadow` `#ffe08a`). Two cards touched almost at once are safe because the comparison only starts when both are fully open (`f === 1`).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (not measured)

- Visual memory and attention (remembering where a picture was).
- Matching identical pictures.
- Patience: a miss simply resets, with no penalty.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The number of cards grows with each completed game up to 20.
- Misses give no negative feedback; matches give a glow.
- Pictures are all different in shape and colour within a game.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Whether the 6 to 20 card progression suits the target age or improves memory. Nothing in the repository measures it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** cards are `<button>` elements, so touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space) work; `aria-pressed` and `aria-label` (`Karta (zakryta)` when face down, `Karta: <Polish name>` when face up, for example `Karta: kotek`) reflect the state. Because all face-down cards share one label, a screen-reader user cannot tell cards apart before turning them (inherent to the game).
- **Target size:** card size `C = clamp(best * 0.92, 56, 170)` px, minimum 56 px (`min-width/min-height: 56px` in CSS); the layout picks the column count that gives the largest square cards.
- **Orientation:** layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`; game state is kept.
- **Colour:** pictures differ in shape as well as colour (a pear, a boat, a house...); no colour-only distinction is needed.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Reduced motion:** the flip, glow and shuffle are driven by the rAF loop. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` cards cross-fade instead of flipping (no horizontal scale) and the flip is 0.36 s; glow and shuffle fade still run.
- **Touch behaviour:** `touch-action: manipulation`, text selection disabled, tap highlight removed.
- **Focus:** 4 px outline `#8f7fd1` on focused cards.
- **Limitations:** 20-card games have small cards on small screens (see section 15); a child must remember positions, which can be frustrating without hints (there are none).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Difficulty can rise quickly: the 8th game already has 20 cards; `Requires verification` with the target age group.
- The game has no hint, undo or reduce-difficulty option; progression resets only by leaving the activity.
- On small screens the 20-card grid has cards close to the 56 px minimum.
- The same pictures can reappear in consecutive games (independent random draws).
- While two mismatched cards are open (1.5 s) and turning back (0.6 s) further taps are ignored; a child may tap and see nothing happen.
- No personal data is collected.

## 8. Configuration

There is no external configuration; constants inside [`js/pamiec.js`](../../js/pamiec.js):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `START_PAIRS` | Pairs in the first game | number | `3` |
| `MAX_PAIRS` | Maximum pairs | number | `10` |
| `FLIP_S` | Flip time | s | `0.6` |
| `BACK_AFTER_S` | Wait before mismatched cards turn back | s | `1.5` |
| `GLOW_S` | Completion glow | s | `3` |
| `NEXT_AT_S` | Completion to next game | s | `7` |
| `SHUFFLE_S` | Shuffle fade | s | `0.8` |
| `P` / `POOL` | Picture definitions and key list | object / array | 14 pictures |
| Card size limits | `56` to `170` px, factor `0.92` | px | `layout` |

No fallback exists because nothing is read from outside. `MAX_PAIRS` must not exceed the pool size (14), otherwise `Rand.pick` would return fewer unique pictures.

## 9. Assets

No external files. All pictures are inline SVG strings in the `P` object (100 x 100 viewBox, rounded white card face): kotek (cat), rybka (fish), kwiatek (flower), ptaszek (bird), gruszka (pear), chmurka (cloud), serduszko (heart), gwiazdka (star), słoneczko (sun), księżyc (moon), jabłko (apple), balonik (balloon), łódka (boat), domek (house) = 14. The card back (`BACK`) is one shared SVG (lilac, dotted border, centre dot and four small dots). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Per game:** `Rand.pick(POOL, n)` selects `n` unique pictures (n = number of pairs); each is duplicated and the 2n cards are ordered with `Rand.shuffle`.
- **Pool size:** 14. Since the maximum is 10 pairs, a game never uses more than 10 of the 14 pictures.
- **Repetition:** pictures can repeat across games; no previous-game exclusion (`Not implemented`). Within a game each picture appears exactly twice.
- **Persistence:** none; every launch starts at 6 cards.
- **Empty/invalid pool:** not applicable (constant pool).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

- **Initial level:** 3 pairs (6 cards).
- **Trigger:** a completed game (`round++` in the shuffle phase).
- **Levels:** game `n` has `min(10, 3 + n)` pairs: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 10, 10, ...
- **Maximum:** 10 pairs (20 cards), repeated afterwards.
- **Reset:** leaving the activity discards `round`; nothing is persisted.
- **Layout by count:** grid is computed (see section 15); no fixed table of rows and columns.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Completion:** all cards matched.
- **Success feedback:** matched pairs glow and stay open; at the end every card glows for 3 s.
- **Failure feedback:** none; mismatched cards turn back after 1.5 s without shake, red colour or message.
- **After completion:** the cards close, fade and a new deal starts automatically.
- **Sound:** none.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches inside the stage; `js/pamiec.js` calls `levelStart(n)` when a deck is dealt (n = number of cards) and `levelComplete(n)` plus `complete(n)` when all pairs are found. Recorded: starts, active time, replays, quick exits, touches, completions (a completion is all pairs found), exits before completion and the highest card count reached. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/pamiec.js`](../../js/pamiec.js) replaces the `mount` of the `pamiec` registry entry and returns a cleanup function.
- **State:** `round` (game number), `deck`, `cards` (objects with flip value `f`, target `t`, `matched`, glow `g`, opacity `op`), `sel` (currently open unmatched cards), `phase` (`play`, `turnback`, `glow`, `close`, `shuffle`), `phaseT`, `backT`, `glow`, `shuf`.
- **Rendering:** each card is a `<button class="pm-card">` with two spans (back and front, each an SVG). The buttons are rebuilt for every game in `deal()`. Position and flip are applied as `transform: translate(...) scaleX(...)`; the picture is swapped at the half-way point; under reduced motion front and back cross-fade by opacity instead.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop (`frame`, `dt` capped at 50 ms) that continues only while something is changing and is cancelled when the tab is hidden, restarted by `start()` and `visibilitychange`.
- **Randomization:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`, `Rand.shuffle`).
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** `Analytics.levelStart` / `levelComplete` / `complete`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame and removes the `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange` listeners and the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.pm-field` is inset 64 px from the top (plus safe area) and 12 px elsewhere.
- `layout()` tries every column count `k` from 1 to the card count, with `rows = ceil(n / k)`, and keeps the one that maximises the square size `min(fw / k, fh / rows)`. Card size `C = clamp(best * 0.92, 56, 170)` is exposed as the CSS variable `--pm-c`.
- Gaps are spread evenly; an incomplete last row is centred. Positions (card centres) are in field pixels and applied as `translate(x - C/2, y - C/2)`.
- Cards share one pixel coordinate space; there is no scaling of an artwork board.
- PR [#149](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/149) reports computed 20-card sizes of 68 px on a 296 x 400 field in both orientations and 75 px on a 568 x 252 field. These were numerical checks in the PR, not device tests, and the PR asked for a device review.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable. |
| Rapid taps | Third and mid-flip taps ignored; simultaneous taps on two cards are safe. |
| Resize/orientation change | `layout` re-flows cards; flip and match state is kept. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; timers use the capped frame step, so a long absence does not skip the sequence. |
| Leaving mid-game | Cleanup cancels the frame; nothing is stored. |
| Insufficient unique items | Not applicable: 14 pictures against at most 10 pairs. |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | `reduced()` returns `false`. |
| Touch cancellation | Not relevant: only `click` is used. |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#149](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/149) reports `node --check` and numeric layout checks for 6 to 20 cards; PR [#84](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/84) states there was no browser in the sandbox. Neither is re-verified here.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: start a game, flip two matching cards (they stay open and glow) and two different cards (they turn back after about 1.5 s).
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap an open card, a third card while two are open, and cards during the turn-back; all are ignored.
- [ ] Completion: find every pair; confirm the 3 s glow, the closing, the shuffle fade and a new game with one more pair.
- [ ] Progression: play until the 8th game (20 cards) and confirm the count stays at 20.
- [ ] Randomization: confirm pictures and positions differ between games and launches; each picture appears exactly twice.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-open; the game starts again with 6 cards.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: check 6, 12 and 20 cards at 320 x 568, 568 x 320 and a tablet; cards at least 56 px and fully visible; rotate mid-game.
- [ ] Touch: tap with a finger; try to tap two cards at the same moment.
- [ ] Mouse and keyboard: click; Tab and Enter/Space.
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab during the mismatch wait and during the glow.
- [ ] Reduced motion: cards cross-fade instead of turning.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- Pictures can repeat across consecutive games; there is no hint or reduced-difficulty option.
- All face-down cards share one `aria-label`.

**Requires verification**

- Card legibility and touch comfort for the 20-card game on small phones.
- Whether the difficulty increase after each game suits the target age.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Another matching activity (by silhouette instead of picture): [Cienie](cienie.md).
- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`, `Rand.shuffle`). It does not use `js/animals.js`.

## 21. Change history

- [#58](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/58) / PR [#84](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/84): activity added with 6 cards and three fixed picture sets.
- [#125](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/125) / PR [#149](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/149): pool of 14 pictures and progression from 6 to 20 cards.

```
