## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/rakieta.md`

```markdown
# Rakieta

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Rakieta |
| Internal ID | `rakieta` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A small rocket with an animal astronaut drifts through a starry night sky with three smiling planets; the child can start or slow it, send it to a planet, make a star twinkle or the astronaut wave. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, observation |
| Interaction type | Tap / click |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Rakieta is the "night sky" member of the vehicle group. It differs from the road and water vehicles in having a free two-dimensional flight path (a smooth loop around the screen) and a "visit" interaction: touching a planet makes the rocket curve over to it, hover next to it while the planet glows softly, and then carry on. Every launch looks different (astronaut, planet colours and the star/planet arrangement are randomised), which gives the activity variety without any goals or scoring.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#rakieta`); `mount` picks the variant, builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The scene is a deep-blue sky with 15 stars, 3 planets with smiling faces and the rocket (with an astronaut in the round window) hovering at about 16 % of the width and 82 % of the height.
3. The child can touch the rocket, the astronaut in the window, a planet or a star.
4. Touching the rocket makes it fly along a loop (ellipse around the screen) or, if flying, slow to a hover in about 2 s. Touching a planet makes the rocket curve to a spot beside it, wait about 3 s while the planet's halo glows, and then return to what it was doing before (flying or hovering). Touching a star makes it twinkle once (2.4 s). Touching the astronaut makes a paw wave (2.4 s).
5. There is no formal completion state.
6. The loop of flying, hovering and visiting repeats for as long as the child plays.
7. A new random variant is drawn every time the activity is launched.
8. The child leaves with Back (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Cruise speed | `sc = W / CROSS_S`, `CROSS_S = 15` s to cross the width |
| Hover slow-down | `HOVER_TAU = 0.5` s time constant (about 2 s to stop); speed snaps to 0 below 1 % of cruise speed |
| Bob while hovering | `BOB_AMP = 4` px, `BOB_W = 1.9` rad/s (about one bob every 3.3 s); fades out as speed rises |
| Time beside a planet | `STAY_S = 3` s |
| Visit spring | `K = 0.8`, `C = 1.8` (about critical damping); speed cap `1.1·sc`; the approach pull vector is rotated by up to `±0.6` rad (curved approach); the visit is abandoned into the "stay" phase after 25 s at the latest |
| Flame puffs | at most `MAX_PUFFS = 8`, one every `PUFF_EVERY = 0.6` s, each lasting `PUFF_S = 2.6` s |
| Astronaut wave / star twinkle | `WAVE_S = 2.4` s, `TW_S = 2.4` s |
| Frame step cap | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |
| Stars / planets | 15 stars and 3 planets per arrangement |

Details:

- **States:** `hover`, `fly`, `visit`. `onRocket` toggles hover and fly; during a visit it ends the visit and toggles the state that was stored as `prev`.
- **Flying** (`updateFly`): speed eases toward `sc`; the heading is steered toward a point on an ellipse centred on the screen (radii `W/2 - m`, `H/2 - m`) a fixed angle (0.6 rad) ahead of the rocket, with turn rate limited to `Om = sc / Rt`, where `Rt = max(0.09·min(W, H), 36)`. The rocket is clamped inside the screen with a margin `m = pw/2 + 6`.
- **Visit** (`updateVisit`): target spot is beside the planet (on the side facing the screen centre). A new planet touch during a visit retargets (the latest planet wins). The planet halo glow eases toward 1 only in the "stay" phase.
- **Displayed angle:** the nose follows the travel direction when moving and returns upright when hovering; the rocket mirrors vertically (`scale(1, sy)`) when travelling leftwards so the astronaut stays upright.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is JS-driven; see section 6. **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touching objects in the sky leads to visible responses.
- Calm observation of slow, smooth flight.
- Choosing between several targets.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- The rocket takes about 2 s to slow down and needs about 15 s to cross the width.
- Planets glow softly when visited; stars twinkle once; the astronaut waves.
- The sky layout, planet colours and astronaut vary between launches.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on attention, curiosity or vocabulary. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** `pointerdown` (touch, mouse, stylus) and `click` with `event.detail === 0` for keyboard activation. The rocket, the astronaut, the planets and the stars are all real `<button>` elements with Polish `aria-label`s, so they can be reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space. The star and planet handlers stop propagation so they never trigger the rocket.
- **Touch handling.** `.rq` uses `touch-action: none`; no drag gesture.
- **Target sizes.** Stars: 56 x 56 px hit boxes with a 24 px visible star. Planets: `pr = clamp(0.2·min(W, H), 64, 140)` px (minimum 56 px). Rocket: `pw = clamp(min(0.3·W, 0.4·H), 150, 260)` px wide (height `pw/2`). The astronaut button is 24 % x 48 % of the rocket with a 56 px minimum.
- **Orientation.** Layout recomputed on `resize`/`orientationchange`; positions are scaled by the new size and clamped.
- **Colour.** Planets differ in colour set, but only the arrangement matters for interaction; nothing depends on colour alone. The rocket is white against a dark sky (good contrast); the focus ring is `#fff4cf` 4 px.
- **Reduced motion.** Rocket, puffs, halos, twinkles and the wave are updated by the rAF loop via inline styles and SVG attributes; the global CSS rule does not stop them. The `.rq-star svg` rule sets `transition: none`. The motion is slow, but it is not reduced for users who asked for reduced motion.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Limitations:** 15 star hit boxes of 56 px could still touch each other in some arrangements on small screens (two stars were moved to avoid overlap, see section 21); the astronaut button sits on top of the rocket button.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Accidental interactions:** a touch on the rocket body always toggles fly/hover, a touch on the window area triggers the wave instead; both are harmless.
- **Visual stimulation:** many small stars and a pulsing flame; there is no flashing, but the flame scale oscillates continuously (about 0.75 ± 0.15 plus speed-dependent growth).
- **Unclear ending:** none; the activity never ends.
- **Performance:** one always-running rAF loop; up to 8 puff elements created and removed over time (DOM churn is small).
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/rakieta.js`](../../js/rakieta.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S` | Seconds to cross the width at cruise speed | number | 15 |
| `HOVER_TAU` | Slow-down time constant (s) | number | 0.5 |
| `BOB_AMP`, `BOB_W` | Hover bob amplitude (px) and angular speed | number | 4, 1.9 |
| `STAY_S` | Time beside a planet (s) | number | 3 |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 |
| `MAX_PUFFS`, `PUFF_S`, `PUFF_EVERY` | Flame puff pool, lifetime, interval | number | 8, 2.6, 0.6 |
| `WAVE_S`, `TW_S` | Wave and twinkle durations (s) | number | 2.4, 2.4 |
| `K`, `C` | Visit spring stiffness and damping | number | 0.8, 1.8 |
| `LAYOUTS` | Star and planet positions per arrangement (fractions of the sky) | array of 4 | 4 entries (15 stars + 3 planets) |
| `PCOLS` | Planet colour sets | array of 6 | 6 entries (3 body/crater colour pairs each) |
| `ASTROS` | Astronaut variants | array of 6 | 6 entries |

No fallback handling exists because there is no external input.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The rocket, astronaut, star and planets are inline SVG strings in the JS file (`rocketSvg`, `astroSvg`, `starSvg`, `planetSvg`); the sky, halo and puffs are CSS (`.rq-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css)). The astronauts are drawn locally and do not use `js/animals.js`. No audio, fonts or data files. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Three independent picks are made on every `mount`, each with `Rand.pickOne` and its own key (so the last-pick memory is separate for each):

| What | Pool | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Star and planet arrangement | 4 layouts (`LAYOUTS`) | `rakieta-layout` |
| Planet colour set | 6 sets (`PCOLS`) | `rakieta-colours` |
| Astronaut | 6 drawings (`ASTROS`: round-eared, long-eared, pointy-eared, floppy-eared, frog-like, panda-like) | `rakieta-astro` |

- `pickOne` never returns the same item as the previous call for the same key within the page session (pools of 2 or more), so consecutive launches always differ in each of the three picks.
- Nothing is persisted; the memory is lost on reload.
- All 6 x 4 x 6 combinations are possible; no combination is excluded.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels or difficulty changes and nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

No formal completion state. Feedback is visual only: the flame grows with speed, the rocket bobs when hovering, the visited planet's halo fades in over about 1 s and out again, the touched star scales up to 1.7x and brightens, the astronaut's paw waves. No sound, no scoring, no automatic restart because nothing ends.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/rakieta.js`](../../js/rakieta.js), assigned to the `rakieta` registry entry; loaded before `js/app.js`. Uses `js/random.js` (`Rand.pickOne`) and the `.rq-*` CSS.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG. Stars, planets and rocket are absolutely positioned elements; the rocket is moved by an inline `transform` (translate, rotate, scale).
- **State:** closure variables: `st` (`hover`/`fly`/`visit`), `prev`, `x`, `y`, `hd` (heading), `spd`, `om` (turn rate), `ang`, `sy`, `face`, `vs` (visit state), `puffs`, `twT[]`, `glow[]`, `waveT`.
- **Animation:** one rAF loop `frame` with a capped dt; paused while the tab is hidden and resumed on `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `bindTap()` wires `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the rAF, removes listeners, puffs and the scene.
- **Persistence/config/analytics:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0`; `W`/`H` come from `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`.
- **Units:** CSS pixels for the rocket (`x`, `y` are its centre); stars and planets are positioned as fractions of the sky (`STARS[k][0]·W`, `STARS[k][1]·H`). Both share the same pixel space.
- **Sizing:** rocket width `pw` 150 to 260 px, planet diameter `pr` 64 to 140 px, margin `m = pw/2 + 6` keeps the rocket fully visible.
- **Resize/rotation:** `layout()` scales `x`, `y` (and the visit velocity) by the new/old size ratios and clamps them, so the rocket is never lost.
- **Arrangement design:** the layouts were hand-checked to keep stars clear of planets; the arrangement is fractional, so star spacing in pixels varies with the viewport.
- Tested sizes: Not currently documented.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Backgrounding:** the loop pauses while hidden; `last` is reset on resume, so there is no jump.
- **Resize during a visit:** the visit state is kept and scaled.
- **Rapid input:** a new planet touch retargets the visit; a rocket touch ends the visit; repeated star or astronaut touches while an animation is running are ignored.
- **Visit that cannot finish:** after 25 s without arriving the rocket switches to the "stay" phase anyway.
- **Edge clamping:** the rocket is clamped to the visible area every frame.
- **Unhandled:** no fallback without `requestAnimationFrame` or `window.Rand`.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#105](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/105) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation in node (hover at start, 60 s of flight stays inside the visible box, planet visit with glow rise and fade, rocket tap mid-trip, puff pool bounded) and asks for a visual device check in portrait and landscape.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Rakieta; the rocket hovers and bobs; touch it and it starts flying along a loop; it crosses the width in about 15 s and never leaves the screen.
- [ ] Touch the flying rocket; it slows to a hover in about 2 s.
- [ ] Touch each of the three planets from hover and from flight; the rocket curves to a spot beside the planet, the halo glows for about 3 s and the rocket then resumes.
- [ ] Touch another planet during a visit; the rocket retargets. Touch the rocket during a visit; the visit ends.
- [ ] Touch several stars (one twinkle each) and the astronaut (a wave).
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch empty sky; nothing happens.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no completion state.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: leave and re-enter 10 times; astronaut, planet colours and arrangement change on every launch; none repeats twice in a row in the same pick.
- [ ] Progression: confirm nothing persists after reload.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate during flight and during a visit; the rocket and planets stay on screen and no star overlaps a planet.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab through the 15 stars, 3 planets, rocket and astronaut).
- [ ] Background the tab during flight; return with no jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled: flight, glow and twinkles still run.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- The motion ignores the reduced-motion preference by design.
- The astronaut is not drawn from `js/animals.js` (a separate local set of 6), so there are two animal systems in the code base.

**Requires verification**

- Whether any two of the 15 stars (56 px hit boxes) or a star and a planet overlap on very small or very narrow screens (a layout fix was made in PR [#154](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/154)).
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Rakieta; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar: [Traktor](traktor.md), [Autobusik](autobusik.md), [Mała Łódka](mala-lodka.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md), [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md), [Balon](balon.md). The night-sky feel is close to the star activities (see the project README).
- Shared helper used: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). `js/animals.js` is not used.
- Shared pattern: rAF loop with capped dt and a damped spring for smooth redirection.

## 21. Change history

- [#93](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/93) / PR [#105](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/105): Rakieta activity added.
- Commit `3fb06b0`: the rocket uses a real `<button>` instead of a nested `role="button"` (review suggestion on #105).
- PR [#154](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/154): random astronaut, planet colours and sky arrangements (a follow-up commit nudged two stars so 56 px hit boxes no longer overlap).
- PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): animal-pool batch listed in the search results for this activity.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/rasy-pieskow.md`

```markdown
# Rasy Piesków

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Rasy Piesków |
| Activity ID | `rasy` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | One dog at a time, drawn large with its Polish breed name underneath; arrows, swipe or arrow keys move between the eight breeds. The dog is alive (blink, wag, idle actions) and a touch triggers one of six gentle actions. |
| Category | Cause and effect; observation; open-ended play |
| Interaction type | Tap, horizontal swipe, arrow buttons, keyboard |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/rasy.js`](../../js/rasy.js) (activity), [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js) (shared drawings, `window.Dogs`), styles with prefixes `rp-` and `dg-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tags in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

## 2. Business purpose

- Introduces the foundation of the dog theme from issue [#175](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/175): one shared set of breed drawings (`window.Dogs`) that later dog activities can reuse, plus an activity that hosts the menu tile, Settings entry and README entry.
- Lets the child look at and name familiar breeds (Labrador, Jamnik, Husky, Pudel, Owczarek, Buldog, Corgi, Dalmatyńczyk), one at a time.
- Complements the animal activities built on [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js), such as [Zwierzątka na Farmie](zwierzatka-na-farmie.md), with a single-theme, breed-specific view.
- Issue [#204](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/204) turned the gallery into a one-dog-at-a-time activity so the child meets each breed in turn and sees it do fun things.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 47.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the eight breeds are shuffled (`Rand.shuffle`) and the first one is shown, drawn large on a soft green background.
2. Initially displayed: one calm dog (blinking, tail wagging gently), its breed name under it, a large arrow button at each side (bottom corners in portrait, vertically centred at the sides in landscape).
3. Interactions: tap the dog (or focus it and press Enter/Space); tap an arrow, swipe horizontally, or press the Left/Right arrow key.
4. Response to a touch: one 2.5 s action chosen at random, never the same twice in a row: wag and smile, jump on the spot, spin around, bark ("Hau!" bubble, no sound), roll over, sit and give a paw. Touches during that action are ignored.
5. Navigation: the next/previous dog of the shuffled cycle fades in over 0.5 s while the old one fades out; the first and last wrap around, so every breed is seen once before any repeats.
6. There is no completion state.
7. Restart: leaving and re-opening reshuffles; nothing is stored.
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Dog size | Drawn with `Dogs.draw(id, { scale: 1 })` (size-class scales are not applied), filling the area between the Back button and the arrows; the visible dog is about 45-65% of the shorter screen side from 568 x 320 up. |
| Order | `order = Rand.shuffle(Dogs.LIST)` per launch, start at index 0; arrows wrap around. |
| Touch actions | `TOUCH` = wag, jump, spin, bark, roll, paw; `Rand.pickOne(TOUCH, 'rasy-touch')` (never the same twice in a row). Each lasts `ACT_S = 2.5` s; the happy face and glow (`rp-on`) show for all of them; touches during an action are ignored. |
| Action motions | wag: tail up to 18 degrees at 2.2 Hz; jump: one 16-unit hop; spin: one turn (mirror flip) in 2.1 s; bark: head up and a "Hau!" bubble; roll: 360 degrees eased over 2.1 s (peak below 260 degrees/s); paw: sits (rotation about the rear feet, front legs kept upright) and lifts the near front paw. |
| Idle life | Blink every 3-5 s (0.16 s); gentle tail wag; every 8-12 s one idle action (`look` back or up, `sniff`, `scratch`, `sit`), calm face, picked with `Rand.pickOne(IDLE, 'rasy-idle')`. A touch during an idle action replaces it (pose values ease at about 6 per second, so there is no jump). |
| Swipe | Horizontal move of at least 50 px that is more than 1.5 times the vertical move navigates; the click that follows a swipe is ignored, so a swipe never starts an action. |
| Navigation during an action | The old dog is reset to its neutral pose at once and fades out. |
| Faces | Only `dg-calm` and `dg-happy`; no angry or sad face. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (touch, the dog reacts).
- Noticing and naming dog breeds (Polish labels).

**Directly observable behavior**

- A touched dog plays one 2.5 s action and looks happy.
- Every dog has a visible Polish name and a distinct colour and silhouette (ear shape, tail shape, markings).

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about breed recognition or vocabulary. Nothing in the code can establish it, and recognisability of the drawings has not been checked on a device.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** the dog and the two arrows are native `<button>`s using `click`; touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space, Left/Right arrow keys) work, swipe uses pointer events. Focus ring: 4 px outline.
- **Labels (Polish):** the dog button has `aria-label` set to the breed name; the arrows are "Poprzedni" and "Następny"; SVG and bubble are `aria-hidden`. There is no state announcement.
- **Target sizes:** arrows are 64 x 64 px; the dog button fills the dog area.
- **Layout:** portrait: dog area below the Back button, arrows in the bottom corners; landscape: dog area between the side arrows (`@media (orientation: landscape)`). The same DOM is kept on rotation, so the dog and its state persist.
- **Colour:** the breed name is always shown as text; the happy state is also shown by the mouth shape, not only by the glow.
- **Reduced motion:** a touch only shows the smile and glow for 2.5 s (class `rp-on`, `display` attributes set from JavaScript); the idle life is just the blink (no wag, no idle actions, no bubble). Navigation works; the CSS fade is disabled by the global rule so the dogs swap instantly.
- **Touch:** `touch-action: none` on the scene (so swipes are delivered), `manipulation` on the buttons.
- **Reading:** not required (names are a parent-facing aid). A young child can use it independently.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Breed recognisability and the size of the smallest drawings (Pudel, Jamnik at 320 x 568) have not been checked on a device (see sections 17 and 18).
- Breeds are stylised cartoons, not accurate depictions.
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.
- No privacy concerns; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/rasy.js`](../../js/rasy.js): `ACT_S` (2.5 s touch action), `FADE_MS` (500), `SWIPE_PX` (50), the action lists `TOUCH` / `IDLE` with `IDLE_DUR`, the sit pivot `RX, RY`, and a frame time cap of 0.05 s in `frame()`; `pose(kind, t, dir)` is the pure table of action motions. Breed data lives in `DEFS` and `ORDER` in [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js): per breed the name, size class, body length/height, leg height, head radius, snout, colours, ear type (`floppy`, `point`, `fold`, `puff`), tail type (`thick`, `curl`, `pom`, `stub`, `bushy`) and decoration (`spots`, `mask`, `saddle`, `none`). `Dogs.SCALE` (size-class scales) is not applied here.

Fallback: `Dogs.byId` returns the first breed (Labrador) for an unknown id. `window.Dogs` is required by `rasy.js` and is not checked for being absent.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Every dog is an inline SVG string built by `Dogs.draw(id, opts)` (`viewBox="0 0 120 100"`, facing right, feet on y = 92). The menu icon is an inline SVG in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js). No images, fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Per launch the breed order is a random shuffle of all eight breeds (each once per cycle, the same cycle repeats on wrap-around). Touch actions and idle actions are picked at random, never the same twice in a row.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels or persistence.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no completion state and no failure. Feedback is the dog's own reaction; nothing starts by itself except the gentle idle life.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to `window.Analytics` (`js/analytics.js`): every dog touch that starts an action and every navigation (arrow, swipe, key) is `track('interaction', { variant: <breed id> })` (for navigation the breed shown after the move). It is open-ended, so there is no `complete`, level or exit-before-completion. Start, active time, replays, quick exits and touches are also recorded by the app shell. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/rasy.js`](../../js/rasy.js) overrides `mount` of the `rasy` entry in `window.ACTIVITIES`; it sets `container.style.display = 'block'` and returns a cleanup function that sets `alive = false`, cancels the frame, removes the `visibilitychange` listener and removes the scene.
- **Rendering:** `div.rp > div.rp-wrap > div.rp-view` (one per visible dog: `button.rp-dog` with the SVG and a "Hau!" `span.rp-bubble`, plus `div.rp-name`) and two `button.rp-arrow`. `makeView` regroups the SVG parts: `all > [fl (front legs, with the near paw group), rot (everything else; head and ears inside `headg`, near rear leg group)]`, so each can be posed separately without changing `js/dogs.js`.
- **State:** per view `act` (kind, t, dur, touch), blink and idle timers and eased pose values `C` (sit, paw, rear leg, head tilt, head flip); `cur` is the only view updated.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, running while the tab is visible and restarted on `visibilitychange`.
- **Drawing:** `Dogs.draw(id, { scale: 1 })`; part classes `dg-tail`, `dg-legs`, `dg-head`, `dg-ears`, `dg-calm`/`dg-happy`; the eye is the `circle[r="2"]` in the head.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** through the app shell only (section 13).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.rp` is fixed full-screen; `.rp-wrap` is inset below the Back button (64 px plus safe area) and above the arrows in portrait, and between the 88 px side insets in landscape. Each `.rp-view` is stacked in it and centres the dog (aspect ratio 6:5, height 100%) over its name.
- The SVG fills the button and keeps its `viewBox="0 0 120 100"`; the orientation switch is CSS only.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tap during a touch action | Ignored until it ends (no restart, no extra metric). |
| Tap during an idle action | The touch action replaces it smoothly. |
| Swipe | Navigates; the click after it is ignored. |
| Navigation during an action | The old dog is reset and fades out; the new one starts calm. |
| Quick repeated navigation | Each outgoing dog is removed 0.5 s after it leaves; timers are cleared in cleanup. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| Resize / orientation | CSS only; dog and state kept. |
| `window.Dogs` / `window.Rand` missing | Not handled (both load before `app.js`). |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] One dog is visible, large (about half of the shorter side or more), with its Polish name under it; each launch starts with a random breed and the eight breeds come in a random order, each once before any repeat.
- [ ] Arrows (Poprzedni / Następny), swipe left/right and the Left/Right keys move between dogs with a 0.5 s fade; the first/last wrap around.
- [ ] A swipe that starts on the dog never triggers an action.
- [ ] Tap the dog many times: six different actions occur, never the same twice in a row; taps during an action are ignored; every action lasts about 2.5 s and is gentle.
- [ ] Wait 30 s untouched: the dog blinks every 3-5 s, wags, and every 8-12 s does an idle action (look, sniff, scratch, sit).
- [ ] Navigate while an action is playing: the old dog fades in a neutral pose, the new one is calm.
- [ ] Sit / paw: the front legs reach the ground and nothing detaches in any breed (check the Jamnik and the Husky).
- [ ] Portrait and landscape down to 568 x 320 and 320 px wide; rotate during an action.
- [ ] Reduced motion: touch gives smile and glow only, blink continues, navigation works.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the dog and arrows, Enter/Space activates; focus ring visible.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Metrics (Settings > Statystyki): touches and navigation count as interactions per breed.

The implementation (issue [#204](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/204)) was checked with a stub-DOM run in Node (shuffle/wrap order, one touch per action, ignored touches, no NaN transforms, cleanup); the visual checks are pending.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Visual quality of the idle and touch actions on a device (sit and paw pose in every breed, the "Hau!" bubble position) and the on-screen size of the dog at 320 x 568 and 568 x 320.

## 19. Planned improvements

Not currently documented; issue [#175](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/175) describes `window.Dogs` as the shared foundation for future dog activities.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other activities with a shared character family: [Zwierzątka na Farmie](zwierzatka-na-farmie.md), [Kąpiel Zwierzątek](kapiel-zwierzatek.md), [Buźki](buzki.md).
- Shared component: [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js) (`Dogs.LIST`, `Dogs.SCALE`, `Dogs.byId`, `Dogs.draw`).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#175](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/175) / PR [#180](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/180): initial activity and shared dog drawings.
- Issue [#204](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/204): one dog at a time with navigation, idle life and six touch actions; metrics added.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/rozmiar.md`

```markdown
# Rozmiar

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#222](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/222)
- Activity id: `rozmiar`
- CSS prefix: `rz-`

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Rozmiar |
| Activity ID | `rozmiar` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Five nesting cups (or matryoshka dolls) of clearly different sizes lie scattered on a table; the child drags each into a bigger one until all five form one stack. |
| Category | Size comparison; dragging; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag (touch, mouse) with a keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/rozmiar.js`](../../js/rozmiar.js), styles with prefix `rz-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- The first activity that orders by size; [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md) only splits into big and small. Issue [#222](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/222).
- No counting numbers, wrong-order messages or scores.

## 3. Activity flow

1. Five items of one set (cups or dolls in one colour scheme) lie scattered on the table in random order; the biggest carries an animal head.
2. The child drags an item onto a bigger one. It slides inside with a soft squash ("click", 0.45 s) and sits snugly in the middle, a little higher than the item below.
3. Dropping an item on a smaller one makes it drift back to where it came from in 0.5 s. Dropping it on the empty table leaves it there.
4. A nested item can be dragged again: it lifts out together with what is inside it (the smallest comes out alone), and drifts back if dropped on a smaller item. A stack is dragged by its biggest item.
5. When all five are one stack it glows for 3 s and the animal waves; then the items fade out (0.5 s) and a new random set fades in scattered on the table (0.6 s).
6. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Sizes | Heights 56, 72, 92, 117, 150 px (ratio 1.28, i.e. at least 25% from item to item), scaled up together on bigger screens (never below 56 px). Width is 0.76 of the height, but never below 56 px (the smallest item gets a 56 px wide touch box; its drawing keeps its proportions, centred). |
| Sets | 12 sets (6 cups, 6 dolls, each with its own colours) via `Rand.pickOne`, so the same set never comes twice in a row. The animal is random from `Animals.pick`. |
| Scatter | Random order and jitter in rows (three rows of 2, 2, 1 in portrait; one row in landscape); no overlaps at 320x568 or 568x320. |
| Nesting | The dragged item (with its contents) may be dropped on any bigger item whose box contains the dragged item's centre; the nearest such item wins. Items already inside the target are merged in size order, so a stack is always sorted. |
| Wrong order | A drop whose centre is over a smaller item (and no bigger one) drifts back in 0.5 s; nothing is reported. |
| Lift out | Touching a nested item and moving it takes it, with everything inside it, out of its container. A tap without moving (under 6 px) changes nothing. |
| Finale | All five nested: glow 3 s with a waving animal (0.7 waves per second), then 0.5 s fade-out and 0.6 s fade-in of a new set. Touches are ignored during the finale. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is stored. |
| Text | None on screen; only Polish screen-reader labels ("Kubek 2 z 5", "Matrioszka 3 z 5"). |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits:** comparing and ordering by size, fitting things into one another, fine motor control of dragging.

**Directly observable behavior:** only a smaller item can go inside a bigger one; a finished stack is always ordered by size.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any effect on understanding of size or seriation.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- Input: touch, mouse, keyboard. Every item is a `<button>` (Tab). Enter/Space selects it (solid outline, `aria-pressed`); arrows (or Tab to another item and Enter/Space) choose the target, shown with a dashed outline; Enter/Space on the selected item nests it. For a nested item the first target is "table", which lifts it out beside its container. Escape cancels.
- All items are at least 56 px; the field starts 64 px below the top so the Back button is never covered.
- Colour is not the only cue: sizes differ in height, the selected item is outlined solid and the target dashed.
- Reduced motion: all movement, the finale and the wave run from one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (not CSS), so every state is reached; nothing is faster than 0.7 waves per second and nothing flashes.
- Only the first pointer drags; a second finger is ignored.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- A big item cannot be nested by tapping alone on a touch screen; dragging is needed (the keyboard path exists).
- The animal head sticks out above the biggest item; its touch area counts as that item.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of `js/rozmiar.js`: `RATIO` (1.28), `BASE_H` (56), `GLOW_MS` (3000), `OUT_MS`, `IN_MS`, `DRIFT_MS` (500), `NEST_MS` (450), `MOVE_PX` (6), and the `SETS` list.

## 9. Assets

No asset files: items are inline SVG (cup or doll, built by `itemSvg`), the animal head comes from `window.Animals`, and the menu icon is in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Set (kind and colours) with no immediate repeat, animal, order and jitter of the scatter. Nothing persists.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None: always five items.

## 12. Completion and feedback

Completed when all five items are in one stack. Feedback: glow, waving animal, then a new set. No failure.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Reports to `window.Analytics` (see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status)):

- `track('interaction', { variant: 's<n>' })` for each nest (touch or keyboard), where `s1`-`s5` is the size of the item that was moved (1 = smallest). Lifts, drifts and taps are not reported.
- `complete()` once per finished stack.

Calls are wrapped in try/catch; nothing is stored by the activity.

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` overrides `mount` of the `rozmiar` entry; the root is attached with `container.appendChild` before layout; returns a cleanup function.
- **Model:** each item has `inside` / `inner` links (a chain sorted by size) and, for chain roots, a fractional anchor (`fax`, `fay`) on the field; rest positions are computed by `computeTargets`, and `settle(ms)` glides items there.
- **Rendering:** `div.rz > div.rz-field > 5 × button.rz-item (svg.rz-svg, optional span.rz-head)`; SVG sizing uses `.stage .rz-svg`.
- **Loop:** one capped-dt rAF loop for glides, the squash, the finale phases (`pre`, `glow`, `out`, `in`) and the wave; it stops when idle and pauses when the tab is hidden.
- **Cleanup:** cancels rAF and removes the listeners and the root.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Positions are stored as fractions of the field, so rotation or resize (`layout()` on `resize` / `orientationchange`) keeps all state; sizes scale with `k` (1 to 1.4). A drag in progress is cancelled (the item drifts back) on resize or when the tab is hidden.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Second pointer ignored while one is dragging; `pointercancel` drifts the item back.
- Items are clamped inside the field; the dragged item keeps its position relative to the finger.
- A missing `Analytics` or `Animals` is tolerated.

## 17. Testing

Manual scenarios:

1. Drag item 1 into item 2: it slides in with a soft squash and sits centred.
2. Drag item 4 onto item 1: it drifts back in about 0.5 s.
3. Nest 1 into 2, then drag 2 (with 1 inside) into 3, then lift 1 out by dragging it away.
4. Nest all five: glow 3 s, the animal waves, then a different set appears scattered.
5. Rotate the device mid-stack: the stack stays together.
6. Keyboard: Tab to item 1, Enter, arrows to choose the target, Enter; select a nested item and choose "table" to lift it out.
7. With the system "reduce motion" setting on, every step above still works.

A throwaway Node stub-DOM simulation (fake rAF, pointer events on the item buttons) was used to check the size ratio, the absence of overlaps at five viewports, wrong-order drift back, merged stacks, completion and the keyboard path; it is not part of the repository.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

None known.

## 19. Planned improvements

None.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md) (size), [Wieża z Klocków](wieza-z-klockow.md) (dragging onto a target).
- Uses `window.Animals`, `window.Rand` and `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Initial implementation ([#222](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/222)).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/rysuj-ksztalty.md`

```markdown
# Rysuj Kształty

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Rysuj Kształty |
| Internal ID | `rysuj-ksztalty` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | Tracing practice: follow a dotted guide (line, circle, zigzag, cross, wave, spiral) with a finger and a soft coloured line appears along the guide. |
| Category | Drawing (tracing) |
| Interaction type | Trace/drag along a path; keyboard alternative: arrows, Enter or Space move the pen forward |
| CSS prefix | `rk-` |
| Source | [`js/rysuj-ksztalty.js`](../../js/rysuj-ksztalty.js), styles in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (section after `/* Gdzie jest Piłka? */`, selectors `.rk-*`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default (no `defaultOff`). Listed 31st in the README Activities list. |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity gives a child a forgiving first experience of following a line, which is a pre-writing movement, without the pressure of exactness: the line only grows where the finger stays near the guide, and nothing negative happens otherwise. It complements the free finger painting of [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md) (glowing colours that fade away) with a guided task. The six shapes progress roughly from simple to harder (straight line to spiral).

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#rysuj-ksztalty`); shape 1 (a horizontal line) is loaded.
2. A square pale board shows a dotted guide and a pen ring (44 px circle) at the start of the guide with an arrow showing the direction.
3. The child touches near the pen ring (within 52 px) and drags along the guide.
4. A thick soft line in gently changing colours appears along the guide as long as the finger stays within about 40 px of the guide and moves forward.
5. If the child lifts the finger, the line stays; touching near the end of the line continues from there.
6. When the whole guide is traced (all strokes), the board glows for about 3 s.
7. About 7 s after completion the board fades out (0.8 s), the next shape loads and fades in (0.8 s). After the spiral the cycle returns to the line.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

Shapes (unit-square coordinates, `y` down), always in this order:

| # | Label (`aria`) | Strokes | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | linia | 1 | horizontal line from (0.1, 0.5) to (0.9, 0.5) |
| 2 | kółko | 1 | circle, centre (0.5, 0.5), radius 0.38, 72 segments, starting at the top and running clockwise |
| 3 | zygzak | 1 | 6 points: (0.1, 0.72), (0.26, 0.28), (0.42, 0.72), (0.58, 0.28), (0.74, 0.72), (0.9, 0.28) |
| 4 | krzyżyk | 2 | vertical (0.5, 0.1) to (0.5, 0.9), then horizontal (0.1, 0.5) to (0.9, 0.5) |
| 5 | fala | 1 | sine wave, 2 periods, amplitude 0.2, x from 0.08 to 0.92, 60 segments |
| 6 | spirala | 1 | outward spiral, 2 turns, radius 0.05 to 0.42, 140 segments, starting at the top, clockwise |

Tracing rules (constants at the top of the file):

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Start/continue touch distance (`START_PX`) | the finger must start within 52 px of the pen |
| Distance from the guide (`NEAR_PX`) | the finger must be within 40 px of the guide to extend the line |
| Direction | only points ahead of the current progress count; movement against the direction, or far from the guide, does not extend the line (no feedback) |
| Reach per update (`MAX_JUMP`) | up to 0.35 of the total shape length ahead of the current progress |
| Fast drags | the finger's path between two events is walked in steps of about 8 px, so quick movements still follow the guide |
| Line width | `max(14, B * 0.05)` px where `B` is the board size |
| Colour | five pastel colours (`PALETTE`) interpolated along the whole shape length |
| Multi-stroke | the cross has 2 strokes; when the first is complete the pen jumps to the start of the second |
| Completion glow / next shape | `GLOW_S = 3` s; `NEXT_AT_S = 7` s; `FADE_S = 0.8` s each way |
| Keyboard step | `STEP = 0.03` of the total length per key press |

Input is ignored during the glow and fade phases (`phase !== 'play'`).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the README and code comments, not measured)

- Practice in following a line with a finger (hand-eye coordination, pre-writing movements).
- Concentration on a simple, repeatable task.
- Familiarity with basic shapes and curves.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The line is drawn only along the guide, so the result always looks neat.
- Movement away from the guide just does nothing; there is no error state.
- Shapes grow in complexity from a line to a spiral.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any link to later handwriting ability or fine-motor development. The activity makes no measurement.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via pointer events with pointer capture; only the primary pointer draws at a time (`drawing` holds one pointer id). Keyboard: the board is focusable (`tabindex="0"`, `role="application"`) and ArrowRight, ArrowDown, Enter and Space advance the pen along the guide; ArrowLeft and ArrowUp are not handled. The `aria-label` names the shape, for example `Rysowanie po kropkach: kółko. Strzałki, Enter lub spacja prowadzą pisak wzdłuż linii.`
- **Target size:** the pen ring is 44 x 44 px (CSS), but the finger may start within 52 px of the pen, so the effective start area is larger; the line is at least 14 px wide.
- **Orientation:** the board is a square of side `B = max(160, min(fieldWidth, fieldHeight, 720))`, centred; layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange` and the drawn progress is redrawn.
- **Colour:** the guide is dotted lilac on a pale board; the drawn colour is not needed to understand the task. The arrow at the pen shows the direction.
- **Sound:** none. **Reading:** not required.
- **Reduced motion:** the glow and fades are driven by the rAF loop and so still run under `prefers-reduced-motion`; they are soft opacity and glow changes (no fast movement).
- **Touch behaviour:** `touch-action: none` on the board prevents scrolling while drawing.
- **Focus:** 4 px box-shadow `#8f7fd1` on the focused board.
- **Limitations:** a child needs to start near the pen; precise tracing of the spiral and zigzag may be hard for the youngest users (`Requires verification`).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Tracing requires some fine motor control; the spiral (140 segments, 2 turns) may be frustrating.
- A finger covering the guide can hide the path; the dotted guide is thin (`stroke-width 0.012` of the board).
- If a child draws far from the guide nothing appears and no hint is given.
- The order of shapes is fixed and always starts with the line.
- No personal data is collected; the drawing is not saved.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants in [`js/rysuj-ksztalty.js`](../../js/rysuj-ksztalty.js):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEAR_PX` | Maximum finger distance from the guide | px | `40` |
| `START_PX` | Maximum distance from the pen to start | px | `52` |
| `MAX_JUMP` | Reach ahead, fraction of shape length | number | `0.35` |
| `STEP` | Keyboard step, fraction of shape length | number | `0.03` |
| `GLOW_S`, `NEXT_AT_S`, `FADE_S` | Completion timing | s | `3`, `7`, `0.8` |
| `PALETTE` | Five RGB colours | array | pink, yellow, green, blue, lilac |
| `SHAPES` | Shape definitions (order is the sequence) | array | 6 shapes |
| Board size | 160 to 720 px | px | `layout` |
| Device pixel ratio | capped at 2 | number | `layout` |

No fallback exists because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The guide is an inline SVG (`viewBox 0 0 1 1`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`) with dotted round-capped paths (`#a99cc4`); the drawing is a 2D `<canvas>`; the pen is a CSS-styled `div`. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No unused assets.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Nothing is randomized: the six shapes always appear in the same order (line, circle, zigzag, cross, wave, spiral, then the line again) and a launch always starts with the line. The colour of the line depends only on the position along the shape.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

- There is no adaptive difficulty. The sequence of shapes is fixed and loops (`load(idx + 1)` with wrap-around).
- The shapes are roughly ordered from easy to hard, but the code does not define difficulty levels.
- Progress is not stored; every launch starts with the line.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Completion:** the last stroke reaches its end (`complete()`).
- **Feedback during play:** the line grows with the finger; the pen ring moves to the end of the line.
- **Feedback on completion:** the board glows (`drop-shadow` in `#ffe08a`) for about 3 s.
- **Afterwards:** the next shape fades in automatically after the fade-out.
- **Failure feedback:** none (movement off the guide is simply ignored).
- **Sound:** none.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/rysuj-ksztalty.js`](../../js/rysuj-ksztalty.js), registered on the `rysuj-ksztalty` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **State:** `idx` (shape index), `shape` (prepared with cumulative arc lengths per stroke), `cur` (current stroke), `s` (progress as arc length in unit coordinates), `drawing` (active pointer id), `phase` (`play`, `done`, `out`, `in`), `glow`, `op`.
- **Rendering:** a board `div` holding an SVG guide, a `<canvas>` for the line and the pen `div`. The canvas has a backing size of `B * dpr`; progress is redrawn from `s` and `cur` in `redraw()`, so resize and rotation keep the drawing relative to the guide.
- **Drawing:** done directly in the pointer handlers (`advanceTo`), using short segments of 5 px coloured by `colorAt`. The rAF loop only runs the glow and fade phases and stops when idle.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture` and `keydown` on the board; `resize`/`orientationchange`; `visibilitychange`.
- **Randomization:** none. **Persistence/analytics:** none.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes window/document listeners and the root element.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The field is the screen minus 64 px at the top and 12 px on the other sides (plus safe areas); the board is a centred square of side `B` (160 to 720 px).
- Coordinates: shapes, progress and the guide use the unit square (0 to 1) on both axes; the SVG guide uses `viewBox 0 0 1 1` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, the canvas draws at `x * B`, `y * B`, and the pen is placed with percentages. All three share one coordinate space. Pointer positions are converted to unit coordinates through the board rectangle.
- Thresholds (`NEAR_PX`, `START_PX`, line width) are in CSS pixels, so tolerance does not shrink on small boards.
- A past bug where the guide appeared squeezed into the top-left 120 px (global `.stage svg` rule overriding `.rk-guide`) was fixed by prefixing the selector with `.stage` (PR [#155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155)).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | Not applicable. |
| Resize/orientation change | `layout` resizes the canvas and `redraw` rebuilds the line from the stored progress. |
| Fast drag between events | Interpolated in steps of about 8 px. |
| Finger far from the guide or moving backwards | Ignored. |
| Second finger while drawing | Ignored (`drawing !== null`). |
| Touch cancel / lost capture | Ends the stroke; progress is kept; the child can continue near the end of the line. |
| Input during glow/fade | Ignored. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted; timers use the capped frame step. |
| Canvas unsupported | Not handled (`getContext('2d')` result is used without a check); `Requires verification` on very old browsers. |

## 17. Testing

**Automated tests:** none (see [shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#87](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/87) describes the design and PR [#155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155) the layout fix; this document does not re-verify them.

**Manual scenarios (not yet recorded as performed):**

- [ ] Normal: trace the line starting at the pen; the coloured line follows the finger.
- [ ] Completion: finish the shape; the glow lasts about 3 s and the next shape fades in about 7 s after completion.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: start far from the pen (nothing happens); drag far from the guide or backwards (the line does not extend); lift and continue from the end.
- [ ] Each shape: complete all six (line, circle, zigzag, cross with two strokes, wave, spiral) and confirm the order and the return to the line.
- [ ] Fast drag: swipe quickly along the shape; the line still follows.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: leave and re-open; the line is first again (no randomization).
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is no difficulty change besides the shape order.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: 320 x 568, 568 x 320, tablet; rotate mid-shape and confirm the drawing stays on the guide.
- [ ] Touch and mouse: finger and mouse drag; Tab to the board and use ArrowRight/ArrowDown/Enter/Space.
- [ ] Background/foreground: hide the tab during the glow.
- [ ] Reduced motion: glow and fades still occur but are soft.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- Fixed order, no randomization, no way to choose a shape.
- ArrowLeft/ArrowUp do nothing; there is no way to undo or erase.
- `getContext('2d')` is not checked.

**Requires verification**

- Tracing difficulty of the zigzag and spiral for the youngest children on small phones.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Related: [Malowanie Światłem](malowanie-swiatlem.md) (free painting with a finger; its line fades away, whereas here the line stays on the guide).
- Shared helpers: none used; the activity uses neither `Rand` nor `Animals`.
- The pattern "state in unit-square coordinates, redraw on resize" is local to this file.

## 21. Change history

- [#65](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/65) / PR [#87](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/87): activity added.
- Merge commits "wider spiral ring pitch" (review suggestion, spiral radius 0.05 to 0.42).
- [#130](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/130) / PR [#155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155): guide layout fix (`.stage .rk-guide`).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/sciezka.md`

```markdown
# Ścieżka

> Documents the current implementation on `main`. Shared platform behaviour (no sound, global reduced-motion rule, menu configuration, playtime, absence of automated tests, analytics status) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Ścieżka |
| Activity ID | `sciezka` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A wide curvy path on a meadow. The child drags a finger along the path and a small figure (snail, car, ladybird or bee) follows slowly to a goal (flower or house). If the finger leaves the path or lifts, the figure waits. |
| Category | Coordination (tracing a path) |
| Interaction type | Drag along a path; keyboard alternative (arrows, Enter, Space) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/sciezka.js`](../../js/sciezka.js), CSS prefix `sc-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

A forgiving tracing activity: the path is wide (68 units), the figure only moves forward at a gentle capped speed, and leaving the path costs nothing. It trains following a line with a finger without any failure state, and complements the free-form drawing activities with a guided path.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the first path (landscape or portrait, depending on the screen) is drawn immediately with the snail at the start and a pink flower at the goal.
2. The child puts a finger on the path (or a mouse button down) near the figure's side of the path and drags along it.
3. The figure moves along the path toward the finger at a capped speed (the whole path takes about 7 s) and leaves a pink trail behind it.
4. If the finger moves off the path or lifts, the figure stops and waits; touching the path again continues.
5. At the goal a soft glow shows for 3 s (0.6 s ramps). About 4 s later the scene fades out (0.9 s) and the next path with another figure and goal fades in (0.9 s).
6. The four paths repeat in a fixed cycle: snail to pink flower, car to house, ladybird to daisy, bee to blue flower, then again.
7. There is no end screen. The child leaves with the Back button.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Path width drawn | 68 units (`PATH_W`), plus a 10-unit edge |
| Touch tolerance | `PATH_W / 2 + 24` = 58 units from the path centreline (`TOL`) |
| Forward window | A touch only counts if its nearest path point lies between the figure's position and half the path ahead (`WINDOW = 0.5` of the length) |
| Speed | Path length divided by `CROSS` = 7 s, so about 7 s for the whole path regardless of size |
| Backwards movement | Never: the target is `max(p, nearest)`; the figure does not return |
| Starting a drag | Must begin within tolerance of the allowed path stretch; otherwise ignored (no capture) |
| Finger off path / lifted | Target set to the current position; the figure stops |
| Keyboard step | Each arrow key, Enter or Space advances the target by 7% (`KEY_STEP`) of the path length; movement stays at the capped speed |
| Glow at goal | 3 s (`GLOW`) |
| Wait | 4 s (`WAIT`) |
| Fade | 0.9 s out, 0.9 s in (`FADE`) |
| Input while changing scene | ignored (phase other than `play`) |

Paths are defined as 8, 8, 6 and 7 control points in a landscape unit square and sampled by a Catmull-Rom spline into a dense polyline (16 steps per segment). Portrait uses the same shape rotated a quarter turn. The figure faces the direction of travel (it flips horizontally when the local direction is clearly left or right).

The pairs (`FIGURES`, `GOALS`, `LABELS`): Ślimaczek and pink flower; Samochodzik and house; Biedronka (coral, not red) and yellow daisy; Pszczółka and blue flower.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**: hand-eye coordination and fine motor control while tracing, attention to a moving figure, calm cause and effect, perseverance without penalty.

**Directly observable behavior**
- The figure follows only while the finger is on the path, and only forward.
- The path width is 68 units, with an extra 24 units of tolerance.
- A pink trail fills along the path behind the figure.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**
- Whether tracing the path improves fine motor skills.
- Whether the 7 s crossing time is appropriate for different children.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse, stylus (pointer events with capture); keyboard: the board is focusable (`tabindex="0"`, `role="application"`) and responds to arrow keys, Enter and Space. The board's label says "Ścieżka: przeciągnij palcem po ścieżce albo naciskaj strzałki, Enter lub spację". Focus outline 4px.
- **`touch-action: none`** on the board so dragging does not scroll the page.
- **Target size:** the path is a large band (68 units of a 400-unit-wide board, about 17% of the board width).
- **Orientation:** a 4:3 board in landscape and a 3:4 board in portrait; the path shape is rotated for portrait.
- **Colour:** the path is a light band on green; the figure's direction and the trail give non-colour cues; goals differ in shape (flower, house).
- **Reading:** none.
- **Sound:** none.
- **Reduced motion:** the figure and the fades are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop rather than CSS, so they still run under the global rule. The activity does not read `prefers-reduced-motion`; the figure's speed is the same.
- **Limitations:** progress along the path is not announced to assistive technology (the board only has a static label and a `data-figure` attribute); a drag requires a pointing device that can follow a curve.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Tracing a curve is demanding for the youngest children; there is no automatic assist other than the wide tolerance and the keyboard alternative.
- The same four paths are always shown in the same order, so the activity repeats after four rounds.
- Rotating the device during play rebuilds the scene and cancels any active drag (section 16).
- No ending; the cycle continues indefinitely.
- Privacy: nothing is stored or transmitted.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in `js/sciezka.js`.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Changeable without code change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PATH_W` | Path width (units) | number | 68 | No |
| `TOL` | Touch tolerance (units) | number | 58 | No |
| `WINDOW` | Forward window (fraction of path) | number | 0.5 | No |
| `KEY_STEP` | Keyboard step (fraction of path) | number | 0.07 | No |
| `CROSS` | Seconds to cross the path at full speed | number | 7 | No |
| `GLOW`, `WAIT`, `FADE` | Goal glow, wait and fade (s) | numbers | 3, 4, 0.9 | No |
| `PATHS` | Four control-point lists | array | see source | No |
| `FIGURES`, `GOALS`, `LABELS` | Inline SVG figures, goals and names | arrays | 4 each | No |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The figures and goals are inline SVG strings in `js/sciezka.js` (drawn around the origin and translated and scaled by 0.85 at runtime); the meadow, sun, path, trail and glow are generated SVG elements. No fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Nothing is randomized. The four paths cycle in a fixed order starting with path 1 on every launch (`si % 4`). The figure and goal are tied to the path index.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No levels or difficulty changes; the four paths differ in shape only. The cycle repeats and nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Completion:** the figure reaches the goal (arc length at the end of the path).
- **Feedback:** the pink trail along the path, the figure's movement, a soft yellow glow around the goal for 3 s.
- **Failure/retry:** none; leaving the path just pauses the figure.
- **After completion:** the next path loads automatically after the wait; no sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** IIFE in [`js/sciezka.js`](../../js/sciezka.js) overriding `mount` for `sciezka`.
- **Rendering:** DOM and SVG: a `.sc-board` (focusable) rebuilt by `build()` with one SVG (path layers, trail, glow, goal, figure).
- **Geometry:** `geometry()` maps control points to board units (400x300 landscape, 300x400 portrait), `sample()` builds a Catmull-Rom polyline with cumulative lengths, `at()` returns a position at an arc length (binary search), `nearest()` returns the arc length of the nearest path point within `TOL` inside a range.
- **State:** `p` (current arc length), `target`, `phase` (`play`, `glow`, `wait`, `out`, `in`), `pid` (active pointer), `si` (path index).
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop `frame()` with capped dt; moves `p` toward `target` at `len / CROSS`; stops when idle or hidden.
- **Events:** pointer events on the board with pointer capture, `keydown`, `visibilitychange`, `resize`, `orientationchange`.
- **Cleanup:** removes the listeners, cancels the frame and removes the root.
- **Shared helpers:** none (`Rand` and `Animals` are not used).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board: landscape `aspect-ratio: 4 / 3`; portrait (`.portrait`, set when the container is taller than wide) `aspect-ratio: 3 / 4`; width `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * ratio)`, with 56px top padding.
- SVG `viewBox` is `0 0 400 300` (landscape) or `0 0 300 400` (portrait), so path, trail, goal, figure and glow share one coordinate space. Pointer coordinates are converted with `toBoard()` using the board's bounding rectangle.
- Portrait mapping: `x = p[1] * W`, `y = (1 - p[0]) * H` of the landscape control points.
- Orientation change: `onResize` rebuilds the scene only when the orientation flips, keeping the progress fraction of the current path.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Finger leaves the path or lifts:** the target is reset to the current position; the figure waits.
- **Pointer cancel / lost capture:** same as release.
- **Orientation change during a drag:** `build(true)` resets the pointer id, so the drag is dropped and the child must touch again; during the glow it also resets the glow.
- **Backgrounding:** loop cancelled while hidden and restarted on return.
- **Second finger:** only the first pointer is tracked (`pid`).
- **Unhandled:** the reduced-motion preference is not used; no handling for a missing `ACTIVITIES` entry other than skipping the override.

## 17. Testing

There are no automated tests. Manual scenarios to perform:

- [ ] Drag along path 1 from start to goal: the figure follows, the trail fills, the glow shows at the goal, and path 2 appears about 4 s later.
- [ ] Start a drag away from the path: nothing moves.
- [ ] Drag off the path mid-way and lift: the figure waits; touching the path ahead of it continues.
- [ ] Try to drag backwards: the figure does not go back.
- [ ] Try to jump to the far end of the path: the figure still moves at the capped speed and only a touch within the first half of the remaining path counts.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the board; arrows, Enter or Space move the figure in steps of about 7%.
- [ ] Play through all four paths and confirm the figure and goal pairs and that the cycle repeats.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate mid-path (progress kept, drag dropped).
- [ ] Touch (phone and tablet), mouse and stylus.
- [ ] Switch tab during a drag and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: the figure still moves and fades still run.
- [ ] Browsers required by the README: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#69](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/69) reports `node --check`, a Node check that all four paths in both orientations have at least 83 units of centre clearance (no self-overlap, inside the board), and a stub-DOM run (off-path drag leaves the figure waiting, keyboard movement at the capped speed, goal reached in about 7 s, next path loads); it lists manual tests (touch/mouse/stylus, rotation, reduced motion, playtime wind-down, offline) as pending.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**
- No automated tests; manual device tests were pending in PR #69.
- Fixed path order and no randomization.
- Rotation during the glow resets the glow and any drag.
- Progress is not announced to assistive technology.

**Requires verification**
- Whether the 58-unit tolerance is comfortable for small fingers on phone-sized boards.
- Behaviour of the first-half forward window if a child lifts and re-starts far ahead.

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Same scene pattern (single rAF loop, glow, wait, cross-fade): [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md), [Co nie Pasuje?](co-nie-pasuje.md), [Wzorki](wzorki.md).
- Related interaction (following a shape with a finger): [Rysuj Kształty](rysuj-ksztalty.md).
- Shared helpers `js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not used.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#48](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/48) / PR [#69](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/69): activity added.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/slady-na-piasku.md`

```markdown
# Ślady na Piasku

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#216](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/216)
- Planned activity id: `slady`
- Planned CSS prefix: `sp-`

## 1. Overview

Ślady na Piasku (`slady`, module `js/slady.js`, CSS prefix `sp-`): a sand beach or a snowy field hides a picture (shell, starfish, snowman or tree). The child drags a finger and leaves paw prints, footprints or a wavy line that dig through the surface and slowly uncover the picture.

## 2. Business purpose

Fills the gap of an activity whose marks stay and uncover something (Malowanie Światłem fades away). Cause and effect with a small, calm reward.

## 3. Activity flow

1. A scene (sand or snow, alternating, the first random) and one of its two pictures are shown with three 56 px buttons (paws, footprints, wavy line; the first type is random). 2. Dragging leaves tracks of the chosen type that dig holes through the surface. 3. At about 70% of the picture uncovered the rest of the surface fades over 1 s, the picture glows for 3 s and a tiny animal (crab on sand, penguin on snow) appears. 4. After those 4 s a new surface and picture start.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Scenes | sand (shell, starfish) and snow (snowman, tree); alternate every round, never the same twice in a row; a picture never repeats twice in a row |
| Paw prints | one every 40 px of path length, drawn along the heading |
| Footprints | one every 48 px, alternating 9 px left and right of the path |
| Wavy line | 16 px wide, round caps, a 9 px sine wiggle (period 56 px) around the finger path, a point every 6 px |
| Buttons | three 56 px buttons with distinct pictures (paw, sole, wave); the chosen one has a thick ring and `aria-pressed` |
| Goal | 40x40 grid of the cells inside the picture; a cell counts when a track centre lies within the track radius (paw 17 px, foot 15 px, line 8 px); at 70% the round ends |
| Pointers | only the first pointer draws; input is ignored during the fade and glow |

No score, no failure, no stored data, no text on screen.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

Cause and effect, fine motor control, patience (the picture appears slowly), imitation of animal and human tracks.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

The board is focusable: arrows move a 56 px ring (3% of the board per press); Enter or Space leaves a track under it, and holding it while pressing arrows draws along (the wavy line needs this). The three type buttons are reachable by Tab. The shape of each button and the different scene textures are the non-colour cues. All targets are at least 56 px; aria labels are in Polish.

## 7. Risks and limitations

Checked only with a node stub DOM (stroke flow, goal, scene alternation, metrics) and syntax checks; no browser or device run was possible, so the real look of the sand, the snow and the pictures still needs a manual look. Track sizes are fixed in px, so after rotation they keep their size while positions scale.

## 8. Configuration

None; enabled by default and appended at the end of the menu list.

## 9. Assets

Inline SVG pictures and animals as strings in `PICTURES` and `ANIMALS`, a canvas for the surface, menu icon in `js/activities.js`. No sound, no external files.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Starting scene and starting track type are random on every mount; the picture is random within the scene (never the same one twice in a row).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None: the same rules throughout.

## 12. Completion and feedback

At 70%: 1 s fade of the remaining surface, 3 s glow of the picture with the animal, then a new scene.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

Each stroke start (touch or Enter/Space): `track('interaction', {variant: 'paw' | 'foot' | 'line'})`; each uncovered picture: `complete()`. Button changes are not reported.

## 14. Technical implementation

`mount` builds the DOM, attaches the root with `container.appendChild(root)` before `layout()` and returns a cleanup that cancels the rAF loop and removes the window and document listeners and the root. Tracks are stored as items (paw/foot: relative position, heading, side; line: relative points). The surface canvas is painted, then each item is dug with `destination-out`; a replay on resize redraws all items. The hit grid is built with `Path2D` + `isPointInPath`. One capped-dt rAF loop (only during fade and glow) drives opacity, so reduced motion changes nothing.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

Portrait: board over the three buttons in a row; landscape: board left, buttons in a column on the right, 72 px left padding keeps the Back button uncovered. The board size is pure CSS (`min(width, height minus reserved)`); SVG sizing uses `.stage .sp-svg` and `.stage .sp-btnsvg`.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

Rotation or resize: canvas redrawn from relative data. Tab hidden: loop stops, strokes end, resumes on return. Second finger: ignored. Fast drags: the path is walked in steps so spacing and the grid have no holes. At most 5000 items per round.

## 17. Testing

Manual scenarios:
1. Open the activity: a scene and three buttons appear, one selected.
2. Drag with each type: spacing about 40 px (paws), 48 px alternating (feet), a smooth 16 px wavy line.
3. Uncover about 70% of the picture: the rest fades in 1 s, the picture glows, an animal appears; after 4 s a new scene of the other kind starts.
4. Rotate the device mid-round: tracks and uncovered area stay.
5. Keyboard: Tab to the board, arrows move the ring, Enter leaves a track, hold Enter with arrows to draw.
6. Touch with two fingers: the second is ignored.

Node stub-DOM simulation (all three types, four rounds each) checks alternation of scenes, one `interaction` per stroke and one `complete()` per round.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

Look and proportions of the pictures not yet checked on a device.

## 19. Planned improvements

Optionally more pictures per scene.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

Related: Malowanie Światłem (fading marks), Lustro (painting that stays), Latarka (revealing hidden items). No shared components.

## 21. Change history

- Implemented from issue #216.

```
