## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/smok.md`

```markdown
# Lot na Smoku

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Lot na Smoku |
| Activity ID | `smok` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A friendly dragon with a small rider flies over a scrolling land. A finger steers it and a tap makes it breathe a little fire to light lanterns. |
| Category | Control skill; cause and effect; open-ended play; calming |
| Interaction type | Finger/mouse drag anywhere, tap on the dragon or a lantern, keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/smok.js`](../../js/smok.js), styles with prefix `sm-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A free-flight activity with a scrolling world and gentle things to do; issue [#186](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/186).
- Differs from [Latawiec](latawiec.md) (a kite on a string above a fixed board) and [Balon](balon.md) (vertical control only) by free two-axis steering over a scrolling landscape with changing biomes.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; a green dragon with a rider flies to the right over hills, a castle and clouds; lanterns drift past.
2. Touching or dragging anywhere steers the dragon; it follows the finger smoothly and stays on screen.
3. Tapping a lantern or the dragon makes it breathe a short puff of fire (0.8 s); the flame reaches the tapped lantern (or the nearest unlit one ahead) after 0.45 s and the lantern glows warm.
4. Every 36 s the scenery blends (over 5 s) into the next biome: meadow, snow, sea, meadow, ... The landscape pattern repeats seamlessly every 60 s. There is no end. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Flight | The dragon never flies by itself; the world scrolls left at 0.12 screen widths per second (so the dragon moves right at constant speed). |
| Steering | Damped spring (stiffness 7, damping 5.4) toward the finger; speed capped at 0.6 screen widths per second. |
| Bounds | The target and the dragon are clamped so the whole dragon, wings and tail included, stays on screen; a resize re-clamps it. |
| Lanterns | A pool of 14 buttons (56 px) spaced screen width / 8 apart on three height levels, so at least 6 are fully visible at any time; they drift left at the scroll speed and are recycled (unlit) on the right. |
| Fire | A puff has a 0.35 s cooldown. Tapped lantern: it is lit; tap on/near the dragon (within about 90 design units) or Enter/Space: the nearest unlit lantern ahead of the mouth is lit (any nearest lantern when none is unlit). |
| Lit lanterns | Stay lit until they leave the screen. |
| Biomes | 36 s each, blended over 5 s: meadow (trees, flowers), snow (pines, snowy castle roofs), sea (waves, boats). |
| Failure, score | None; no obstacles, nothing hurts the dragon; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Faces, text, sound | The dragon always smiles (open mouth while breathing); no text, no sound. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Smooth control of a following object in two directions; cause and effect (fire lights a lantern).

**Directly observable behavior**

- The dragon follows the finger smoothly and cannot leave the screen; lanterns light up after a puff.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events on the whole screen (touch, mouse, stylus); the child does not have to grab the dragon. Lantern buttons are 56 px; the dragon button is at least 56 px.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to the dragon (visible 4 px focus ring); arrow keys move the target by 10% of the screen width per press; Enter or Space breathes fire. Lanterns are also buttons (Tab, Enter).
- **Labels (Polish):** "Smok. Strzałki sterują lotem, Enter lub spacja zieje ogniem."; lanterns "Lampion"; scenery is decorative.
- **Non-colour cues:** a lit lantern also gains a glow and a brighter body.
- **Reduced motion:** everything moves from one JavaScript loop (wings, scenery, fire), so it behaves the same under `prefers-reduced-motion`; no end state exists only in a CSS keyframe.
- **Text:** none.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Visual quality (dragon proportions, wing flap, scenery colours, biome blend) has not been checked on a device (sections 17 and 18).
- The activity never goes idle (the world always scrolls), so the loop runs until the child leaves or the tab is hidden.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/smok.js`](../../js/smok.js): `LOOP_S` (60), `BIOME_S` (36), `BLEND_S` (5), `SPEED_W` (0.12), `VMAX` (0.6), `SK`, `SD`, `NL` (14), `LT_DIV` (8), `FIRE_S`, `HIT_S`, `COOLDOWN_S` and the `BIOMES` colour table.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The canvas scenery, the dragon (inline SVG) and the lanterns (inline SVG) are created by `js/smok.js`; the menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

None; the biome order and the lantern heights follow a fixed pattern.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

Feedback: a flame stream and a glowing lantern. No failure state and no completion; the activity is open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/smok.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant })` with `steer` (a steering touch starts), `fire` (a puff) and `lantern` (a lantern newly lit). It never calls `complete()`; the activity is not in the module's `COMPLETABLE` list. All calls are wrapped so nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. Data stays on the device; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/smok.js`](../../js/smok.js) overrides `mount` of the `smok` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.sm > canvas (scenery) + 14 button.sm-lt + svg.sm-svg (dragon) + button.sm-kb`. Layers (clouds, far hills, castle, near ground) scroll with a shared loop phase and have a whole number of pattern periods per loop, so the loop is seamless.
- **State:** dragon position and velocity, target, pitch, wing phase, lantern pool (x, level, lit, glow), current puff, time.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, guarded by `!raf`, cancelled while the tab is hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.sm` is fixed full-screen; the canvas is resized to the screen times the device pixel ratio (at most 2). The dragon width is `clamp(0.36 x min(width, 1.5 x height), 110, 260)` px. Lantern x positions are rescaled when the width changes; their heights come from a band between the top and 78% of the height.
- Works from 320 x 568 to 1920 x 1080, portrait and landscape.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Finger near an edge | The target is clamped so the whole dragon stays visible. |
| Very fast finger | Dragon speed is capped at 0.6 screen widths per second. |
| Resize / orientation | Layout recomputed; the dragon is re-clamped; the scenery keeps scrolling without a jump of the loop phase. |
| Rapid taps | The 0.35 s cooldown limits puffs. |
| No lantern on screen | The puff goes forward and fades. |
| Several fingers | Only the first pointer steers. |
| Leaving mid-flight | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag to all four corners; the whole dragon stays on screen.
- [ ] Tap a lantern; a flame reaches it and it stays lit until it leaves the screen.
- [ ] Tap the dragon; the nearest lantern ahead lights.
- [ ] Watch 40 s; the scenery changes smoothly from meadow to snow, then to sea.
- [ ] Watch past 60 s; no jump in the scenery.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to the dragon, arrows, Enter/Space.
- [ ] Rotate the device mid-flight.
- [ ] Leave and reopen ten times quickly.
- [ ] Small screens (320 x 568, 568 x 320) and 1920 x 1080; reduced motion.

The PR for issue [#186](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/186) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM (bounds at the corners, speed cap, number of visible lanterns, cleanup); no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel of the dragon, scenery and biome blend on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Latawiec](latawiec.md), [Balon](balon.md), [Mały Samolot](maly-samolot.md).
- No shared component is used besides `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#186](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/186): initial activity.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/traktor.md`

```markdown
# Traktor

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Traktor |
| Internal ID | `traktor` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A little tractor with a random animal driver drives a closed serpentine loop over a three-row field and leaves sprouts that grow into flowers and carrots. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, observation |
| Interaction type | Tap / click (also Enter and Space on the tractor, barn and driver) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Traktor is one of the "vehicle" activities (Traktor, Autobusik, Rakieta, Mała Łódka, Łódź Podwodna, Kolejka Linowa, Balon) that give a young child a slow, predictable machine to start and stop by touch. Its particular contribution is a visible consequence of the child's action: the longer the tractor drives, the more of the field fills with growing plants, and when the field is full it quietly resets. The activity has no goal, score or time pressure; touching the barn, a plant or the driver adds small, harmless reactions.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity from the menu (`#traktor`); `mount` builds the scene and starts one `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
2. The scene shows a sky, a sun, a barn at the top left, a field with three furrows and the tractor parked at the left end of the first row. The field is empty (all 36 plant nodes are hidden). One of six animal drivers sits in the cab.
3. The child can touch the tractor, the barn, the driver (in the cab window) and any visible plant.
4. Touching the tractor starts it (2 s smooth acceleration) or, when it is moving, slows it to a halt (2 s). While driving it plants a sprout at each slot it crosses on a row; each sprout grows over 3 s. Touching the barn makes the tractor drive to the start position and park. Touching the driver makes the animal wave for 2.4 s. Touching a grown or growing plant makes it wiggle for 1.2 s.
5. There is no formal completion state. When all 36 plants are fully grown the field waits 1.5 s, fades all plants out over 3 s and starts again empty. No message is shown.
6. The cycle repeats for as long as the tractor keeps driving.
7. There is no restart control; the field restarts by itself (see above) and leaving and re-entering the activity builds a new scene with a new random driver.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (or browser Back); see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Time to cross the visible width at cruise speed | `CROSS_S = 12` s (speed `V = W / 12` px/s, scaled with the scene width) |
| Start / stop ramp | `RAMP_S = 2` s, smoothstep (`sm`) easing; the tractor never reverses |
| Max frame step | `MAX_DT = 0.05` s |
| Route | One closed loop of 4 straight pieces and 4 U-turns over rows 1, 2, 3, 2 (then back to row 1); each U-turn is a half-ellipse sampled with `TURN_N = 24` segments of constant arc length |
| Plant slots | `SLOTS = 12` per row, 3 rows = 36 plants |
| Growth | `GROW_S = 3` s (smoothstep) |
| Plant wiggle | `WIG_S = 1.2` s, rotation `sin(2πk)·10°·(1−k)` |
| Driver wave | `WAVE_S = 2.4` s, arm rotation up to about -70° with a small oscillation |
| Field reset | `FULL_WAIT_S = 1.5` s after all plants are fully grown, then `FADE_S = 3` s fade of the plant layer |
| Wheel rotation | Driven by the odometer (`odo / 15` rad), rear wheel factor 0.8, front wheel 1.2 |

Rules in detail:

- **Tractor touch.** `onTractor` clears the parked flag and starts a ramp toward `V` (if stopped) or toward 0 (if moving or driving to the barn, `plan` set). Touches on the driver button are ignored by the tractor handler (guard on `.tk-dr`).
- **Barn touch.** `goBarn` computes the remaining distance `D` to the loop start and drives there along a cubic Hermite curve with duration `T = max(2.5, 1.2·D/V)` (capped so the initial speed is never exceeded in a way that would reverse); if the tractor is already within 1 px and slow it parks at once. When parked, a barn touch does nothing.
- **Planting.** `crossings` plants every unplanted slot passed on a row piece during a frame. It does nothing while the field is waiting to reset or fading. A planted slot is not replanted until the reset.
- **Plant kinds.** Slot kind is `(slot + row) mod 3`: 0 pink flower, 1 yellow flower, 2 carrot. A flower scales from 0.3 to 1 and its head fades in; a carrot's stem and leaves stay fixed (head opacity fades in over the first 20 % of growth) and the orange root scales down from the stem anchor (`CAR_TOP = 30`).
- **Wiggle** only starts on a plant that exists (`age >= 0`) and is not already wiggling.
- **Reduced motion.** Everything moves from the rAF loop and JS-set attributes (transform, opacity), so the activity animates fully under the global reduced-motion rule; see section 6.
- **Sound:** none.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (from the activity design, not measured):

- Cause and effect: touching the tractor starts and stops it; driving produces plants.
- Calm observation of slow, smooth motion and of growth.
- Simple independent play with large targets.

**Directly observable behavior:**

- The tractor takes 2 s to start or stop and crosses the screen in 12 s, so changes are gradual.
- Plants appear only where the tractor has just driven and take 3 s to grow.
- Every touch has a small, immediate, non-failing reaction (wiggle, wave, drive to the barn).

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about effects on attention, understanding of cause and effect or fine motor development. Not currently documented.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input.** Pointer events (`pointerdown`, touch, mouse and stylus) with `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation`, plus a `click` handler that only acts when `event.detail === 0` (keyboard activation). The tractor is a `div` with `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"` and also handles Enter and Space on `keydown`; the barn and the driver are real `<button>` elements. Plants are `aria-hidden` and are not keyboard reachable.
- **Touch handling.** `.tk` sets `touch-action: none` and disables text selection; there is no drag gesture.
- **Target sizes.** Plant hit boxes `.tk-pl` are 56 x 56 px; barn and driver have `min-width`/`min-height: 56px`; the tractor is `min(rh·1.6, 0.3·W, 230)` px wide. Plant hit boxes overlap on narrow screens (12 slots per row); a touch then goes to the topmost plant, which only wiggles (PR [#103](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/103) notes this).
- **Orientation.** Layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange` (section 15).
- **Colour.** Plant kinds differ in shape (carrot vs. round flower) and colour; no information depends on colour alone.
- **Sound.** None; see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).
- **Reduced motion.** The activity's own motion is not affected by the global rule because it uses a rAF loop and JS-set SVG attributes, not CSS animations or transitions. The scene therefore keeps moving for a user who asked for reduced motion; the motion is slow (2 s ramps, 12 s per width).
- **Focus.** `.tk-barn`, `.tk-tr`, `.tk-dr` have a 4 px focus outline.
- **Reading.** No reading required; accessible names (`aria-label`) are in Polish.
- **Limitations.** Plants cannot be reached by keyboard; the scene is not announced when plants grow.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- **Motion:** continuous slow motion; no flashing or rapid animation. The plant layer fade is 3 s.
- **Unclear ending:** the activity never ends; the field resets silently, which a child may not notice.
- **Overlapping plant targets** on narrow viewports (see section 6).
- **Performance:** one rAF loop running at all times (including while the tractor is parked), 36 pooled plant nodes and per-frame attribute updates for plants that are growing; no throttling on slow devices beyond the `MAX_DT` cap.
- **Privacy:** nothing is stored and no personal data is used.

## 8. Configuration

The activity has no external configuration; everything is a constant in [`js/traktor.js`](../../js/traktor.js). Values cannot be changed without editing the file.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CROSS_S` | Seconds to cross the width at cruise speed | number | 12 | top of IIFE |
| `RAMP_S` | Start/stop ramp duration (s) | number | 2 | top of IIFE |
| `MAX_DT` | Frame step cap (s) | number | 0.05 | top of IIFE |
| `SLOTS` | Plant slots per row | number | 12 | top of IIFE |
| `GROW_S` | Plant growth duration (s) | number | 3 | top of IIFE |
| `WIG_S` | Wiggle duration (s) | number | 1.2 | top of IIFE |
| `WAVE_S` | Driver wave duration (s) | number | 2.4 | top of IIFE |
| `FULL_WAIT_S` | Pause after the field is full (s) | number | 1.5 | top of IIFE |
| `FADE_S` | Field fade-out duration (s) | number | 3 | top of IIFE |
| `TURN_N` | Segments per U-turn table | number | 24 | top of IIFE |
| `DRIVERS` | Driver animal drawings (6) | array of `{arm, svg}` | 6 entries | `DRIVERS` |
| `CAR_TOP` | Carrot stem anchor y (viewBox units) | number | 30 | `CAR_TOP` |

There is no fallback handling for invalid values because there is no external input. The enabled state and position in the menu are configured in the Settings (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything is inline SVG generated in JS (`tractorSvg`, `barnSvg`, `plantSvg`, the six `DRIVERS` heads) and CSS (`.tk-*` rules in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css): sky gradient, sun, field gradient, furrows). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio, images or data files. No unused assets found.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **What:** the driver animal, chosen once per `mount` with `Rand.pickOne(DRIVERS, 'traktor')`.
- **Pool:** 6 drawings (according to PR [#153](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/153): bear, bunny, cat, pig, dog, mouse). The pool is local to the file and does not use `js/animals.js`.
- **Repetition:** `pickOne` never returns the item it returned last time for the key `traktor` in the same page session (pools of 2 or more). The memory is in memory only and is lost on reload.
- **Everything else is deterministic:** the route, plant slots and plant kinds are fixed.
- An empty pool would return `undefined` (not possible with the constant pool).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression, levels or difficulty. The only state that accumulates is the number of planted slots, which resets when the field is full. Nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no formal completion state, success criterion or failure. Feedback is visual only:

- The tractor accelerates, brakes and its wheels turn with the distance driven.
- Sprouts appear behind the tractor and grow; a touched plant wiggles; the driver waves; the barn touch drives the tractor home.
- A full field fades out and the field starts again automatically. No celebration, no sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/traktor.js`](../../js/traktor.js), assigned to the `traktor` registry entry; loaded from `index.html` before `js/app.js`. Other sources: `js/random.js` (`Rand.pickOne`), `.tk-*` CSS rules in `css/style.css`, README entry 33.
- **Rendering:** DOM + inline SVG. 36 plant nodes are created once and shown/hidden with `visibility`; tractor and plants are positioned with inline `left/top` and `transform`.
- **State:** closure variables: `s` (arc-length position on the loop), `v` (speed), `ramp` (start/stop easing), `plan` (Hermite drive to the barn), `parked`, per-plant `age`/`wig`, `waveT`, `fullT`/`fadeT`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop `frame(now)` with dt capped at 0.05 s; it is cancelled when `document.hidden` and restarted on `visibilitychange` (resetting `last`, so there is no time jump).
- **Path:** `layout()` builds `pieces` (rows and turns) and `pointAt(q)` returns the position and horizontal direction (the tractor is mirrored with `scale(nx, 1)` through the turn).
- **Events:** `bind()` registers `pointerdown` and keyboard `click`; resize/orientation call `layout()`; the keyboard handler covers Enter/Space on the tractor.
- **Cleanup:** the function returned by `mount` cancels the rAF, removes all listeners and the scene node.
- **Persistence/config:** none. **Analytics integration:** none.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The scene is `position: fixed; inset: 0` and measures `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` (fallback `window.innerWidth/innerHeight`).
- **Units:** CSS pixels. Row height `rh = min((H - fieldTop - 8) / 2.85, 0.28·W)`; `fieldTop` is about `0.3·H`, adjusted between `0.2·H` and `H - 2.85·rh - 6`; row centres are at `fieldTop + rh·(i + 0.5)`. Plant size `ps = max(26, min(0.5·rh, 1.6·W/12))`. The loop runs between `xl = tw/2 + rx + 6` and `xr = W - xl` with U-turn radius `rx = 0.35·rh`.
- **Shared space:** tractor, plants, furrows and barn are all positioned in the same pixel space from the same `rowY`/`slotX` values. The tractor's wheels contact the row line at `rh·0.3` below the row centre.
- **Resize/rotation:** `layout()` keeps the tractor's position as a fraction of the loop (`s / Ltot`), rescales the speed to the new width and re-places the plants. A drive to the barn in progress is re-planned.
- **Viewport coverage:** tested sizes are Not currently documented.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Missing assets / invalid config:** not applicable (no external assets or config).
- **Backgrounding:** the rAF loop stops while the tab is hidden and resumes without a time jump.
- **Long frames:** dt is capped at 0.05 s.
- **Rapid input:** tractor taps just re-target the ramp (a tap during a stop ramp restarts the movement from the current speed); wave and wiggle ignore taps while already running.
- **Touch cancel:** only `pointerdown` is used, so cancellation is not relevant.
- **Orientation change:** handled by `layout()`.
- **Unhandled:** browsers without `requestAnimationFrame` are not handled (no fallback).

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#103](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/103) reports `node --check` and a stubbed-DOM simulation (fill, fade, restart in 90 s and parking at the barn) and states that the manual device check in portrait and landscape was still pending; PR [#153](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/153) reports `node --check` and that the SVGs parse as XML.

Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: open Traktor; the tractor is parked and the field is empty; touch it, it accelerates smoothly and crosses the width in about 12 s.
- [ ] Sprouts appear behind the tractor on all three rows and grow into pink flowers, yellow flowers and carrots within about 3 s.
- [ ] Touch the tractor while driving: it slows down over about 2 s and stops; touch again to restart.
- [ ] Completion: let it drive until all 36 plants are grown; after about 1.5 s the plants fade and the field restarts empty.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch empty field, sky and unplanted slots; nothing breaks. Touch the barn while parked; nothing happens.
- [ ] Touch the barn while driving: the tractor drives to the start and parks without reversing abruptly.
- [ ] Touch a plant (wiggle once), the driver (wave) and the driver while the tractor drives.
- [ ] Restart: leave and re-enter; the driver is different from the previous visit (repeat several times).
- [ ] Randomization: open the activity 10 times and note that all six drivers appear and the same one never appears twice in a row.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that nothing changes between rounds and nothing persists after a reload.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape: rotate during driving; the tractor stays on the loop, plants stay on the furrows, nothing is cut off.
- [ ] Touch (phone/tablet) and mouse (desktop); keyboard: Tab to the tractor, barn and driver; Enter and Space work.
- [ ] Background the tab or lock the screen while driving, return: no jump and no double speed.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: the tractor and plants still move and the grown plants are fully visible.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests. Analytics is covered in section 13.
- Plants cannot be reached with the keyboard.
- The activity's motion ignores the reduced-motion preference by design (it is rAF-driven).
- Plant hit boxes (56 px) overlap on narrow screens.

**Requires verification**

- Visual layout on very small or very wide viewports.
- Frame rate on slow devices.

No open issue specifically concerns Traktor; the metrics (#164), visual fixes (#167) and documentation (#168) issues are all merged or in review.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned for this activity.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar vehicle activities: [Autobusik](autobusik.md), [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Mała Łódka](mala-lodka.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md), [Kolejka Linowa](kolejka-linowa.md), [Balon](balon.md).
- Shared helper used: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pickOne`). `js/animals.js` is not used (drivers are drawn locally).
- Shared pattern: a rAF loop with a capped dt, restarted on `visibilitychange`, so motion survives the global reduced-motion rule.

## 21. Change history

- [#91](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/91) / PR [#103](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/103): Traktor activity added.
- [#129](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/129) / PR [#153](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/153): random animal driver (6) and carrot root growing from its stem.
- [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): random animal pools for seven activities (listed in the PR title as touching Traktor).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/ubierz-misia.md`

```markdown
# Ubierz Misia

> Documents the current implementation on `main`. Shared platform behaviour (no sound, global reduced-motion rule, menu configuration, playtime, absence of automated tests, analytics status) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Ubierz Misia |
| Activity ID | `ubierz-misia` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A teddy bear stands in a room with a window. The child changes the weather in the window (sun, rain, snow) and dresses the bear with six clothes. A fitting item gives a happy hop and glow; any other item gives a small head tilt. |
| Category | Sorting / matching (open-ended, no wrong answers) |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop, with a tap-to-select alternative; tap on the window |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/ubierz-misia.js`](../../js/ubierz-misia.js), CSS prefix `um-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity lets a child play with the idea that clothes belong to weather, without testing the child. Every item is accepted for every weather; the only difference is the bear's reaction. It complements the open-ended scenes by adding a drag-and-drop interaction with a gentle, non-judging response.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the scene appears immediately (no fade-in): a bear in a room, a window with sunshine on the left, six clothes in two columns on the right.
2. The child can touch the window to change the weather (sun to rain to snow to sun).
3. The child dresses the bear in one of two ways: drag an item onto the bear, or tap an item (it is highlighted) and then tap the bear.
4. The item glides onto the bear. When it arrives, the bear reacts: a happy hop with a soft glow (2 s) if the item fits the current weather, otherwise a small neutral head tilt (1.4 s).
5. Tapping a worn item takes it off and it glides back to its place on the right.
6. There is no completion state. The child leaves with the Back button.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Item (`id`) | Polish label | Fits weather | Worn position (x, y units) | Home slot (x, y) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sunhat` | kapelusz słoneczny | sun (0) | 165, 110 | 288, 70 |
| `umbrella` | parasol | rain (1) | 222, 184 | 356, 70 |
| `scarf` | szalik | snow (2) | 165, 184 | 288, 150 |
| `boots` | kalosze | rain (1) | 165, 241 | 356, 150 |
| `warmhat` | ciepła czapka | snow (2) | 165, 112 | 288, 230 |
| `sunglasses` | okulary przeciwsłoneczne | sun (0) | 165, 144 | 356, 230 |

- **Weather:** `target` cycles 0, 1, 2 (sun, rain, snow) on each tap of the window; each weather layer eases in or out over 3 s (`WEATHER_S`). Rain has 10 falling streaks and snow 10 flakes (fixed pools); particles are not animated under reduced motion.
- **Reaction rule:** when a worn item finishes gliding onto the bear, its `fits` value is compared with the current weather `target` (not the partially faded display). Equal gives `happy` (2000 ms, `HAPPY_MS`: glow plus two 6-unit hops), otherwise `neutral` (1400 ms, `NEUTRAL_MS`: 5-degree tilt around the feet pivot at 165, 258).
- **Drop zone:** the bear rectangle x 95-235, y 100-275 expanded by 18 units. Dropping elsewhere glides the item home.
- **Glide time:** `min(1200, 600 + distance_px * 0.8)` ms; 300 ms when reduced motion is requested.
- **Dragging:** only unworn items can be dragged; the item centre is clamped to the visible screen.
- **Hat exclusivity:** `wear()` is meant to send the other hat home when a hat is put on (it compares the worn `wx`/`wy` of two items). See section 18: the two hats have different `wy`, so the check never matches today.
- **No wrong answers:** every item can be worn in any weather, any number of items can be worn together, and nothing is scored or stored.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**: connecting weather with fitting clothes, hand-eye coordination through dragging, cause and effect (weather, clothes, bear reaction), calm independent play.

**Directly observable behavior**
- The bear always reacts to a worn item, differently for fitting and non-fitting items, but never negatively (no angry or sad expression exists).
- The window visibly changes sky, ground and particles.
- A keyboard or tap-tap alternative to dragging exists.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**
- Whether children learn which clothes suit which weather from this activity.
- Whether the difference between hop and tilt is noticeable to young children.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse and stylus via pointer events on the items (`touch-action: none` on items so dragging does not scroll); `touch-action: manipulation` on the window and bear buttons. Keyboard: items are buttons (`aria-pressed`, label ends with "Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz misia"), the bear is a button ("Miś (wybierz ubranie, potem miś)") and the window is a button ("Okno: zmień pogodę"), all with a 4px focus outline.
- **Target size:** items are `max(56px, 15% of the board width)` square; the window and bear buttons cover the drawn window (33% x 40% of the board) and the bear (35% x 58%).
- **Orientation:** one 4:3 board scaled to fit; portrait just gives a smaller board.
- **Colour:** the item drawings differ in shape (hat, umbrella, scarf, boots, hat, glasses); weather is conveyed by the picture (sun, drops, flakes), not by colour alone. Fit is not shown by colour.
- **Reading:** none; labels are for assistive technology.
- **Sound:** none.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop and the code reads `prefers-reduced-motion` itself (`reduced()`): under reduced motion rain and snow stay still, the happy hop and tilt are dropped (only the glow remains for the happy reaction; neutral shows no movement), and glides last 300 ms. Weather colour cross-fades (3 s) still run.
- **Limitations:** the current weather and which items are worn are not announced to assistive technology; the window label does not name the current weather.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Multi-touch: up to six items can be dragged at once (each tracks its own pointer); the PR reports a multi-pointer test in a stub only.
- Items can overlap on the bear (no layering rules besides the hat check) and both hats can currently be worn together (section 18).
- An item dropped over the bear always counts as worn, even if the child only meant to move it.
- No ending; the activity can be played indefinitely.
- Privacy: nothing is stored or transmitted.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in `js/ubierz-misia.js`.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Changeable without code change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ITEMS` | Clothes: id, label, `fits`, worn position, SVG art | array | 6 entries | No |
| `HOME_X`, `HOME_Y` | Home slots (units) | arrays | [288, 356], [70, 150, 230] | No |
| `BEAR_RECT`, margin 18 | Drop zone (units) | object | x 95-235, y 100-275 | No |
| `BX`, `PIVOT_Y` | Bear centre x and tilt pivot | numbers | 165, 258 | No |
| `WEATHER_S` | Weather change duration (s) | number | 3 | No |
| `HAPPY_MS`, `NEUTRAL_MS` | Reaction durations (ms) | numbers | 2000, 1400 | No |
| `SKY`, `GROUND` | Colours per weather (sun, rain, snow) | RGB arrays | see source | No |

There is no fallback for invalid values; the constants are not user-editable.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The room, window, bear, six items (`ITEMS[].art`, 100x100 viewBox each) and weather particles are inline SVG built in `js/ubierz-misia.js`. A single CSS rule enlarges worn boots (`.um-item[data-id='boots'].um-worn svg { transform: scale(1.4) }`, added so the boots fit the bear's feet, PR #155). The expression `def.art.replace('', '')` in the code has no effect.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Nothing is randomized. The weather always starts as sun and cycles in a fixed order; items always start in the same home slots.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression, levels or difficulty. State (weather, worn items) is not persisted; each launch starts with sun and no clothes worn.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no completion state and no failure. Feedback: item selection outline, glide of the item, bear reaction (happy hop and glow, or head tilt), weather transition. No sound.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** IIFE in [`js/ubierz-misia.js`](../../js/ubierz-misia.js) overriding `mount` for `ubierz-misia`.
- **Rendering:** one SVG (400x300 viewBox, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`) for room, window, bear and weather; two transparent hit buttons (window, bear) and six item `<button>` elements positioned over it with CSS `transform: translate(...)`.
- **State:** `target` and `wts[3]` (weather weights), `pose` and `react` (bear reaction), per item `{x, y, worn, mode ('idle' | 'drag' | 'glide'), pending, ...}`, `selected`.
- **Events:** pointer events (`pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`) with pointer capture on each item; `click` for select, take off, wear (via bear) and weather; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with capped dt (50 ms) that runs only while something moves and stops while the tab is hidden.
- **Coordinates:** all positions are stored in board units and converted with `k = boardWidth / 400`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the window listeners and removes the root.
- **Shared helpers:** none (`Rand` and `Animals` are not used).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board: `aspect-ratio: 4 / 3`, `width: min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 4 / 3)`, inside a container with 56px top padding and safe-area insets.
- Coordinate space: 400 x 300 units for the SVG and for item positions; `layout()` measures the board and recomputes `k` and the item size `S = max(56, 0.15 * width)` on mount, resize and orientation change.
- On resize any item being dragged is cancelled and glides home; idle items are re-placed (worn items follow the bear).
- Hit areas for the window and bear are percentages of the board, so they stay aligned with the drawing.
- Drag is clamped so an item centre stays inside the viewport.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Resize or orientation during a drag:** the drag is cancelled and the item returns home.
- **Pointer cancel / lost capture:** handled as release (`up`).
- **Rapid input:** a short suppression (60 ms) prevents the click after a drag from also selecting the item; extra pointers on an item already being dragged are ignored; secondary mouse buttons are ignored.
- **Backgrounding:** the loop is cancelled while hidden and restarted on return.
- **Synthetic pointers:** `setPointerCapture` is wrapped in `try/catch`.
- **Unhandled:** the hat exclusivity check (section 18); no handling of an unexpected missing `ACTIVITIES` entry beyond skipping the override.

## 17. Testing

There are no automated tests. Manual scenarios to perform:

- [ ] Tap the window repeatedly: sun, rain, snow, sun, each fading over about 3 s.
- [ ] Drag each item onto the bear: it glides on; a fitting item (see table in section 4) gives hop and glow, a non-fitting one a tilt.
- [ ] Change the weather while an item is gliding and check which reaction occurs on arrival.
- [ ] Tap an item, then tap the bear: same result as dragging; tap the item again to deselect.
- [ ] Drop an item away from the bear: it returns home. Tap a worn item: it returns home.
- [ ] Wear both hats at once and confirm what is shown (see section 18).
- [ ] Reload or leave and re-enter: weather is sun and nothing is worn.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape, and rotate while dragging.
- [ ] Touch (phone/tablet, including two fingers on two items), mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space).
- [ ] Switch tab during a reaction and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: rain and snow static, no hop or tilt, glow still shown for fitting items.
- [ ] Browsers required by the README: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#73](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/73) reports `node --check` and a Node stub-DOM run (drag onto bear, take-off, six-item multi-pointer run, cleanup leaves no nodes); it lists the manual device tests as pending. PR [#155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155) reports that the boots fix was verified by reasoning from the geometry only.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from the code)**
- Hat exclusivity does not work: `wear()` returns another item only when both `wx` and `wy` are equal, but `sunhat` has `wy: 110` and `warmhat` has `wy: 112`, so both hats can be worn at the same time and overlap. The commit that added the check ("wearing a hat returns the other hat home") intended otherwise.
- No automated tests; manual tests were pending when the PRs were opened.
- Weather and worn state are not announced to assistive technology.

**Requires verification**
- Visual overlap of several worn items (umbrella, scarf, boots, glasses) on small boards.
- Behaviour with several simultaneous touches on real devices.

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar drag-and-select interaction with a keyboard alternative: [Cienie](cienie.md).
- Weather/sky scenes: [Deszczyk i Tęcza](deszczyk-i-tecza.md), [Dzień i Noc](dzien-i-noc.md) (thematic only; no shared code).
- No shared helpers are used (`js/random.js` and `js/animals.js` are not referenced).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#61](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/61) / PR [#73](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/73): activity added.
- Review follow-up on PR #73: wearing a hat returns the other hat home (not effective, see section 18).
- Issue [#130](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/130) / PR [#155](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/155): bear boots fit the feet.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/wedkowanie.md`

```markdown
# Wędkowanie

Status: implemented

- Issue: [#219](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/219)
- Planned activity id: `wedkowanie`
- Planned CSS prefix: `wd-`

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Wędkowanie |
| Activity ID | `wedkowanie` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), appended last) |
| Description | An animal fisher on a jetty: holding a finger lowers a hook into a pond, releasing pulls it up with a catch (fish, boot, star or bottle) that goes into a bucket. |
| Category | Cause and effect; hold and release; calming |
| Interaction type | Press and hold anywhere, keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/wedkowanie.js`](../../js/wedkowanie.js), styles with prefix `wd-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A hold-and-release mechanic; no other activity uses it ([Akwarium Artura](akwarium-artura.md) and [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md) are touch-to-watch scenes); issue [#219](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/219).

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile: a jetty on the left with a random animal fisher and a red bucket, a pond with six slowly swimming fish and toys.
2. Holding a finger anywhere lowers the hook; releasing pulls it up.
3. While the hook is down, a swimmer within 56 px latches on. If nothing latched, the nearest swimmer of an allowed kind is drawn to the hook when the finger is released, so every pull-up brings one catch.
4. The catch swings on the hook; at the surface it flies into the bucket in 1.5 s and a new swimmer enters from an edge.
5. After five catches the fisher hops (0.8 s), the bucket glows for 3 s, the bucket empties and the pond is refilled with a new random set. The play repeats without end. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Hook speed | 25% of the pond depth per second down and up; maximum depth 90%. |
| Latch | Any swimmer within 56 px of the hook while it is down and the finger is held. |
| Catch kinds | Fish (random colour), boot, star, bottle with a small heart; the kind that was caught twice in a row is skipped (not latched, not pulled) so no kind appears three times in a row. |
| Swimmers | Six at a time, at most 15% of the screen width per second (0.05-0.12 used), at least three kinds present; leaving swimmers are replaced by random new ones. |
| Set | Five catches in the bucket: hop, 3 s glow, new pond (old swimmers fade out and re-roll). |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Text, sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Holding and letting go on purpose; cause and effect of a held touch.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The hook goes down while the finger stays down and up when it is released; each pull-up shows one picture that ends in the bucket.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events on the whole stage; the touch area is the full screen. A second pointer is ignored while the first is down.
- **Keyboard:** Tab to the rod button (at least 56 px, visible focus ring); Enter or Space held lowers the hook, released raises it (key repeat ignored; losing focus releases).
- **Label (Polish):** "Wędka. Przytrzymaj Enter lub spację, żeby opuścić haczyk, puść, żeby go podciągnąć."; the SVG is decorative.
- **Non-colour cues:** all four catch kinds differ by shape; colour is only decoration on fish.
- The Back button area (top-left) is above the pond and the bucket.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- No renderer was available while writing the code: layout was checked by arithmetic and a scripted simulation, not by looking at it on a device.

## 8. Configuration

None; nothing is stored.

## 9. Assets

All pictures are inline SVG drawn in code (the fisher is a random head from `window.Animals`, bear, rabbit, cat or dog).

## 10. Randomization and variants

Random fisher animal per launch; random kind, colour, direction, speed and depth of each swimmer; the same catch kind never occurs three times in a row.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A set of five catches: fisher hop and bucket glow (3 s, a smooth fade, no flashing), then a new pond.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

- `track('interaction', { variant })` once per lowering, when the finger is released, with the catch kind (`fish`, `boot`, `star`, `bottle`) as variant.
- `complete()` when the fifth catch reaches the bucket. Nothing is stored beyond the shared module's aggregates.

## 14. Technical implementation

One SVG scene updated every frame by a single capped-dt `requestAnimationFrame` loop (paused while the tab is hidden). It deliberately keeps running while the tab is visible: the swimmers always drift, so there is never a resting state to idle in; everything is set from JS, so reduced motion does not hide any state. The root is attached with `container.appendChild(root)` before `layout()`; the returned cleanup removes the listeners, the loop and the root.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

The pond starts at 40% of the height; unit sizes derive from min(width, 1.4 x height); the hook column sits right of the fisher; the jetty and bucket are on the left. Rotation re-runs `layout()` and keeps all state.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

Rotation or resize, hidden tab, very fast repeated taps (every release still brings one catch), second finger (ignored), pointer cancel (treated as release), blur during a key hold (released).

## 17. Testing

No automated tests in the repository. Manual scenarios:

1. Hold on the pond: the hook sinks about 25% of the pond depth per second and stops at 90%; release: it rises at the same speed.
2. Hold until a swimmer is within 56 px: it hangs on the hook and swings.
3. Tap very briefly: the release still brings one catch.
4. Pull up five catches: the fisher hops, the bucket glows about 3 s, the bucket empties, a new pond appears.
5. Watch ten catches: no kind three times in a row.
6. Keyboard: Tab to the rod, hold Enter/Space, release.
7. Rotate in the middle of a pull-up: the scene keeps its state.
8. Put a second finger down while holding: nothing breaks.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

- A swimmer drawn to the hook on release moves faster than the normal swim speed (a short 0.5 s glide).

## 19. Planned improvements

None.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

[Akwarium Artura](akwarium-artura.md), [Łódź Podwodna](lodz-podwodna.md); `window.Animals`.

## 21. Change history

- Implemented for issue [#219](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/219).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/wiatraczki.md`

```markdown
# Wiatraczki

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Wiatraczki |
| Activity ID | `wiatraczki` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A pastel meadow with nine pinwheels of different colours, heights and centre shapes, grass and a windsock. Touching a pinwheel spins it; sliding a finger across the meadow makes a soft gust. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, exploratory |
| Interaction type | Tap (pinwheels), slide/swipe (gust) |
| Status | Implemented; **disabled in the menu by default** (`defaultOff: true`). A parent enables it in the gated Settings; see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour). |

Source: [`js/wiatraczki.js`](../../js/wiatraczki.js), CSS prefix `wi-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html). Introduced by issue #100 / PR [#170](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/170).

## 2. Business purpose

- A pure cause-and-effect scene with two ways to act: a precise touch on one pinwheel, and a sweeping gesture that sets several pinwheels spinning as a wave.
- Every pinwheel has its own colour and centre shape, so they are distinguishable without relying on colour alone.
- Complements [Karuzela](karuzela.md) (also a rotation that the child starts and stops) and [Latawiec](latawiec.md) (also reacts to a finger moving across the scene).
- It ships disabled by default; the reason is not documented in the code or PR description (`Not currently documented`).

## 3. Activity flow

1. A parent enables the activity in Settings; the child opens the tile; `mount(container)` builds the scene. The loop is not running yet.
2. All nine pinwheels are at rest; the windsock hangs down and the grass is still.
3. The child can tap a pinwheel or slide a finger over the meadow.
4. A tapped pinwheel spins up and rests after about 6 s. A sliding finger spins pinwheels near its path (nearer ones stronger and sooner), and the windsock and grass lean in the direction of the slide.
5. There is no completion state.
6. Everything settles by itself; the loop stops when all motion has ended.
7. A new scene starts each time the activity is opened.
8. The child leaves with the Back button.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Per-pinwheel state | `level` (0..1, the spin it is heading for) and `omega` (actual speed). `level` decays linearly at `DECAY` = 0.7 / 6 per second; `omega` eases toward `level` with rate 2.4 per second. Speed in turns per second = `OMAX` (1) x `omega`, never negative and never above 1. |
| Tap on a resting pinwheel | `level` = `TOUCH_LVL` = 0.7; it rests again after about 6 s (plus easing). |
| Tap on a spinning pinwheel (`level` or `omega` above 0.05) | `level` += `PUSH` = 0.12, capped at 1. |
| Gust | While a pointer is pressed and moving, the path since the last move is sampled every `STEP` = 10 units (at most 40 samples per event). A pinwheel within `RADIUS` = 90 units of a sample gets a candidate level `GUST_MAX` x (1 - d/90) with `GUST_MAX` = 0.55 (so at most 0.55). Candidates below 0.04, or not above the current or already pending level, are ignored. The kick is applied after a delay of d / `WAVE_V` seconds (`WAVE_V` = 200 units/s) and only raises `level` to a maximum, never adds. |
| Wind | Every move sets `wind` to at least 0.85; it decays linearly over `WIND_T` = 5 s. `dir` is the sign of the last horizontal movement. A smoothed signed wind `sg` follows `dir * wind` (rate 2.5 per s). |
| Windsock | Rotates by `-sg * 75` degrees about its pole top (28, 40), plus a flutter of up to 4 degrees. |
| Grass | The grass layer is skewed by `sg * 8` plus a small oscillation (up to 3 degrees). |
| Pinwheels | Head positions (x, y) and stem lengths: (100, 62, 52), (215, 56, 58), (330, 66, 50), (125, 142, 46), (240, 148, 44), (355, 138, 48), (100, 222, 50), (215, 216, 54), (330, 226, 48). Each head has four blades (two coloured, two white) of radius about 25 units. |
| Colours / centre shapes | Pink, yellow, blue, purple, mint, peach, green, lilac, turquoise; centres: circle, square, triangle, diamond, star, hexagon, plus, droplet, pentagon. |

No sound, scoring, failure or retry. Pinwheel spin direction is always clockwise (angle only increases).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect between a touch or a sliding gesture and the response.
- Calm observation of slowly spinning shapes and a wave of motion.
- Distinguishing shapes and colours (each pinwheel is unique).

**Directly observable behavior**

- Spin speed is capped at one turn per second and changes smoothly.
- Gust strength depends on distance, with a delay proportional to distance, producing a wave effect.
- The windsock and grass follow the last gust direction and settle.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on fine motor skills, attention or colour/shape learning is not established by the code and is not claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events on the whole scene for gusts (touch, mouse, stylus; first pointer only); `click` on nine `<button>`s for taps, so keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space) works for taps. The sliding gust has no keyboard equivalent.
- **Targets:** each pinwheel button is `max(56, 50k)` px square, centred on the head; the nearest pinwheel centres are 80-115 board units apart (PR [#170](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/170) reports a minimum centre distance of 58 px at the narrowest layout, k = 0.8).
- **Labels:** each button has `aria-label` such as "Wiatraczek 1 – różowy, zakręć" (colour name in Polish); the scene SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible` outline 4px `#8f7fd1`.
- **Orientation:** the board keeps its 400:300 ratio and is sized `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 400/300)`; works in portrait (smaller) and landscape.
- **Colour:** each pinwheel also has a unique centre shape; no task depends on colour.
- **Reduced motion:** motion is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop and is not disabled by the global rule. A one-turn-per-second spin is the maximum; there is no separate reduced-motion variant.
- **Reading:** none required; a young child can use it independently.
- **Limitations:** `touch-action: none` on the scene; the gust cannot be triggered from the keyboard.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Rotating blades with white and coloured quarters at up to one turn per second could look flickery on some displays; the speed cap is deliberate. No flashing is implemented.
- Ten or so quick sliding gestures keep many pinwheels spinning; the cap prevents growth beyond 1 turn/s but several spinning at once increases visual motion.
- On a 320 px wide portrait screen the targets are close (see section 6); not verified on a real device.
- Disabled by default, so children will not see it unless a parent enables it.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in [`js/wiatraczki.js`](../../js/wiatraczki.js) and require a code change. The only runtime-configurable aspect is whether the activity is enabled in the menu (menu-config, stored in `localStorage`; default off through `defaultOff`). Nothing else is stored.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BW` x `BH` | 400 x 300 | Board units |
| `OMAX` | 1 turn/s | Maximum spin |
| `TOUCH_LVL` | 0.7 | Level after a tap on a resting pinwheel |
| `PUSH` | 0.12 | Level added by a tap on a spinning pinwheel |
| `DECAY` | 0.7 / 6 per s | Level decay (a single tap rests in about 6 s) |
| `GUST_MAX`, `RADIUS`, `WAVE_V` | 0.55, 90 units, 200 units/s | Gust strength, reach, wave speed |
| `STEP` | 10 units | Sampling step along the finger path |
| `WIND_T` | 5 s | Wind decay time |
| `COLS`, `NAMES`, `CENTRES`, `PW` | 9 entries each | Colours, Polish colour names, centre shapes, head positions and stem lengths |
| `SOCK_X`, `SOCK_Y` | 28, 40 | Windsock pole top |
| `MAX_DT` | 0.05 s | Frame time cap |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Sky, hills, windsock, grass, stems and pinwheels are inline SVG built by `scene()`; each pinwheel's centre shape is a small inline path. This activity does not use [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Nothing is randomized: colours, centre shapes, positions and stem lengths are fixed, and the same scene appears on every visit.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression or levels. Spin state is transient and not stored.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- No completion state; open-ended.
- Feedback is visual only: spinning pinwheels, wave-like start, windsock and grass motion.
- No failure; no sound; the loop stops by itself when all motion has ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` assigned to the registry entry `wiatraczki`; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** one SVG (`viewBox 0 0 400 300`) inside `.wi-board` with groups `.wi-spin` (one per pinwheel, rotated each frame), `.wi-sock` and `.wi-grass`; nine transparent buttons overlay the heads for taps and accessibility.
- **State:** per pinwheel `{ ang, omega, level, pendAt, pendLvl }`; global `time`, `wind`, `dir`, `sg`; pointer `pid`, `px`, `py`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`/`paint`) with capped dt, started by `start()` on a tap or gust and stopped when `active()` is false and no pointer is held; paused while `document.hidden` and resumed only if still active.
- **Events:** `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel` on the root (coordinates via `getBoundingClientRect`), `click` on pinwheel buttons, `resize`/`orientationchange` call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes window/document listeners and removes the root node.
- **Dependencies:** none other than the registry. No persistence or analytics integration. See [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board 400 x 300 units, scale `k = board.clientWidth / 400`; the scene, pinwheels and gesture sampling all use board units, so the gust radius scales with the board.
- Pointer positions are converted to board units with the current bounding rectangle.
- Pinwheel buttons are placed at head position times `k` with a minimum size of 56 px.
- The grass is skewed about the bottom edge of the board (`translate(0 300) skewX(...) translate(0 -300)`).
- All pinwheels stay inside the board in any orientation (only the board scales).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/orientation change: `layout()` repositions the buttons; pinwheel state continues.
- Backgrounding: loop cancelled while hidden; restarted only if there is still motion; dt capped at 0.05 s.
- Rapid repeated input: levels only ever rise to a maximum (gust) or by a small capped push (tap), so speed stays at or below 1 turn/s; the number of samples per move event is capped at 40.
- Touch cancellation: `pointercancel` ends the gesture like release.
- Second finger: ignored while a pointer is active.
- Pointer capture is not used, so a gesture that leaves the board continues to be tracked only while events reach the root (see section 18).
- Missing assets / empty pools: not applicable (inline SVG).

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#170](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/170) reports `node --check` and a node stub-DOM simulation (single tap peak 0.57 turn/s, rest after about 6.3 s, repeated taps maximum 0.85, gust reaches near pinwheels and not far ones, loop stops once idle, windsock returns to 0) and states it was not checked in a real browser or on a device.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Enable Wiatraczki in the parent-gated Settings; confirm the tile appears and the activity opens. With it disabled, confirm the tile is absent.
- [ ] Normal: tap a pinwheel; it spins up smoothly (at most one turn per second) and rests after about 6 s.
- [ ] Tap a spinning pinwheel; it speeds up slightly, never above one turn per second.
- [ ] Gust: slide a finger slowly across several pinwheels; nearer ones spin more strongly and a little earlier; far ones (more than about 90 units away) do not move.
- [ ] Slide left-to-right, then right-to-left; the windsock and grass lean in the direction of the last slide and settle within about 5 s.
- [ ] Fast back-and-forth sliding; spin speed stays within the cap and nothing flickers.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no end state and the loop stops when everything is still (check CPU).
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the sky or grass; nothing happens (only sliding creates a gust).
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and re-enter; all pinwheels are at rest.
- [ ] Randomization: confirm the scene is identical on each visit.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape on phone and tablet, including a 320 px wide portrait screen; targets stay at least 56 px and do not overlap.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard Tab and Enter/Space on each pinwheel.
- [ ] Background the tab while pinwheels spin and return.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: pinwheels still spin.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; no documented real-device verification.
- Disabled by default; the reason is not documented.
- The gust gesture has no keyboard alternative.
- Pointer capture is not used on the scene, so `pointerup` outside the browser window may not be received.

**Requires verification**

- Whether a gesture released outside the window leaves the loop running until the next pointer event (`pid` stays set until a `pointerup`/`pointercancel` reaches the root).
- Visual comfort of white-and-coloured blades at the maximum speed on real displays.

No open GitHub issue targets this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar scenes: [Latawiec](latawiec.md) (finger-following), [Karuzela](karuzela.md) (touch-started rotation), [Zegar z Kukułką](zegar-z-kukulka.md) (several independent touch targets).
- Shared components: none specific; `js/animals.js` and `js/random.js` are not used. It follows the common pattern of one capped-dt `requestAnimationFrame` loop paused on `visibilitychange`.
- Menu default-off behaviour: `defaultOff` in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js) and [`js/menu-config.js`](../../js/menu-config.js).

## 21. Change history

- Issue #100, PR [#170](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/170): activity added (commit 58b0fb0), shipped with `defaultOff: true`.

```
