## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/wieza-z-klockow.md`

```markdown
# Wieża z Klocków

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Wieża z Klocków |
| Internal ID | `wieza` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | 5 to 9 soft pastel blocks wait at the bottom (portrait) or on one side (landscape). The child drags them onto a tower base in any order; each settles on top with a tiny sway, and the tower can never fall. |
| Category | Open-ended play / coordination (building) |
| Interaction type | Drag (pointer events); keyboard alternative (select a block, then activate the tower) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/wieza.js`](../../js/wieza.js), CSS block `/* Wieża z Klocków */` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (prefix `wk`) |

## 2. Business purpose

A gentle building game designed so that failure is impossible: blocks are stacked in any order, the tower never collapses, and a block released elsewhere just drifts back. This gives the child the satisfaction of building without the frustration of a falling tower, which a physical block tower can cause. It is the least rule-bound of the drag activities (no correct order, no matching), which distinguishes it from [Puzzle](puzzle.md) and the sorting activities ([Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md), [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md)). The number and colours of the blocks vary on every launch.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity (`#wieza`); a set of 5 to 9 blocks is generated and laid out.
2. A flat base is shown (centred in the upper area in portrait, in the left half in landscape); the blocks wait in a grid of three columns at the bottom or in the right half.
3. The child drags a block. It follows the pointer and cannot leave the visible screen.
4. Released over or near the tower column and above the base, the block glides to the top of the stack, is centred, and the whole tower sways for about 1.2 s.
5. Released elsewhere, the block drifts back to its waiting place; it can be picked up again.
6. When all blocks are stacked the top block glows for 3 s.
7. At 7 s after completion all blocks drift back to their starting places and the tower can be built again with the same blocks.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (from `js/wieza.js`) |
|---|---|
| Block count | 5 to 9 (`MIN_BLOCKS`, `MAX_BLOCKS`), chosen once per launch |
| Order of stacking | Any: blocks are added to the stack in the order they are dropped |
| Accept area | Block centre within `max(1.8 * Ut, 0.7 * tw)` horizontally of the tower axis and above the base (`y < by + 2`), where `Ut` is the stacked unit and `tw` the base width |
| Wrong drop | Block glides back to its waiting place |
| Placed blocks | Disabled (not draggable); scaled by `sc = Ut / U` and centred on the tower axis |
| Sway | `SWAY_S = 1.2` s, amplitude `SWAY_DEG = 2` degrees, damped (`exp(-t / 0.45)`), period 0.8 s, rigid rotation of the whole stack about the base; not applied with reduced motion |
| Glide duration | `min(1500, 700 + distance * 0.8)` ms; 300 ms with reduced motion; 200 ms for re-layout glides |
| Glow | `GLOW_S = 3000` ms on the top block only |
| Reset | `RESET_S = 7000` ms after completion |
| Failure | None; the tower cannot fall and nothing is ever lost |
| Sound | None ([shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)) |

- Keyboard: Enter or Space (a `click` with `detail === 0`) on a block selects it (`aria-pressed`, outline); activating the "Wieża" button stacks it. Placed blocks leave the tab order.
- Block geometry (width x height in block units): 9 shapes from 0.8 x 0.8 up to 1.6 x 0.8; two are "daszek" (roof, triangle) shapes. Any block can be placed under or over any other (including roofs in the middle of the stack).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (design intent, not measured):
- Hand-eye coordination and controlled dragging.
- Free constructive play without a wrong order.
- Cause and effect (a block placed makes the tower sway slightly).

**Directly observable behavior:**
- Blocks settle centred on the stack regardless of where they were dropped.
- The tower only sways a little and always recovers.
- When complete, only the top block glows.
- No scores, timers or error messages.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about motor skill, spatial reasoning or developmental effect.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) with pointer capture and `touch-action: none`; keyboard alternative as above with a 4 px outline (`#8f7fd1`).
- **Screen readers:** blocks are labelled "Klocek: <colour> <shape> (Enter lub spacja, potem wybierz wieżę)", for example "różowy kwadrat"; the tower button is labelled "Wieża"; `aria-pressed` marks the selection. The stack order is not announced.
- **Target size:** the block unit `U` is floored at 70 px (maximum 84 px) so that every waiting block is at least 56 px wide and high (smallest block 0.8 units = 56 px). Stacked blocks are scaled to fit the tower height and may be smaller (section 18).
- **Orientation:** portrait places the waiting grid at the bottom, landscape in the right half with the tower in the left half; recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`.
- **Colour:** colours are decorative; blocks also differ by shape and size, but no decision depends on colour.
- **Reduced motion:** movement and glow are driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with inline styles, so they still run under the global CSS rule; with `prefers-reduced-motion` the sway is skipped and glides shorten to 300 ms.
- **Reading:** none required.
- **Limitations:** the tower area is a single large invisible button; the blocks' vertical order is only visual.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- On short screens, stacked blocks shrink to fit the whole tower; PR [#78](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/78) noted about 47 px on a 360x640 landscape phone and asked for a human check.
- With 9 blocks (three rows) in short landscape the waiting area may be tight; PR [#148](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/148) asked the reviewer to check it.
- Slight sway of the stack may be noticeable; it is limited to 2 degrees and 1.2 s and is skipped with reduced motion.
- No privacy concerns; nothing stored or sent.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants are inside [`js/wieza.js`](../../js/wieza.js).

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SHAPES` | 9 block shapes (noun, width, height in units, `rect` or `roof`) | array | 9 entries | top of IIFE |
| `PALETTE` | 10 pastel colours with Polish names | array | 10 entries | top of IIFE |
| `MIN_BLOCKS`, `MAX_BLOCKS` | Range of the random block count | numbers | 5, 9 | top of IIFE |
| `GLOW_S` | Top-block glow duration | ms | 3000 | top of IIFE |
| `RESET_S` | Time from completion to the blocks returning | ms | 7000 | top of IIFE |
| `SWAY_S`, `SWAY_DEG` | Sway duration (s) and amplitude (degrees) | numbers | 1.2, 2 | top of IIFE |
| Layout numbers | `U` clamp 70-84, waiting grid 3 columns, base height 12 px, `Ut <= 1.25 * U` | numbers | see `layout()` | `layout()` |

No fallback for invalid values because nothing is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external files. Blocks are inline SVG (`blockSvg`): a rounded square (`rect`) or a rounded triangle (`roof`) with a small highlight, stretched to the block's width and height (`preserveAspectRatio="none"`, `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`). The base is a CSS rounded bar (`#d9c9ea`), the background a CSS gradient (`#f3eefb` to `#fdf0d5`). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, images or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | How | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| Number of blocks | `5 + floor(Math.random() * 5)` once per launch | 5 to 9 |
| Shapes | `Rand.pick(SHAPES, n)`: unique shapes | 9 shapes |
| Colours | `Rand.pick(PALETTE, n)`: unique colours, so no colour repeats within a tower | 10 colours |

- Block set persists for the visit (reset only returns the blocks to their waiting places; it does not reshuffle or change them). A new set is generated each time the activity is opened. Nothing is stored.
- The waiting positions follow the block order (`i % 3`, `floor(i / 3)`); they are not shuffled.
- Pools are fixed arrays; `n` never exceeds the pool sizes (9 shapes, 10 colours).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. Only the random block count (5 to 9) differs between launches; it does not grow within a visit. Nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion: all blocks stacked and idle (`stack.length === BLOCKS.length`).
- Feedback: the top block glows (yellow drop-shadow `#ffe08a`, eased in about 400 ms) for 3 s. Each placement shows a small sway of the tower.
- Failure: none. No sound.
- After 7 s the blocks glide back to their waiting places and play can repeat.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/wieza.js`](../../js/wieza.js), replacing `mount` of the `wieza` registry entry; returns `cleanup`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `div.wk > div.wk-field` with a `div.wk-base`, one `button.wk-tower` (invisible tower area) and one `button.wk-block` per block, each with inline SVG. Elements are moved with `transform: translate() rotate() scale()`.
- **State:** `BLOCKS` (from `makeBlocks()`), `stack` (ordered placed blocks), per block `{ b, i, W, H, x, y, hx/hy (home), tx/ty (stack target), s (scale), mode, placed }`; `swayT`, `doneActive`, `doneT`, `glow`.
- **Stacking:** `stackTargets()` computes each stacked block's centre from the base upwards (`top -= h`), so the stack is always contiguous and centred.
- **Events:** `pointerdown/move/up/cancel`, `lostpointercapture` per block; `click` on blocks (keyboard) and on the tower; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Animation:** one `frame()` loop (dt capped at 50 ms), smoothstep glides; sway applied in `place()` by rotating placed blocks' positions about the base; stops when idle; paused while hidden.
- **Dependencies:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`). **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** none from the activity itself (reported by `js/app.js`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the three listeners and the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.wk` is fixed full-screen; `.wk-field` is inset by the safe-area variables plus 64 px at the top and 12 px elsewhere. All coordinates are CSS pixels relative to the field.
- Portrait (`fh >= fw`): waiting grid across the full width at the bottom (`rows = ceil(n / 3)`), `U = clamp(min(fw / 3 / 1.7, 0.13 fh), 70, 84)`; the tower area is everything above it (`th0 = wy0 - 8`).
- Landscape: the waiting grid fills the right half, vertically centred, `U = clamp(min(fw / 2 / 3 / 1.7, fh / rows / 1.2), 70, 84)`; the tower area is the left half.
- The stacked unit `Ut = min(1.25 U, (th0 - 12 - 4) / totalU)` where `totalU` is the sum of the block heights, so the whole tower always fits; `sc = Ut / U` scales placed blocks. The base is centred in the tower area (`bx`), `by` is just above the base; the tower button spans `1.2 * tw` wide (`tw = max(2.2 * Ut, 80)`).
- Blocks, base and tower area share the field's pixel space; resize and rotation re-run `layout()` and cancel active drags.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | N/A (inline SVG); `Rand` is required and not guarded |
| Resize / rotation | `layout()` re-run; active drag cancelled and block sent home; placed blocks follow the new targets |
| Backgrounding | Loop paused while hidden; completion timers advance only while visible |
| Multi-touch | Each block tracks its own pointer; a second pointer on the same block is ignored |
| Pointer cancel / lost capture | Treated as release |
| Same block snapped twice | `snap` returns early if the block is already placed or in the stack |
| Dragging outside the screen | Centre clamped to the visible window |
| Right mouse button | Ignored |
| Not enough height | `Ut` shrinks so the tower fits; stacked blocks can become smaller than 56 px (section 18) |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` cancels the frame |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#78](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/78) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM run of the keyboard flow (stack all blocks, glow, reset, three times); PR [#148](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/148) reports `node --check` and a node harness over 2000 launches (counts only 5 to 9, colours always unique), without a visual check. The scripts are not in the repository. Manual checklist (not yet performed):

- [ ] Normal: drag a block onto the tower; it settles on top, centred, and the tower sways briefly.
- [ ] Stack blocks in different orders; the tower is always contiguous and never falls.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: release a block far from the tower; it drifts back and can be picked up again.
- [ ] Completion: stack all blocks; only the top glows for about 3 s; after about 7 s all blocks return.
- [ ] Restart: leave and reopen several times; the block count (5 to 9), shapes and colours change and no colour repeats within a tower.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that nothing changes between rounds.
- [ ] Portrait (about 360x640): waiting grid at the bottom, with 9 blocks (three rows) still fully visible; tower fits above.
- [ ] Landscape (about 640x360): tower left, waiting blocks right; with 9 blocks check that nothing overlaps and measure the stacked block size (PR #78 reported about 47 px on a short screen).
- [ ] Rotate the device mid-drag and with a partly built tower.
- [ ] Touch: two fingers dragging two blocks; mouse: left-button drag.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to a block, Enter selects, Enter on "Wieża" stacks it.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: no sway, short glides, glow still shown.
- [ ] Background the tab during the glow and return.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from code reading):**
- No automated tests.
- Stacked blocks are scaled down to fit the tower and can become smaller than the 56 px target size on short screens (acknowledged in PR #78).
- Any block can go anywhere in the stack, including roof shapes in the middle (no stability logic by design).
- The set of blocks is fixed for the whole visit.
- The shape pool (9) is not reduced for tower height; a stack of nine blocks has total height 7.8 units at most.

**Requires verification:**
- Fit of three waiting rows with 9 blocks in short landscape (PR #148 reviewer focus).
- Appearance of stretched shapes (`preserveAspectRatio="none"`) for the widest block (1.6 x 0.8).

No open GitHub issue concerns this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other drag activities: [Koraliki](koraliki.md), [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md), [Kolorowe Kubeczki](kolorowe-kubeczki.md), [Puzzle](puzzle.md).
- Shared helper used: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`). [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) is **not** used.

## 21. Change history

- [#53](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/53) / [PR #78](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/78): activity introduced (6 blocks); block unit floored at 70 px after review (commit `127b990`).
- [#123](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/123) / [PR #148](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/148): random block count (5 to 9) and unique colours per launch.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/wyscig-pieskow.md`

```markdown
# Wyścig Piesków

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Wyścig Piesków |
| Activity ID | `wyscig` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A friendly race of four dogs of different random breeds: the child cheers them on with taps, they all finish together, wag their tails under confetti, and a new race starts. |
| Category | Cause and effect; open-ended play; calming |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse), keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/wyscig.js`](../../js/wyscig.js), shared drawings in [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js), styles with prefix `wp-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A dog activity with a different mechanic from washing ([Myjnia](myjnia.md), [Psia Myjnia](psia-myjnia.md)): cheering a runner along a track (issue [#177](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/177)).
- Uses the shared dog drawings of [Rasy Piesków](rasy-pieskow.md) (`window.Dogs`, issue [#175](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/175)).
- Gives a parent the Polish breed names, shown small under each dog.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; four different random breeds are placed in four lanes in random order and start running at their own base speeds.
2. Initially displayed: a green track with four lanes, a chequered finish strip at the right end of each, and the dogs at the left.
3. Interactions: tap a dog (or focus it with Tab and press Enter/Space).
4. Response: the dog gets a smooth speed boost of about 1 s with a dust puff behind it.
5. Each dog that reaches the finish smiles and wags its tail; its name stays visible.
6. When all four are in, confetti falls for about 4 s.
7. The field fades out (0.7 s) and a new race with a new set of breeds fades in. Restart is automatic; there is no menu or button.
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Lanes and breeds | 4 lanes, each at least 60 px tall; 4 different breeds from `Dogs.LIST`, random order; a new race never has the same set of breeds as the previous one. |
| Base speed | Per dog `1 / T` track fractions per second with `T` random in 25-35 s; dogs keep running untouched. |
| Boost | A tap raises the boost target by +0.4, capped at +0.6, for 1 s after the last tap; the boost factor follows its target at 1.2 per second (no jump). |
| Slew limit | The speed changes by at most 0.02 track fractions per second squared. |
| Never decided | From the moment the leader passes 50% of the track each dog's speed is blended towards the speed that would finish at the group's mean remaining time (full blend at 90%). Once a dog has finished, the others are guaranteed a speed that finishes them within 2.5 s. In a Node simulation of 15 races the gap between the first and last dog was about 0.03-0.13 s. |
| Running legs | While a dog runs its four legs swing about the hips as a trot (diagonal pairs alternate). Step rate = speed x 70 per second (about 2-3 steps/s at base speed, never above 5), so a boost speeds the legs up and back down smoothly. The body bobs up by at most 3% of the dog height. Swing angle is 18-40 degrees depending on leg length, so short-legged breeds (Jamnik, Corgi, Buldog) keep their legs attached and visible. |
| Reduced motion (legs) | Step rate is halved and the bob is switched off; the legs still alternate. |
| Finish | The dog stays at the finish, smiles (`dg-happy`), wags its tail at 2.2 Hz (+/-26 degrees). The running legs ease out to standing within 0.35 s of finishing (the wag and smile begin at once). Tapping a finished dog only makes it wag more for 0.8 s. |
| Reward | Confetti: pool of 36 pieces, about 2.2 s fall each, staggered over 4 s. |
| Faces | Only `dg-calm` and `dg-happy`; no angry or sad face exists. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect (a tap speeds the dog up) and gentle tapping.
- Noticing different dog breeds and sizes.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Tapped dogs visibly speed up for about a second; all dogs finish together.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about breed recognition, counting or turn-taking; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus; each dog is a native `<button>`); keyboard: Tab moves between the four dogs (visible 4 px focus ring), Enter/Space cheers the focused dog.
- **Labels (Polish):** each dog button has an `aria-label` with the breed ("Piesek: Labrador. Dotknij lub naciśnij Enter, aby zachęcić do biegu."); the SVG is decorative.
- **Target sizes:** a dog button is at least 56 px high (dog plus name line) and normally much larger.
- **Layout:** four lanes below the Back button, portrait and landscape from 320 x 568 to 1920 x 1080.
- **Colour:** the finish is shown by the position at the strip, the happy mouth and the tail wag, not by colour alone.
- **Reduced motion:** all movement is driven from JavaScript, so positions, smiles, wagging and confetti behave the same; the running legs alternate at half rate without the body bob; no state exists only in a CSS keyframe.
- **Text:** none except the small parent-facing breed names.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Visual quality (dog size in lanes, dust puff, confetti) has not been checked on a device (sections 17 and 18).
- A race lasts about 25-35 s; a child who does not tap simply watches.
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/wyscig.js`](../../js/wyscig.js): `LANES` (4), `T_MIN`/`T_MAX` (25/35), `BOOST_ADD` (0.4), `BOOST_MAX` (0.6), `BOOST_S` (1), `BOOST_SLEW` (1.2), `ACC` (0.02), `BLEND_FROM`/`BLEND_TO` (0.5/0.9), `END_GAP_S` (2.5), `CONFETTI` (36), `CONFETTI_S` (4), `FALL_S` (2.2), `PUFFS` (12 per lane), `PUFF_S`, `SWAP_S` (0.7), `WAG_HZ` (2.2), `STEPS_PER_SPEED` (70), `STEPS_MAX` (5), `RUN_IN_S`/`RUN_OUT_S` (0.3/0.35), `BOB` (0.03). Changing them needs a code edit.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Dogs are inline SVG built by `Dogs.draw(id)`; the menu icon is an inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- Breeds: 4 of 8, uniformly, random lane order; the set differs from the previous race (module variable `lastSet`, so also across launches).
- Base time per dog: uniform 25-35 s.
- Confetti positions, drift and rotation are random.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A race is complete when all four dogs have finished. Feedback: happy mouth, tail wag, confetti. No failure state. The next race starts automatically.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/wyscig.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant: breedId })` on each cheer (tap or keyboard Enter/Space) and `Analytics.complete()` when all four dogs have finished. All calls are wrapped so that nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. Recorded: starts, active time, replays, quick exits, touches, breed variants and the number of finished races. The activity is not in the module's `COMPLETABLE` list (it repeats endlessly), so exit-before-completion is not defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/wyscig.js`](../../js/wyscig.js) overrides `mount` of the `wyscig` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.wp > div.wp-field > 4 x div.wp-lane (finish strip, puff layer, button.wp-dog > art + name) + confetti layer`.
- **State:** phase (`run`, `party`, `out`, `in`), per-dog progress fraction `p`, speed `v`, base speed, boost factor/target/timer, finished flag; puff and confetti pools.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, guarded by `!raf`, cancelled while the tab is hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Legs:** `setupLegs` wraps each leg (rect + foot) of the shared `dg-legs` group in its own `<g>` once per race; `poseLegs` runs in the same frame loop and sets one `rotate` per leg and one `translateY` on the art element (no per-frame DOM creation, no CSS animation). A run factor eases the swing in/out; the gait phase keeps accumulating across tab-hidden gaps (capped `dt`), so there is no jump.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.wp` is fixed full-screen; `.wp-field` is inset below the Back button (64 px plus safe area) with 12 px margins.
- Lane height is `max(60, field height / 4)`; the dog (plus an 18 px name line) fits inside it and is at most 130 px high and at most 34% of the track width, 6:5 aspect.
- Progress is a fraction (0-1) of `trackW - dogWidth`; the pixel position is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`, so rotation never makes a dog jump.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Leaving mid-race | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. Ten quick open/close cycles leave no loop running. |
| Tap on a finished dog | Only a bigger wag for 0.8 s. |
| Many taps | The boost target is capped at +60%. |
| Tap during fade between races | Ignored. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| Resize / orientation | Lanes re-laid out; progress fractions unchanged. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |
| `window.Dogs` missing | Not handled. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] A race lasts 25-35 s with no taps and all four dogs finish within 3 s of each other.
- [ ] Tapping a dog speeds it up smoothly for about a second; repeated taps do not make it jump or stop.
- [ ] Legs alternate while running, faster during a boost, stand within 0.4 s at the finish; Jamnik/Corgi/Buldog legs stay attached; landscape 568 x 320 legs stay inside the lane.
- [ ] Confetti for about 4 s, then a new race with a different set of breeds.
- [ ] Rotate the device mid-race; the dogs keep their relative positions.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab to a dog, Enter/Space cheers it.
- [ ] Leave mid-race and reopen ten times quickly.
- [ ] Small screens (320 x 568) and 1920 x 1080, portrait and landscape.
- [ ] Reduced motion: movement, smiles, wagging and confetti still work.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

The PR for issue [#177](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/177) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM; no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.
- On screens where four 60 px lanes do not fit (field shorter than 240 px) the lower lanes are clipped.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel of the dust puff, confetti and dog size on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Psia Myjnia](psia-myjnia.md), [Myjnia](myjnia.md), [Rasy Piesków](rasy-pieskow.md).
- Shared component: [`js/dogs.js`](../../js/dogs.js) (`Dogs.LIST`, `Dogs.draw`).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#177](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/177): initial activity.
- Issue [#205](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/205): running legs animation and body bob.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/wzorki.md`

```markdown
# Wzorki

> Documents the current implementation on `main`. Shared platform behaviour (no sound, global reduced-motion rule, menu configuration, playtime, absence of automated tests, analytics status) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Wzorki |
| Activity ID | `wzorki` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A string of beads shows four beads of a simple repeating pattern and an empty slot. Two large beads below are offered; touching the one that continues the pattern glides it into the slot, the other only wobbles. After three correct beads the whole string glows and a new pattern appears. |
| Category | Matching / pattern continuation |
| Interaction type | Tap |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu |
| Source | [`js/wzorki.js`](../../js/wzorki.js), CSS prefix `wz-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

The activity introduces simple patterns (such as ABAB or AABB) by asking the child to say what comes next, with a free retry on a wrong choice. It is the application's pattern-recognition activity; beads differ by shape and inner mark as well as colour, so the pattern can be followed without relying on colour.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the string fades in (0.9 s) with four beads placed and a dashed empty slot after them.
2. After a 0.5 s fade, two large choice beads appear at the bottom.
3. The child touches a choice.
   - Correct: the bead glides (0.8 s, with a small arc) from the choice into the slot, grows or shrinks to the string size and glows; two new choices appear for the next slot.
   - Other: that choice wobbles gently (0.55 s) and stays available.
4. After three correct beads (7 beads on the string) the whole string glows for 2 s.
5. About 4 s later the scene fades out (0.9 s) and a new pattern fades in (0.9 s).
6. There is no end screen; the activity continues with new patterns. The child leaves with the Back button.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| String length | 7 beads (`N`), of which 4 are given (`GIVEN`) and 3 to be placed |
| Bead types | 4 (`TYPES`): Różowe kółko (pink circle with a white dot), Niebieski kwadrat (blue rounded square with two bars), Żółta gwiazdka (yellow star), Zielony romb (green diamond with a white diamond) |
| Pattern sets | 12 (`PATTERNS`), see below |
| Choices | 2 per slot: the correct bead and one different type, chosen at random from the 3 other types |
| Correct side | Random left or right; the same side is never used three times in a row |
| Correct touch | Bead glides 0.8 s (`GLIDE`); glows for 1.4 s decay |
| Wrong touch | Wobble 0.55 s (`WOB`), rotation up to 9 degrees; no change otherwise; unlimited retries |
| Touches accepted | only in phase `play`, once the choices have finished fading in; ignored during glide, glow, fade |
| Completion glow | 2 s (`GLOW`), 0.5 s ramps |
| Wait | 4 s (`WAIT`) |
| Fade | 0.9 s out and 0.9 s in (`FADE`) |

The 12 pattern sets (symbols are bead types repeated across the 7 positions): ABAB, AABAAB, ABCABC, ABBABB, AABB, ABCC, ABCD, AABC, ABBC, ABAC, AAAB, ABCB (as listed in the code, `[0,1]`, `[0,0,1]`, `[0,1,2]`, `[0,1,1]`, `[0,0,1,1]`, `[0,1,2,2]`, `[0,1,2,3]`, `[0,0,1,2]`, `[0,1,1,2]`, `[0,1,0,2]`, `[0,0,0,1]`, `[0,1,2,1]`). The symbols 0 to 3 are always the same bead types (pink circle, blue square, yellow star, green diamond) in every set.

A wrong choice is never a failure; it only wobbles and the right bead remains available.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**: noticing repetition and sequence (patterns), visual discrimination of shapes, anticipation ("what comes next"), calm trial and error.

**Directly observable behavior**
- The first four beads of the pattern are shown; the three remaining slots are filled one at a time.
- The two options always differ in both shape and colour.
- A wrong choice does not change the state, so the child can retry.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**
- Whether the activity helps pattern recognition or mathematical readiness.
- Whether four given beads make every pattern unambiguous to a child (for example AAAB with four beads).

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch, mouse, stylus, keyboard (the two choices are `<button>` elements with a descriptive `aria-label`, for example "Żółta gwiazdka"); 4px focus outline; `touch-action: manipulation`.
- **Target size:** choice buttons are `max(56, min(H * 0.26, W * 0.3, 132))` px square, so at least 56px.
- **Bead size:** string beads are up to 110px; at least 56px in the two-row layout.
- **Orientation:** the layout is computed in pixels for the current field size: a single row of 7 beads when each bead can be at least 62px, otherwise two rows (4 and 3 beads). Choices are always at the bottom, one each side of the centre.
- **Colour:** bead types differ by shape and inner mark as well as colour (stated in the source).
- **Reading:** none required.
- **Sound:** none.
- **Reduced motion:** the glide, wobble, glow and fades are drawn by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop rather than CSS, so they still run under the global rule. The activity does not read `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Limitations:** the pattern itself (which beads are on the string) is not described to assistive technology (the string SVG is `aria-hidden`); only the two choices are labelled.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Some patterns may be ambiguous with only four given beads (for example AAAB or ABAC can be read in more than one way); the intended continuation is fixed by the pattern, which may differ from a child's reading. This is a design property, not a defect in the code.
- The correct choice can appear on either side; the choice buttons are hidden during the fade between rounds, so touches there do nothing.
- No ending; patterns keep coming (the cycle of 12 repeats).
- Privacy: nothing is stored or transmitted.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in `js/wzorki.js`.

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Changeable without code change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | Beads on the string | number | 7 | No |
| `GIVEN` | Beads shown at the start | number | 4 | No |
| `GLIDE`, `WOB` | Glide and wobble durations (s) | numbers | 0.8, 0.55 | No |
| `GLOW`, `WAIT`, `FADE` | Completion glow, wait, fade (s) | numbers | 2, 4, 0.9 | No |
| `MAXDT` | Frame cap (s) | number | 0.05 | No |
| `TYPES` | The four bead types (label and SVG) | array | 4 | No |
| `PATTERNS` | The 12 pattern sets | array | see section 4 | No |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The four bead drawings are inline SVG strings in `js/wzorki.js` (100x100 viewBox; the star polygon is generated). The string, slot ring, beads, glows and choices are created with `createElementNS`. No fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- **Pattern order:** at launch, and again after every 12 rounds, the indices 0 to 11 are shuffled with `Rand.shuffle`; each pattern set is used once per block of 12 before any repeats. When a new block starts, if its first set equals the last set of the previous block, the first and last entries are swapped, so there are no back-to-back repeats at block boundaries (PR #145 reports a simulation over 36 rounds).
- **Wrong option:** `other = (correct + 1 + floor(random * 3)) % 4`, so it is always a different type; chosen with `Math.random`.
- **Side:** random left/right; after two identical sides in a row the next one is forced to the opposite side (history of the last 3).
- **Persistence:** none; every launch has a fresh order.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No levels or difficulty changes. Within a round, the child places three beads (the 5th, 6th and 7th). The set of patterns includes simple ones (ABAB) and longer or less regular ones (ABCD, ABAC), but the order is random, not graded. Nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- **Per bead:** correct bead glides in and glows; wrong choice wobbles.
- **Round completion:** all 7 beads placed; the whole string glows for 2 s.
- **After completion:** the choices are disabled, then a new pattern fades in automatically after the wait and fade. No sound, no scoring.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** IIFE in [`js/wzorki.js`](../../js/wzorki.js) overriding `mount` for `wzorki`.
- **Rendering:** one `.wz-field` containing an SVG (`.wz-svg`: two polylines for the string, a dashed ring for the empty slot and 7 bead groups) and two `<button class="wz-btn">` choices, each with its own SVG. `layout()` computes pixel positions for the current field size, `render()` applies them.
- **State:** `phase` (`in`, `play`, `glide`, `glow`, `wait`, `out`), `filled`, `seq` (7 symbols), `correct`, `other`, `side`, `glide`, `wob`, `glow` values.
- **Animation:** a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop `frame()` with capped dt, stopped when idle or hidden; `wake()` restarts it.
- **Randomization:** [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.shuffle`) for the pattern order; `Math.random` for the option and side.
- **Events:** `click` on the choices; `resize`, `orientationchange`, `visibilitychange`.
- **Cleanup:** removes the listeners, cancels the frame and removes the root.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.wz-field` is absolutely positioned: top = safe-area + 56px, bottom = safe-area + 8px, left and right = safe-area + 8px.
- The string SVG has a `viewBox` equal to the field's pixel size (`0 0 W H`), so bead positions are in field pixels and the choice buttons (positioned with `left`/`top` in px) share the same space. Beads are scaled by `S / 100 * 0.9`.
- Choice size `cs = max(56, min(H * 0.26, W * 0.3, 132))`; top area height `H - cs - 40`; choices centred with an offset of `cs * 0.78` either side of the centre line.
- Bead size: `S1 = min((W - 24) / 7.6, topH * 0.6, 110)`; if `S1 >= 62` the string is one row, otherwise two rows of 4 and 3 with `S = max(56, min((W - 24) / 4.5, (topH - 8) / 2.5, 110))`. A glide goes from the choice position to the slot with a small arc (`S * 0.25`).
- `onResize` recomputes layout and re-renders; the current state is kept.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- **Rapid input:** touches are ignored unless the phase is `play` and the choices are fully faded in; repeated wrong touches only restart the wobble.
- **Resize/orientation change:** layout recomputed immediately; positions are reapplied, including mid-glide.
- **Backgrounding:** loop cancelled while hidden and restarted on return.
- **Zero-size field:** `layout()` returns without changes if the field has no size.
- **Leaving during an animation:** cleanup cancels the frame.
- **Unhandled:** no handling of a missing `Rand` helper (not an issue with the shipped files); reduced-motion preference is not read.

## 17. Testing

There are no automated tests. Manual scenarios to perform:

- [ ] A string of four beads and an empty slot appears, followed by two choices.
- [ ] Touch the correct bead: it glides into the slot with a glow and the next two choices appear.
- [ ] Touch the other bead: it wobbles and nothing else changes; touch it repeatedly.
- [ ] Complete the string (3 beads): glow for about 2 s, then a new pattern about 4 s later.
- [ ] Play 24 or more rounds: each pattern appears once per block of 12 and no pattern appears twice in a row.
- [ ] Check the correct side varies and is never on the same side three times in a row.
- [ ] For each of the 12 patterns, confirm that the continued beads follow the pattern.
- [ ] Narrow portrait (for example 320x568): the string wraps to two rows, beads and choices are at least 56px and do not overlap.
- [ ] Landscape (for example 640x360 and 1920x1080): one row and a visible, reachable choice row.
- [ ] Rotate the device mid-round: the string and choices re-layout and the state is kept.
- [ ] Touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space).
- [ ] Switch tab during a glide and return.
- [ ] Reduced motion on: glide and wobble still run.
- [ ] Browsers required by the README: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#74](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/74) reports a Node stub-DOM run over five rounds (wrong and correct taps, glow, automatic new round, cleanup) and lists manual device tests, in particular the narrow portrait two-row layout and orientation change, as pending. PR [#145](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/145) reports `node --check` and a Node simulation of the order logic over 36 rounds (each block of 12 is a full permutation, no back-to-back repeats); no browser test.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**
- No automated tests; manual device tests were pending in the PR descriptions.
- Only 12 pattern sets and 4 bead types; bead symbols are fixed per index (the same shape always plays "A").
- Reduced-motion preference is not read; the pattern is not described to assistive technology.

**Requires verification**
- Whether every pattern is unambiguous for a child with only four given beads.
- Appearance of the two-row layout on narrow screens and on orientation change (flagged as pending in PR #74).

No open GitHub issue is specific to this activity.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Shared helper: [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.shuffle`). `js/animals.js` is not used.
- Same scene pattern (single rAF loop, glow, wait, cross-fade): [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md), [Co nie Pasuje?](co-nie-pasuje.md), [Ścieżka](sciezka.md).
- Related theme (beads): [Koraliki](koraliki.md).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#50](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/50) / PR [#74](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/74): activity added.
- Issue [#119](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/119) / PR [#145](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/145): 12 pattern sets in random order per launch.
```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/zabawa-w-chowanego.md`

```markdown
# Zabawa w chowanego

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Zabawa w chowanego |
| Internal ID | `chowany` (entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A garden with four hiding places (krzak, pudło, drzewo, beczka). Touching a place slowly lifts its cover and shows what hides there: an animal peeking out, or a flower when the place is empty. |
| Category | Observation / cause and effect (peek-a-boo style) |
| Interaction type | Tap (button `click`) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled by default in the menu (no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/chowany.js`](../../js/chowany.js), CSS block `/* Zabawa w chowanego */` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) (prefix `hd`) |

## 2. Business purpose

Based on the issue and the code, the activity offers a slow, predictable "where is it hiding?" game: the child lifts covers one at a time and sees what is behind. Nothing can be answered wrongly, nothing is timed against the child and nothing is scored. It complements the drag-based sorting activities (for example [Koraliki](koraliki.md)) with the simplest possible interaction, a single tap, and complements the other animal activities by using the shared animal family with a hide-and-reveal mechanic. The set of animals changes on every launch, so repeated play shows different characters.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the activity from the menu (`#chowany`); `mount` builds the scene and starts the animation loop immediately.
2. Four closed hiding places are shown on a sky-to-grass gradient. Three hide an animal, one hides a flower (not visible while closed).
3. The child taps a place. The cover slides up and fades (about 1.5 s) and the animal (or flower) is revealed; the animal then makes one small hop (0.7 s).
4. Tapping an open place closes it again (about 1.5 s). Taps on a place that is currently moving are ignored.
5. Completion: when every one of the four places has been opened at least once (and nothing is moving), all four glow warmly for 2 s, then all covers close slowly.
6. After the covers have closed, the animals fade out and back in (0.9 s) and reappear in a new arrangement. The child can start opening places again straight away.
7. There is no end: the cycle repeats indefinitely. While all places are closed and nothing has been touched for 7 s, two places quietly swap their occupants with a short fade.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Value (from `js/chowany.js`) |
|---|---|
| Hiding places | 4: krzak (bush), pudło (box), drzewo (tree), beczka (barrel) |
| Occupants | Exactly 3 animals and 1 flower at any time |
| Cover open/close duration | `MOVE_S = 1.5` s (0.75 s when reduced motion is requested) |
| Cover motion | Moves up by 38% of its height (`translateY(-38 * u %)`) and fades to 40% opacity; with reduced motion it does not move and fades to 0% opacity |
| Hop after opening | `HOP_S = 0.7` s, peak 7% of the box height; skipped with reduced motion |
| Completion glow | `GLOW_S = 2` s, yellow drop-shadow (`#ffe08a`, 6-20 px blur) on all places, eased with time constant 0.4 s |
| Rearrangement fade | `FADE_S = 0.9` s; arrangement is changed at the half-way point |
| Idle swap | After `SWAP_IDLE_S = 7` s with all covers closed and no animation running |
| Input while moving | A tap on a moving place, or any tap during the glow and closing phases, is ignored (`toggle`) |
| Wrong answers | None; there is no failure, scoring or timer |

- The tree cover (crown radius 41 plus a 56-unit-wide trunk, in the 100-unit SVG) is wide enough to hide a whole animal, so the tree's animal is no longer shifted (`ox: 0` for all four places) and is fully hidden while the tree is closed.
- Rustle cue: while the tree is fully closed (`o === 0`) and an animal hides behind it, the tree cover rustles gently, a soft pulse about every 7 s (`sin(clock * 0.9)` squared on its positive half; rotation up to 2.6 degrees about the bottom centre, wobbling at `sin(clock * 11)`). With reduced motion it is an opacity dip of up to 14% instead of a rotation. The empty (flower) place does not rustle. `clock` is the sum of the capped frame times.
- Opening state is tracked per place (`opened`) and reset when the round rearranges.
- Sound: none ([shared behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits** (stated by the code comments and the README, not measured):
- Cause and effect: a touch produces a visible, slow result.
- Object permanence style play and calm observation of animals.
- Simple, independent tapping with no wrong action.

**Directly observable behavior:**
- Each tap reveals one occupant; the reveal is slow and ends with a single small hop.
- All places opened leads to a gentle glow and a new arrangement.
- No timers, scores or failure messages are shown.

**Requires professional or research-based validation:** any claim about attention, memory or developmental effect. The repository contains no evidence for such claims.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** touch and mouse via `click` on native `<button>` elements; keyboard works through the native button behaviour (Tab, Enter/Space) with a visible `:focus-visible` outline (4px `#8f7fd1`). Stylus is treated as a pointer click.
- **Screen readers:** each place has `aria-label="Kryjówka: <name>"` and an `aria-expanded` state that follows opening and closing. The occupant itself is not announced (its SVG is `aria-hidden`).
- **Target size:** square buttons `--hd-s` between 64 and 200 px (CSS `min-width/min-height: 64px`); computed in `layout()` from the field size.
- **Orientation:** portrait (height >= width) uses a 2x2 grid, landscape a single row of four; layout is recomputed on `resize` and `orientationchange`.
- **Reduced motion:** the global rule disables CSS animations and transitions ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)), but this activity's motion is driven from a `requestAnimationFrame` loop with inline styles, so it still works. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it switches to a gentler variant: covers fade instead of sliding, no hop, 0.75 s opening time. The completion glow is still shown.
- **Colour:** not used for any decision; places are distinguished by shape.
- **Reading:** no reading required. A young child can use it independently.
- **Limitations:** the only text is the (non-visible) aria labels, which are in Polish. Occupants are not announced to assistive technology.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- The activity has no formal ending; the cycle repeats until the child leaves (the playtime limit in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) still applies).
- The unrequested idle swap (every 7 s with nothing touched) changes what is behind a closed cover; it is visible only as a short fade of the animal layer behind the covers, but it could be surprising if a child expects a fixed hiding place.
- Opening a place during an idle swap fade shows the swapped occupant appearing while the cover is open (see section 16).
- Soft glow uses `drop-shadow` filters on four elements for 2 s; this may be costly on very slow devices (requires verification).
- No privacy concerns: nothing is stored and nothing is sent.

## 8. Configuration

The activity has no external configuration; everything is a constant in [`js/chowany.js`](../../js/chowany.js). Tunable constants (all numbers, change only by editing the file):

| Name | Purpose | Type | Default | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MOVE_S` | Open/close duration (seconds) | number | 1.5 | top of IIFE |
| `GLOW_S` | Completion glow duration (s) | number | 2 | top of IIFE |
| `HOP_S` | Hop after opening (s) | number | 0.7 | top of IIFE |
| `SWAP_IDLE_S` | Idle time before an idle swap (s) | number | 7 | top of IIFE |
| `FADE_S` | Fade out/in used by swap and rearrangement (s) | number | 0.9 | top of IIFE |
| `PLACES` | Four places: label, horizontal offset `ox` (0 for all), optional `rustle` flag (tree only), cover SVG | array | see code | top of IIFE |
| Layout numbers | Max size 200, min size 64, 0.92 scale factor, 0.4 extra row for the animal head room | numbers | see `layout()` | `layout()` |

There is no fallback for invalid values because no value is read from outside.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything is inline SVG built from string constants: the four cover drawings (`PLACES[].cover`), the flower (`FLOWER`) and the animal figure (`animalSvg`: a body ellipse in the animal's fur colour plus `Animals.head(id)` from [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js), scaled 1.3). The background is a CSS gradient (`.hd`, `#d9eefb` to `#e8f5dc` to `#cfe8b8`). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js` (green bush with rabbit ears and a yellow sun). No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

| What | How | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| Four animals for the launch | `Animals.pick(4)` (unique) | 13 animals in the shared family |
| Which place is empty | `Math.floor(Math.random() * 4)` | 4 places |
| Which 3 of the 4 chosen animals are out | `Rand.pick([0,1,2,3], 3)` | 4 indices |
| New arrangement after a round | `arrangement(old)`; repeated until it differs from the previous arrangement | - |
| Idle swap | One random pair from the pairs whose occupants differ | at most 6 pairs |

- Choice of the four animals persists until the activity is left; it is re-chosen every time it is opened. Nothing is stored.
- Because exactly one animal is "waiting" at any time, over a number of rounds every chosen animal appears.
- The idle swap does nothing if no pair differs (cannot happen with 3 animals and 1 flower; guard `if (!pairs.length) return`).

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression, levels or difficulty. Behaviour is identical for every round and nothing is persisted.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- Completion is informal: all four places opened at least once. Feedback is a 2 s yellow glow around all places, then slow closing and a fade to a new arrangement. No sound, text or score.
- There are no failure states; any tap is valid, and taps during movement are ignored silently.
- A new round starts automatically after the rearrangement fade.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/chowany.js`](../../js/chowany.js), registered by replacing `mount` of the `chowany` entry. It returns `cleanup`.
- **Rendering:** DOM: `div.hd > div.hd-field > 4 x button.hd-spot`. Each button holds an inline-SVG flower, an animal container and a cover SVG (class `hd-cov`). Buttons are positioned by `transform: translate()` in `layout()`.
- **State:** per-place object `{ o (current openness 0..1), t (target 0/1), opened, hop, op, shown }`; global `occ` (occupant per place: animal index 0-3 or -1 for the flower), `phase` (`play`, `glow`, `close`), `phaseT`, `idleT`, `glow`, `fadeJob`, `clock` (seconds, drives the tree rustle).
- **Animation:** one `frame()` loop with dt capped to 0.05 s. `o` moves linearly towards `t` and is shaped with `smooth` (smoothstep) in `paintSpot`. The loop requests the next frame only while the page is visible.
- **Phases:** `play` -> (all opened) `glow` (2 s) -> `close` (all targets 0; when nothing moves, start a fade job that applies `arrangement(old)` at 50%) -> `play`.
- **Events:** `click` on each button; `resize`, `orientationchange` and `visibilitychange` on window/document.
- **Dependencies:** `window.Animals` (`pick`, `head`) and `window.Rand` (`pick`).
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** none from the activity itself (reported by `js/app.js`).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the animation frame, removes the three listeners and removes the board.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.hd` fills the viewport (`position: fixed; inset: 0`); `.hd-field` is inset by the safe-area variables plus 64 px at the top (room for the Back button) and 12 px on the other sides.
- `layout()` reads the field size: portrait (`fh >= fw`) gives `cols = 2, rows = 2`, otherwise `cols = 4, rows = 1`. Size `S = max(64, min(200, fw/cols*0.92, fh/(rows+0.4)*0.92))`, stored in CSS variable `--hd-s`. Rows are centred vertically with an extra 0.4*S on top for the animal that appears above the cover.
- Each cover/animal/flower SVG uses `viewBox="0 0 100 100"` and fills its button, so artwork scales with `S`. Hop and cover movement use percentages of the button height, so they scale too.
- Orientation change and resize call `layout()`; there is no other scaling logic.
- Very small fields are clamped to 64 px; the grid may overflow the field in that case (requires verification).

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Missing assets | N/A (inline SVG). If `window.Animals`/`window.Rand` were missing the mount would throw (no guard). |
| Resize / rotation | `layout()` re-run; animation state is unaffected. |
| Backgrounding | The loop stops while `document.hidden` and restarts on return; dt is capped so nothing jumps. |
| Rapid taps | Ignored while a place is moving or while the phase is not `play`. |
| Tap during idle-swap fade | Allowed; the swap is applied at the 50% point even if that place was just opened (the occupant changes behind the lifted cover). |
| Unsupported `matchMedia` | `reduced()` falls back to normal motion. |
| Touch cancel | Uses `click`, so a cancelled touch simply produces no tap. |
| Leaving mid-animation | `cleanup` cancels the frame; all state is local to `mount`. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist for this activity or the repository ([README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). Manual checklist (not yet performed unless noted):

- [ ] Normal: tap a place; the cover rises over about 1.5 s and the animal or flower appears, with one small hop.
- [ ] Tap an open place; it closes; taps while it is moving are ignored.
- [ ] Completion: open all four places once; they glow for about 2 s, close, and the animals appear in a different arrangement.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap rapidly on several places, tap during glow and closing; nothing breaks and no failure feedback appears.
- [ ] Restart: leave and reopen; new random set of four animals and arrangement.
- [ ] Randomization: over several rounds the arrangement never equals the previous one; exactly one place shows a flower.
- [ ] Idle swap: leave all places closed for about 7 s; two occupants swap with a short fade when opened afterwards.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that no difficulty change occurs.
- [ ] Portrait: 2x2 grid, all four places fully visible, buttons at least 64 px.
- [ ] Landscape: one row of four; rotate while a cover is open and check nothing is cut off.
- [ ] Touch (iPhone/iPad, Android): taps register once; no zoom or scroll.
- [ ] Mouse (desktop): click works; keyboard Tab/Enter opens and closes places with a visible focus ring.
- [ ] Reduced motion (OS setting on): covers fade instead of sliding, no hop, glow still shown.
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tabs mid-opening and return; the animation continues without a jump.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad (the README's required set).

PR [#81](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/81) is the introducing pull request; this document did not independently verify its test claims.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed (from code reading):**
- No automated tests.
- Idle swap or rearrangement can change an occupant behind an already lifted cover if the child opens a place during the fade (section 16).
- Occupants are not exposed to assistive technology; only the places have labels.
- The tree rustle is the only cue for which place hides an animal while all covers are closed; it is subtle and its visibility on real devices is not documented.

**Requires verification:**
- Layout on very small viewports (below the 64 px minimum cell).
- Rendering cost of the glow filters on slow devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned. (The tree that fully hides the animal and rustles as a cue is done, see issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173).)

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Shared helpers: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`) and [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`).
- Other activities that draw their animals from the shared family: [Zwierzątka na Farmie](zwierzatka-na-farmie.md) and [Kąpiel Zwierzątek](kapiel-zwierzatek.md).
- Rearranging after completion follows the same "soft glow then new round" pattern as [Koraliki](koraliki.md) and [Duże i Małe](duze-i-male.md).

## 21. Change history

- [#55](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/55) / [PR #81](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/81): activity introduced.
- [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113): random animal pool via the shared helpers (commit `dae142c`).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): fixed on `main`; the tree fully hides the animal and rustles as a cue.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/zakupy.md`

```markdown
# Zakupy

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Zakupy |
| Activity ID | `zakupy` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A role-play shop: the child takes products (several units of each on the shelves, 22 kinds in total) into a big basket, brings it to the counter and drags each item across a barcode scanner; a numeral counts the scanned items and a receipt lists each product with a count. |
| Category | Role play; dragging; counting |
| Interaction type | Drag (and tap / press) with a keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/zakupy.js`](../../js/zakupy.js), styles with prefix `zk-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A shopping role play that combines dragging with counting, without payments or reading; issue [#185](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/185).
- Related: [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md) (counting).

## 3. Activity flow

1. A shop with six shelf slots (each shows 2-4 units of one product), a big basket, a register button and a shop owner (random animal) is shown; a shopping list of pictures (1-5, kinds that are on the shelves) and the numeral `0` are at the top.
2. The child drags a product onto the basket: one unit leaves the shelf and goes into the basket (its picture, at least 44 px wide, shows in the pile). A product can be taken any number of times; a slot whose last unit was taken stays empty for 2 s and is then restocked with 2-4 fresh units.
3. Dragging the basket into the shop area, tapping it or pressing the register button brings the basket to the counter. Basket items come first; list products that were not picked are added until the counter has as many items as the list.
4. Each counter item is dragged across the scanner (or activated with Enter/Space). The scanner flashes a green line and the numeral rises by 1; the item lands in the bag row.
5. When everything is scanned a receipt (a picture and a count numeral such as `x3` per distinct product) slides out of the scanner and the owner smiles. About 4 s after that the counter fades out and a new list starts with a different random set of products on the shelves.
6. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Rounds | List length is round 1 = 1 item, round 2 = 2 ... round 5 = 5, then it starts again from 1; the count restarts on every launch. |
| List | Distinct products drawn at random; a new list never equals the previous one. |
| Shelves | Six slots, each a random kind from a pool of 22 (fruit, vegetables, bread, milk, cheese, eggs, juice, fish, sweets, a toy duck ...); each round a different set than the previous one. Each slot shows 2-4 units; taking one removes one unit; an emptied slot is restocked after 2 s with a new batch of the same kind. |
| Basket | At most 15 items (the same kind any number of times); a further product just glides back and stays on the shelf. The pile shows 8-12 items at once (rows overlap at most about a quarter); further items are stacked on top and a count numeral appears above 8 items. |
| Counter items | Basket items plus missing list products up to the list length. The counter shows 5 items at a time; for a bigger basket the next wave appears after the previous one is scanned. Any product is accepted; the same product several times counts normally. |
| Scanning | Crossing or dropping an item on the scanner zone scans it once; a fast drag is walked in ~8 px steps so the scanner is never skipped. An unscanned item released elsewhere glides back to the belt in 0.4 s. |
| Finish | Receipt slides out in 0.9 s (at least twice the former area, up to three columns of picture + `xN` rows so 15 items fit); owner smile; the next list starts 4 s after the receipt appears. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Text, faces, sound | Only the counter numeral (and Polish screen-reader labels); the owner never shows an angry or sad face; no sound. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Dragging with a goal; one-to-one counting with a numeral that rises with each item; everyday role play.

**Directly observable behavior**

- The numeral increases by 1 per scanned item; the list grows gradually.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** pointer drags; shelf slots are at least 64 px (the dragged unit at least 64 px), counter items, basket and register at least 56 px.
- **Keyboard:** arrows move focus between the visible products (and basket, register) or counter items; Enter or Space puts a product in the basket, presses the register or scans an item; visible 4 px focus ring.
- **Labels (Polish):** Polish product names (for example "Jabłko", "Chleb", "Mleko", "Jajka", "Ryba"), "Koszyk", "Kasa" with instructions; the pictures are decorative.
- **Non-colour cues:** the basket gets a glowing outline when a product is over it; scanned items are dimmed and move to the bag row.
- **Layout:** shelves 3 x 2 or 6 x 1, whichever gives larger products; the basket is 1.6 x its former width and its pile reserves room above the bottom band; works from 320 x 568 to 1920 x 1080 in both orientations (nothing clipped, Back button not covered).
- **Reduced motion:** all movement is driven from JavaScript (one rAF loop), so every state is reached.
- **Text:** numerals only (counter, basket count above 8 items, `xN` on the receipt).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Look and feel on real devices has not been checked (sections 17-18).
- An item scanned by a fast drag that ends away from the scanner still counts as scanned.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/zakupy.js`](../../js/zakupy.js): `SCAN_FLASH_S` (0.45), `BACK_S` (0.4), `TO_S` (0.6), `RECEIPT_S` (0.9), `DONE_S` (4), `MAX_ROUND` (5, counter wave size), `MAX_BASKET` (15), `SHELF_N` (6), `RESTOCK_S` (2), plus the `PRODUCTS` list (22 kinds). Changing them needs a code edit.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Products, basket, register, receipt and the owner (via [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js)) are inline SVG; the menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Six random kinds on the shelves per round (never the same set twice in a row), 2-4 random units per slot, a list of distinct kinds drawn from the shelf kinds, a random owner animal per round.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

List length grows from 1 to 5 over five rounds and then repeats from 1; nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A round is complete when every counter item has been scanned; feedback is the receipt, the owner's smile and an automatic new list. No failure state. The activity is open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches; `js/zakupy.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant })` with `variant` the product id (22 kinds, for example `apple`, `bread`, `eggs`) for each product put in the basket and each scan, and `Analytics.complete()` when a list is fully scanned. The activity stays open-ended (a new list starts by itself). All calls are wrapped so that nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. See [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/zakupy.js`](../../js/zakupy.js) overrides `mount` of the `zakupy` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.zk` with a wall, floor, top strip (list pictures and numeral), shelf planks, a counter scene (belt, bag row, scanner), a receipt, the owner, six `button.zk-prod` shelf slots (each with up to four unit pictures) with a floating `div.zk-ghost` each for the dragged unit, `button.zk-basket`, `button.zk-reg` and five `button.zk-item`.
- **State:** phase (`fadein`, `shop`, `to`, `scan`, `wave`, `finish`, `receipt`, `out`), round number, list, basket, queued counter items, per-kind scan tally, scanned count, per-slot stock / restock timer and per-item mode.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, cancelled while the tab is hidden, restarted on `visibilitychange` and input, stopped when idle; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `layout()` runs on `resize` and `orientationchange`. The top strip is 12% of the height (48-64 px), a bottom band holds the basket, register and owner, and the shelf grid and counter scene share the space between. The scanner is at least as wide as five counter items.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Checkout with an empty basket | The list products appear on the counter. |
| Basket full (15) | Further products glide back; the shelf keeps its units. |
| Last unit taken | The slot is disabled for 2 s, then restocked; one take removes exactly one unit (a unit in flight cannot be taken again). |
| Same product several times | Counted normally; the receipt shows one row with `xN`. |
| Resize / orientation | Layout recomputed; items keep their state. |
| Leaving mid-round | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag products to the basket: one unit leaves the shelf, the pile grows (8+ items individually visible), an emptied slot refills after 2 s; fill 15 items and try a 16th.
- [ ] Tap the basket, drag it into the shop and press the register; each brings the items to the counter.
- [ ] Drag every item across the scanner: green flash, numeral +1, receipt, owner smile, new list after about 4 s.
- [ ] Play five rounds: list lengths 1 to 5, then 1 again.
- [ ] Keyboard: arrows, Enter and Space.
- [ ] 320 x 568, 568 x 320 and 1920 x 1080; reduced motion; leave and reopen ten times quickly.

The PR for issue [#185](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/185) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel and drag comfort on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Policz Razem](policz-razem.md); uses `window.Animals` and `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#185](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/185): initial activity.
- Issue [#209](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/209): bigger basket (15 items), shelf units with restocking, 22 product kinds, bigger receipt with counts.

```
