## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/zbuduj-rakiete.md`

```markdown
# Zbuduj Rakietę

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour) and is not repeated here.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Zbuduj Rakietę |
| Activity ID | `zbuduj` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | The child assembles a rocket from four parts (three variants each), launches it with a 3-2-1 countdown and watches it fly and land on the Moon, where an astronaut waves. |
| Category | Build and reward; choice; cause and effect; calming |
| Interaction type | Drag and drop, tap on the launch button, keyboard alternative |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (appended last, no `defaultOff`) |
| Source | [`js/zbuduj.js`](../../js/zbuduj.js), styles with prefix `zr-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css) |

## 2. Business purpose

- A build-and-reward activity: assemble first, then launch; issue [#183](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/183).
- Differs from [Rakieta](rakieta.md), which is only free flight with a ready-made rocket.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; an empty rocket outline with four dashed slots (nose, body, fins, engine) stands on a sky background and a tray holds 12 part pictures grouped by kind (nose, body, fins, engine: one column in portrait, one row in landscape).
2. Interactions: the child drags a part onto its slot (a glowing outline appears when the part is over its slot); it snaps in with a soft pop and stays in the tray so it can be swapped for another variant.
3. When all four slots are full a large glowing launch button appears beside the rocket.
4. Tapping launch hides the tray and moves the rocket to the launch pad; the numerals 3, 2, 1 appear one second each.
5. The rocket flies up for 9 s through the sky, which first stays blue, then darkens into a starry night; only once the sky is dark does the Moon surface slide in from the top.
6. The rocket lands on the Moon in 2 s; an astronaut appears next to it and waves for 4 s.
7. The scene fades out and a new empty assembly with a tray with the variants reshuffled within each group fades in. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Slots | Nose, body, fins, engine; each has 3 variants differing in shape and colour. A part's picture is its slot's rectangle of the rocket, so it looks the same in the tray and on the rocket. |
| Drop | A release inside the part's own slot rectangle (plus 20 px margin) snaps it in; any other release drifts it back to the tray in 0.5 s. |
| Same slot twice | The new part replaces the earlier one. |
| Launch | Enabled only when all four slots are full. |
| Flight | The rocket in flight is the same element as the assembled one, so it uses exactly the chosen parts. |
| Timing | Count 3 x 1 s, flight 9 s, landing 2 s (11 s from the end of the count to touchdown), astronaut 4 s, fade 0.5 s each way. |
| Reduced motion | Count 3 x 0.5 s, flight 1.2 s, landing 0.4 s; the astronaut only raises an arm. |
| Failure, score | None; nothing is scored or stored. |
| Text, faces, sound | Only the numerals of the countdown; the astronaut smiles; no sound. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Choice and decision (which part), matching a part to a place, cause and effect (build, then launch).

**Directly observable behavior**

- Parts snap into their slots and the flown rocket shows the chosen parts.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about learning or developmental benefits; nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Touch targets:** tray parts are 72 px or larger (76 px at 320 x 568, up to 120 px on large screens, picture fills the whole button); the launch button is 72-104 px.
- **Input:** pointer events (touch, mouse, stylus) with pointer capture; the tray buttons have `touch-action: none`.
- **Keyboard:** Tab through the 12 parts (random order) and the launch button; Enter or Space on a part places it in its slot; Enter on the launch button launches.
- **Labels (Polish):** parts "Część rakiety: dziób 1. Przeciągnij na rakietę lub naciśnij Enter."; launch "Start rakiety. Naciśnij Enter, aby wystrzelić rakietę na Księżyc."; the SVGs are decorative.
- **Non-colour cues:** a thicker outline on the slot under a dragged part; dashed outlines mark empty slots; parts differ in shape as well as colour.
- **Reduced motion:** every visual is driven from JavaScript (one rAF loop), so all states are reached under `prefers-reduced-motion`; no end state exists only in a CSS keyframe.
- **Text:** only the countdown numerals.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Visual quality (part drawings, the flight scene, the astronaut) has not been checked on a device (sections 17 and 18).
- The rocket is small on a 320 x 568 screen (about 240 px tall).
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants at the top of [`js/zbuduj.js`](../../js/zbuduj.js): `COUNT_S` (1), `FLY_S` (9), `LAND_S` (2), `ASTRO_S` (4), `FADE_S` (0.5), `BACK_S` (0.5), the reduced-motion `RM_*` values, `SLOT_PAD` (20), `SLOTS` and `PARTS` (the drawings). Changing them needs a code edit.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Everything (parts, rocket, flame, sky, stars, Moon, ground, astronaut) is inline SVG or CSS created by `js/zbuduj.js`; the menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`.

## 10. Randomization and variants

The 12 tray parts are grouped by kind (nose, body, fins, engine; a column each in portrait, a row each in landscape); the three variants inside each group are shuffled (`Rand.shuffle` when available) at the start of every round; stars are placed randomly on each open. The rocket variants are chosen by the child.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None; there are no levels and nothing persists.

## 12. Completion and feedback

A round completes when the rocket has landed. Feedback: glowing slot, snap pop, glowing launch button, countdown, flame, landing and the waving astronaut. No failure state. The activity is open-ended.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`). `js/app.js` records the activity start and end and the module counts touches in the stage; `js/zbuduj.js` additionally calls `Analytics.track('interaction', { variant })` for each placed part (`n1`-`n3` nose, `b1`-`b3` body, `f1`-`f3` fins, `e1`-`e3` engine) and for the launch (`launch`), and `Analytics.complete()` when the rocket has landed. All calls are wrapped so that nothing changes if `window.Analytics` is missing. The activity is not in the module's `COMPLETABLE` list (it repeats endlessly), so exit-before-completion is not defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/zbuduj.js`](../../js/zbuduj.js) overrides `mount` of the `zbuduj` entry; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** `div.zr` with sky, night overlay, star layer, Moon, ground, tray panel, the rocket (one SVG with a flame, four part groups and four dashed slot outlines), the astronaut, the launch button, the countdown numeral, a fade veil and the 12 part buttons.
- **State:** phase (`build`, `count`, `fly`, `land`, `astro`, `fadeout`, `fadein`) with a phase timer `t`; `chosen` part index per slot; per-part pop animation; part buttons in modes `home`, `drag`, `back`, `fly`. `render()` derives every position from the phase, so resizing at any time is safe.
- **Loop:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `dt` capped at 0.05 s, guarded by `!raf`, cancelled while the tab is hidden and restarted on `visibilitychange`; it stops when idle (building with nothing moving) and restarts on input; cleanup cancels it and removes listeners and DOM.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** section 13.

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- `.zr` is fixed full-screen. Landscape (width above 1.05 x height): the tray is 3 columns x 4 rows on the right and the rocket sits in the remaining area; portrait: 4 columns x 3 rows below the rocket. The top 56 px stay free for the Back button. Part size is 72-120 px, the rocket scale is 0.4-1.8 and is limited so the launch button fits beside the rocket.
- Rocket units are 120 x 240; slot rectangles are computed from the rocket's current scale and position, so they follow a resize or rotation and the assembled parts are kept.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Wrong slot or release elsewhere | The part drifts back to the tray in 0.5 s; nothing is recorded. |
| Same slot twice | The earlier part is replaced. |
| Launch before all slots are full | The button is hidden and disabled. |
| Resize / orientation | Layout recomputed; chosen parts and the phase are kept. |
| Leaving mid-round | Cleanup cancels the frame, removes listeners and the DOM. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled and restarted on return; the `dt` cap prevents a jump. |
| `window.Analytics` missing | Calls are skipped. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Drag each of the 12 parts to its slot; it snaps in. Drag one to a wrong slot and to the sky; it drifts back.
- [ ] Place a second variant in a filled slot; it replaces the first.
- [ ] Fill all four slots; the launch button appears and glows.
- [ ] Launch; count 3-2-1, flight of about 9 s, landing, waving astronaut, then a new empty assembly with a reshuffled tray.
- [ ] The flown rocket has the chosen parts.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab, Enter on parts and on the launch button.
- [ ] Rotate the device in the building and flight phases.
- [ ] Leave and reopen ten times quickly.
- [ ] Small screens (320 x 568, 568 x 320) and 1920 x 1080; reduced motion.
- [ ] Regression (#208, parts and rocket invisible): at 320 x 568, 390 x 844 and 568 x 320 drop a part on its slot; it is visible on the rocket in its own shape and colour (a second variant replaces it). A wrong drop stays visible while drifting back and ends in its tray spot. Launch right after the last part; the rocket is visible during the count, the whole flight and landing, and the astronaut appears. Repeat with reduced motion and with a rotation in each phase.

The PR for issue [#183](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/183) reports a Node simulation with a stub DOM (placement, wrong drops, launch, the full timeline, reset, reduced motion, cleanup); no visual check was possible.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- Look and feel of the part drawings, the flight scene and the astronaut, and the layout on real devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- [Rakieta](rakieta.md), [Koparka](koparka.md).
- Uses `window.Rand.shuffle` and `window.Analytics`.

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#183](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/183): initial activity.
- Issue [#208](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/208): placed parts and the rocket were invisible because the part groups in the rocket SVG were never filled; they are now filled on placement.
- PR [#229](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/229) feedback: tray parts are grouped by kind (column per kind in portrait, row per kind in landscape); variants shuffled within a group.
- PR [#229](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/229) feedback: the Moon surface appeared right after take-off (it started over the screen and covered the sky); the sky now stays blue, darkens into stars (progress 0.2-0.65), and the Moon slides in from above the screen only after progress 0.7.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/zegar-z-kukulka.md`

```markdown
# Zegar z Kukułką

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Zegar z Kukułką |
| Activity ID | `kukulka` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A wooden cuckoo clock on a pastel wall with a clock face (two hands), a swinging pendulum and three little doors; a bird, a mouse and a bear come out of the doors when touched. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, exploratory |
| Interaction type | Tap (doors, hands, pendulum) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |

Source: [`js/kukulka.js`](../../js/kukulka.js), CSS prefix `kk-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html). Introduced by issue #101 / PR [#166](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/166). Note that the file name is `zegar-z-kukulka.md` but the activity ID and script are `kukulka`.

## 2. Business purpose

- A small "surprise" scene: three separate things to touch, each with a clear, slow response (a door opens and a character waves; the hands turn; the pendulum swings wider).
- Characters are told apart by shape (bird: beak and tuft; mouse: big round ears, thin tail and pointed snout; bear: small ears), not by colour alone.
- Differs from the playground scenes ([Karuzela](karuzela.md), [Zjeżdżalnia](zjezdzalnia.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md)) by having several independent touch targets that can run at the same time.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; `mount(container)` builds the scene and starts the loop immediately.
2. The clock shows the hands at about 10:10, the pendulum swings at its normal amplitude, and the three doors (top, left, right) are closed.
3. The child can touch a door, the clock face (hands), or the pendulum.
4. Door: opens (1 s), the character rises (0.6 s), waves twice (1.8 s), sinks (0.6 s), the door closes (1 s): 5 s in total. Hands: the minute hand turns 90 degrees slowly. Pendulum: swings wider for 4 s.
5. There is no completion state.
6. After a door sequence ends the door can be touched again; hands and pendulum can be touched at any time.
7. A new scene starts each time the activity is opened; there is nothing to restart.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Element | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Doors | Top (bird) at board (200, 62), left (mouse) at (50, 196), right (bear) at (350, 196). Timeline per door: open 1 s (`T_OPEN`), character out 0.6 s (`T_OUT`), wave 1.8 s (`T_WAVE`, two waves), back in 0.6 s (`T_IN`), close 1 s (`T_CLOSE`); total `T_ALL` = 5 s. The door leaf is scaled horizontally to 8% about its hinge (left hinge for top and left doors, right hinge for the bear door). |
| Busy door | Touching a door that is already running does nothing (no restart). Different doors run independently and can be open at the same time. |
| Character | Slides from y = 100 to y = `UP` = 56 of the door box (44 units) with smoothstep easing, so the roughly 43-unit body fills the 56-unit opening with its top at y = 13, below the upper edge at y = 8; shown only while it is out. It is clipped by a rectangle that ends at y = 60 of the 72-unit door box, so it appears to emerge from the opening. |
| Minute hand | Each touch adds 90 degrees to the target (`minTarget`); touches queue (no limit). Motion is slew-limited: acceleration `HAND_ACC` = 45 degrees/s^2, maximum `HAND_MAX` = 30 degrees/s, with deceleration so it arrives smoothly; it never moves backwards. |
| Hour hand | Follows at 1/12 of the minute hand's rotation. Start angles: minute 60, hour 305 degrees clockwise from 12 (about 10:10). |
| Pendulum | Period `PERIOD` = 2.4 s; normal amplitude `AMP0` = 11 degrees. A touch sets the target to `AMP1` = 24 degrees for `BOOST_T` = 4 s, then back to 11; amplitude eases with rate `AMP_EASE` = 1.6 per second. |

- No sound, scoring, failure or time-of-day logic: the clock does not show the real time and does not strike.
- Touching a character above a door does not trigger anything; only the door box is a button (noted in PR [#166](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/166)).

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect across three different controls.
- Calm observation of slow, regular motion (pendulum, hands) and of a short "peek-a-boo" sequence.
- Telling characters apart by shape.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Doors, hands and pendulum respond to a touch with slow, eased movement and cannot be restarted or broken by repeated touches.
- The hour hand moves with the minute hand, in the correct 1:12 ratio.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- The clock does not teach reading time (it does not show or ask for a time). Any benefit for time understanding, attention or development is not established by the code and is not claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** `click` on `<button>` elements, so touch, mouse, stylus and keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space) all work. No gestures or multi-touch.
- **Targets:** door buttons `max(64, 72k)` px square; hands button `max(56, 92k)` px circle over the clock face; pendulum button `max(56, 96k)` x `max(56, 76k)` px centred at (200, 240).
- **Labels:** "Górne drzwiczki – otwórz", "Lewe drzwiczki – otwórz", "Prawe drzwiczki – otwórz", "Wskazówki – przekręć", "Wahadło – pchnij"; the scene SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible` outline 4px `#8f7fd1`.
- **Orientation:** the board keeps its 400:300 ratio and is sized `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 400/300)`; works in portrait (smaller) and landscape.
- **Colour:** doors have different leaf colours but the three characters differ by shape.
- **Reduced motion:** all motion is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop and is therefore not disabled by the global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule; there is no separate reduced-motion variant (the motion is slow and bounded). Note the pendulum swings continuously even without touch.
- **Reading:** none required; usable independently by a young child (door labels are for assistive technology only).
- **Limitation:** the tiny clock tick marks have no numerals, and nothing communicates the time to assistive technology.

## 7. Risks and limitations

- Continuous gentle motion: the pendulum always swings and the loop never stops while the activity is open.
- The hands target can accumulate many queued quarter turns if the child taps repeatedly; the hand keeps turning slowly (max 30 degrees/s) until it catches up.
- Characters rise only until fully visible in the opening (`UP` = 56); the top of a bird or mouse stays below the door's upper edge (fixed on `main`, issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)).
- Visual check in a real browser is not documented.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in [`js/kukulka.js`](../../js/kukulka.js) and require a code change. Nothing is stored; no fallback logic.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BW` x `BH` | 400 x 300 | Board units |
| `FX`, `FY`, `FR` | 200, 150, 46 | Clock face centre and radius |
| `PX`, `PY`, `PL` | 200, 204, 58 | Pendulum pivot and rod length |
| `PERIOD` | 2.4 s | Pendulum period |
| `AMP0`, `AMP1`, `BOOST_T`, `AMP_EASE` | 11, 24 degrees, 4 s, 1.6 per s | Pendulum amplitudes, boost time, easing |
| `HAND_ACC`, `HAND_MAX` | 45 deg/s^2, 30 deg/s | Minute hand slew limits |
| `MIN0`, `HOUR0` | 60, 305 degrees | Starting hand angles |
| `T_OPEN`, `T_OUT`, `T_WAVE`, `T_IN`, `T_CLOSE` | 1, 0.6, 1.8, 0.6, 1 s | Door timeline (total 5 s) |
| `UP` | 56 | Feet height of an emerged character in door units (rest position is 100) |
| `DOOR_MIN` | 64 px | Minimum door button size |
| `DOORS` | 3 entries | Door id, position, label, character, leaf colour, hinge side |
| `MAX_DT` | 0.05 s | Frame time cap |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The wall, clock case, face, hands, pendulum, doors and the three characters are inline SVG generated by `scene()`, `doorSvg()` and `characterSvg()`. This activity does not use [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js). The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

Nothing is randomized. The doors, characters and starting hand positions are fixed; every visit is identical. There are no variants.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression or levels. The hand and pendulum state is transient and not stored.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- No completion state; open-ended.
- Feedback is visual only: door leaf, character slide, wave, hand rotation, pendulum amplitude.
- No failure or retry; touching a busy door is silently ignored. No sound. Nothing starts automatically except the pendulum swing.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` assigned to the registry entry `kukulka`; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** one background SVG (`viewBox 0 0 400 300`) with the wall, case, face, hands (`.kk-hour`, `.kk-min`) and pendulum (`.kk-pend`); three door buttons each containing a 72 x 72 SVG (frame, character group `.kk-ch`, leaf `.kk-leaf`); two transparent buttons for the hands and the pendulum.
- **State:** `doors[]` (each with a timer `t`, -1 when idle), `minCur`/`minTarget`/`minVel`, `amp`/`ampTarget`/`boost`/`phase`.
- **Animation:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`/`paint`) with capped dt that runs for the whole time the activity is mounted (never idles) and is cancelled while `document.hidden`.
- **Events:** `click` on the door, hands and pendulum buttons; `resize`/`orientationchange` call `layout()`.
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the window/document listeners and removes the root node.
- **Dependencies:** none other than the registry. No persistence or analytics integration. See [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board 400 x 300 units, scale `k = board.clientWidth / 400`.
- The background SVG, the hand angles and the pendulum rotation use board units directly; the buttons are placed with `place(el, cx, cy, w, h)` from board centres times `k`, with minimum pixel sizes (64 px doors, 56 px others).
- Door SVGs use their own 72-unit viewBox with `overflow: visible`, so characters can extend outside the door box.
- Portrait and landscape use the same aspect-ratio rule; `layout()` re-runs on resize and orientation change.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/orientation change: `layout()` repositions buttons; door timelines and hand state continue.
- Backgrounding: the loop is cancelled while hidden and restarted with a fresh `last`; dt capped at 0.05 s.
- Rapid repeated input: a busy door ignores touches; repeated hand touches queue extra 90 degree steps; repeated pendulum touches restart the 4 s boost.
- Interrupted animation: not applicable (sequences cannot be interrupted).
- Missing assets / empty pools: not applicable (inline SVG).
- The clip path ids (`kk-clip-0..2`) are unique per door within one mount; if the activity were mounted twice the ids would repeat (not reachable in the app).

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#166](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/166) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation that verified the door timeline (leaf scale, character slide, no restart on a second touch), the hands (+90 degrees, at most 30 degrees/s, no backward motion) and the pendulum (11 to about 24 to 11 degrees), and states that no browser was available.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: touch each door in turn; it opens in about 1 s, the character rises, waves twice, sinks and the door closes; the whole sequence takes about 5 s.
- [ ] Touch all three doors quickly; they run at the same time.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch a door that is already open or moving; nothing restarts. Touch the character above a door; nothing happens.
- [ ] Hands: touch the face; the minute hand turns 90 degrees slowly and the hour hand follows; tap several times quickly and check that the hand never moves backwards or faster than about 30 degrees/s.
- [ ] Pendulum: touch it; the swing widens for about 4 s and eases back.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no end state.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and re-enter; doors are closed and the hands are at the start position (about 10:10).
- [ ] Randomization: confirm nothing varies between visits.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape on phone and tablet; rotate during a door sequence; targets remain at least 56 px (doors 64 px).
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard Tab and Enter/Space on all five buttons.
- [ ] Background the tab during a door sequence and return; the sequence continues without a jump.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: doors, hands and pendulum still move.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; no documented real-device verification.
- Only the door box is touchable; touching the character does nothing.
- The animation loop never idles.

**Requires verification**

- How the characters look at the clip edge on real devices (clip at y = 60 of 72 units).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned.

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar multi-target scenes: [Karuzela](karuzela.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md) (pendulum motion), [Wiatraczki](wiatraczki.md).
- Shared components: none; `js/animals.js` and `js/random.js` are not used.

## 21. Change history

- Issue #101, PR [#166](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/166): activity added (commit 519a854).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): fixed on `main`; the emerging character rises only to `UP` = 56 so it is fully visible in the opening.

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/zjezdzalnia.md`

```markdown
# Zjeżdżalnia

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Zjeżdżalnia |
| Activity ID | `zjezdzalnia` (`js/activities.js`) |
| Description | A pastel playground with a ladder, a slide, a soft mat, a bench and three different animals. Touching an animal sends it up the ladder and down the slide. |
| Category | Open-ended play, cause and effect, calm observation |
| Interaction type | Tap (animals, mat) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default (no `defaultOff`) |

Source: [`js/zjezdzalnia.js`](../../js/zjezdzalnia.js), CSS prefix `zj-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html). Introduced by issue #97 / PR [#160](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/160).

## 2. Business purpose

- Gives the child a small, predictable story that they trigger themselves: an animal queues, climbs, slides and returns.
- Several animals can be sent at once and take turns, so the child sees a queue form and drain without any possibility of failure.
- Complements [Karuzela](karuzela.md) and [Huśtawka](hustawka.md) as a playground scene whose motion is a one-shot sequence per touch rather than a continuous ride.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; `mount(container)` builds the scene.
2. Three different animals stand at their "home" spots at the right of the ladder; the slide and mat are empty.
3. The child can touch an animal, or the mat.
4. A touched ready animal joins the queue and walks to the ladder foot; when the slide is free it climbs (3 s), pauses at the top (1 s), slides (4 s), lands on the mat with a squash (0.9 s), walks home and rests (3 s).
5. There is no completion state; after resting the animal is ready again.
6. The child can send the same or other animals again without limit.
7. A new scene with a new animal selection is created each time the activity is opened.
8. The child leaves with the Back button (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)).

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Animal states | `ready`, `queued`, `climb`, `top`, `slide`, `land`, `walk`, `rest`, then back to `ready`. |
| Touch a `ready` animal | Becomes `queued` and is appended to the queue. |
| Touch an animal in any other state | It waves for `WAVE_T` = 1.6 s (raised paw); its path and state are not changed. |
| One on the slide | Only one animal is in climb/top/slide/land at a time (`active`). The queue head starts climbing only once it has reached the ladder foot (`FOOT_X`) and `active` is empty. |
| Durations | Climb 3 s (`CLIMB_T`), top pause 1 s (`TOP_T`), slide 4 s (`SLIDE_T`), land squash 0.9 s (`LAND_T`), rest 3 s (`REST_T`). |
| Walking | `WALK` = 55 board units per second, straight line to the target at ground height `GY` = 262, with a small tilt wobble (3 degrees). |
| Queue spots | While the slide is busy: first waiting animal at x = 116, others at x = 176 (`QS`); when idle the head goes to the foot x = 56. Homes: x = 149, 209, 269 (`HOME`). Spots are 60 units apart. |
| Climb easing | `p = 0.6u + 0.4 smoothstep(u)` along the ladder line from (56, 262) to (96, 96). |
| Slide path | Quadratic Bezier P0 (96, 96), P1 (235, 175), P2 (335, 252), parameter `q = 0.65u + 0.35 smoothstep(u)` (never stalls); tilt follows the tangent at half strength. The drawn slide band covers the curve up to 0.9 (`SLIDE_END`). |
| Landing | Horizontal squash up to +12%, vertical -18%; the mat dips by about 3 px while the animal lands. |
| Touch the mat | The mat bounces up to `MAT_BOUNCE_PX` = 6 px over `BOUNCE_T` = 0.7 s. This does not affect animals. |

- No sound, scoring or failure state.
- The active animal is drawn above the others (z-index 6 vs 4).
- The animals are not blocked from overlapping while walking to queue spots; spacing of 60 units keeps overlap small.

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect: a touch triggers a visible sequence.
- Calm observation of a slow routine (climb, slide, return).
- Informal turn-taking: animals wait in a queue.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Animals queue in touch order and only one uses the slide at a time.
- Touching a busy animal only waves; it never interrupts the path.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any effect on patience, social understanding or development is not established by the code and is not claimed.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** the animals and the mat are `<button>` elements that react to `click`, so touch, mouse, stylus and keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space) all work. No drag or multi-touch is needed.
- **Targets:** animal buttons are at least 56 px (`max(56, 60 * k)` wide, `max(56, 80 * k)` high); the mat button is at least 56 x 56 px (`max(56, 76 * k)` x `max(56, 40 * k)`).
- **Labels:** animal buttons have `aria-label` "<name> – wejdź na zjeżdżalnię"; the mat button "Mata – podskocz". Decorative SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible` outline 4px `#8f7fd1`.
- **Orientation:** the board keeps its 440:300 aspect ratio and is sized `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 440/300)`; works in portrait and landscape (in portrait the scene is simply smaller).
- **Colour:** no meaning is carried by colour alone; animals differ by shape and name.
- **Reduced motion:** all movement is driven by a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so it is not disabled by the global rule; the activity does not offer a calmer variant for users who prefer reduced motion (speeds are already slow).
- **Reading:** none required; a young child can use it independently.
- **Limitation:** the animal buttons have no hint to a screen reader of their current state (queued, climbing, etc.).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- On a narrow portrait screen the sprites are clamped to 56 px while the 60-unit spacing scales down, so neighbouring animals can overlap slightly (noted in PR [#160](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/160)). Not verified on real devices.
- A queued animal may walk through other animals' spots; there is no collision avoidance.
- An animal that is resting cannot be queued again until its 3 s rest ends (touching it only waves).
- Visual check in a real browser is not documented.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration; constants live in [`js/zjezdzalnia.js`](../../js/zjezdzalnia.js) and need a code change. Nothing is stored; no fallback logic.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BW` x `BH` | 440 x 300 | Board units |
| `GY`, `FOOT_X`, `TOP_X`, `TOP_Y` | 262, 56, 96, 96 | Ground line, ladder foot x, ladder top |
| `QS`, `HOME` | [116, 176], [149, 209, 269] | Queue spots and home spots |
| `P0`, `P1`, `P2` | (96, 96), (235, 175), (335, 252) | Slide Bezier |
| `CLIMB_T`, `TOP_T`, `SLIDE_T`, `LAND_T`, `REST_T` | 3, 1, 4, 0.9, 3 s | Phase durations |
| `WAVE_T`, `BOUNCE_T` | 1.6 s, 0.7 s | Wave and mat bounce |
| `WALK` | 55 units/s | Walking speed |
| `MAT_BOUNCE_PX` | 6 px | Mat bounce height |
| `SLIDE_END` | 0.9 | Share of the curve drawn as the slide band |
| `MAX_DT` | 0.05 s | Frame time cap |

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. The scene (sky gradient, clouds, hills, bench, posts, ladder, deck, slide band, mat) is generated as inline SVG by `scene()`; the animals are inline SVG built from `Animals.head(id, { body: true })` plus feet and a paw circle in `figure()`. The menu icon is inline SVG in `js/activities.js`. No fonts, audio or images.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- `Animals.pick(3, { distinct: true })` on every `mount`: three unique animals, preferring different silhouette groups (see [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js), [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)). The pool has 13 animals.
- Not persisted; the same animals can reappear on a later visit.
- Home positions are assigned in the picked order. Nothing else is random.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

No progression or difficulty. Nothing persists between sessions.

## 12. Completion and feedback

- No completion state; open-ended.
- Feedback is visual only: movement, squash on landing, mat dip and bounce, waving paw.
- No failure or retry. No sound. Nothing starts automatically; each cycle needs a touch.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` assigned to the registry entry `zjezdzalnia`; returns a cleanup function.
- **Rendering:** a fixed DOM: `.zj-board` containing one background SVG (`viewBox 0 0 440 300`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`), the mat button and three animal buttons. Animals are moved with CSS `transform` set from JS each frame (`paint()`).
- **State:** closure variables: `animals[]` (each with `state`, `x`, `y`, `t`, wave timer `wv`, tilt/squash), `queue[]`, `active`, `matT`.
- **Animation:** a `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`frame`) with capped dt that stops itself when nothing is busy (`busy` false) and restarts via `start()` on a touch. Paused while `document.hidden`; resumed by `visibilitychange`.
- **Events:** `click` on animals and the mat; `resize`/`orientationchange` call `layout()` (scale `k = board width / 440`, sprite and mat sizes).
- **Cleanup:** cancels the frame, removes the window/document listeners and removes the root node.
- **Dependencies:** `window.Animals`. No persistence or analytics integration. See [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- Board: 440 x 300 units, aspect ratio fixed by CSS, scale `k = board.clientWidth / 440`.
- Animals are feet-anchored: position (x, y) in board units times `k`, with the transform origin at the feet; the sprite box is `max(56, 60k)` x `max(56, 80k)` px.
- The background SVG and the mat button share the same board space (mat button centred at (335, 258) units).
- On resize or orientation change `layout()` recomputes `k` and repaints; an animal mid-slide is just redrawn at its board position.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

- Resize/orientation change: handled as above; animations continue.
- Backgrounding: loop is cancelled while hidden and resumed with a fresh `last`; dt is capped at 0.05 s.
- Rapid repeated touches: a second touch on a non-ready animal only waves; a queued animal cannot be queued twice.
- Interrupted animation: not applicable; paths are never altered once started.
- Mid-queue recompute: queue slots are recomputed every frame, so changes when the slide frees up are smooth.
- Missing assets / empty pools: not applicable (inline SVG, 13 animals).
- Unused code: in the landing branch `matT = Math.max(matT, -2)` has no effect (matT is -1 or higher), and the header comment says the mat bounces at most 8 px while the constant is 6 px.

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist (see [shared platform behaviour](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour)). PR [#160](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/160) reports `node --check` and a stub-DOM simulation (single-animal timeline of climb 3 s, 1 s on top, 4 s slide, return home; three queued animals with a repeated touch; mat dy minimum -6) and states that no browser was available.

Manual scenarios (all unchecked):

- [ ] Normal: touch one animal; it walks to the ladder foot, climbs in about 3 s, pauses 1 s, slides in about 4 s, squashes on the mat, walks home and rests about 3 s.
- [ ] Queue: touch all three animals quickly; they take turns, only one is on the ladder or slide at a time.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: touch an animal that is climbing, sliding, queued or walking; it waves and its path is unchanged.
- [ ] Touch the mat; it bounces once by a few pixels without affecting animals.
- [ ] Completion: confirm there is no end state; an animal can be sent again after its rest.
- [ ] Restart: leave with Back and re-enter; fresh scene, usually different animals.
- [ ] Randomization: enter several times; three different animals each time.
- [ ] Progression: confirm there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape on phone and tablet; rotate during a slide; the animal stays on the slide path.
- [ ] Narrow portrait (about 320 px wide): check overlap of animals and the 56 px targets.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard Tab and Enter/Space on animals and mat.
- [ ] Background the tab mid-slide and return; the animation continues without a jump.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.
- [ ] Reduced motion enabled in the OS: animals still move.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- No automated tests; no documented real-device verification.
- The `matT = Math.max(matT, -2)` statement and the "max 8 px" header comment are inconsistent with the code (6 px).
- No collision avoidance between walking animals.

**Requires verification**

- Overlap of sprites on very narrow portrait screens (PR #160 notes this as a review focus).

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (no open issue targets this activity).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Similar scenes: [Karuzela](karuzela.md), [Huśtawka](hustawka.md), [Latawiec](latawiec.md).
- Shared helpers: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.pick`, `Animals.head`), which uses [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js).

## 21. Change history

- Issue #97, PR [#160](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/160): activity added (commit a83baf2) and a follow-up fix to 60-unit queue spacing and homes clear of the mat (commit 326f441, review suggestions).

```

## File: `child-page-main/docs/activities/zwierzatka-na-farmie.md`

```markdown
# Zwierzątka na Farmie

Platform-wide behaviour (no sound, reduced motion, menu configuration, playtime limit, absence of automated tests, privacy) is described in [README.md](README.md#shared-platform-behaviour); this document only records what is specific to this activity.

## 1. Overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | Zwierzątka na Farmie |
| Activity ID | `farma` (registry entry in [`js/activities.js`](../../js/activities.js)) |
| Description | A pastel farm with a barn and five random animals. Touching an animal makes it react slowly; touching the barn opens its door so that a round face peeks out. |
| Category | Cause and effect; exploratory; open-ended play |
| Interaction type | Tap (touch, mouse, keyboard) |
| Status | Implemented; enabled in the menu by default |
| Source | [`js/farma.js`](../../js/farma.js), styles with prefix `fm-` in [`css/style.css`](../../css/style.css), script tag in [`index.html`](../../index.html) |

## 2. Business purpose

- Offers a gentle "touch an animal and see how it reacts" toy where every animal has its own small movement (sheep sways, cow nods its head, hen flaps, cat swishes its tail).
- Variety: the five animals are drawn at random from 11, so the farm differs between launches.
- Complements [Mały Pociąg](maly-pociag.md) and [Dobranoc](dobranoc.md), which also use the shared animal family, but with farm-themed reactions and a barn that can be opened.
- Described in the README Activities list as item 12.

## 3. Activity flow

1. The child opens the tile; the farm is built and an animation loop starts.
2. Initially displayed: a pale sky with sun, hills, a fence, a barn on the left and five animals. All animals breathe slowly and blink every few seconds.
3. Interactions: tap an animal or the barn.
4. Response: the animal reacts for 2.6 s (taps meanwhile are ignored); the barn door opens, a face peeks out and the door closes over 4.6 s.
5. There is no completion state.
6. Everything returns to idle by itself and can be tapped again.
7. Restart: leave and re-open for a new random selection and arrangement.
8. Exit: Back button or browser Back.

## 4. Rules and behavior

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Animal reaction | `REACT = 2.6` s, eased with `sin(pi * p)` (smooth in and out). A tap on an animal that is already reacting is ignored. |
| Barn | `BARN = 4.6` s. Door opens during the first 25 %, the face rises between 20 % and 40 %, stays until 60 %, goes down by 75 %, and the door closes from 75 % to 100 %. Door scaling is `1 - 0.88 * door` horizontally; the face rises 26 board units. Taps during the sequence are ignored. |
| Reaction per animal | Sheep: rotates up to 4 degrees back and forth. Cow: head rotates up to 12 degrees. Hen: hops up to 3 units and wings flap up to 14 degrees. Cat: tail swishes up to 22 degrees. Shared-family animals (dog, pig, rabbit, mouse, frog, bear, fox): rotate up to 4 degrees and hop up to 2 units. |
| Idle | Breathing: vertical scale `1 + 0.018 * sin(1.3 * t + phase)` (random phase). Blinking: the first blink after 2 to 5 s, then every 3 to 6 s, lasting 0.18 s. Cow and barn have no breathing or blinking (the cow's SVG has no `fm-body` or `fm-eyes` group). |
| Peeking face | A generic round cream face with eyes and a mouth, not one of the five animals on screen. |
| Sound | None. |

## 5. Educational and developmental benefits

**Intended design benefits**

- Cause and effect with different results for different animals.
- Noticing and naming animals (labels are Polish names).
- Calm observation of slow movement.

**Directly observable behavior**

- Each animal reacts in its own way after touch; the barn door opens and closes slowly.
- Taps on empty space do nothing; no failure or score.

**Requires professional or research-based validation**

- Any claim about animal recognition or vocabulary. Nothing in the code can establish it.

## 6. Accessibility and usability

- **Input:** all 6 interactive elements are native `<button>`s using the `click` event; touch, mouse and keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space) work.
- **Labels (Polish):** hand-drawn animals "Owieczka", "Krowa", "Kura", "Kotek"; barn "Stodoła"; shared animals use the name from `js/animals.js`. There is no state announcement.
- **Target sizes:** buttons are square, `min-width/min-height: 56px`; widths are 10 to 27 % of the board for animals (by size class, see section 10) and 32 % for the barn; the 56 px minimum still applies on narrow boards (see section 15).
- **Layout:** 4:3 board fitted into the viewport (with padding for the Back button and safe areas); works in portrait and landscape (a smaller board in portrait).
- **Colour:** nothing depends on colour.
- **Reduced motion:** all idle and reaction movement is driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` loop and `transform`s, so it survives the global reduced-motion rule.
- **Touch:** `touch-action: manipulation`.
- **Reading:** not required. A young child can use it independently.
- **Animal sizes:** drawn width follows the animal's real-life size class (`SIZE`), so a small animal never looks bigger than a clearly larger one (fixed via issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) item 5 / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)).

## 7. Risks and limitations

- A loop that runs continuously (breathing and blinking), even when nothing was touched; on slow devices this is constant work (requires verification).
- Animal sizes follow a fixed size table (`SIZE`); animals of similar size (for example pig and sheep, both 19 %) are drawn equally large.
- The five hit areas can overlap slightly (see section 18).
- No ending; relies on the global playtime limit.
- No privacy concerns; nothing is stored.

## 8. Configuration

No external configuration. Constants in [`js/farma.js`](../../js/farma.js):

| Constant | Purpose | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `REACT` | Animal reaction duration | 2.6 s |
| `BARN` | Barn sequence duration | 4.6 s |
| `MAXDT` | Frame time cap | 0.05 s |
| `HAND` | Hand-drawn animals | sheep, cow, hen, cat |
| `SHARED` | Animals drawn by `Animals.head` | dog, pig, rabbit, mouse, frog, bear, fox |
| `BARN_POS` | Barn left, top, width (percent of board) | 3, 14, 32 |
| `SLOTS` | Animal slots (left, top, width in percent); an animal keeps its slot's centre and ground line but is drawn at its own `SIZE` width | (38,36,30), (79,36,18), (4,58,26), (64,66,20), (40,74,16) |
| `SLOT_ORDER` | Order in which animals, sorted from largest to smallest, take the slots (indexes into `SLOTS`) | 0, 2, 3, 1, 4 |
| `SIZE` | Drawn width (percent of the board) by animal; mouse is 48 % of the dog | mouse 10, frog 11, hen 13, rabbit 14, cat 16, fox 17, sheep 19, pig 19, dog 21, bear 25, cow 27 |

Fallback: none; `window.Animals` is required for the shared animals and `window.Rand` for the selection, and neither is checked for being absent.

## 9. Assets

No external asset files. Hand-drawn animals (`SVG.sheep`, `SVG.cow`, `SVG.hen`, `SVG.cat`), the barn (`SVG.barn`) and the backdrop (`BACKDROP`: sky, sun, hills, fence, `viewBox="0 0 400 300"`) are inline SVG strings in the JavaScript. The seven shared animals come from `Animals.head(id, { body: true, eyesClass: 'fm-eyes' })` in [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js), scaled by 1.2. No images, fonts or audio.

## 10. Randomization and variants

- `window.Rand.pick(HAND.concat(SHARED), 5)` selects **5 unique animals from 11** ([`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js)): 462 possible sets. The five picks are then sorted by `SIZE` (largest first) and assigned to the slots in the order `SLOT_ORDER`, so the biggest animals take the biggest slots; which animals appear is random, their positions follow from their sizes. Small, medium, medium-large and large classes: small (mouse, frog, hen, rabbit) < medium (cat, fox, sheep, pig) < dog < large (bear, cow).
- The barn and backdrop are fixed.
- Random breathing phase and blink timing per animal.
- Nothing is stored; there is no guard against the same selection on consecutive launches.

## 11. Progression and difficulty

None. There are no levels or persistence.

## 12. Completion and feedback

There is no completion state and no failure. Feedback is the animal's own reaction, or the barn door and the peeking face. No sound; nothing starts automatically except the idle breathing and blinking.

## 13. Analytics and metrics

This activity reports to the shared on-device module `js/analytics.js` (`window.Analytics`) through the app shell only: `js/app.js` records the activity start and end, and the module counts touches inside the stage. The activity file itself calls no `Analytics` function. Recorded for it: starts, active time, replays (re-opening in the same session), quick exits (within 10 s) and touches. It is open-ended, so no completion, level or exit-before-completion is defined for it. Data stays on the device as anonymous daily aggregates; see [README.md](README.md#analytics-status).

## 14. Technical implementation

- **Entry point:** `mount(container)` in [`js/farma.js`](../../js/farma.js); sets `container.style.display = 'block'` (not restored; `app.js` empties the stage on exit). The cleanup function removes the `visibilitychange` listener, cancels the frame and removes the scene.
- **Rendering:** a `div.fm-board` with the backdrop SVG and 6 absolutely positioned `<button>`s (barn plus 5 animals), each containing an SVG; percent-based `left`, `top`, `width`. Fixed DOM; nothing is added or removed after mount.
- **State:** per figure `t` (reaction time, -1 when idle), breathing phase, blink timer, references to its SVG parts.
- **Loop:** `frame()` with `dt` capped at 0.05 s sets `transform`s on the SVG groups (`transform-origin` set from JavaScript). It re-requests itself on every frame while the tab is visible (it does not stop when idle); it is cancelled when the tab is hidden and restarted by `wake()`.
- **Events:** `click` on each button; `visibilitychange`.
- **Shared code:** `Rand.pick`, `Animals.head`, `Animals.byId`, `Animals.eyes`.
- **Persistence:** none. **Analytics:** through the app shell only (section 13).

## 15. Responsive layout and coordinate system

- The board is 4:3, width `min(100%, (100dvh - safe areas - 64px) * 4 / 3)`. Buttons are positioned in percent of the board (left, top, width) and are square (`aspect-ratio: 1`), so their height is `width * 4/3` of the board height in percent terms.
- The backdrop is an SVG with `preserveAspectRatio="none"` in the same 4:3 box, so it aligns with the buttons.
- Each figure SVG uses `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`; the reaction animations use SVG units (for example a 26-unit rise of the barn face).
- Portrait and landscape share one layout; the 56 px minimum size can make buttons larger than their percentage on narrow boards.

## 16. Error and edge-case handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tap during a reaction | Ignored. |
| Tab hidden | Loop cancelled; restarted on return with `last = 0`, so no catch-up. |
| Resize / orientation | CSS only. |
| Pool smaller than 5 | Not applicable (11 animals available). |
| Leaving mid-reaction | Cleanup cancels the frame. |
| `window.Animals` / `window.Rand` missing | Not handled. |

## 17. Testing

No automated tests exist. Manual scenarios (none are claimed as done):

- [ ] Normal: open the activity; five animals and the barn are visible; animals breathe and blink; tap each animal; it reacts for about 2.6 s.
- [ ] Tap an animal repeatedly during its reaction; extra taps are ignored and nothing breaks.
- [ ] Barn: tap the barn; the door opens, a face peeks out and the door closes over about 4.6 s; extra taps are ignored.
- [ ] Incorrect interaction: tap the sky, hills and fence; nothing happens.
- [ ] Restart/randomization: re-open the activity about 15 times; the five animals and their positions vary; no duplicate animal in one scene; all 11 animals can appear.
- [ ] Progression: confirm that there is none.
- [ ] Portrait and landscape; rotate on a running reaction.
- [ ] Hit areas: tap the overlapping edges of neighbouring animals (see section 18) and confirm which one reacts.
- [ ] Small screens: every animal is at least 56 px and reachable.
- [ ] Touch and mouse; keyboard (Tab through all 6 buttons, Enter/Space activates, focus ring visible).
- [ ] Background/foreground: switch tab during a reaction; it continues without a jump.
- [ ] Reduced motion: idle movement and reactions still play.
- [ ] Browsers: Chrome desktop, Chrome Android, Safari iPhone/iPad.

PR [#42](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/42) reports a Node run of the loop against a DOM stub and lists manual browser tests as pending. PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137) lists the fifth slot on narrow portrait screens and the visual fit of larger animals as pending manual checks.

## 18. Known limitations and open issues

**Confirmed**

- Animal sizes follow the `SIZE` table (fixed on `main`: item 5 of issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167), PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173)); the former problem of a mouse drawn larger than a dog no longer exists.
- The peeking face in the barn is a generic cream face, not one of the displayed animals (`A.barn.who` is set but never read).
- The cow neither breathes nor blinks (its SVG lacks the `fm-body` and `fm-eyes` groups).
- Hit boxes can still overlap. Computed from `SLOTS`, `SLOT_ORDER` and `SIZE` over all 462 possible animal sets, the largest animal (slot 1) overlaps the third largest (slot 4) by at most about 3 % x 11 % of the board and the smallest (slot 5) by at most about 18 % x 6 %; no other pair, and not the barn, overlaps. The later button in DOM order is on top. The visible artwork may not fill the boxes (requires verification).
- The animation loop never idles while the activity is open.
- No automated tests.

**Requires verification**

- The fifth slot on narrow portrait screens (pending manual check in PR #137).
- Constant frame work on low-end devices.

## 19. Planned improvements

None currently planned (the animal size classes from issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) are done, see section 21).

## 20. Related activities and reusable components

- Other activities with the shared animal family: [Mały Pociąg](maly-pociag.md), [Dobranoc](dobranoc.md), [Zabawa w Chowanego](zabawa-w-chowanego.md), [Cienie](cienie.md), [Buźki](buzki.md), [Autobusik](autobusik.md).
- Shared helpers: [`js/animals.js`](../../js/animals.js) (`Animals.head`, `Animals.byId`, `Animals.eyes`) and [`js/random.js`](../../js/random.js) (`Rand.pick`).

## 21. Change history

- Issue [#32](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/32) / PR [#42](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/42): initial activity (sheep, cow, hen, cat and barn).
- Issue [#66](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/66) / PR [#68](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/68): the barn door's X is part of the door group, so it scales with the door.
- Issue [#113](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/113) / PR [#137](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/137): five random animals from a wider pool (shared family added); the pool was later widened to 11 (commit `a312c6d`).
- Issue [#167](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/issues/167) / PR [#173](https://github.com/BielinskiLukasz/child-page/pull/173): animals are drawn by real-life size class and the biggest take the biggest slots.
```

```javascript
// Activity "Aport": a park with a dog of a random breed (window.Dogs) and a ball. The child drags the ball and lets go; the ball lands
// in a short arc (0.8 s) at the release point (clamped inside the grass), the dog runs to it on a curved path (speed never above 60% of
// the screen width per second), picks it up and brings it back to its starting spot, where it sits and wags; one fetch takes 3-6 s.
// Throwing again while the dog is running redirects it smoothly (velocity is kept, only the target changes). Tapping the dog switches
// to another random breed with a sparkle. After 3 fetches in a row the dog spins happily and a heart rises (no counter).
// Positions are fractions of the grass area (rotation-safe); one capped-dt rAF loop that pauses while hidden and stops when idle.
// Keyboard: Tab to the ball, arrows move a ring, Enter/Space throws the ball to the ring; Tab to the dog, Enter/Space changes breed.

  var DIP_DEG = 30, CATCH_S = 0.2, HELD = 0.6;   // head dip at the catch, ball-to-mouth time, size of the held ball
```

```javascript
(function () {
  var menu = document.getElementById('menu-view');
  var view = document.getElementById('activity-view');
  var stage = document.getElementById('stage');
  var tiles = document.getElementById('tiles');
  var favTiles = document.getElementById('fav-tiles');
  var favHead = document.getElementById('fav-head');
  var backBtn = document.getElementById('back');
  var cleanup = null;
  var currentId = null;
  var pushedByApp = false;
  var lastTile = null;
  var menuScroll = 0;

  function byId(id) {
    return window.ACTIVITIES.filter(function (a) { return a.id === id; })[0];
  }

  function addTile(parent, a) {
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    var btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.type = 'button';
    btn.className = 'tile';
    btn.innerHTML = a.icon + '<span></span>';
    btn.lastChild.textContent = a.name;
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
      lastTile = btn;
      menuScroll = window.pageYOffset || 0;
      if (location.hash !== '#' + a.id) { pushedByApp = true; location.hash = a.id; }
    });
    li.appendChild(btn);
    parent.appendChild(li);
  }

  // Tiles are the enabled activities in the parent-configured order (see menu-config.js); parent-starred
  // ones go in the "Ulubione" section above and are not repeated below.
  function buildTiles() {
    tiles.textContent = '';
    favTiles.textContent = '';
    lastTile = null;
    var favs = window.MenuConfig.favouriteActivities();
    var isFav = {};
    favs.forEach(function (a) { isFav[a.id] = true; addTile(favTiles, a); });
    window.MenuConfig.enabledActivities().forEach(function (a) {
      if (!isFav[a.id]) { addTile(tiles, a); }
    });
    favHead.hidden = favTiles.hidden = favs.length === 0;
    tiles.hidden = tiles.children.length === 0;
  }
  buildTiles();
  document.addEventListener('menuconfig', buildTiles);
  window.addEventListener('storage', function (e) { if (e.key === 'swa.menu') { buildTiles(); } });

  function unmount() {
    window.Analytics.activityEnd();
    window.Playtime.stop();
    if (typeof cleanup === 'function') { cleanup(); }
    cleanup = null;
    currentId = null;
    stage.textContent = '';
  }

  // Renders whatever the URL hash says; hash changes give browser Back for free, no reload.
  function render() {
    var a = byId(location.hash.replace(/^#\/?/, ''));
    // A disabled activity cannot be opened by any route: fall back to the menu.
    if (a && !window.MenuConfig.isEnabled(a.id)) { a = null; }
    if (a && a.id === currentId) { return; }
    unmount();
    if (!a) {
      view.hidden = true;
      menu.hidden = false;
      pushedByApp = false;
      // Restore the menu's scroll position (it collapses while hidden) before focusing without scrolling.
      if (lastTile) { lastTile.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }
      window.scrollTo(0, menuScroll);
      return;
    }
    if (!menu.hidden) { menuScroll = window.pageYOffset || 0; }
    menu.hidden = true;
    view.hidden = false;
    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
    currentId = a.id;
    var expired = window.Playtime.isExpired();
    var shownLater = expired;
    window.Playtime.start(function () {
      // Time is up: stop the activity and show the gentle "later" screen; Back/menu stay usable.
      if (shownLater) { return; } // already shown; don't re-render on every tick
      shownLater = true;

    if (expired) {

      cleanup = a.mount(stage) || null;
```

```javascript
// Activity "Autobusik": a little bus loops slowly along a village road with 3 bus stops. Touch the bus -> it starts /
// slows to a halt; touch a stop -> the bus brakes there (only the last touched stop counts), its doors open and the waiting
// animal hops in; touch an animal in a window -> it steps out at the stop (bus stopped) or waves (bus moving).
// All motion is driven by one rAF loop (capped dt, paused when the tab is hidden) so it keeps working under the global
// prefers-reduced-motion rule that disables CSS animations. The bus position is a loop fraction f (0 = just off the left
// edge, 1 = just off the right edge) so speed and stops stay valid after a resize / orientation change.
(function () {
  var CROSS_S = 24;            // seconds for a full loop at cruise speed (the front crosses the visible width in >= ~14 s)
  var V = 1 / CROSS_S;         // cruise speed, loop fractions per second
  var RAMP_S = 2.2;            // gentle start / slow-down
  var BRAKE_S = 3;             // braking into a stop takes about this long
  var DOOR_S = 1.8;            // doors open / close slowly
  var HOP_S = 1.8, WAVE_S = 2.2;
  var MAX_DT = 0.05;
  var VB_W = 340, VB_H = 110;  // bus viewBox
  var WIN_X = [58, 140, 222];  // window centres in viewBox units (spacing 82/340 of the bus width)
  var STOP_X = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8];

  function sm(u) { return u * u * (3 - 2 * u); }
  function wrap(x) { return x - Math.floor(x); }
  function clamp(x, a, b) { return Math.max(a, Math.min(b, x)); }

  function animalSvg(animal) {
    return '<svg viewBox="-28 -22 56 56" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><g transform="translate(0 6)">' +
      window.Animals.head(animal.id) + '</g></svg>';
  }

  function busSvg() {
    var s = '<svg viewBox="0 0 ' + VB_W + ' ' + VB_H + '" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">' +
      '<rect x="2" y="8" width="336" height="84" rx="22" fill="#ffd98a"/>' +
      '<rect x="2" y="64" width="336" height="8" fill="#fff" opacity=".5"/>' +
      '<rect x="2" y="78" width="336" height="14" rx="7" fill="#f7a8c9"/>';
    WIN_X.forEach(function (x) { s += '<rect x="' + (x - 33) + '" y="20" width="66" height="46" rx="14" fill="#cfeaf7"/>'; });
    // door: dark interior + a panel that slides away (width set from JS)
    s += '<rect x="262" y="24" width="46" height="62" rx="8" fill="#8a84a8"/>' +
      '<rect class="ab-door" x="262" y="24" width="46" height="62" rx="8" fill="#a8d8f0"/>' +
      '<rect x="314" y="26" width="20" height="30" rx="8" fill="#cfeaf7"/>' +
      '<circle cx="330" cy="70" r="5" fill="#fff3b8"/>';
    [70, 270].forEach(function (wx) {
      s += '<g class="ab-wheel" data-cx="' + wx + '"><circle cx="' + wx + '" cy="94" r="13" fill="#6b6585"/>' +
        '<circle cx="' + wx + '" cy="94" r="6.5" fill="#cfc9e6"/><path d="M' + wx + ' 87v14M' + (wx - 7) + ' 94h14" stroke="#6b6585" stroke-width="2.5"/></g>';
    });
    return s + '</svg>';
  }

  function stopSvg() {
    return '<svg viewBox="0 0 60 120" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMax meet" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">' +
      '<rect x="27" y="30" width="6" height="90" rx="3" fill="#8a84a8"/>' +
      '<circle cx="30" cy="26" r="22" fill="#fdfbff" stroke="#a8d8f0" stroke-width="4"/>' +
      '<rect x="17" y="16" width="26" height="15" rx="5" fill="#ffd98a"/><rect x="20" y="19" width="6" height="6" rx="2" fill="#cfeaf7"/>' +
      '<rect x="28" y="19" width="6" height="6" rx="2" fill="#cfeaf7"/><rect x="36" y="19" width="5" height="6" rx="2" fill="#cfeaf7"/>' +
      '<circle cx="23" cy="33" r="3" fill="#6b6585"/><circle cx="38" cy="33" r="3" fill="#6b6585"/></svg>';
  }

  function houseSvg(wall, roof) {
    return '<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMax meet" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">' +
      '<rect x="10" y="40" width="80" height="60" rx="6" fill="' + wall + '"/><path d="M2 44L50 6l48 38z" fill="' + roof + '"/>' +
      '<rect x="42" y="64" width="16" height="36" rx="5" fill="#b9b3e0"/><rect x="18" y="52" width="16" height="16" rx="4" fill="#cfeaf7"/>' +
      '<rect x="66" y="52" width="16" height="16" rx="4" fill="#cfeaf7"/></svg>';
  }

  function treeSvg() {
    return '<svg viewBox="0 0 60 100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMax meet" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">' +
      '<rect x="26" y="60" width="8" height="40" rx="3" fill="#c9a98a"/><circle cx="30" cy="40" r="26" fill="#9fd694"/><circle cx="20" cy="50" r="14" fill="#8cc982"/></svg>';
  }

  function mount(container) {
    var scene = document.createElement('div');
    scene.className = 'ab';
    scene.setAttribute('role', 'group');
    scene.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Autobusik');
    var deco = '<div class="ab-sun"></div><div class="ab-cloud ab-c1"></div><div class="ab-cloud ab-c2"></div>';
    var houses = [[0.07, '#fdf0d5', '#f7b7a5'], [0.35, '#e6e0f7', '#c9b8f2'], [0.65, '#d8ecfb', '#f7a8c9'], [0.93, '#fde3ef', '#ffc9a0']];
    houses.forEach(function (h, i) { deco += '<div class="ab-house" data-x="' + h[0] + '">' + houseSvg(h[1], h[2]) + '</div>'; });
    [0.21, 0.5, 0.79].forEach(function (x) { deco += '<div class="ab-tree" data-x="' + x + '">' + treeSvg() + '</div>'; });
    var stops = '';
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
      stops += '<button class="ab-stop" type="button" data-i="' + i + '" aria-label="Przystanek ' + (i + 1) + ' – zatrzymaj autobusik tutaj">' + stopSvg() + '</button>';
    }
    var animalsHtml = '';
    var picks = window.Animals.pick(3); // one random animal per stop, new on every launch, nothing stored
    for (var k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
      animalsHtml += '<button class="ab-an" type="button" data-i="' + k + '" aria-label="' + picks[k].name + '">' + animalSvg(picks[k]) + '</button>';
    }
    scene.innerHTML = deco + '<div class="ab-sidewalk"></div><div class="ab-road"><div class="ab-dash"></div></div>' + stops +
      '<div class="ab-bus" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Autobusik – ruszaj lub zatrzymaj">' + busSvg() + '</div>' + animalsHtml;
    container.appendChild(scene);

    var bus = scene.querySelector('.ab-bus');
    var door = scene.querySelector('.ab-door');
    var wheels = [].slice.call(scene.querySelectorAll('.ab-wheel'));
    var stopBtns = [].slice.call(scene.querySelectorAll('.ab-stop'));
    var houseEls = [].slice.call(scene.querySelectorAll('.ab-house'));
    var treeEls = [].slice.call(scene.querySelectorAll('.ab-tree'));
    var animals = [].slice.call(scene.querySelectorAll('.ab-an')).map(function (el, i) {
      return { el: el, i: i, stop: i, st: 'wait', t: 0, p0: [0, 0], noBoard: i === 0, wave: -1, x: 0, y: 0 };
    });

    var W = 0, H = 0, bw = 0, bh = 0, L = 1, AS = 56, sy = 0, roadBase = 0, busTop = 0;
    var sx = [0, 0, 0], fs = [0, 0, 0];
    var f = 0, v = 0, odo = 0;
    var ramp = { v0: 0, vt: 0, t: RAMP_S, dur: RAMP_S };
    var brake = null;          // {v0, T, t, f0, sPrev}
    var target = -1;           // stop the child asked for (only the last one counts)
    var skip = false;          // the target was too close to brake for: wait until the bus has gone round
    var go = false;            // doors are closing / animals finishing, then the bus drives off
    var parkedAt = 0;          // stop index the bus stands at, -1 when moving or halted mid-road
    var door1 = 0;             // 0 closed .. 1 open
    var raf = 0, last = 0;

    function layout() {
      W = scene.clientWidth || window.innerWidth;
      H = scene.clientHeight || window.innerHeight;
      bw = Math.min(Math.max(W * 0.64, 240), W * 0.8, 460, H * 0.26 * VB_W / VB_H);
      bh = bw * VB_H / VB_W;
      L = W + bw;
      roadBase = H * 0.88;
      busTop = roadBase - bh;
      sy = H * 0.6;
      AS = Math.max(56, Math.min(76, bw * 0.24));
      for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        sx[i] = W * STOP_X[i];
        var c = clamp(sx[i], bw / 2, W - bw / 2);   // bus centre when stopped: the bus always stays fully on screen
        fs[i] = (c + bw / 2) / L;
      }
      scene.style.setProperty('--sy', sy.toFixed(1) + 'px');
      scene.style.setProperty('--ry', (H * 0.62).toFixed(1) + 'px');
      scene.style.setProperty('--rh', (H * 0.3).toFixed(1) + 'px');
      scene.style.setProperty('--bw', bw.toFixed(1) + 'px');
      scene.style.setProperty('--bh', bh.toFixed(1) + 'px');
      scene.style.setProperty('--as', AS.toFixed(1) + 'px');
      var hh = Math.min(H * 0.22, W * 0.2);
      houseEls.forEach(function (h) {
        h.style.width = h.style.height = hh.toFixed(1) + 'px';
        h.style.left = (parseFloat(h.getAttribute('data-x')) * W - hh / 2).toFixed(1) + 'px';
        h.style.top = (sy - hh).toFixed(1) + 'px';
      });
      treeEls.forEach(function (t) {
        var th = hh * 0.9;
        t.style.width = (th * 0.6).toFixed(1) + 'px'; t.style.height = th.toFixed(1) + 'px';
        t.style.left = (parseFloat(t.getAttribute('data-x')) * W - th * 0.3).toFixed(1) + 'px';
        t.style.top = (sy - th).toFixed(1) + 'px';
      });
      var sh = Math.max(sy * 0.45, 96);
      stopBtns.forEach(function (b, i) {
        b.style.width = Math.max(56, sh * 0.5).toFixed(1) + 'px';
        b.style.height = sh.toFixed(1) + 'px';
        b.style.left = (sx[i] - Math.max(56, sh * 0.5) / 2).toFixed(1) + 'px';
        b.style.top = (sy - sh).toFixed(1) + 'px';

      if (parkedAt >= 0 && v === 0) { f = fs[parkedAt]; }
      else if (brake) { brake = null; ramp = { v0: v, vt: V, t: 0, dur: RAMP_S }; }   // stop moved: re-plan from the current speed, no snap
    }

    function anyHop() { return animals.some(function (a) { return a.st === 'hopin' || a.st === 'hopout'; }); }
    function parkedNow() { return parkedAt >= 0 && v === 0 && !brake; }

    function slotOf(a) {

      animals.forEach(function (b) { if (b.i < a.i && b.stop === a.stop && (b.st === 'wait' || b.st === 'hopout')) { n++; } });

    function waitPos(a) {

    function depart() {

        if (parkedAt >= 0) { go = true; } else { ramp = { v0: 0, vt: V, t: 0, dur: RAMP_S }; target = -1; skip = false; }
      } else {

        go = false; target = -1; skip = false; brake = null;
        ramp = { v0: v, vt: 0, t: 0, dur: RAMP_S };

    }

      if (parkedNow() && parkedAt === j) {
        go = false; target = -1;
        animals.forEach(function (a) { if (a.stop === j) { a.noBoard = false; } });
        return;
      }
      if (target === j) { return; }
      target = j;
      skip = false;
      if (v === 0 && !brake) {
        if (parkedAt >= 0) { go = true; } else { ramp = { v0: 0, vt: V, t: 0, dur: RAMP_S }; }
      } else {
        go = false;
        if (brake) { brake = null; ramp = { v0: v, vt: V, t: 0, dur: RAMP_S }; }
        else if (ramp.vt < V) { ramp = { v0: v, vt: V, t: 0, dur: RAMP_S }; }

      // boarding: one animal at a time, only while the doors are open
      if (parkedNow() && !go && door1 >= 0.95 && !anyHop()) {
        for (var q = 0; q < animals.length; q++) {

        a.el.style.transform = 'translate(' + (p[0] - AS / 2).toFixed(1) + 'px,' + (p[1] - AS / 2).toFixed(1) + 'px) rotate(' + rot.toFixed(1) + 'deg)';

    }

    }

    var offs = [];
    function bind(node, fn) {
      var h = function (e) { e.preventDefault(); fn(); };
      var k = function (e) { if (e.detail === 0) { fn(); } };
      node.addEventListener('pointerdown', h);
      node.addEventListener('click', k);
      offs.push(function () { node.removeEventListener('pointerdown', h); node.removeEventListener('click', k); });
    }
    bind(bus, onBus);
    stopBtns.forEach(function (b, i) { bind(b, function () { onStop(i); }); });
    animals.forEach(function (a) { bind(a.el, function () { onAnimal(a); }); });
    var onKey = function (e) { if ((e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') && e.target === bus) { e.preventDefault(); onBus(); } };
    bus.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    window.addEventListener('resize', layout);
    window.addEventListener('orientationchange', layout);
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVis);

    layout();
    f = fs[0];
    start();

    return function () {
      if (raf) { cancelAnimationFrame(raf); raf = 0; }
      offs.forEach(function (o) { o(); });
      bus.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey);
      window.removeEventListener('resize', layout);
      window.removeEventListener('orientationchange', layout);
      document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVis);
      if (scene.parentNode) { scene.parentNode.removeChild(scene); }
    };
  }

  window.ACTIVITIES.forEach(function (a) { if (a.id === 'autobusik') { a.mount = mount; } });
})();
```

```javascript
// Activity "Balon": a hot-air balloon with two animals in the basket rests on a meadow under a pastel sky with 4 clouds.
// Touch the balloon -> it rises slowly (drifting sideways) or, in the air, floats gently back down; touch a cloud -> it
// drifts aside by about one cloud width and returns over ~8 s; touch an animal -> it waves once.
// Everything is driven by one rAF loop (capped dt, paused when the tab is hidden), so it also works under the global
// prefers-reduced-motion rule that disables CSS animations. Altitude is a fraction a (0 = on the meadow, 1 = top) and
// its speed only ever changes through a limited acceleration, so there are no jerks.

  var VA = 1 / 15;            // cruise climb / descent speed, altitude fractions per second (top third takes >= 12 s)
  var ACC = 0.04;             // max change of that speed per second (full speed in ~1.7 s)

  var VMIN = 0.006;           // creep speed so the end of the way is actually reached
  var DRIFT_T = 40;           // seconds for one sideways drift cycle

        '<ellipse cx="' + (cx - 7) + '" cy="' + (cy - 21) + '" rx="1.8" ry="7" fill="#f7b7cf"/><ellipse cx="' + (cx + 7) + '" cy="' + (cy - 21) + '" rx="1.8" ry="7" fill="#f7b7cf"/>'
      : '<circle cx="' + (cx - 12) + '" cy="' + (cy - 11) + '" r="5.5" fill="' + fur + '"/><circle cx="' + (cx + 12) + '" cy="' + (cy - 11) + '" r="5.5" fill="' + fur + '"/>';
    var nose = kind === 'bear'
      ? '<ellipse cx="' + cx + '" cy="' + (cy + 5) + '" rx="5.5" ry="4" fill="#f3dcc4"/><circle cx="' + cx + '" cy="' + (cy + 3.5) + '" r="1.8" fill="#6b5a73"/>'
      : '<circle cx="' + cx + '" cy="' + (cy + 4) + '" r="1.8" fill="#e99bb5"/>';

      '<circle cx="' + cx + '" cy="' + cy + '" r="14" fill="' + fur + '"/>' +

      '<g class="bn-paw" data-px="' + (cx + 12) + '" data-py="' + (cy + 22) + '"><ellipse cx="' + (cx + 12) + '" cy="' + (cy + 17) + '" rx="4.5" ry="5.5" fill="' + fur + '"/></g>';
  }

  function balloonSvg() {
    return '<svg viewBox="0 0 200 280" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">' +

      '<path d="M100 4C38 4 10 52 14 92C18 126 56 150 72 172H128C144 150 182 126 186 92C190 52 162 4 100 4Z" fill="#f7a8c9"/>' +
      '<path d="M100 4C66 28 52 120 72 172H128C148 120 134 28 100 4Z" fill="#fff3b0"/>' +
      '<path d="M100 4C84 40 82 120 90 172H110C118 120 116 40 100 4Z" fill="#a8d8f0"/>' +

      animalSvg('bear', 62, 204) + animalSvg('rabbit', 138, 204) +
```

```javascript
// Activity "Deszczyk i Tęcza": touch a cloud -> gentle rain for ~5 s; puddles ripple and fill a little;
// after 30 cloud-seconds of rain (each raining cloud adds 1 s per second) a soft rainbow fades in, stays, then fades out.
// All motion (rain, ripples, puddles, rainbow) runs in one rAF loop with a capped dt, so it works under
// prefers-reduced-motion and pauses (never replays) while the tab is hidden. DOM is bounded by fixed pools.
```

```javascript
// is a smooth pendulum (period 3.6 s) that never jerks and settles to rest in about 15 s. While the amplitude is above
// 20 deg up to 6 leaves at a time drift down slowly (5-7 s each) and are hidden again after their fall (pooled DOM).
// Touching the tree sways its crown once. Nothing is scored or stored.
```

```javascript
// Activity "Zegar z Kukułką": a wooden cuckoo clock on a pastel wall with a clock face (2 hands), a swinging pendulum

// out of it (0.6 s), waves slowly twice (1.8 s), slides back (0.6 s) and the door closes (1 s): 5 s in total. Touching
// a door that is already busy does nothing (no restart); different doors can be busy at the same time.
// Touch the hands -> the minute hand turns 90 degrees slowly (slew-limited speed, never backwards), the hour hand follows
```

```javascript
// Activity "Kulkowy Tor": four ramps the child turns (left / flat / right) steer a soft ball dropped from the top down to a
// basket with a friendly bear. Scripted, not full, physics in a fixed 400x360 board scaled by k:
//   - the ball is either falling straight down, sliding along the ramp it landed on, resting on the cushion or in the basket;
//   - a sliding ball follows the ramp's CURRENT target position (flat = slide to the nearer end), so turning a ramp under it
//     simply sends it the other way and it can never get stuck; falling and sliding use one constant speed (VEL), well under
//     the cap of 40% of the board height per second;
//   - every route ends in the basket or on the cushion; the cushion returns the ball to the top after 1 s and it falls again;
//   - the 3rd ball in the basket makes the track glow for 3 s and the ramps move to a new random arrangement
//     (never equal to the previous starting arrangement nor to the one they have just been left in).
// One rAF loop (capped dt, stopped when idle or the tab is hidden) drives everything, so reduced motion does not disable it.
// All state is in JS; layout only repositions the transparent buttons, so rotation / resize keeps the state.
// Nothing is scored or stored.

  var BW = 400, BH = 360;
```
